units.text: A resolution of the Citv of Boca Raton considerinq tentative plat approval for the proposed Oceanside Townhomes Plat ( Oceanside Townhomes PUD) located at 949, 959, and 969 Sweetwater Lane, subiect to conditions; providina for severability; providinq for repealer; providinq an effective date ( SUB- 15-03) Resolution No. 3-2016 Plans Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Items A and B would be conducted contemporaneously, as the petitions were related, and pursuant to quasi- judicial procedures. A separate vote would be taken on each resolution The City Attorney reviewed the quasi- judicial procedure that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Regular Minutes 4 January 11, 2016 Jim Bell, Planning & Zoning Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location, size, zoning and land use of the property were provided. The master plan was reviewed. Topics included, but were not limited to, size of units, building height, open space, and vehicular access. The PUD modifications were then detailed, including lot size and width, setbacks, plat size, access to arterial roadways, open space and perimeter landscape setback. Mr. Bell then explained the reasons that staff supports the modifications, before reviewing the parking and traffic analysis. Staff believes that the project is a good fit for the property. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval as does staff. Mr. Bell then responded to a number of questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, GrayRobinson, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. He addressed density, the PUD modifications being requested, and similar setbacks of other projects. In conclusion, he advocated approval and made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Bell then addressed a question about the acreage. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Resolution No. 2-2016. Members identified several points of concern, including the setbacks and conditions for the east landscape buffer. The City Attorney drafted language for a condition regarding the landscape buffer that would be added as new i) under Section 2, sub 3) of Planning & Zoning Board Resolution No. 2015-019, which is an exhibit of Resolution No. 2-2016. The language was generally consistent with " additional landscaping shall be installed along the eastern property line, subject to review and approval by City staff, to provide adequate screening for the adjacent property." The petitioner indicated that there was no objection to the condition. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, to amend Resolution No. 2-2016, to include the language as read by the City Attorney. Motion carried 4-0 on a voice vote. Main motion on Resolution No. 2-2016 as amended carried 4-0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Reso/ution No. 3-2016. Motion carried 4-0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the Citv of Boca Raton considerinq tentative plat approval for the proposed plat entitled Roval Palm Polo Plat Two ( a replat of the prior Roval Palm Polo PUD Plat) located at 6300 Old Clint Moore Road, subiect to conditions; providing for severabilitv; providinq for reqealer; providinq an effective date ( UC- 13-02R1/ SC) Resolution No. 5-2016 Plans Mayor Haynie indicated that the public hearings on items C, D, and E would be conducted contemporaneously, as the petitions were related, and pursuant to the quasi- judicial procedures still in effect. A separate vote would be taken on each resolution. IVlembers made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Planning & Zoning Manager, began the PowerPoint presentation with background information on Royal Palm Polo development. The changes requested were then reviewed, with the notation that said changes would have minimal impacts. Topics included, but were not limited to, setbacks, open space, lot width, parking requirements and trip generation. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the petitions. It was noted that a upper majority vote of Council is required for the modification of the Future Land Use Map ordinance. Staff recommends approval of the modification to the Universal Conditional Approval and the related resolutions. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to questions from Council members. Mr. Bell addressed a question regarding the parking requirements. The public hearing was opened. Jeff Brophy, Wantman Group, Inc. on behalf of Toll Brothers, addressed the question about parking requirements and then made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5338. Council Member Singer asked about the parking requirement at the clubhouse. Mr. Bell explained that deed restriction allowed for a lower number of parking spaces at a private clubhouse. Discussion ensued. Motion carried 4-0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Reso/ution No. 4-2016. Motion carried 4-0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton requesting the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District consider acquisition of oceanfront properties in the City for preservation and public use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mayor Haynie requested this resolution be drafted in light of the recent public response to the variance hearing for 2500 N. Ocean Boulevard. She noted that there are three buildable oceanfront properties which she felt could be acquired by the Beach and Park District, thus preventing any future development. Discussion ensued. Council Member Singer addressed his reluctant vote on the lot width variance for 2500 N. Ocean Boulevard, the Petruzzelli lot and the legal standing of a potential variance request, and recognition of a landowner' s right to develop a lot. He requested to amend the resolution in Section 1, line 11 to specify undeveloped oceanfront properties in the City of Boca Raton and not enumerate the addresses. Mayor Haynie accepted the friendly amendment. Discussion ensued. The City Attorney read into the record language generally consistent with the following in Section 1: on line 11, strike the word " certain"; strike the remainder of the Section; add, at the end of the Section, the parenthetical phrase " this request has no impact on the development potential, or lack thereof, of any property." Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution 12-2016 as amended. Motion carried 4-0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes. Regular Minutes 7 January 11, 2016

units.text: Deputy Mayor Weinroth noted that members will be travelling to Tallahassee for the opening of the legislative session. Council Member Singer provided information on House Bill 1051, which would prohibit overnight mooring of boats. Members agreed that Boca Raton should be included in the legislation. He then asked for information on the steps being taken to address the complaints about activities at Silver Palm Park. Members commented on homelessness and the use of the Park. Mr. Singer then addressed the manner in which past public input on the Wildflower property was categorized. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, provided background on the web page that allowed people to submit comments on the use of the property and how the responses were categorized. Some discussion ensued. Council Member Rodgers wished everyone happy new year. Mike Woika, Assistant City Manager, addressed Mayor Haynie' s question regarding the Florida Municipal Insurance Trust, noting that the City uses them for property insurance only, not liability.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 3. 04, of the City of Boca Raton Charter to establish new annual salaries for the Mayor and members of the City Council; providing that the annual salary of the Mayor shall be 40% of the salary of a member of the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners ( 40% of a County Commissioner' s salary is currently 38, 355. 20); providing that the annual salary of the other Council Members shall be 30% of the salary of a member of the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners ( 30% of a County Commissioner' s salary is currently $ 28, 766. 40); providing that the annual salaries for the Mayor and members of the City Council shall be increased each year by the increase, if any, in the salary of the members of the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners; providing for the submission of the proposed Charter Amendment to the electors of the City at a special election to be held on August 30, 2016 ( the date of the Primary Election); repealing Section 2-26, Code of Ordinances, which provides for annual salaries; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revision to the City Charter and for codification in the City Code of Ordinances; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5340 City Manager Leif Ahnell noted that this ordinance was consistent with the direction provided by Council. The public hearing was opened. John Gore offered suggestions that he felt would improve the ordinance. Al Zucaro stated his opposition to the ordinance and offered a number of suggestions. James Hendrey commented on the proposed salary increase and made several suggestions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Singer noted his opposition to passage of the ordinance at this time, citing his preference for this to come forward through a citizen petition and the timing of the election, among other issues. Council Member Mullaugh offered support of the ordinance. Council Member Rodgers inquired as to the cost of the election, as well as other topics, and then offered his support. units.text: City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser gave a brief report on Airport Authority appointments regarding unresolved issues as to who can serve on the Authority and what relationships could rise to the level of a prohibitive conflict. Ms. Frieser suggested that any applicant be asked to complete a supplemental disclosure of any potential conflicts that could affect their service. She sought direction on how to proceed. In light of the Commission on Ethics inaction with regard to this issue, Deputy Mayor Weinroth suggested that a court be asked to opine on the matter. Discussion ensued. Members agreed it was appropriate that a disclosure of this information be provided to any applicant to the Airport Authority and that an applicant acknowledge any relationship that could potentially pose a conflict.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to a Conditional Use approval (Resolution No. 23-2014) extending the closing hours of operation of the tasting room of a previously approved microbrewery, Barrel of Monks Microbrewery, located in the Penn-Florida Commerce Center at 1141 South Rogers Circle; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-13-04R1) Resolution No. 1-2016 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Planning and Zoning Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the microbrewery was provided and the previous conditional use approval was reviewed . The requested changes to the hours of operation were then detailed, and it was noted that no adverse impacts were identified by staff. After discussing a concern related to trash, the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff also recommended approval of the petition. The public hearing was opened. Mitch Kirschner, GrayRobinson, gave a brief PowerPoint, explaining the need for the extended hours and requesting approval. He also addressed the concern regarding adequate trash receptacles . Dr. William McFee, a proprietor of the brewery, addressed the request for extended hours for tours and tastings and addressed security and trash concerns . He also noted that Barrel of Monks supports various charities. Dr. McFee then responded to questions from Council members. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, addressed a question regarding the hours of operation for tours of the brewery and for the tasting room. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 1-2016. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 20-2016 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal by Taxi USA of Palm Beach, LLC d/b/a Taxi Taxi of the decision of the Hearing Officer denying an amendment to an existing Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for an additional 30 taxicabs; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 20-2016 Taxi USA Appeal Documents Part I Taxi USA Appeal Documents Part II The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jenny Wright, Senior Code Compliance Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with a brief review of process to obtain a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. A history of the Taxi Taxi application for an additional 30 taxicabs and the subsequent denial was provided. In conclusion, Ms. Wright reviewed the actions available to the Council as they consider this appeal. She then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Appellant Michael Solomon, Taxi Taxi, presented his case for granting the appeal thereby allowing his company to add 30 taxicabs that could not only drop off but also pick up passengers in Boca Raton. He addressed the population growth that could support more taxicabs, as well as the increase in illegal operators, and transportation network companies such as Uber and Lyft. Mr. Solomon then countered a number of points made by the Hearing Officer in his Final Order. In conclusion, he requested that Council reverse the decision of the Hearing Officer. Neil Schiller, presenting on behalf of Yellow Cab, gave a PowerPoint presentation challenging the application of Taxi Taxi and supporting the decision of the Hearing Officer. Mr. Schiller argued that Taxi Taxi did not prove the need for additional taxi service in Boca Raton. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council members. Brock Rosayn, Metro Taxi, gave a presentation in support of the decision of the hearing officer. He maintained that there is not a need for additional taxi service in Boca Raton. James Parks, A1A Limousine Service, read into the record a letter from the company's president in support of the addition of 30 taxicabs. Jerry Goldman, Personal Limousine Service, spoke in support of the additional taxicabs requested by Taxi Taxi. Ray Garcia, Prestige Limousine, requested that Council reverse the decision of the Hearing Officer. No one else came forward to speak. There was no cross examination. The appellant, Michael Solomon, offered comments in rebuttal and in support of the appeal. He then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was then closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 20-2016 affirming the decision of the Hearing Officer. Members made comments, asked questions, and offered their positions. The Mayor provided information on what may be happening at the state level regarding vehicles for hire. Motion carried 3 to 2; Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Michael Mullaugh voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Sections 16-32 and 16-33, Code of Ordinances, to prohibit commercial loading and unloading from public rights-of-way within the Community Redevelopment Area; including a reference to the definition of "collection services" and correcting a cross-reference; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5343 Ruby Childers, Downtown Manager, gave the presentation. She noted the revisions that were made to the ordinance in response to Council's direction at the March 8 Council meeting. Streets on which loading and unloading would be prohibited were identified. Upon concluding, Ms. Childers made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. The City Attorney noted that there was a scrivener's error, on page 3, line 11 of the ordinance, a missing comma after 'Road.' Deputy Mayor Weinroth asked if a Chamber of Commerce representative wanted to comment; they did not. Motion was made by Council Member Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5343 as amended. Members made final comments. Motion passed 4 to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Deputy Mayor Robert S. Weinroth voting no. units.text: Resolution No. 31-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to conditional use approval Resolution No. 123-2011 {as amended by Resolution No. 65-2013) (which authorized a school in a R-1-A Zoning District) to allow the construction of a 6,981 square foot addition to an existing 9,311 square foot building, a 7,003 square foot addition to an existing 3,721 square foot building, a new 2,350 square foot building and a new 486 square foot clock tower, and parking lot modifications to provide twenty-five {25) additional parking spaces {for a total number of parking spaces of 688) and to allow three {3) non-residential improvements in a residential district exceeding 25 feet in building height: {1) a 29 foot 5 inch building addition; {2) a 28 foot building; and (3) a new 35 foot 8 inch clock tower; for St. Andrew's School located at 3900 Jog Road; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date {UC-07-01 R3/CA) Resolution No. 31-2016 Plans Elizabeth Anderson, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with a review of the petition and the location of the site. The improvements, including the Entrepreneurial Center, the gateway building, the Learning Lab and the clock tower, were described. Ms. Anderson reviewed the additional parking and noted the lack of any traffic impacts. The conditional uses required are for height. PZB approved unanimously and staff recommends approval. The public hearing was opened. Mary Jo Finnocchiaro, on behalf of St. Andrew's School, briefly addressed the School's commitment to excellence in education and the need for these new spaces in that endeavor. She expressed thanks for the Council's consideration. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 31-2016. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

Kevin Meaney expressed concern about changing the zoning to allow increased building height on the barrier island. Ben Donne commented on the property at 2500 North Ocean Boulevard. Richard Gonzalez introduced his company that provides paratransit services. Raymond Blasi commented on the increase in trash along area roadways that may be caused by the increase in the number of college students. The City Manager noted that additional crews have been added to pick up liter. Members noted that FAU could be alerted to this problem. Katie MacDougall expressed concern about the building height ordinance and commented on development along Palmetto Park Road. James Hendry commented on development on the beach. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton to amend Chapter 28 "Zoning," City's Code of Ordinances, relating to building height and height provisions; amending Section 28-391 to delete allowance for additional building height in the R-2 Zoning District; amending Sections 28-451, 28-481, and 28-511 to set the maximum height for accessory structures at 25 feet (and delete allowance for additional height) in the R-3-A, R-3-B, and R-3-C Zoning Districts; amending Section 28-780 to delete allowance for additional building height in the B-1 Zoning District; amending Sections 28-874, 28-983, 28-1074, and 28-1099 to delete the reference to "stories" and retain measurement of height in feet in the C-1, LIRP Employee Service Node, M-1 and M-2 Zoning Districts; amending Section 28-1126 to delete allowance for additional height for accessory structures in the M-3 Zoning District; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-14) Ordinance No. 5345 Council Member Weinroth addressed the request for postponement and asked for an abbreviated presentation and public comment. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with an overview of the history of this item. The various height references in the code for the B-1, R-2, R-3-A, R-3-B, R-3-C, C-1, LIRP Employee Service Node, M-1, M-2, and M-3 zoning districts were provided, followed by the recommendations of staff and the Planning & Zoning Board. Ms. Allen noted that the proposed changes are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and Council's direction. Upon concluding, she responded to a number of questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Evan Aronson, in-house counsel for James and Marta Batmasian, reiterated his clients' request to postpone the public hearing on this ordinance until the May 24, 2016 City Council meeting. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 3.08, of the Charter of the City of Boca Raton to amend the method for filling vacancies on the City Council, including the office of mayor; providing that vacancies shall be filled by special election; providing for the submission of the proposed Charter amendment to the electors of the City at a special election to be held on August 30, 2016 (the date of the primary election); amending Section 6-4, Code of Ordinances to delete a provision rendered obsolete and establish a minimum qualification period for special elections; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revision to the City Charter and for codification in the Code of Ordinances; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5347 Council Member Singer, having requested that the ordinance be drafted, provided the rationale for the amendments which would provide for elections to fill Council vacancies. Mr. Singer noted the importance of allowing voters to have their say and then addressed the cost of special elections. Members weighed in and expressed their support or lack thereof. Council Member Weinroth asked that the City Attorney share the amendment he requested which addressed only vacancies in the event a Council member resigns to run for another City office. Discussion of the current code and charter, the ordinance as introduced, and the proposed amendment ensued. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann and Alan Feinberg, Jr. expressed their opposition to the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer to approve Ordinance No. 5347. Motion died for lack of a second. Members made final comments. Council Member Singer expressed disappointment and asked again for a second to his motion. Mayor Haynie echoed the sentiment that this topic has merit and should be addressed and discussed in the future.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to its Comprehensive Plan to update the City's 10-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan; amending the Conservation, Infrastructure, Intergovernmental Coordination Elements, and map series of the City's Comprehensive Plan related to the 10-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan Update; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-15-01) Ordinance No. 5342 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with background information on the Work Plan. The Plan updates were then summarized and the proposed amendments to the City's Comprehensive Plan were detailed. It was noted that no comments were received from the various state agency that reviewed the amendment. Ms. Allen noted that the Treasure Coast Regional Planning Council unanimously approved the Comp Plan amendments. The Planning & Zoning Board also unanimously recommended approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen made herself available for questions. Lisa Wilson-Davis, Utility Services Operations & Environmental Compliance Manager, responded to questions. Then public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5342. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton to amend Chapter 28 "Zoning," City's Code of Ordinances, relating to building height and height provisions; amending Section 28-391 to delete allowance for additional building height in the R-2 Zoning District; amending Sections 28-451, 28-481, and 28-511 to set the maximum height for accessory structures at 25 feet (and delete allowance for additional height) in the R-3-A, R-3-B, and R-3-C Zoning Districts; amending Section 28-780 to delete allowance for additional building height in the B-1 Zoning District; amending Sections 28-87 4, 28-983, 28-1074, and 28-1099 to delete the reference to "stories" and retain measurement of height in feet in the C-1, LIRP Employee Service Node, M-1 and M-2 Zoning Districts; amending Section 28-1126 to delete allowance for additional height for accessory structures in the M-3 Zoning District; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-14) Ordinance No. 5345 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this public hearing was continued from the April 23, 2016 City Council meeting. She provided brief background information and then detailed the proposed changes to the various height provisions in Chapter 28. The changes to the ordinance recommended by the Planning & Zoning Board were reviewed. Ms. Allen then responded to questions about the specific recommendation to treat certain B-1 areas differently. The public hearing was opened. Robert Eisen, on behalf of Investments Limited and a number of other property owners, gave a PowerPoint presentation beginning with brief comments on B-1 zoning districts. He was joined by Doug Mummaw who advocated retaining flexibility in the zoning code. Mr. Eisen then spoke in opposition to the ordinance, suggested that a planning task force be created to review the bridge to ocean area of Palmetto Park Road and advocated tabling the ordinance. Kevin Meaney, Riviera Civic Association, voiced support of a task force to look at Palmetto Park Road east of the lntracoastal Waterway and advocated capping building height at 30 feet in that area. Mark Simmons voiced support of the ordinance as well as the task force. Glenn Gromann voiced his concerns regarding the ordinance, addressed flexibility, and advocated treating the east area of Palmetto Park Road differently. Nancy Hendrey agreed with comments of previous speaker regarding a different treatment of the east area of Palmetto Park Road. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. George Brown, Acting City Manager, responded to a question regarding creating a new zoning district in the bridge to ocean area of Palmetto Park Road. Council members offered their thoughts. In general, members agreed to go ahead with a task force, as proposed by several previous speakers, to look at a new zoning district for this area. Members commented. The City Attorney noted that a new zoning district could not be created through an amendment to this ordinance. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5345 as amended, with respect to the 8-1 district, to remove the strikethrough in Section 5, lines 16 through 19 and change "shall" to "may" on line 18. The City Attorney provided clarification and further information on Mr. Rodgers' proposed amendments with regard to theB-1 zoning district. Discussion ensued regarding the proposed amendments, tabling the ordinance, zoning in progress, and protecting residential areas abutting B-1 zoning districts from additional height. Motion was withdrawn by Council Member Rodgers. The City Attorney spoke to the time frame for zoning in progress versus declaring a moratorium to protect the status quo while a task force is underway. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth to table Ordinance No. 5345. Motion died for lack of a second. Discussion of possible amendments to the ordinance continued. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5345 as amended to remove the strikethrough in Section 5, lines 16 through 19 and change "shall" to "may" on line 18. A brief discussion ensued Motion was withdrawn by Council Member Rodgers. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to table Ordinance No. 5345 and bring forward a moratorium. Once again, brief comments ensued. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Mayor Susan Haynie voting no. The City Attorney commented on the task force. Acting City Manager Brown noted that the ordinance could be adopted without section 5, leaving the B-1 zoning district unchanged. He provided information on other sections of the ordinance that address height in other zoning districts, all of which staff felt should be addressed. Mr. Brown noted that staff recommended adopting the ordinance as is. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5345 amended to delete Section 5. Several suggestions for an amendment to the motion followed. Motion second by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers was withdrawn. Motion died for lack of a second. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5345 as amended to change Section 5. The Mayor announced a short break to allow the City Attorney to craft the amendments. The meeting was recessed at approximately 7:30 pm. The meeting reconvened at approximately 7:45 pm. The City Attorney detailed the proposed amendments, generally consistent with the following: in the title, delete the phrase "amending Section 28-780 to delete allowance for additional building height in the B-1 Zoning District" and insert "replacing the word "shall" with "may" in Section 28-780; on page 3, line 25, add after Code, "with the exceptions of amendments proposed for the B-1 Zoning District which were modified"; and on page 5, lines 16 through 19, the deleted text will be reinstated and on line 18, the word "shall" will be struck and the word "my" will be inserted. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5345 as amended. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Jeremy voting yes; Rodgers Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, Mayor Susan Haynie voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to table Ordinance No. 5345. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Mayor Susan Haynie voting no. Ordinance No. 5348 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for the vacation and abandonment of portions of a water easement located at 6101 Park of Commerce Boulevard, as more specifically described herein; approving and accepting a replacement water easement deed over certain lands located at 6101 Park of Commerce Boulevard; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (EA-16-06) Ordinance No. 5348 Lynn Bodor, Property Appraiser/Specialist, gave a brief presentation detailing the necessity for the easement abandonment and acceptance of the easement deed. It was noted that all agencies approved the abandonment. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5348. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Council Member Singer asked if these types of ordinances could be handled administratively. In general, members agreed that doing so was appropriate for utility easements.

units.text: Jim Utterback commented on the decision by the Palm Beach County School District Adult Education Department to close two community school programs in Boca Raton. James Hendrey commented on the comprehensive waterfront study and advocated that no negotiations go forward on the Wildflower property until the study is complete. Glenn Gromann commented on streamlining the IDA process. Kevin Meaney commented on the proposed Council salary increases. Matt Welhaf, president of firefighters union, recognized five recently honored firefighters. Troy McClellan commented on the development of the Wildflower property. He then offered thanks to Council and staff as well as providing further comments. Al Zucaro commented on the change in tone of recent discussions as well as other topics. He then addressed ethics complaints he had filed.

units.text: Council Member Weinroth announced the Memorial Day commemoration and concert. Council Member Singer addressed the proposed 1% sales tax and his desire to discuss the matter. He presented a slide detailing sales tax inequality and again asked that the agenda be amended to consider his resolution which would state Boca Raton's lack of support. Discussion followed. Members expressed their positions. In general, the majority agreed to draft a letter expressing concern about the impact of the tax on our community. Mr. Singer then advocated consolidating the Green Living Advisory Board and the Environmental Advisory Board. The Acting City Manager provided information. In general, there was support for a consolidation. Mr. Singer also advocated that the Downtown Advisory Committee review the open space policy. Regarding a parking study, Mr. Brown noted that staff would provide an update. In conclusion, Mr. Singer highlighted upcoming events downtown. Council Member Rodgers addressed comments made during public requests regarding adult education and Wayne Barton's request for assistance with a permit, as well as other topics. Deputy Mayor Mullaugh discussed the importance of programs that help parents to help their children with homework. Mayor Haynie asked that the staff research the parking garage issue and the permitting issue brought up by Wayne Barton. She advocated working with all parties to address the noise at Blue Martini. She also reported on a recent meeting with Office Depot and announced the upcoming Architectural Roundtable that she and Community Appearance Board Chairman Juan Caycedo would be hosting on June 8.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 3.08 of the Charter of the City of Boca Raton to amend the method for filling vacancies on the City Council, including the office of Mayor: providing that vacancies shall be filled by special election; providing for the submission of the proposed Charter Amendment to the electors of the City at a special election to be held on August 30, 2016 (the date of the Primary Election); amending Section 6-4, Code of Ordinances, to delete a provision rendered obsolete and establish minimum requirements for the qualification period for special elections; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revision to the City Charter and for codification in the Code of Ordinances; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5350 Council Member Singer gave a brief PowerPoint presentation explaining his reasoning for bringing this ordinance forward. He noted that this legislation would allow the people to have their say with regard to filling a vacancy on the Council. Upon concluding, Mr. Singer responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Andrea Steckloff, Nanette Gordon, Geraldine Allerman, Cindy Bloom, Lenore Wachtel, Betty Grinnan, Andrea O'Rourke, Kevin Meaney, Elizabeth Hoffman, Eddie Weinstein, George O'Rourke, JoAnn Landon, James Hendrey, Jack Fox, Beth Di Prato, Al Zucaro, and Helene Eichler expressed their support of the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5350. Deputy Mayor Mullaugh offered brief comments in support of the ordinance. Council Member Weinroth commented on special elections and Council seat openings due to a resign-to-run situation. Council Member Singer explained that this issue is addressed by this ordinance. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5351 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for the vacation and abandonment of a portion of a public utility and drainage easement located at 284 Northeast 7th Street, as more specifically described herein; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date {EA-15-04) Ordinance No. 5351 Lynn Bodor, Property Specialist/Appraiser, gave a brief presentation, identifying the need for and location of the requested easement vacation and abandonment, noting staff's recommendation to grant the request. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5351. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5352 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 2-26, Code of Ordinances, to increase the annual salaries of the Mayor and members of the City Council as of October 1, 2016; providing that the annual salary of the Mayor shall be $38,000.00; providing that the annual salary of the other Council Members shall be $28,000.00; providing for the submission of the proposed salary increases to the electors of the City at a special election to be held on August 30, 2016 {the date of the Primary Election); repealing Ordinance No. 5340; providing for severability; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5352 Council Member Weinroth gave a brief explanation of this ordinance, which he brought forward. He noted that he did so in response to many comments he received regarding the automatic salary increases provided for in Ordinance 5340 that are not included in this ordinance. The public hearing was opened. James Hendrey, Kevin Meaney, Eddie Weinstein, and Helene Eichler offered supportive comments regarding increasing Council salaries. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5352. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Singer voting no.

Ordinance No. 5352 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 2-26, Code of Ordinances, to increase the annual salaries of the Mayor and members of the City Council as of October 1, 2016; providing that the annual salary of the Mayor shall be $38,000.00; providing that the annual salary of the other Council Members shall be $28,000.00; providing for the submission of the proposed salary increases to the electors of the City at a special election to be held on August 30, 2016 {the date of the Primary Election); repealing Ordinance No. 5340; providing for severability; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5352 Council Member Weinroth gave a brief explanation of this ordinance, which he brought forward. He noted that he did so in response to many comments he received regarding the automatic salary increases provided for in Ordinance 5340 that are not included in this ordinance. The public hearing was opened. James Hendrey, Kevin Meaney, Eddie Weinstein, and Helene Eichler offered supportive comments regarding increasing Council salaries. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5352. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Singer voting no.

units.text: Jackie Reeves spoke in support of a restaurant at the Wildflower property and noted her lack of support for an upcoming ballot question. Jack Fox, speaking on behalf of the Beach Condo Association, offered support for a restaurant at the Wildflower property. Margaret Fitzsimons requested amendments to the site plan and Hillstone restaurant lease. She presented several slides illustrating her suggestions for a public walkway. Elisabeth Hoffman commented on having accessible open space at the Wildflower project. Eddie Weinstein commented on pedestrian traffic and advocated that the City become more pedestrian friendly. Lenore Wachtel advocated that the public be allowed to vote on use of the Wildflower property and expressed her disapproval of the Hillstone lease. Kevin Meaney commented on the use of Wildflower property and advocated having the people vote. Jack McWalter commented on the proposed one cent tax increase. Susan Saturday, on behalf of BlueGreen Corporation, supported a restaurant on the Wildflower property. James Hendrey commented on the stance of previous speakers regarding the Wildflower property. Valentina Moretti spoke in support of a restaurant at the Wildflower property. Jerry Fedele, on behalf of the Chamber of Commerce, offered support of the ordinance increasing Council salaries and commented on the Wildflower property and the democratic process. Jim Wood commented on aspects of the Hillstone lease as presented at the June 9 Planning and Zoning Board meeting. Joseph Graubart commented on quality of life issues in the Miami area as compared to Boca Raton. Stephanie De Martino expressed support of the Hillstone restaurant at the Wildflower property and opposition to a park at that location. Andrea O'Rourke commented on creating an overall vision for the City through place-making and the use of the Wildflower property. Deborah Cusick commented on the motivation for increased density and the Wildflower property. Bob Tucker advocated having a waterfront restaurant at the Wildflower property. George O'Rourke commented on aspects of the Hillstone lease proposal, the recent Planning & Zoning Board meeting, and the walkability of the downtown. Al Zucaro commented on the Hillstone lease proposal and asked about the timeframe for an appeal of a Planning & Zoning Board decision. The City Attorney provided information in response to Mr. Zucaro's question. Helene Eichler commented on the referendum on city-owned intracoastal land and other topics related to the Hillstone restaurant. Lynette Gordon expressed opposition to a restaurant on the Wildflower property. Jacqueline Dheere commented on the many resources that can be enjoyed in Boca Raton and advocated approval of a restaurant at the Wildflower property. JoAnn Landon advocated having a park at the Wildflower property and commented on having a pedestrian­ friendly city. Gene Folden provided historical information on public input in support of a restaurant at the Wildflower property and expressed his support of a restaurant at that location. Jose Barrera addressed the RFP for the Wildflower property and advocated a combination of a restaurant use and an important public space. He also commented on civic space.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan for certain property consisting of 1.1337 acres, located on the northern portion of 551 East Palmetto Park Road, as more specifically described herein, from Residential Low (RL) to Commercial (C); providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-14-03) Ordinance No. 5353 Ordinance No. 5354 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton rezoning a parcel of land consisting of 1.1337 acres located on the northern portion of 551 East Palmetto Park Road, as more specifically described herein, from Single Family Residential (R-1-B) zoning district to Local Business (B-1) zoning district; providing for revisions to the Zoning District Map: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (ZC-14-01) Ordinance No. 5354 Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on items A and B would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures as required for Ordinance 5354. A separate vote would be taken on each ordinance. The Mayor also stated that Ordinance 5353 required four votes for \passage. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk read the administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, identifying the location, zoning and future land use designation of the property. Ms. Allen reviewed the past priorities of the City Council with regard to the acquisition and development of the Wildflower property. The analysis of the flum amendment and the rezoning were reviewed. Several tables illustrating the trip generation associated with the proposed changes were presented and explained. Ms. Allen noted that staff recommends approval of both petitions as does the PZB. She then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Andrea O'Rourke commented on place-making. She was joined by Margaret Fitzsimmons and Jose Berrera who pres.ented an alternative plan for the Wildflower property. Bobra Bush, Peg Anderson, Gwen Tucker, Bob Tucker, Jackie Reeves, Jacqueline Dheere, Lee Babey, Tom Zeichman, Rick Howard, Phillip Kittell, Troy Mclellan, Jon Carter expressed support of a restaurant on the Wildflower property. Emily Gentile, representing the Beach Condo Association, expressed support of the Hillstone restaurant. Jerry Fedele, Chamber of Commerce Board Chair, expressed support of a restaurant and noted that walking paths and other amenities are not mutually exclusive with a restaurant. Jim Wood gave a brief PowerPoint presentation commenting on the revenue potential of the Wildflower property and expressed his lack of support for the ordinances. James Hendrey commented on the initiative petition referendum and aspects of the proposed restaurant lease. Lenore Wachtel expressed support of a park on the Wildflower property. Helene Eichler expressed lack of support for a restaurant and urged residents to vote on the referendum, as did Joe Pedalino. Mitch Kirschner commented on the initiative petition referendum and the Wildflower. Kim Heisey expressed support of open natural areas and parks. Eve Reed commented on the proposed lease, her lack of support of a restaurant, and public art. Glenn Gromann expressed support for both ordinances. George O'Rourke addressed a 2014 traffic study and advocated tabling the ordinances, as did Al Zucaro. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Under cross examination, George O'Rourke asked questions of Ingrid Allen regarding the traffic analysis. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Ordinance No. 5353. Members offered numerous comments addressing many of the statements made during the public hearing. Maria Tejara, City Traffic Engineer, responded to questions about the traffic analysis and provided information on her update to the original analysis. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Scott Singer voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5354. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Scott Singer voting no. At this time, the meeting was recessed without objection at approximately 9:06 pm. The meeting was reconvened at approximately 9:15 pm.

The Deputy Mayor acknowledged that he would again introduce the ordinance. nd Lee Babey commented on the Boca Inlet and the traffic light at 32 Street and Federal Highway. Gene Folden commented on the Inlet and a recent presentation by Steve Alley on the Lake Wyman project, advocating moving the project forward. Margaret Fitzsimmons commented on the consolidation of the Green Living Advisory Board and the Environmental Advisory Board.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5356 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton proposing an amendment to the City Code of Ordinances creating new City Code Section 28-1308, City Owned lntracoastal Lands; providing that city­ owned parcels adjacent to the lntracoastal Waterway shall only be used for public recreation, public boating access, public streets, and city stormwater uses only; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5356 .L Resolution No. 60-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton providing for a special election regarding an ordinance proposed by initiative to regulate the use of city-owned lntracoastal lands; providing for submission of the ballot question to the electors of the City at a special election on November 8 1 2016 (the date of the General Election); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 60-2016 Jim Bell, Planning and Zoning Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. A brief overview of the background of this initiative petition ordinance. The numerous easements that exist on cit-y land adjacent to the lntracoastal were listed. The differences in code section 28-1307 and the proposed section were identified. It was noted that the PZB review resulted in a 3-3 vote; so there was no recommendation. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to questions from Council members. The City Attorney addressed Resolution 60-2016 noting that it provides for a vote should the ordinance not be adopted. The public hearing was opened. Jim Wood gave a PowerPoint presentation identifying and discussing a number of public/private partnerships for parks, recreation and art. He advocated passage of the ordinance. James Hendrey and Jo-Ann Landon advocated passage of the ordinance. Winnie and Joe Pedalino commented on the City's parks and beaches and advocated passage of the ordinance. Andrea O'Rourke advocated having waterfront public spaces and passage of the ordinance. Jose Barerra commented on the site plan for the restaurant proposed for the Wildflower property and use of the property for public recreation. He advocated passage of the ordinance. Nancy Liu commented on congestion caused by recent development and advocated having a park on the Wildflower property. Ryan Dick commented on development in the city and advocated saving green space for the public and passage of the ordinance. Nancy Hendrey advocated passage of the ordinance and having green space and public parks. Joe Graubart, Kevin Meaney, George O'Rourke, Robbie Denman advocated passage of the ordinance. Linda Marinas advocated having a restaurant on the Wildflower property. Al Zucaro commented on Mr. Bell's presentation and the Planning & Zoning Board review of the ordinance, advocating its passage. Phillip Kittell expressed his view that the ordinance should be voted on by all the people. Margaret Fitzsimmons commented on protecting waterfront property and establishing guidelines for same. She advocated adoption of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann addressed aspects of the proposed ordinance and the Planning & Zoning Board review. Anthony Majhess addressed previous comments and his recollections of the Wildflower property acquisition during his tenure on City Council. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 60-2016. Discussion ensued. The City Attorney addressed questions regarding Ordinance 5356. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer to lay Resolution No. 60-2016 on the table and vote on Ordinance No. 5356. Motion died for lack of a second. Members commented further. Motion to approve Resolution No. 60-2016 carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to indefinitely postpone consideration of Ordinance No. 5356. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Scott Singer voting no. The meeting went into recess at approximately 8:05 pm. Florida. as initiated by the City of Boca Raton; providing for a referendum on the question of annexation for the registered electors within the property proposed for annexation; providing for a revision of the City's boundaries pursuant to the City Charter to include the property annexed; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5357

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for the involuntary annexation of property generally located north of Clint Moore Road and west of Military Trail and comprising all currently unincorporated property in the following subdivisions: Azura (Oxley Northern PUD). Newport Bay Club. Tides at Newport Bay, Copper Lake, Hampton Club. Fieldbrook, Boniello's Acres. and Boniello's Acres Phase 2. as more particularly described herein, to the corporate limits of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, as initiated by the City of Boca Raton; providing for a referendum on the question of annexation for the registered electors within the property proposed for annexation; providing for a revision of the City's boundaries pursuant to the City Charter to include the property annexed; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5358 Mayor Haynie noted that this was the first of two public hearings on Ordinance 5357 and Ordinance 5358 and no votes would be taken. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation on both of the proposed annexation areas based on the analysis completed by PMG Associates. The revenues and expenses associated with the annexations were reviewed as was the impact to the homeowners in each area. The analysis estimated the net fiscal impact at just over $764,000. The recommendation of the report was to move forward. The annexation actions calendar was reviewed. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Michael Vislocky, a resident of Boniello Acres, gave a PowerPoint presentation making the case that the City should not annex his neighborhood. He provided a handout for the Council in support of his position. Arlene Vislocky also expressed a lack of support for annexation. Jonathon Silver commented on what the impacts, other than financial, would be to the residents of Boniello Acres. He advocated having all city residents vote on this annexation. Daria Wells voiced her lack of support for annexation. Paula Winker asked a number of questions regarding annexation. Susan Silver advocated against annexation. George O'Rourke advocated having all City residents vote on annexations. George Gersh and Al Zucaro expressed opposition to this annexation. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council members weighed in and posed a number of questions to which George Brown responded. In general, direction was given to explore the opportunity for all City residents to vote on annexation as well as the opportunity for Boniello Acres to vote separately on annexation of their neighborhood. Ordinance No. 5359 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Fiscal Year 2015-2016 budget through the First Budget Amendment; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5359 Sharon McGuire, Office of Management & Budget Director, gave a brief presentation reviewing the proposed budget amendment. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Ordinance No. 5359. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton equalizing the assessments; levying the same as assessments against benefited properties within the Downtown Special Assessment District, City of Boca Raton, Florida; directing the City Clerk to record assessments in the Improvement Lien Book; establishing priority of lien and payment of principal and interest; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 87-2016 Stephen Timberlake, Special Projects Manager, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation on the proposed 2017 Downtown Special Assessment. units.section: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES. AND CAPITAL
units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES. AND CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM Proposed CIP City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a PowerPoint presentation reviewing the proposed budget for the coming fiscal year. The goals and priorities set by Council during the May 2016 Strategic Planning Sessions were listed; details were provided. The recommended millage rate for the 2016-17 fiscal year is 3.6789, which is a slight decrease from last year. Mr. Ahnell then reviewed proposed increases and decreases in various operating costs, as well as detailing new personnel. There followed a number of charts and graphs illustrating the various taxing authorities on a resident's tax bill; assessed property values in Boca Raton; tax rate history; and tax rates, fire assessment, library, and water/sewer rates comparing Boca Raton favorably with other neighboring municipalities. He then turned the presentation over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2016/17-2021-/22 Capital Improvement Program (CIP). Ms. McGuire noted the sources of revenue that will fund capital improvements and then reviewed, by department, the projects, vehicles and equipment included in the CIP for 2016-2017 fiscal year. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire and Mr. Ahnell responded to questions from Council members.

units.text: Resolution No. 90-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the 900 Broken Sound PMD Master Plan, Resolution No. 56-2014, to amend the approved Phase I Planned Mobility Matrix to delete requirements for an internal shuttle circulator, van pool and MOV preferential parking, and shower and locker facilities on site, and reduce the discounted rate for transit fare subsidy passes provided to residents; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-13-01 R2/SC) Resolution No. 90-2016 Resolution No. 91-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the 900 Broken Sound PMD Site Plan, Resolution No. 57-2014, to modify the declaration of covenants and restrictions related to private solid waste pickup and to amend the approved Phase I Planned Mobility Matrix to delete requirements for an internal shuttle circulator, van pool and MOV preferential parking, and shower and locker facilities on site, and reduce the discounted rate for transit fare subsidy passes provided to residents, and modifying conditions for Phase I and Phase II of the site plan for 900 Broken Sound located at 900 NW Broken Sound Boulevard and 900 NW Broken Sound Parkway; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-13-01 R2/SPA) Resolution No. 91-2016 The Mayor noted that items A. and B. would be heard together as the petitions are related. A separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner with Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with background information on the project. The requested modifications to the Declaration of Covenants and Restrictions and the Planned Mobility Matrix were then reviewed. Details were provided. It was noted that the Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approved of the requested modifications. the petition. Staff recommends approval of the petition as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the petitioner, made brief comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members discussed the requests, noting various concerns with, in particular, the elimination of the internal circulator. Ms. Miskel explained that the requested modifications were grounded in the City's revision of the PMD requirements and the decrease in the required PMD points. Members offered further comments regarding the change to the matrix, the reasons for same, and the need to review the matrix further. In response to a question, Ms. Eassa explained that this submittal would meet the current matrix requirements. She then pointed out a scrivener's error in Resolution 91-2016: on page 9, line 6 the word 'within' should be delted. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 90-2016. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to a site plan to allow the demolition of an existing 6,025 square foot building to allow the construction of an approximately 7,350 square foot two-story community center (to include general offices and meeting chambers for the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District), an approximately 3,510 square foot maintenance building, an approximately 2,320 square foot addition to the existing tennis pro­ shop, and additional site improvements for the Boca Raton Swim and Racquet Club located at 21618 St. Andrews Boulevard; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-15-12) Resolution No. 94-2016 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that hearings on items C., D. and E. would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related, and pursuant to the same quasi-judicial procedures as previously stated. A separate vote would be taken on each petition. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa gave the PowerPoint presentation. She reviewed the location, site plan, elevations, Pod redesignation, conditional use, and traffic analysis. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the requested modifications. In conclusion, Ms. Eassa stated staff's recommendation for approval, and then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation on the project. He provided a history of the site and reviewed the condition of the current buildings as well as the plans for the renovated facilities, including additional amenities. Mr. Mummaw described the architecture as depicted in elevations of the new buildings, noting that the designs had been modified from the original submission to Council. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council members. Arthur Koski, Interim Executive Director of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District, the petitioner, responded to questions regarding fees for and access to various areas of the park. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Resolution No. 92-2016. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, advised that Mr. Mummaw mentioned that the architectural treatments of the buildings had been modified from the plans provided to Council. Mr. Brown suggested that, to avoid any confusion, Mr. Mummaw's presentation showing the appropriate architectural treatment should be referenced in the appropriate location in Resolutions 92, 93, and 94-2016, and attached as an exhibit. Mr. Mullaugh and Ms. Haynie accepted the amendment to the motion on the floor. Mr. Rodgers expressed concern in regard to the government use of the main building.
