units.text: Resolution No. 76-2016 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal by M.E. Signs, Inc., on behalf of Investments Limited, of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying approval of, alteration and relocation of an existing freestanding sign with new tenant copy (to be located at 351 East Yamato Road), and denying approval of sign copy for four (4) tenants on a new freestanding sign (to be located at 331 East Yamato Road); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 76-2016 Mayor Haynie noted that the agenda had been reordered to hear item 17. C. first. She also stated that the same quasi-judicial procedures explained earlier in the meeting would continue to apply. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the site plan and the location of the two signs in question. Descriptions were provided. Staff does not support the existing sign at 351 Yamato Road and recommends that Council affirm the Community Appearance Board (CAB) denial of permit# 16-2481. With regard to the new sign at 331 Yamato Road, staff recommends that Council grant the appeal and reverse the CAB decision. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the appeal. He began with a discussion of architectural signage, way finding, sign color, branding and other related topics. The two signs were described; the objections of the CAB were listed. In conclusion, Mr. Mummaw requested that both signs be approved and then responded to questions. Juan Caycedo, CAB chairman, addressed the subjectivity of signage and the way in which CAB has evolved in its consideration of signage. He then addressed the signs in question, expressing his opinion, and that of the CAB, that both signs should be of the same design. Mr. Caycedo asked that Council carefully consider all sign variances and, in this case, not grant the appeal. He reiterated his comments about sign pollution and then responded to Council members' questions. During rebuttal, Mr. Mummaw responded to Mr. Caycedo's comments and continued to explain his position with respect to signage. Mr. Caycedo made final comments noting that signs on building may be colorful but monument signs should have monochromatic letters with colorful logos. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments, expressing opinions on the subject of signage and these appeals. The Mayor noted that the matters could be remanded to CAB or the matter could be postponed. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to adopt Resolution No. 76-2016 to remand both matters to the Community Appearance Board. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 35-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from the provisions of Section 24-96(b)(1 ), Code of Ordinances, to allow one free-standing sign with eleven (11) tenant names on two sign faces (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on two sign faces): and a second free-standing sign with six (6) tenant names on each sign face (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on each sign face), for a commercial property located at 1944 NE Fifth Avenue: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SCV-15-02) Resolution No. 35-2016 Again, Mayor Haynie reminded everyone noted that quasi-judicial procedures continued to apply.. Members made their ex parte disclosers. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the shopping center and the location of the proposed monument signs were identified. The variance is for the number of tenant names on each sign. Mr. Harbilus noted that staff recommends denial of the variances as no undue hardship exists. Upon concluding, Mr. Harbilas responded to questions from Council members. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, provided further information on the provisions of the sign code and offered historical perspective on the subject. He also responded to further questions for Council members. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw presented on behalf of the petitioner. He addressed the City's current sign code. He noted that the proposed signs would only increase the number of tenant names on the sign, not the overall size of the monument. Numerous examples of signs were provided. Mr. Mummaw detailed the hardships asserted by his client. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council members. Discussion ensued. Topics included, but were not limited to, allowing more monuments based on linear feet of the center, color on signs, height of signs, the number of tenants in the center, and architectural integration of signs. Mr. Mummaw provided a depiction of a compromise sign with fewer panels. Juan Caycedo, chairman of CAB, commented on the proposals and the discussion at CAB. He noted that the variance was only for the number of tenants on a sign, not color or design. He reiterated his views on visual contamination and asserted that approving this variance could change the character of the City. He then responded to members' questions. It was suggested that this matter be remanded to CAB. Robert Eisen commented on a discussion of the number of tenant names on signs that took place at a CAB meeting. Doug Giordano commented on the use of the term 'subjective.' Barry Pokrifcsak commented on remanding this matter back to CAB and advocated continuing with a workshop on signage. Mr. Mummaw and Mr. Caycedo made final remarks in response to previous comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney addressed the fact that this is a variance and proposed the option of continuation so that the parties would have the opportunity to work on a solution. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to continue Resolution No. 35-2016 to the second City Council meeting in November. Members made final comments and suggestions Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.
units.full: Resolution No. 76-2016 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal by M.E. Signs, Inc., on behalf of Investments Limited, of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying approval of, alteration and relocation of an existing freestanding sign with new tenant copy (to be located at 351 East Yamato Road), and denying approval of sign copy for four (4) tenants on a new freestanding sign (to be located at 331 East Yamato Road); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 76-2016 Mayor Haynie noted that the agenda had been reordered to hear item 17. C. first. She also stated that the same quasi-judicial procedures explained earlier in the meeting would continue to apply. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the site plan and the location of the two signs in question. Descriptions were provided. Staff does not support the existing sign at 351 Yamato Road and recommends that Council affirm the Community Appearance Board (CAB) denial of permit# 16-2481. With regard to the new sign at 331 Yamato Road, staff recommends that Council grant the appeal and reverse the CAB decision. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the appeal. He began with a discussion of architectural signage, way finding, sign color, branding and other related topics. The two signs were described; the objections of the CAB were listed. In conclusion, Mr. Mummaw requested that both signs be approved and then responded to questions. Juan Caycedo, CAB chairman, addressed the subjectivity of signage and the way in which CAB has evolved in its consideration of signage. He then addressed the signs in question, expressing his opinion, and that of the CAB, that both signs should be of the same design. Mr. Caycedo asked that Council carefully consider all sign variances and, in this case, not grant the appeal. He reiterated his comments about sign pollution and then responded to Council members' questions. During rebuttal, Mr. Mummaw responded to Mr. Caycedo's comments and continued to explain his position with respect to signage. Mr. Caycedo made final comments noting that signs on building may be colorful but monument signs should have monochromatic letters with colorful logos. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments, expressing opinions on the subject of signage and these appeals. The Mayor noted that the matters could be remanded to CAB or the matter could be postponed. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to adopt Resolution No. 76-2016 to remand both matters to the Community Appearance Board. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 35-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from the provisions of Section 24-96(b)(1 ), Code of Ordinances, to allow one free-standing sign with eleven (11) tenant names on two sign faces (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on two sign faces): and a second free-standing sign with six (6) tenant names on each sign face (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on each sign face), for a commercial property located at 1944 NE Fifth Avenue: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SCV-15-02) Resolution No. 35-2016 Again, Mayor Haynie reminded everyone noted that quasi-judicial procedures continued to apply.. Members made their ex parte disclosers. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the shopping center and the location of the proposed monument signs were identified. The variance is for the number of tenant names on each sign. Mr. Harbilus noted that staff recommends denial of the variances as no undue hardship exists. Upon concluding, Mr. Harbilas responded to questions from Council members. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, provided further information on the provisions of the sign code and offered historical perspective on the subject. He also responded to further questions for Council members. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw presented on behalf of the petitioner. He addressed the City's current sign code. He noted that the proposed signs would only increase the number of tenant names on the sign, not the overall size of the monument. Numerous examples of signs were provided. Mr. Mummaw detailed the hardships asserted by his client. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council members. Discussion ensued. Topics included, but were not limited to, allowing more monuments based on linear feet of the center, color on signs, height of signs, the number of tenants in the center, and architectural integration of signs. Mr. Mummaw provided a depiction of a compromise sign with fewer panels. Juan Caycedo, chairman of CAB, commented on the proposals and the discussion at CAB. He noted that the variance was only for the number of tenants on a sign, not color or design. He reiterated his views on visual contamination and asserted that approving this variance could change the character of the City. He then responded to members' questions. It was suggested that this matter be remanded to CAB. Robert Eisen commented on a discussion of the number of tenant names on signs that took place at a CAB meeting. Doug Giordano commented on the use of the term 'subjective.' Barry Pokrifcsak commented on remanding this matter back to CAB and advocated continuing with a workshop on signage. Mr. Mummaw and Mr. Caycedo made final remarks in response to previous comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney addressed the fact that this is a variance and proposed the option of continuation so that the parties would have the opportunity to work on a solution. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to continue Resolution No. 35-2016 to the second City Council meeting in November. Members made final comments and suggestions Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

Ms. McGuire noted the sources of revenue that will fund capital improvements and reviewed, by department, the projects, vehicles and equipment included in the GIP for 2016-2017 fiscal year. She then made herself available for questions from Council members.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton adopting an amended and restated Boca Raton Municipal Facilities and Services User Fee Schedule; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 103-2016 Shannon Crouch, Processing and Compliance Manager, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation on the proposed changes to the Boca Raton Municipal and Services User Fee Schedule effective October 1, 2016. Ms. Crouch then made herself available for questions. The City Manager responded to a question regarding cemetery fees. The public hearing was opened. Rebecca Hahessy, Jennifer Bielec and Joseph Forstot advocated not increasing the non-resident youth athletic fees. Bob Rollins, Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District Commissioner, commented on the philosophy of user fees and asked that the increase in the non­ resident sports fee be tabled. Caroline Linden, Geoff Solomon and Scott Shields also spoke against the fee increase. Lenore Wachtel commented on the lack of transportation for some children to participate in youth sports. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council discussion ensued. Mickey Gomez, Recreation Services Director, responded to questions regarding the way in which fee increases were calculated, field capacity, and the possibility of offering a family discount. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to adopt Resolution No. 103-2016 as amended to maintain the non-resident youth athletic fee at $55 and to explore a family discount. Members made final comments. Council Member Weinroth suggested raising the non-resident fee to $65. Motion to adopt Resolution No. 103-2016 as amended to maintain the non-resident youth athletic fee at $55 and to explore a family discount failed 3 to 2; Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no; Mayor Susan Haynie and Council Member Scott Singer voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to adopt Resolution No. 103-2016 as amended to increase the non-resident youth athletic fee to $65 and to explore a family discount. Members agreed to also explore a bulk discount for youths playing multiple sports, as suggested by Council Member Singer. Final Budget Hearing Minutes September 26, 2016 3 Motion to adopt Resolution No. 103-2016 as amended to increase the non-resident youth athletic fee to $65 and to explore family and bulk discounts carried 3 to 2; Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Mayor Susan Haynie and Council Member Scott Singer voting no.

units.text: Resolution No. 105-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a planned mobility development (PMD) master plan and site plan to allow for a single phase development of a 90-unit multifamily residential development with 6 parking structures in 6 buildings for APOC Townhomes PMD generally located at 950 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway; considering modifications of development parameters related to: (I) required sidewalks; (II) planted buffer zones for the sidewalks; (Ill) allowance for utilities to be located in the sidewalk along Northwest Broken Sound Parkway; (IV) buffering/screening or wrapping of parking structures; and (V) pedestrian walkways separated from the drive aisles near all entrances and exits to and from parking structures; considering a waiver of plat requirements; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-15-01/SPA-15-11) Resolution No. 105-2016 Part I Resolution No. 105-2016 Part II Plans The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the petition including details of the master plan/site plan, zoning, land use, location, and project components. Details of the master plan/site plan, including types of units, parking, amenities, and building elevations were provided. The Community Appearance Board approved the project, making several recommendations. Mr. Bell reviewed the traffic impacts and the project's compliance with PMD requirements, noting that the minimum number of points was reached. The requested project modifications were then detailed, as were the improvements being made to the master plan/site plan. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval. Staff also recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to questions from the Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation reviewing the project and advocating passage of the resolution. Ms. Miskel addressed some questions posed regarding the garages in this townhome project under the PMD regulations. The presentation was then turned over to project architect Juan Caycedo who described the project design. Both Mr. Caycedo and Ms. Miske! then addressed questions about the open parking structures and the FAR cap in the PMD requirements. It was noted that a text amendment to fix these limitations on parking structures in PMDs was intended to be proposed. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 105-2016. Members made final comments. The City Manager noted that condition (o) on page 15 of the resolution prohibits any modifications, such as doors or walls, to the open parking structures. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, suggested a solution that, should the Code be amended as discussed, would allow the addition of doors and walls with the approval of the Community Appearance Board (CAB). The petitioner confirmed that the footprint will not change; only walls and doors would be added if a Code text amendment is adopted. Mr. Brown confirmed that the text amendment that would have limited application. The City Attorney then read into the record language to be added to condition (o) on page 15, addressing the enclosure of six parking structures with walls and doors should the Code be amended as discussed and noting that only CAB review would be required. Council Member Weinroth and Deputy Mayor Mullaugh, motion maker and seconder, accepted the amendment. The petitioner had no objection. Motion on Resolution No. 105-2016 as amended carried 4 to 0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.header: Municipal Golf Course West - Potential Sale of Property
units.text: George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a brief presentation, reviewing the process for the potential sale of the western municipal golf course. Staff is requesting formal direction from Council, in the form of a motion, to proceed with the process that would request submittal of best offers by October 21 which City Council would then consider at their November 22 meeting. Mr. Brown then responded to a number of questions. The City Attorney and the City Manager provided further information. The floor was opened for public comment. Ellyn Bogdanoff, representing GL Homes, and Debbie Leising both commented on the process as proposed. Don Huber commented on his group's proposal for the Ocean Breeze golf course. Doug Coller advocated having a public golf course in the City. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued. Members agreed to modify the process to entertain only highest, best and last offers submitted on October 21; to stipulate that the City will continue to operate the course until closing; and that the offers must be delivered to the City Manager's Office on October 21 between 4:30 and 5 pm. The City Attorney addressed some of the proposed changes to the process. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to move forward with the process as presented and modified. The motion carried 4 to 0 on a voice vote. The City Manager had no further reports.

units.text: Resolution No. 116-2016 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying Orangetheory Fitness' requested two (2) flat wall signs (Permit Numbers 16-4802 and 16-4803) to be located on the North and West elevation of a commercial building located at 10 East Palmetto Park Road; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 116-2016 The Senior Assistant City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The locations of the wall signs on the property were provided. Mr. Harbilas provided background information on the Community Appearance Board (CAB) consideration of both permits and the reasons for the denials. Staff finds that both signs are acceptable and recommends granting the appeals, reversing the decisions of the CAB. Mr. Harbilas then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Angela Ryan, Bergen Sign Company on behalf of Orangetheory Fitness, addressed the sign and wall colors. She stated the position of the appellant with regard to the colors, pointing out that other nearby companies have multi-colored signs and that the color of the building is so pale as to be neutral. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chairman, stated that the Board only considers aesthetics and explained the board's reasons for denial of both permits. He responded to questions of members. Glenn Gromann expressed his support of the position of CAB and suggested that the building should be painted a neutral color. Alex Lashnikov with Orangetheory addressed the history of the permit hearings and resulting CAB decisions, explaining that Orangetheory is working to standardize their company brand as reflected in their signs. He advocated allowing the use of their trademark sign. During rebuttal, Mark Jacobsen stated that the Board is willing to work with the company. Ms. Ryan passed her phone to Council members to illustrate the paleness of the pink building color. The public hearing was then closed. Members commented and expressed their positions. In response to a question, City Manager Leif Ahnell stated that Code Enforcement could look into any possible violation related to the lack of maintenance of the building. The paleness of the building color was discussed. Mayor Haynie agreed with Council Member Weinroth's position that the Council and CAB need to have a joint workshop to discuss the evolving sign code and requirements. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 116-2016 granting the appeal and reversing the decision of CAB. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting no. ·

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying Garden Cemetery's requested freestanding sign (Permit No. 16-5088) in the entrance median for a property located at 4103 N Military Trail; providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing an effective date Resolution No. 117-2016 Mayor Haynie confirmed that the same quasi-judicial procedures would govern this public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the sign on the site was identified and the sign was described. It was noted that the sign met Code. The site was further described and the history of the Community Appearance Board (CAB) review was provided. Staff, having reviewed the sign, recommended that the appeal be granted and the decision of CAB be reversed. Mr. Harbilas then responded to questions. It was noted that CAB took issue with the placement of the sign. The public hearing was opened. Sherry Dillard, Art Sign Company, made the case for the placement of the sign as necessary to identify the property. Ryan Leeds, on behalf of the property owner, explained the company's need for the sign, noting that currently many people cannot locate the property. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chairman, explained the Board's position on the placement of the sign and the lack of landscaping due to the size of the median. He also shared the suggestions offered by CAB for improving the property's signage in other ways. At Mayor Haynie's request, Mr. Leeds addressed the landscaping issue, the size of the sign and the median, as well as the appearance of the sign. Ms. Dillard stated that the sign footer could be put below grade in order to accommodate the landscaping CAB requested. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members offered comments. Mayor Haynie suggested a condition to require landscaping at the base of the sign. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 117-2016 granting the appeal subject to the applicant providing landscaping at the base of the sign. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5367 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a temporary moratorium on the operation of Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers and Medical Marijuana Dispensing Organizations within the City for a period of one (1) year; providing for severability; providing an effective date (SC-14-04R2) Ordinance No. 5367 Mayor Haynie noted that this was the first of two public hearings on this ordinance and no vote would be taken. Tamashbeen Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on the Compassionate Medical Cannabis Act of 2014, Ordinances 5285 and 5323, and House Bill 307 was provided. The justifications for imposing a moratorium were reviewed. It was noted that if Amendment 2 on the November ballot does not pass, the moratorium would terminate. The Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval, as does staff. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. units.text: Ordinance No. 5367 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a temporary moratorium on the operation of Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers and Medical Marijuana Dispensing Organizations within the City for a period of one (1) year; providing for severability; providing an effective date (SC-14-04R2) Ordinance No. 5367 Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with background information on the Compassionate Medical Cannabis Act of 2014 and previous City ordinances related to moratoriums on medical marijuana dispensing organizations. Ms. Rahman briefly reviewed Amendment 2 that would legalize medical marijuana and is on the November 8 ballot. Justifications for the moratorium were provided. It was noted that, if Amendment 2 does not pass, this moratorium will terminate. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to several questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5367. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5368 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the future land use element of the City's Comprehensive Plan; amending Policy LU.1.1.5 to increase the maximum intensity (floor area ratio) in the commercial, general industrial, light industrial, and manufacturing future land use designations for a self-storage facility (interior storage unit access) where permitted in Chapter 28 "Zoning", Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-16-03) Ordinance No. 5368 Ordinance No. 5369 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to self-storage facilities (interior storage unit access); amending Section 28-307(1) relating to building intensity; amending the C-1 District regulations, Sections 28-872 and 28-873; amending the W-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1017 and 28-1019; amending the IG/SI District regulations. Sections 28-1042 and 28-1043; amending the M-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1072 and 28-1073; amending the M-2 District regulations, Sections 28-1097 and 28-1098; amending the M-3 District regulations, Sections 28-1123 and 28-1124; amending Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, by creating a new Section 28-1310 entitled "Self-Storage Facility (interior storage unit access)" and establishing development standards for such use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-03) Ordinance No. 5369 Mayor Haynie noted that this is a transmittal hearing for Ordinance 5368 and the first of two public hearings on both Ordinance 5368 and Ordinance 5369. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation on both ordinances contemporaneously.. The intent of the ordinances was briefly reviewed and background information was provided. It was noted that the amendments to the Comprehensive Plan and the Code of Ordinances, which would increase the floor area ratio (FAR) for interior self-storage facilities in certain zoning districts, were triggered by the applicant's site-specific project. Details of the amendments were provided. Ms. Allen then explained staff's analysis and the recommended denial of the petitions. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the ordinances with several amendments to Ordinance 5369. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen responded to a number of questions centered on the ramifications of the code amendments. The City Attorney provided clarification. Deputy City Manager George Brown addressed a number of questions and suggested several changes to the ordinances that would help clarify some of the questions posed. Further discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Charles Siemon, Gray Robinson, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the ordinances. He addressed some of the comments made during the discussion of the staff presentation and then asked that Council vote to transmit the Comprehensive Plan ordinance. Upon concluding, Mr. Siemon responded to questions from Council. Deputy City Manager George Brown also responded to questions, providing information on mezzanines and other topics. Chris Baczewski commented on both ordinances, contending that their passage would result in over­ development of self-storage in Boca Raton and have other unintended consequences. Tom Head addressed some of Mr. Baczewski's comments. Charles Siemon made final comments and responded to questions about roll-up doors. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney reviewed the suggested language to be added to both ordinances which would specify that the maximum FAR of 1.0 would only apply if the self-storage use were the only use on the property. In Ordinance 5368, said language would be inserted in the paragraphs related to the increase in intensity for self-storage facilities in various zoning districts. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to transmit Ordinance No. 5368, as amended, to the appropriate agency. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Members then discussed the Ordinance 5369, the proposed Code amendments, noting that no vote would be taken and further discussion would serve to inform staff. It was suggested that the amendment be revised to limit it to a conversion of existing buildings. Further concerns were expressed.

units.text: Resolution No. 135-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan and Site Plan to allow for a single phase development of a 180-unit multifamily residential development for the 5500 Broken Sound PMD generally located at 5500 Northwest Broken Sound Boulevard ; considering a modification of development parameters related to el iminating a planted buffer for the sidewalk along NW 56th Street; considering a waiver of plat requirements: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (PMD-15-04ISPA-14-03R1) Resolution No. 135-2016 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk ad ministered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the planned mobility development (PMD) project, including the zoning, land use, acreage and location. Details of the master plan/site plan were provided. Topics reviewed included, but were not limited to, number of units, site access, parking, building elevations, traffic analysis and compliance with PMD requirements. The Community Appearance Board reviewed the project and recommended several landscape enhancements. The modification of a development parameter related to the relocation of a required planted buffer adjacent to sidewalks was supported by staff. The Planning & Zoning Board did not support the project due to the applicant's request related to a reduced degree of participation in the City's transit program. However, the developer has eliminated that request and, as a result, staff recommends approval of the project. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the applicant, made brief comments in support of the project and then introduced the project architect, Juan Caycedo, who gave a PowerPoint presentation providing details of the development. Upon conclud ing, Mr. Caycedo made himself available for questions as did Ms. Miske!. Glenn Gromann commented on the Planning and Zoning Board's vote. John Gore, on behalf of Boca Beautiful, offered support of the project. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Resolution No. 135-2016. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

Lenore Wachtel commented on the plans for Lake Wyman Park and the lack of bike riders at FAU. Rabbi Rafi Draiman, Torah Academy principal, and Daniel Abrams commented on the school and asked that Council reconsider the Compson golf course proposal. Dick Wiggins commented on growth in the City and requested that new building be halted. Al Zucaro commented on public awareness of planned projects in the City and the agenda review process. Paul Preste commented on process for consideration of the various golf course proposals. Jo-Ann Landon commented on traffic and the need to study same before more projects are developed.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton supporting reasonable efforts to maintain the Ocean Breeze property located at 5800-5801 NW 2nd Avenue as an operational golf course; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Council Member Rodgers addressed this resolution, explaining his reasons for bring it forward. The public hearing was opened. Lenore Wachtel offered support of the resolution and also advocated accepting the GL Homes offer to purchase the western golf course. In the interests of clarity, Mr. Rodgers read the entirety of the resolution and then offered further comments in support of the resolution. Robert DuKate advocated passage of the resolution. Al Zucaro com mented on the language of the resolutions. Paul Preste commented on the Lennar and GL Homes golf course proposals. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Weinroth offered an amendment to Section 1 of the resolution to read "The City Council expresses its support for maintaining the Ocean Breeze property as an operational golf course." Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to amend Resolution No. 147-2016 as stated. Discussion ensued. Mr. Rodgers explained his rational for the wording he requested. The City Attorney commented on the language, noting that the resolution is non-bind ing. She suggested modifying Council Member Weinroth's language, changing 'support for maintaining' in Section 1 to 'support for the maintenance of' and to modify the title on line 3 to read 'supporting the maintenance of ... ' Both Council Member Weinroth and Deputy Mayor Mullaugh accepted those changes to their amendment. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 147-2016 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Council Member Weinroth then asked for consensus to include the Compson golf course bid in the direction given to the City Manager at the Workshop meeting to further analyze two purchase offers and report back to Council for further discussion . Members discussed the matter. In general, it was agreed to include the Compson offer.

units.text: Resolution No. 35-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from the provisions of Section 24-96(b)( 1), Code of Ordinances. to allow one free-standing sign with eleven (11) tenant names on two sign faces (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on two sign faces); and a second free-stand ing sign with six (6) tenant names on each sign face (where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on each sign face). for a commercial property located at 1944 NE Fifth Avenue; providing for severability: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SCV-15-02) Resolution No. 35-2016 Mayor Haynie stated that the petitioner requested that this item be continued to the December 13, 2016 Council meeting . Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to continue Resolution No. 35-2016 to December 13, 2016. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 144-2016 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying the Mae Volen Senior Center's requested entrance frees tanding sign (Permit Number 16-4386) and a driveway directional sign (Permit Number 16-4387) for a property located at 1515 West Pal metto Park Road: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date Resolution No. 144-2016 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The subject property and sign locations were identified, and the previously approved signs were described. The signs that are the subject of the appeal were then described. The Community Appearance Board (CAB) decisions for denial of the permits due to the size of the logo and the nature of the tag line were reviewed . Mr. Harbilas noted that staff recommends granting the appeals and reversing the decisions of the CAB. Upon concluding, Mr. Harbilas responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Dave Freudenburg, on behalf of the appellant, addressed sign tag lines and provided a handout illustrating another sign with a tag lines. He advocated granting the appeal, addressed the lack of Hospice signage, and responded to questions. Elizabeth Lugo, Volen Center director, addressed the reason that Hospice did not choose to participate in the proposed signage and then responded to members' concerns and questions. Deputy City Manager George Brown responded to a question about the allowance of any future Hospice sign. Discussion ensued. Jessica Dornblaser, CAB member, gave a PowerPoint presentation explaining why the Board denied both sign permits . She provided background, addressed the Reed v Gilbert Supreme Court ruling on signs, reviewed CAB standards and the Board's position on effective taglines. Upon concluding, she responded to questions. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chairman, offered comments regarding the Board's position on allowing taglines. Members asked further questions of both Ms . Dornblaser and Mr. Jacobsen. B ill Reicherter, Priority 1 Signs, expressed his position that the CAB decisions with respect to these signs are subjective. Glenn Gromann commented on taglines on signs and advocated granting the appeal. There was no cross examination . Dave Freudenberg made brief final comments, again requesting that Council grant the appeal. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed . The City Attorney commented on the rules and regulations of the CAB, noting that their decisions are not random . The City Manager noted that a sign code rewrite is in the works in light of the Reed decision. The amended Code should be brought to Council next spring. Discussion ensued. Information was provided about the size of logos and other topics. Comments followed about the content of taglines. Members addressed the appeal, thanked the CAB, and further expressed their opinions. Council Member Weinroth moved that, on the monument sign, the butterfly logo be reduced to 1½ times the size of the largest letter and the tag line be retained; on the directional sign, the logo be reduced to 1½ the size of the largest letter and the tag line be removed. The City Attorney stated that these conditions were clear and would be included in the resolution. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 144-2016 reversing the decisions of the CAB with the conditions as stated. Members made final comments and stated positions. Motion carried on a 4-1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting no. 1§.. CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS : Deputy City Manager George Brown provided an update regarding the permit status for 2500 N. Ocean Boulevard, reviewing the status of the proposed building and the required permit approvals that must be issued in order for construction to commence. In particu lar, Mr. Brown discussed the issuance of a permit by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection. Upon concluding, he responded to questions. tl, CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS: The City Attorney requested authorization to schedule an Executive Session to receive advice regarding the pending litigation described as the Fair Housing Center of the Palm Beaches versus D.B. Priest, Inc. and the City of Boca Raton related to the City's student housing. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to authorize an Executive Session as requested by the City Attorney. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The City Attorney then provided brief information on Representative Lois Frankel's success in getting direction from federal agencies to assist local governments in addressing sober houses. Ms . Frieser noted that the joint statement issued by the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the Department of Justice recaps the central themes in the current case law on sober houses.

units.text: Resolution No. 148-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to conditional use Resolution No. 3-95 to allow for a child care facility for up to 60 children in an existing building located at St. David Armenian Church, located at 2300 West Yamato Road: providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing an effective date (CA-94-11 R1) Resolution No. 148-2016 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members noted their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Tam ash Rahman, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the request. The site location and zoning were provided. The site plan was also presented and its details were reviewed. It was noted that the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approved the amendment. The petitioner has asked that two conditions of the approval related to accessible routes to the building and a sidewalk along Yamato road be removed. Upon conclusion, Ms. Rahman responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Douglas Mummaw, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. He noted that this is one of several churches on Yamato Road that have similar programs. He then reviewed the site plan, noting the location of the building and the routes for accessibility and parking. Robert Eisen then addressed the conditions that the petitioner is requesting be eliminated from the site plan approval, making the case for the request related to accessible route for drop off and noting that the condition for an 8 foot sidewalk is acceptable to the petitioner. Both gentlemen then responded to questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 148-2016 striking condition 8.c. Council Member Singer addressed the width of the Yamato Road sidewalk and how to address the zoning code that stipulates the 8 foot width. Discussion ensued. The City Attorney provided language to be added as a notation to condition 8.e. generally consistent with "in the event that the City Code is amended to reduce the required width of the sidewalk to less than 8 feet, then the 8 feet requirement will be reduced, but nothing herein suggests an entitlement to a reduction of the sidewalk width." Both Council Member Weinroth and Deputy Mayor Mullaugh accepted the amendment to the main motion. Members made final comments. Motion as amended to approve Resolution No. 148-2016 striking condition 8.c. and adding language to condition 8.e. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Jack McWalter commented on the one cent sales tax vote, several meetings he attended regarding the use of the sales tax revenue, the City's list of priorities and its plan for receiving a fair share of revenues. Regina Ecklund, on behalf of a number of Boca Teeca unit owners, advocated keeping Ocean Breeze as a golf course and addressed the three proposals for purchase of the municipal course. Jim Knight commented on the rebuilding of the bridge at Havana Drive and requested the City meet with the neighbors regarding same. Neil Schiller, representing GL Homes, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation regarding the process and the GL Homes offer for the municipal course. Attorney David Smolker addressed the possible condemnation of the Ocean Breeze course, providing a letter presenting his opinion regarding eminent domain. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council. Robert DuKate, on behalf of Keep Golf in Boca, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation advocating that the City acquire the Ocean Breeze golf course. George O'Rourke commented on an item concerning the rezoning of an area of the City to be considered at the December 22 Planning and Zoning Board meeting, asking that it the item be rescheduled. Doug Coller commented on the golf course proposals and advocated for the Lennar proposal. Al Zucaro commented on the economic development presentation made at the Workshop, the direction given regarding height in the B-1 zoning district along East Palmetto Park Road, an upcoming Planning and Zoning Board meeting on December 22, and the process for golf course proposals. JoAnn Landon voiced concern with over-development in the City. At request of Council Member Weinroth, the City Attorney addressed the provisions of the cone of silence with regard to the golf course proposals.

units.text: Resolution No. 151-2016 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from the provisions of Section 24-96{b){1 ), Code of Ordinances, to allow one free-standing sign with eight {8) tenant names on two sign faces {where only four (4) tenant names are allowed on two sign faces): and a second free­ standing sign with six (6) tenant names on each sign face {where only four {4) tenant names are allowed on each sign face), for a commercial property located at 1944 NE Fifth Avenue; providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date {SCV-15-02) Resolution No. 151-2016 The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures reviewed earlier would continue to govern this public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilas, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the property as well as the location of the two monuments signs on the site were identified. A history of the petitioner's requests was provided. Both monument signs were described. It was noted that the signs met code with the exception of the number of tenant names on the signs. Staff determined that the criteria needed for granting a variance have not been met and therefore recommend denial. The Community Appearance Board (CAB) actions and recommendations were reviewed. Mr. Harbilas concluded, again noting that staff recommends denial. He then responded to a number of questions from Council members, including regarding the allowable number of signs at the property and the Council's continuation of the variance to allow applicant to work on an acceptable solution. The public hearing was opened. Douglas Mummaw, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He began by addressing the number of signs allowed on the property. He then addressed the variance being requested, noting that the brands of the businesses in the plaza need to be recognized. Topics included, but were not limited to, the color and number of individual panels and the hardship justifications, Mayor Haynie noted her intent to have a roundtable with CAB to discuss many of the issues discussed tonight. She also noted that tonight's request is for the number and colors of the sign panels only. The City Manager noted that a rewrite of the sign code was underway. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chair, provided insight into the decisions of the Board with regard to this request, noting that, as this property is quite long, the Board would allow more signs but not more than four panels per sign. He then responded to a number of questions. Mr. Mummaw responded to further questions about suggestions for changing the proposed signs. No one else came forward to speak. Mr. Mummaw made closing remarks. The public hearing was then closed. Mayor Haynie reiterated the need for a roundtable with CAB to discuss signage policy as it will affect the aesthetics of the community. Council members offered their comments and opinions with regard to a roundtable to discuss policy and the variances under consideration. In response to a questions, the City Attorney commented on the recent Supreme Court decision on signage, changes to policy with regard to signs and Council's options for this variance request. In response to Council Member Singer, Mr. Mummaw requested that Council rule on these variances. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 151-2016 to grant the variances for two six-panel signs. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting no. The City Attorney reviewed the rules of the Council with regard to a motion to reconsider in order to continue the item. Ms. Frieser noted that the rules have an unusual carve out exception not allowing reconsideration with regard to ordinances and resolutions. However, the Council is not barred from making a motion to allow for a lesser variance. Discussion ensued Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 151-2016 to grant the variances for two five-panel signs. After discussion of possible action that could be taken at this meeting, the current motion was set aside. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to postpone consideration of Resolution No. 151-2016. Final discussion ensued, noting that this action preserves the fees already paid by the applicant. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. 1!, CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS: Mr. Ahnell provided an update on the golf course proposals and noted that the matter will likely come back for Council discussion at the second meeting in January.

units.text: Council Member Rodgers asked about the scheduling of the December 22 Planning & Zoning Board meeting at which the midtown rezoning is to be discussed. The City Manager provided information on the Planning & Zoning Board calendar. He also addressed Boca Raton's share of the revenues from the one cent sales tax. The City Manager provided further information on the process going forward for funding projects with the one cent sales tax revenues. Council Member Singer addressed the Planning & Zoning Board schedule and postponement of the upcoming meeting. He then highlighted upcoming holiday events. Council Member Weinroth addressed the one cent sales tax, the positive position of the Council on a having golf course in the City, and commented on statements made during public requests regarding development and zoning. Mayor Haynie commented on the recent 20th Street summit and shared a 'town and gown proposal' on which she would like to move forward. She received consensus for moving forward with a charette on the 20th Street corridor vision to be conducted by the Treasure Coast Regional Planning Council, including funding of same. She also announced the upcoming Boca Bowl. All members wished everyone happy holidays. ll:, ADJOURNMENT: The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 9:15 pm. ATTEST:

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a request for a payment in lieu of environmental set aside to allow for the elimination of three conservation easements at the Boca Villa Apartments site, located at 100 West Hidden Valley Boulevard; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (EAB-16-01) Resolution No. 3-2017 Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on items D, E and F would be conducted contemporaneously, as the petitions are related and a separate vote would be taken on each petition. The Mayor also stated that the quasi-judicial procedures remain in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The petitioner's request for an amended land use and rezoning were reviewed, and the location, zoning, and history of the project were provided. Staff reviewed the future land use map amendment for consistency, compatibility and concurrency of the project with the Comprehensive Plan and found that the project to be compliant. Ms. Rahman then turned to an analysis of the rezoning, which staff also finds to be consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. The traffic analysis for the proposed project was reviewed. Details of the site plan and the project were provided. It was noted that the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval of the future land use map amendment and the rezoning. Staff also recommends approval of both petitions. Nora Fosman, Senior Environmental Officer, explained the purpose of a payment in lieu of an environmental set-aside. She reviewed the conservation areas on the property. It was noted that the applicant has met the requirements consideration of a payment in lieu of a set aside. The method of calculation of the payment was reviewed. Ms Fosman noted that the Environmental Advisory Board unanimously recommended approval of the payment in lieu. Upon concluding, both Ms. Fosman and Ms. Rahman responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, Gray Robinson on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation addressing the future land use map amendment and the rezoning. He began by addressing the history of the property, noting that the new owner has provided a much needed upgrade to the development. Details of further planned improvements that necessitated the requested changes were reviewed, noting that the proposal exceeds minimum requirements of the Code. Mr. Marshall explained the technical deviation with respect to the driveway reservoir. Upon concluding, he responded to questions from Council members. John Donaldson, traffic engineer, addressed the trip generation nd analysis for the project as it relates to an increase in traffic on NW 2 Avenue. Council Member Rodgers asked that the open space in the rezoning ordinance be limited to 40% to which the applicant agreed. Ashley Harden, representing the Board of Directors of the Royal Poinciana community, stated the Board's support of the petitions. Lenore Wachtel voiced opposition to increasing density and traffic in the City. nd Sally Friedman voiced concern about increased traffic on NW 2 Avenue, a constrained roadway. Irina nd Borisova voiced concern with the traffic on NW 2 Avenue and opposed increased building in the area. nd Harold Chafee also commented on congestion in the north end of the City and traffic on NW 2 Avenue. nd Robert DuKate commented on the bad traffic on NW 2 Avenue and voiced opposition to increased rental units in the City and the resulting traffic. There was no cross examination. Mr. Marshall offered rebuttal regarding traffic and the manner in which the analysis was done. He emphasized that the proposed improvement to the existing development would benefit the neighborhood. Mr. Donaldson then addressed traffic and noted that actual data collected in the field was used to complete the analysis. He also addressed the traffic situation occurring at the train crossing, before responding to further questions. Mr. Marshall addressed a question about the demand for rental units. The public hearing was then closed. Ms. Rahman addressed the driveway reservoir distance requirement. Jim Bell, Deputy Development Services Director, responded to a question about shorter reservoir distances. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5373. Mayor Haynie noted that four votes are required for passage of the ordinance. Members then made final comments. Council Member Rodgers proposed an amendment requiring a minimum of 40% open space, noting that this amendment would also apply to the rezoning ordinance. Council Member Weinroth accepted the amendment to his motion. The City Attorney suggested language to be added to both ordinances. Discussion ensued regarding the percentage of open space required and noting that any future change to the open space would be subject to Council approval. The applicant did not object. Deputy Mayor Mullaugh, as the motion seconder, did not object to the amendment. Members made further final comments. The City Attorney clarified that the plan references 48% open space and suggested that perhaps the amendment should be for 48% not 40%. Discussion continued. Ms. Rahman clarified that 48% was an approximation and the exact amount of open space was 47.86%. Consensus was to amend both ordinances to reflect a requirement of 47.86% open space. Motion on Ordinance No. 5373 as amended carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5374 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 3-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 9-2017 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal by Yamato Investments LLC of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying approval of two freestanding signs, the eastern sign with tenant sign copy for three (3) tenants and the western sign with tenant sign copy for four (4) tenants; to be located at 331 and 351 East Yamato Road; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 9-2017 Mayor Haynie noted that the same qj will govern this hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. John Harbilus, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with the history of the various Community Appearance Board (CAB) and City Council reviews of the signs at the site. Renderings of the two signs were provided. Staff recommends granting the appeals and reversing the CAB decisions. Upon concluding, Mr. Harbilus responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of the appellant, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of granting the appeals. Upon concluding, he responded to questions. Members commented and voiced their opinions. Mark Jacobson, CAB chair, addressed the Board's decisions. He noted that the denials were concerning the color in the sign panels. Barry Pokrifcsak, sign designer, commented on signs representing company brands with color. He then responded to questions. Lenore Wachtel advocated updating the sign code. Mr. Jacobson addressed the Learning Experience signs, offered support for having a sign professional on the Community Appearance, and responded to questions. There was no cross examination. Mr. Mummaw made rebuttal comments regarding establishing a master sign criteria. Members commented. Council Member Weinroth proposed approval of sign with condition that no panel has more than 3 colors. The City Attorney read language that addressed the number of colors. Members commented on the allowable number of colors on sign panels. The City Attorney provided clarification. Deputy Mayor Mullaugh suggested that the staff recommendation be followed. The City Attorney addressed a second option for an amendment which would be to approve with the Sound Advice and Dunkin Donuts panels only; other panels would have to be approved by CAB. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 9-2017 granting the appeal and reversing the decision of the Community Appearance with conditions. Members offered comments and stated their positions. Motion carried on a 3 to 2 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting no. ~ CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS: The City Manager reminded Council members of the summer schedule discussion at the next meeting.

Ele Zachariades, Dunay Miskel on behalf of the petitioner, made brief comments in support of the approval of the ordinance and responded to questions from Council members. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton adopting an amended Investment Policy for the City of Boca Raton; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Council Member Rodgers asked for an explanation of the changes to the Investment Policy. Council Member Weinroth provided information on Council's direction with regard to Israeli bonds. The City Manager pointed out the changes to the policy. A brief discussion followed. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to postpone consideration of Resolution No. 26-2017. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Further discussion ensued. Mayor Haynie provided an opportunity for public input. Alan Feinberg, Jr. commented on the quality and rating of Israeli bonds. George O'Rourke commented on the appropriateness of this type of investment for a pension plan. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Resolution No. 26-2017. In response to a question, Linda Davidson clarified that this Investment Policy is for the City not for the pension funds. Members made final comments. Ms. Davidson addressed the rate of return for this type of bond as opposed to treasury securities, and provided further information. It was noted that these bonds are allowed by the State of Florida. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5368 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the future land use element of the City's Comprehensive Plan; amending Policy LU.1.1.5 to increase the maximum intensity (floor area ratio) in the commercial, general industrial, light industrial, and manufacturing future land use designations for a self-storage facility (interior storage unit access) where permitted in Chapter 28 "Zoning", Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-16-03) Ordinance No. 5368 Drawings Ordinance No. 5369 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to self-storage facilities (interior storage unit access); amending Section 28-307(1) relating to building intensity; amending the C-1 District regulations, Sections 28-872 and 28-873; amending the W-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1017 and 28-1019; amending the IG/SI District regulations, Sections 28-1042 and 28-1043; amending the M-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1072 and 28-1073; amending the M-2 District regulations, Sections 28-1097 and 28-1098; amending the M-3 District regulations, Sections 28-1123 and 28-1124; amending Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, by creating a new Section 28-1310 entitled "Self-Storage Facility (interior storage unit access)" and establishing development standards for such use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-03) Ordinance No. 5369 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Ordinances 5368 and 5369 would be conducted contemporaneously as these related petitions, and a separate vote would be taken on each ordinance. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with a review of the ordinances followed by background information on the presentations to date. The amendments proposed by the applicant to policy LU.1.1.5 of the Comprehensive Plan (Comp Plan) as well as the numerous amendments to the Code of Ordinances (Code) were detailed. Staff's analysis was presented, noting that the increase in FAR (floor area ration) limits the amount of construction on a parcel. The Comp Plan amendment was transmitted to the State land planning Agency as required. The City received no comments resulting from that review. Based on review of the petitions, the Development Services Department recommended denial of both the amendment to the Comp Plan and the Code. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the Comp Plan amendment and the Code changes, and also approved a site plan for reconfiguration of an existing building; said approval would only become effective should the both ordinances be adopted. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen responded to a number of questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Charles Siemon, Gray Robinson on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He noted this request began as a proposed renovation to the applicant's existing building. So as to avoid spot zoning, the Comp Plan and Code amendments were proposed. Mr. Siemon then provided details. It was noted that there is one active opponent to this proposal. In conclusion, he advocated approval and then responded to questions. Michael Weiner, attorney for Madison Holdings, addressed numerous aspects of the initial proposal and the resulting proposed Comp Plan and Code amendments. He opined that the Comp Plan should not be changed nor should the Code for a particular building configuration. Mr. Weiner urged that Council follow staff's recommendation to deny the petitions. Chris Baczewski, owner of Addison Storage, addressed both the numerous reasons that he would be aggrieved by passage of these ordinances and the unintended consequences resulting from said passage. He then responded to questions. Bonnie Miske! shared her opinion that there is a need for self-storage in Boca Raton. She also posed a question related to the loss of warehouse space that might result from passage of these ordinances. Tom Head, petitioner, addressed a number of comments made by a previous speaker, asserting a lack of veracity. He then made himself available for questions. Mike Krones offered his support of the project. Lenore Wachtel inquired as to how to prevent people from living in self-storage facilities. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney addressed a question about re-transmittal and the initial need for the Comp Plan amendment. Council members directed a number of questions to staff and the petitioner, as well as offering further comments. A number of suggestions for changes to Ordinance 5369 (the Code amendments) were made. Discussion of building spacing ensued. At approximately 7:48 pm, Council Member Rodgers left the meeting. Mr. Weiner addressed various previous statements and advocated denial of the petitions. The City Attorney read language into the record that would amend Ordinance 5369 with regard to roll up doors, a requirement for a manned onsite presence, and the prohibition of cantilevering. In response to a question from Council Member Weinroth, the petitioner agreed to go ahead with vote tonight despite only four Council members being present to vote. Further discussion ensued; staff responded to questions about the building spacing requirement. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided a handout of minor clean up changes to Ordinance 5369. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5368. Mayor Haynie noted that this ordinance requires four votes for adoption. In response to Council Member Singer comments, the City Attorney addressed the time limit on adopting Land Development Regulations (i.e., Code of Ordinances) to effectuate Comp Plan amendments. Motion carried on a 4-0 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Discussion of building spacing requirements and postponing a decision on Ordinance 5369 ensued. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided information. The petitioner agreed to a postponement. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to postpone Ordinance No. 5369 to February28, 2017. Motion carried on a 4-0 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton to amend Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to specialty storage and storage (interior access); amending the Definitions. Section 28-2. to define "Collectibles", "Specialty Storage", and "Storage (Interior Access)"; amending the LIRP District, Section 28-977, to allow specialty storage and storage (interior access) as permitted uses: amending the LIRP District, Section 28-979(j), to remove storage uses as a prohibited use: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-05) Ordinance No. 5377 Beth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. As this is the first of two public hearings, it was noted that no vote would be taken. Ms. Eassa reviewed the proposed changes to the Code of Ordinances that would accommodate high-end specialty storage as a permitted use. Staff's analysis was detailed. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the amendment. Staff recommends approval as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the applicant, made brief comments, noting that this is a reuse of an existing building on the old IBM site. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Haynie reiterated that this is the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. The ordinance would be heard again at the next Coucil meeting.
