Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the applicant, made brief comments, noting that this is a reuse of an existing building on the old IBM site. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Haynie reiterated that this is the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. The ordinance would be heard again at the next Coucil meeting.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 1, Section 1-2, "Definitions and Rules of Construction," Code of Ordinances, affirming that the City Code is construed in compliance with all applicable Federal and State laws: amending Chapter 28, Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," Code of Ordinances, amending certain definitions and creating new definitions related to student housing; amending Chapter 28, Article Ill, Division 7, "M-2 General Industrial District," Section 28-1106, "Minimum Floor Area: Student Housing," amending the minimum floor area of a student sleeping room: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5378 Beth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on student housing regulations in the Code of Ordinances and the resulting lawsuit were provided. It was noted that the Code does not expressly prohibit minor children from residing in a student housing facility and that this ordinance clarifies that children living with a qualified student are not prohibited. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the text amendment. Staff recommends approval as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa made herself available for questions. Council Member Weinroth inquired about including students in two year programs as well. Ms. Eassa noted that the Planning & Zoning Board also asked about that situation. The City Attorney suggested not making any changes until the lawsuit is resolved; further changes can be made to the Code afterward. Discussion followed. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to approve Ordinance No. 5378. Motion carried on a 3-1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Weinroth voting no. units.text: Ordinance No. 5369 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to self-storage facilities (interior storage unit access); amending Section 28-307(1) relating to building intensity; amending the C-1 District regulations, Sections 28-872 and 28-873; amending the W-1 District regulations, Sections 28-101 i and 28-1019; amending the IG/SI District regulations, Sections 28-1042 and 28-1043; amending the M-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1072 and 28-1073; amending the M-2 District regulations, Sections 28-1097 and 28-1098; amending the M-3 District regulations, Sections 28-1123 and 28-1124; amending Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, by creating a new Section 28-1310 entitled "Self-Storage Facility (interior storage unit access)" and establishing development standards for such use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-03) Ordinance No. 5369 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She provided detailed background information, reviewing the revisions made to the ordinance at the February 14 City Council meeting. Ms. Allen also noted the changes proposed by Council Member Singer. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Charles Siemon, on behalf of the petitioner, made brief comments in support of the ordinance, noting the benefits of rehabilitating existing warehouse buildings. Michael Weiner, on behalf of Madison Holdings and Chris Baczewski, made his case for not approving the ordinance, advocating taking a slower approach and not rush into changes to six zoning districts. He provided an email from a storage owner who addressed what he feels he could now build should this pass. Upon concluding, he responded to questions. Tom Head, petitioner, commented on the length of time that this ordinance has been under consideration and made himself available for questions. Chris Baczewski addressed comments made at a previous meeting and contended that the proposed changes are not known in the industry locally. He advocated holding a workshop on this topic and not adopting the ordinance. Ele Zachariades offered support of language proposed by Council Member Singer. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. At Council Member Singer's request, the City Attorney reviewed multiple changes to the ordinance that he proposed to address a number of the concerns expressed. A copy of the revised ordinance was distributed. Members discussed the proposals. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, responded to a question about the genesis of this ordinance. Discussion continued; members expressed concerns. Council Member Weinroth moved to adopt the original ordinance without any modifications. After further discussion, he modified his motion. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, to adopt Ordinance No. 5369 as revised on November 8, 2016. Members provided further comments. Discussion of a postponement followed. Charles Siemon, on behalf of the applicant, suggested that Council adopt the ordinance. Members discussed the ramifications of voting on the motion and a motion to reconsider. Mr. Siemon proposed a number of revisions that might satisfy Council's concerns. Further changes were proposed by Council Member Singer. Council Member Weinroth withdrew his motion. Members continued to discuss a number of changes while also expressing their concerns. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to continue Ordinance No. 5369 to March 28, 2017. Members made final comments. It was suggested that staff hold a workshop with stakeholders on this subject. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Ordinance No. 5377 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton to amend Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to specialty storage and storage (interior access); amending the Definitions, Section 28-2, to define "Collectibles", "Specialty Storage", and "Storage (Interior Access)"; amending the LIRP District, Section 28-977, to allow specialty storage and storage (interior access) as permitted uses; amending the LIRP District, Section 28-979(j), to remove storage uses as a prohibited use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-05) Ordinance No. 5377 Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information was provided and the proposed revisions were reviewed. Staff's analysis was presented, and it was noted that the petition is consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval. Ms. Eassa then reviewed several changes that staff proposed for clarification and she noted that staff recommends approval. The public hearing was opened. Andrea Keiser, on behalf of the petitioner, began by offering an explanation of the distinctions between this ordinance and the last one Council considered. Ms. Keiser gave a PowerPoint presentation illustrating the type of self-storage being proposed in the LIRP district. Upon concluding, she responded to questions from Council members. Michael Weiner advocated that consideration of this ordinance be postponed in order for Council to look at the local self-storage industry as whole. Chris Baczewski commented on aspects of the industry and advocated holding a workshop on this and the previous ordinance. Danielle Vennett commented on the amount of self-storage square footage proposed to be allowed by the ordinance, among other topics. She then responded to questions regarding the former IBM facility which is the site that prompted this request. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Weinroth asked about having on-site administration during hours that the facility is open. The City Attorney addressed the proposed revisions proposed by staff. Ms. Eassa addressed how both specialty storage and interior access self-storage came to be included in the ordinance. Andrea Keiser and Danielle Vennett responded to that question and other questions from Council members. Discussion ensued. Members expressed concerns. The City Attorney proposed language to address the definition of specialty storage to include business records, as well as including a requirement for an on-site attendant during hours when the facility is open to the public. Ms. Frieser noted that all reference to "storage (interior access)" would be deleted in the title and recitals. The definition of same would be deleted in its entirety. After further discussion, it was decided to revise the cap downward to 500,000 square feet. Ms. Vennett voiced her disappointment with some of the changes proposed. Further discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Ordinance No. 5377 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 28-780, Code of Ordinances, relating to the maximum building height for properties zoned B-1 and located both adjacent to East Palmetto Park Road and east of the Atlantic lntracoastal Waterway; clarifying language related to requests for additional height; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-01) Ordinance No. 5384 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She provided extensive background information on consideration of this ordinance. Location of the affected parcels was provided. The text revisions were reviewed. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to self-storage facilities (interior storage unit access); amending Section 28-307(1) relating to building intensity; amending the C-1 District regulations, Sections 28-872 and 28-873; amending the W-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1017 and 28-1019; amending the IG/SI District regulations, Sections 28-1042 and 28-1043; amending the M-1 District regulations, Sections 28-1072 and 28-1073; amending the M-2 District regulations, Sections 28-1097 and 28-1098; amending the M-3 District regulations, Sections 28-1123 and 28-1124; amending Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, by creating a new Section 28-1310 entitled "Self-Storage Facility (interior storage unit access)" and establishing development standards for such use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15-03) Ordinance No. 5369 The City Manager noted that this item had been presented and continued multiple times and staff recently held a workshop on the subject with interested parties, an update on which was presented at the March 27 Workshop Meeting. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Senior Planner Ingrid Allen were available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Charles Siemon, Gray Robinson, shared that an agreement on ordinance language was reached with Bonnie Miske!, Dunay Miske! Backman, but not with Michael Weiner. Ele Zachariades, Dunay Miske! Backman, provided information on the work being done on language intended to satisfy all parties. She provided a handout identifying proposed language changes and reviewed the recommendations. She then responded to members' questions. Michael Weiner, on behalf of Chris Baczewski, stated that work on acceptable language continued but felt that an agreement would not be reached tonight. Mr. Baczewski distributed a letter was to Council members and requested that the item be continued to provide adequate time to reach agreement on language that will address everyone's concerns. Mr. Weiner commented further, expressing concerns with passage of the ordinance and possible detriment to the self-storage industry in Boca Raton. Glenn Gromann commented on the possibility of including self-storage as a use in LIRP districts to address the underuse of properties in the Park at Broken Sound. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council members briefly discussed a continuance. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to postpone Ordinance No. 5369 to the next regular City Council meeting. Members made final comments. The City Attorney provided an update on the legal challenge to the previously adopted Comp Plan amendment and the effect of same on consideration of this ordinance. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Michael Mullaugh, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes.

units.header: Discussion of the Sale of the Western Golf Course
units.text: George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the three proposals for the western golf course - Compson Boca Argent, GL Homes, Lennar. A handout was provided. Topics included, but were not limited to contingencies, price, various deposits, inspection period, closing date, and unique options. The possible actions for Council were listed. Mr. Brown then responded to questions from Council members. Representatives of the three proposers were invited to speak. Richard Siemens, on behalf of the Compson proposal, noted that Compson was reconsidering their position and is serious about making a sale work. Kevin Ratterree, Vice President of GL Homes, gave a PowerPoint presentation reviewing the company's offer, comparing said offer to those of Lennar and Compson. He stated that the Lennar and Compson offers had a number of contingencies that the GL Homes contract offer did not. Mr. Ratterree concluded by advocating for acceptance of the GL Homes offer. Alan Fant, Senior Vice President of GL Homes, advocated for their offer and asked that Council give staff direction to work with them on a contract. Mitch Kirschner, GrayRobinson on behalf of Lennar, rebutted many of the claims made regarding contingencies. He advocated for the Lennar contract. Bruce Grundt, Lennar Vice President, responded to a number of previous comments, noting that Lennar has worked with the City in the past. Bob Comparato, Compson Development, voiced objection to the rushed process and requested a postponement of any decision. The public comment period was opened. Larry Snowden commented on the vulnerability of the City to possible environmental impacts. Jack Johnson commented on traffic and voiced opposition to development at the golf course. Mitch Kirschner objected to allowing Neil Schiller to speak on behalf of GL Homes. Mr. Schiller asked to be allowed to respond to several previous points. Chaim Glazer commented on the Compson pledge to donate land to the Torah Academy. Terri Murru thanked the Council for their service and addressed the charitable element of the offers. Doug Coller suggested that negotiations on the western course would affect the efforts on the Ocean Breeze course He requested any decision be continued. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment was period close. Time was provided for rebuttal. Mitch Kirschner, on behalf of Lennar, noted that the contracts speak for themselves and reiterated his feeling that the process has not been fair. Neil Schiller, on behalf of GL Homes, turned to Kevin Ratterree to rebut various previous comments with regard to Lennar's contingencies. Bob Comparato, Compson, noted the support their proposal has received and reiterated his objection to the proceedings. Mr. Kirschner responded to questions regarding provisions of the Lennar contract. Deputy City manager George Brown noted that the staff performed summary reviews of the contracts. Members commented. In general, members agreed that a decision was premature and thanked all those who spoke tonight. Mr. Brown responded to a question regarding issuing a form contract which proposers would complete and the process thus far. The Mayor noted that clarity was needed with regard to the contingencies. Mr. Brown recommended that staff work on a full picture. City Manager Leif Ahnell provided information on the progress of the Beach & Park District's acquisition of the Ocean Breeze property. He noted that the Council's joint meeting with the Beach & Park District is scheduled for May 8.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from the provisions of Section 24-96( c)(3), Code of Ordinances, to allow a total of two (2) flat signs where only one (1) flat sign is permitted for a location with one (1) frontage for McDonald's located at 2140 North Federal Highway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SCV-16-04) Resolution No. 37-2017 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Keith Carney, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The property location was identified, as was the location of the wall signs at the site. The variance request for the second wall sign was reviewed. Illustrative photographs of the property were provided. It was noted that the petitioner met all criteria demonstrating undue hardship. The Community Appearance Board (CAB) recommended approval. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan and Site Plan to allow development of a 322-unit multifamily residential project generally located at 777 West Yamato Road and 750 Park of Commerce Boulevard (based upon Planning and Zoning Resolution No. 86-9 as amended and the new site plan considered together); considering seven (7) modifications of development parameters, pursuant to Section 28-50, Code of Ordinances, related to eliminating sidewalks on one (1) side of a right-of-way (where a sidewalk is required on both sides of a right-of-way), eliminating planted buffers along sidewalks, and five (5) separate modifications related to reducing building setbacks fronting Congress Avenue and West Yamato Road; considering a waiver of plat requirement; considering repealing a condition of Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 06-11 requiring replatting of conservation easements; considering increasing and altering the location of the conservation easements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-15-03) Resolution No. 48-2017 Plans Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the site was identified and details of the project were provided. Elements of the current and proposed modifications to the Master Plan were provided. Topics included, but were not limited to, parking, vehicular and pedestrian access, cross-access, sidewalks, and bus shelters. Details of the site plan and the residential project were also provided; renderings and elevations were displayed. Ms. Rahman then reviewed the modifications requested by the applicant that affect sidewalks, landscape buffers along sidewalks, and building setbacks. The traffic analysis was reviewed. Ms. Rahman noted that the project meets the mobility objectives of the Comprehensive Plan. The applicants request to waive platting requirements was explained. The Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval with additional conditions. Staff clarified language in conditions (4)r, (4)s, (4)t, and (7)(b) and recommends approval with said clarifications. Ms. Rahman and Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, Dunay Miske! Backman on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation. The existing site conditions of the property were illustrated. Details of the compliance with the PMD parameters of this third phase and the first two phases of the project were provided. Project architect Juan Caycedo commented on the design of the buildings and the landscaping, which was modified in response to the suggestions of the Community Appearance Board. Ms. Miske! reported on a meeting with Lake Worth Drainage District (LWDD) regarding landscaping on the LWDD easement along Yamato Road. She noted the petitioner's commitment to continue to work with LWDD. She then addressed the undergrounding of utilities and the limitations that exist in along Yamato. Ms. Miske! then responded to a number of questions. Paul Borman commented on the project. Jo Ann Landon commented on the need for shade trees on the property. Glenn Gromann offered support of the project. There was no cross examination. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Ms. Rahman read the several modifications to conditions (4)r, (4)s, and (4)t addressing undergrounding utilities and correction of a scrivener's error in condition (7)(b). The City Attorney then read into the record a new condition (4)v relating to supplemental landscaping in the LWDD easement. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 48-2017 as amended. Deputy Mayor Rodgers inquired as to the timeline for completion of the tunnel under Yamato Road for the El Rio Trail. The City Manager provided information. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. units.full: Resolution No. 48-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan and Site Plan to allow development of a 322-unit multifamily residential project generally located at 777 West Yamato Road and 750 Park of Commerce Boulevard (based upon Planning and Zoning Resolution No. 86-9 as amended and the new site plan considered together); considering seven (7) modifications of development parameters, pursuant to Section 28-50, Code of Ordinances, related to eliminating sidewalks on one (1) side of a right-of-way (where a sidewalk is required on both sides of a right-of-way), eliminating planted buffers along sidewalks, and five (5) separate modifications related to reducing building setbacks fronting Congress Avenue and West Yamato Road; considering a waiver of plat requirement; considering repealing a condition of Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 06-11 requiring replatting of conservation easements; considering increasing and altering the location of the conservation easements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-15-03) Resolution No. 48-2017 Plans Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the site was identified and details of the project were provided. Elements of the current and proposed modifications to the Master Plan were provided. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 4-2 , Code of Ordinances; affirming and providing for uniform hours of operation for all alcoholic beverage vendors in the City; providing a time period for compliance in annexed areas; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification in the Code of Ordinances; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5385 Mayor Haynie noted that she requested th is ordinance be brought forward and deferred to the City Attorney to explain the substance of the ordinance and the timeframe for compliance. Police Chief Dan Alexander provided information on the numerous police calls that have been made at the two locations affected by this ordinance. He stated that the Police Department supports the passage of this ordinance. The public hearing was opened . Karl Dickey, representing the Libertarian Party, stated his opposition to the ordinance. Bob Zeigler and Cyndi Bloom commented on the ramifications of the noise generated at Blue Martini over the last five years and stated their support of the ordinance. Ryan Moyer stated opposition to the ordinance. Jeff Brown , representing Blue Martini, asked that Council consider postponing a decision on the ordinance. Una Kohmann , noting that everyone deserves a good night's sleep, stated her support of the ordinance. Bruce Tumin offered his opposition to the ordinance. Thomas Mullin read into the record comments from Cindy Oliveri in opposition to the ordinance. Mr. Mullin, representing Nippers, then offered a suggestion to revise the ordinance to extend the transition time to 18 months and offered to work with police on problems. He provided handouts of the suggested language and a petition opposing the ordinance. Danny Rosenberg, General Manager of Nippers, addressed comments made regarding noise and other complaints. Roberto Roman , Yasmin Silva , Jarett Loperfito, and Anni-May Hurmemaa spoke in support of Blue Martini and in opposition to the ordinance. Sergio Vera and Daniel Cardenas spoke in opposition to the ordinance. Bruce Gregory, General Manager of Blue Martini, stated opposition to the ordinance but also asked that the time for implementation be extended. Amy Liga McNamara spoke in support of Blue Martini, the charitable work of the bar and in opposition the ordinance. She advocated postponement. Byron Gardiner, founding partner of Blue Martini, commented on the efforts that they have made to mitigate the sound issues. He requested that the time for implementation be extended. Michael Marshall, Gray Robinson on behalf of Crocker Partners, expressed support of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann commented on the crime statistics presented and supported the extension of the time for implementation and passage of the ordinance. Alan Fineburg Jr. offered comments in opposition to the ordinance. Jerry Ruderman addressed a number of previous comments and offered his support of the ordinance. Scott Roseman, marketer for Blue Martini, responded to previous comments and stated his opposition to the ordinance. Jeff Brown, again on behalf of Blue Martini, requested a postponement of consideration of the ordinance. He noted willingness to work with the Council, the police and code enforcement to address problems and reach a solution. Adam Beighley, attorney representing Via Verde, addressed comments made by the previous speaker and stated the residents need to have the ordinance passed. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney summarized the proposed legislation and Council's ability to proceed with a decision regarding this legislation. She then responded to questions including the potential for litigation. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5385. Members commented and offered opinions. Mr. Begley addressed the possibility of an extended time for implementation, noting that his client's support the ordinance as proposed. Discussion continued. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers to amend ordinance No. 5385 to extend the closing date for establishments farther than 1000 feet from residential property. Motion failed for lack of a second. Council Member Singer and Mayor Haynie made final comments. Motion on Ordinance No. 5385 carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5388 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the fiscal year 2016-2017 budget through the Second Budget Amendment to create an Infrastructure Surtax Fund for the purpose of accepting and disbursing funds received from the Florida Department of Revenue for the Palm Beach County Infrastructure Surtax; providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5388 Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, gave a brief presentation explaining the intent of the ordinance and then made herself available for question. The public hearing was opened. Jo Ann Landon commented on the need to fund roadway resurfacing and repair of railroad crossings. She also inquired about motion-activated traffic lights. Glenn Gromann commented on median landscaping on Clint Moore Road. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium 6500 Congress Avenue Monday, May 8, 2017 4:30 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Susan Haynie Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr., Chairman Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang Council Member Scott Singer Commissioner Erin Wright Council Member Robert S. Weinroth Commissioner Craig Ehrnst City Manager Leif J. Ahnell Arthur C. Koski, Attorney and Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser I. Welcome and Introductions - Mayor Susan Haynie and Chairman Bob Rollins Mayor Susan Haynie called the meeting to order at 4:30 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics A. Ocean Breeze Golf Course Commissioner Robert Rollins, Chairman of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) provided brief comments before turning the meeting over to Executive Director Koski. Executive Director Koski showed a slide of an aerial view of the golf course, reviewed the history of the property and how the District became involved in the acquisition of the course. Mr. Koski proceeded to show a short video illustrating the current condition of the property and the District vision of a world class golf resort including a pro shop, lounge, hotel and golf academy in partnership with Greg Norman. He explained how the District was ready to move forward with an lnterlocal Agreement with the City Council for the benefit of the community. A financial pro forma comparing national and local golf courses was reviewed along with estimated revenues and expenditures for Ocean Breeze. Discussion followed; members of both bodies offered comments. Mr. Koski addressed the District's financial ability to go forward with the purchase, the purchase price, and the community benefits of acquiring Ocean Breeze. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Betty Grinnan, Judith Teller Kaye, John Mendozza, Ed Grecsek and Richard Siemens expressed concerns with the purchase price of Ocean Breeze while supporting acquisition of the property. Lupe Eyde, Annabelle Silverman, Barbara Fulkerson, Regina Ecklund, Harold Chaffee, Kate Handley, Steven Gross, Mary LaFuente, Dottie Provenzano, Michael Heymann, Charles Ventre, Jerry Becker, James Rubino, Lenore Wachtel, Eric Leder, Anthony Ciliberti, Joseph Good, Doug Coller, Dale Oliver, Connie Sutherland and Robert DuKate expressed their support of acquiring the Ocean Breeze course and the purchase price. Karl Dickey, representing the Libertarian Party, did not support purchasing the Ocean Breeze course. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Executive Director Koski responded to concerns expressed by previous speakers. Mayor Haynie asked whether Lennar would be willing to pull out the hotel parcel from the sale. Executive Director Koski replied they would not. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser clarified that, should the District proceed with the purchase, the City Council's role would be as a lender and an interlocal agreement would provide for repayment. City Council and District members offered final comments. After further discussion, Council members directed the City Attorney to move forward with drafting an interlocal agreement. IV. Adjournment Both Chairman Rollins and Mayor Haynie thanked everyone for their input. The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 6:45 pm. a leen Maxwell, Recorder o Susan S. Saxton, City Clerk Joint Meeting Minutes May 8, 2017 Page 2

City Council and District members offered final comments. After further discussion, Council members directed the City Attorney to move forward with drafting an interlocal agreement. IV. Adjournment Both Chairman Rollins and Mayor Haynie thanked everyone for their input. The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 6:45 pm. a leen Maxwell, Recorder o Susan S. units.text: Resolution No. 52-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amended and restated master plan/site plan for the Fairway Commons PMD, Resolution No. 13-2015, as amended, to i) amend the approved Planned Mobility Matrix to delete the requirement for an internal shuttle circulator and adjust matrix points allocated to Pedestrian/Bicycle Paths and Physical Character-Amenities to reflect current Matrix scoring methodology, ii) modify the previously approved Shared Parking Analysis to allow additional fast food restaurant floor area and bar area in exchange for a comparable decrease in retail and restaurant floor area and allow for future reallocations of retail/restaurant floor area, and iii) amend conditions related to an updated Overall Master Plan/Site Plan (Sheet C-02), Planned Mobility Matrix Evaluation, Shared Parking Analysis, and modifications to the Master Plan/Site Plan and Shared Parking Analysis to allow for future reallocations of retail/restaurant floor area for the Fairway Commons PMD located at 5500-5580 North Military Trail; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-14-01 R2/SPA-14-01 R2) Resolution No. 52-2017 Drawing The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Development Services Acting Deputy Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on the project was provided. The location of the site was identified and the requested modifications were reviewed. Mr. Bell detailed the proposed changes to the Planned Mobility Matrix, which would reduce the matrix points, and then reviewed the shared parking analysis. The proposed amendments to the Master Plan/Site Plan were listed and the changes to the text of the conditions were provided. The Planning & Zoning Board unanimously approved the requested modifications. Staff also recommended approval of the petition. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, GrayRobinson on behalf of the petitioner, discussed the timing of the initial approval of this project and the changes to the matrix. He also explained the changes that occurred as the project was leased, addressed previous comments and answered further questions. Brian Schmier, developer of Fairway Commons, provided further information in response to several previous questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 52-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 47-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a wireless communication facilities site plan approval for a 98 foot tall stealth communication tower and compound area at the Broken Sound Old Golf Course, located at 1401 West Yamato Road; providing for repealer, providing an effective date (WCF-16-01 & SPA-16-12) Resolution No. 47-2017 Acting City Manager George Brown noted that the applicant had requested the item be continued to the June 13 City Council meeting, at which meeting Council will also hear an appeal associated with this application. He recommended that the hearing be opened to allow public input. Mayor Haynie asked if there was anyone present who wished to speak. No one came forward. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to postpone Resolution No. 47-2017 to the June 13, 2017 City Council meeting. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 59-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to a Conditional Use Approval (Resolution No. 192-78, as amended) for Temple Beth El to allow an expansion of approximately 7,868 square feet to the existing structure, to accommodate the demolition of a portion of the structure and new construction of an enlarged chapel and administration area, new learning center, mezzanine and other improvements, to allow minor modifications to the parking area to meet the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and to allow building height of a non residential structure in a single family residential zoning district to exceed twenty-five (25) feet in height, at Temple Beth El, located at 333 Southwest 4th Avenue; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-16-04) Resolution No. 59-2017 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Susan Lesser, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a summary of the application. The size, zoning, and location of the property were provided. Details of the current and proposed uses were listed. The modified master site plan was discussed. It was noted that the requested variance was unanimously approved by the Zoning Board of Adjustment. The proposed increase in height, the basis of the conditional use, was not considered adverse by staff. Ms. Lesser presented details of parking and traffic analysis. The Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval as does staff. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Council Member O'Rourke made final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 59-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5369 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to incorporate new provisions relating to self-storage facilities (interior storage unit access); amending Section 28-307(1) relating to building intensity; amending the following District regulations to add "Self-Storage Facilities (interior storage unit access)" to the list of permitted and conditional uses, respectively: Sections 28-872 and 28-873 (C-1 District}, Sections 28-1017 and 28-1019 (W-1 District), Sections 28-1042 and 28-1043 (IG/S1 District), Sections 28-1072 and 28-1073 (M-1 District), Sections 28-1097 and 28-1098 (M-2 District), and Sections 28-1123 and 28-1124 (M-3 District); amending Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, by creating a new Section 28-1310 for "Self-Storage Facilities (interior storage unit access)" and establishing development standards for such use, including a distance separation requirement, and establishing a distance separation requirement for "Self-Storage Facilities"; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-15- Q]_l Ordinance No. 5369 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a brief review of the text amendment and provided an update on the work done by the principals/attorneys representing the interested parties. The proposed agreed upon changes to the Code included in this ordinance were listed. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen made herself available for questions. Michael Marshall, GrayRobinson, addressed the process thus far and reviewed the agreed upon revisions to the ordinance. He requested that Council adopt the ordinance. Michael Weiner, on behalf of Madison Holdings, asked about the addition of language to the comprehensive plan. The City Attorney provided information. Ele Zachariades, with Dunay, Miskel and Backman, recommended approval. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Members commented and asked several questions of staff. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, addressed the distance separation requirements and the applicability of same. Discussion of amended language followed. Changes to the language on page 11, lines 21 and 22 of the ordinance were recited by the City Attorney. In response to Council Member O'Rourke, Mr. Schaad stated that staff does not recommend approval of the ordinance. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5369 as amended. In response to Deputy Mayor Rodgers question, Acting City Manager George Brown explained why staff recommends against passage. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. !i Ordinance No. 5389 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for the vacation and abandonment of a portion of a drainage and public utility easement located at 424 Northeast 5th Street, as more specifically described herein; providing for repealer: providing an effective date (EA-16-06) Ordinance No. 5389 Lynn Bodor, Property Specialist Appraiser, gave a brief presentation explaining the need for the abandonment. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5389. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to Planned Mobility Developments; amending Code of Ordinances, Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article I, "In General," Section 28-2, "Definitions" to modify and change the definition of "Garage, Private" to "Garage", define "Parking Structure", define "Rear Loaded Garage", and define "Rear Loaded Unit", amending Sections 28-986, 28-1028, and 28-1132.1 in the LIRP, W-1, and M-3 Zoning Districts of the City to exclude rear loaded garages for rear loaded units in a Planned Mobility Development from the calculation of floor area; amending Sections 28-742, 28-777, 28-797, 28-822, 28-1072, 28-1242, 28-1247, 28-1250, and 28-1850 to change references from "Parking Garages" to "Parking Structures"; amending Section 28-1655 to change the reference from "Private Garage"; providing for repealer; providing for severability; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-09) Ordinance No. 5392 Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with detailed background information on the genesis of the proposed Code amendment, including recommendations from the Planning and Zoning Board, discussions with the petitioner and staff's position. A summary of the revised text amendment was provided. Mr. Bell discussed density and intensity, reviewed new definitions in the Code, clarified the difference between parking garages and parking structures, noted the amendment's consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and the Code, and reviewed staff's analysis of the amendment. In conclusion, Mr. Bell noted that both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. He then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the petitioner, thanked Mr. Bell for an excellent presentation and thanked all involved for the collaborative effort. She advocated passage of the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5392. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5393 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, relating to the Medical Center (MC) and Motel-Business (R-B-1) zoning districts to provide regulations for parking structures and master plans; amending Section 28-925 to provide for the height, length and location (yard/setback) of parking structures in order to allow parking structures (accessory to a hospital) to be located closer to single family residential properties than other buildings and structures in the MC zoning district; amending Section 28-927(6) to establish yard (setback) measurements where a master plan is applicable; creating new Section 28-932 of the MC zoning district to establish development parameters which relate to a master plan and subsequent site plans; amending the R-B-1 Zoning District, Section 28-742, to allow master plan approval for property contiguous to a hospital; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-13-04) Ordinance No. 5393 Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with background information and a summary of the proposed text amendment. Topics included, but were not limited to, parking structure height, length, setback, and screening; parameters for MC Master Plans; relationship of structures to adjacent multi-family residential; and permitted uses. Mr. Bell reviewed a revision to page 4 of the ordinance that was provided to Council. It was noted that the proposed amendment is compatible and consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. Staffs analysis of the various elements of the ordinance was reviewed in detail. Mr. Bell noted that the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommends approval as well. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available to answer questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of Boca Raton Regional Hospital, gave a PowerPoint presentation, noting that should the ordinance be approved, the Hospital would have to get approval, in a quasi-judicial proceeding, for any change to their property. She summarized the three parts of the Code amendment: parking structure distance from residential, yard measurement in master plans, and allowing R-B-1 zoned property contiguous to MC districts to be included in a master plan. Ms. Miske! then discussed the changes being requested, comparing setbacks in various zoning districts. She noted her client had no objection to a condition for additional screening, advocated passage of the ordinance, and made herself available for questions. Colleen White, president of Spanish Oaks Condominium Board of Directors, expressed opposition to passage of the ordinance, noting that a parking structure would affect the residents' quality of life. Krista Maki proposed a number of ways in which the Hospital could address the parking issue. She advocated postponement of a decision in order to study the proposal for a different location of the parking gorge. Barring postponement, Ms. Maki suggested that the distance of a structure from residential be increased to 140 feet. lgal Bloch, on behalf of Spanish Oaks Condominium Association, expressed concerns with the negative effects of the ordinance. Michael Weiner, on behalf of Spanish Oaks Condominium, asserted that the proposed zoning changes should be considered a quasi-judicial matter because the changes proposed benefit only the Hospital. He advocated that the process start over again. Michelle Valle expressed opposition to the ordinance. Peter Gary commented on the current state of the Hospital, addressed the existing parking issue, and advocated passage of the ordinance. Andrew McLaughlin expressed opposition to the ordinance and advocated having a 250 foot setback. Malka Cabal expressed a number of concerns including safety and security, and stated her opposition to the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Singer proposed three amendments to the ordinance including increasing the distance of a parking structure from single family homes to 140 feet (page 3, line 25), new language specifying a standard for the fac;;ade to prevent light spillage for a parking structure (page 4, new section 28-925.c.), and signage to prevent non-official use of any access road (page 4, after line 10). In response to a question from Deputy Mayor Rodgers, Bonnie Miskel stated her client's agreement to the distance increase to 140 feet. Jim Bell then read into the record a revision to c.ii. on page 4 of the ordinance that would require a double of row of landscaping between a parking structure and single family homes. Council was provided with a handout containing the language. Members suggested that this revision should also apply to multi-family residential. Mr. Bell noted that staff had prepared a revision that would include multi-family residential buffering. This amendment would be a new subsection 28-925 d. Some discussion followed, after which Mr. Bell read the new language into the record. Mayor Haynie noted that five amendments had been proposed. The City Attorney suggested a brief recess to allow staff to organize and review the language suggested for the various amendments. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to recess the meeting. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The meeting recessed at approximately 8:15 pm and reconvened at approximately 8:24 pm. Acting City Manager George Brown reviewed the proposed amendments, identified where in the ordinance the new language would be inserted, and noted that the amendments had been reorganized with subsection d. now having three paragraphs requiring landscaping, fac;;ade, and access road signage that would be applicable to all residential, both single and multi family. Discussion ensued. Bonnie Miskel noted that there were no objections to most proposed amendments, but that the fac;;ade requirements should not be specific. The City Attorney noted that the design of any facade would be dealt with in a future site plan. However, Ms. Miskel stated that her client could not to agree to an amendment specifying fac;;ade design. Members discussed a possible change to the language addressing the fac;;ade requirements. The City Attorney addressed the objection to the legislative language. Mr. Brown suggested alternate language that eliminated the reference to 'shutters' and 'window-like' to which Ms. Miskel agreed. The City Attorney addressed at length Mr. Weiner's earlier comments with regard to legislative matters versus quasi-judicial matters, noting that the decision before Council is a policy decision, not one granting any development rights. When the Hospital submits a site plan, it will be considered at a quasi-judicial hearing. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Ordinance No. 5393 as amended. Members made final comments. Ms. O'Rourke posed several questions. Staff provided responses, in particular regarding height, location and employee parking. The City Attorney noted that this conversation is theoretical as there is no plan being considered at this time. All are questions that are appropriate when a site plan is before Council. Mr. Singer suggested that the rules be suspended and that the Hospital be allowed to respond. Ms. Miskel provided a response. Deputy Mayor Rodgers and Council Member Singer weighed in. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

Staffs analysis of the various elements of the ordinance was reviewed in detail. Mr. Bell noted that the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommends approval as well. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available to answer questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of Boca Raton Regional Hospital, gave a PowerPoint presentation, noting that should the ordinance be approved, the Hospital would have to get approval, in a quasi-judicial proceeding, for any change to their property. She summarized the three parts of the Code amendment: parking structure distance from residential, yard measurement in master plans, and allowing R-B-1 zoned property contiguous to MC districts to be included in a master plan. Ms. Miske! then discussed the changes being requested, comparing setbacks in various zoning districts. She noted her client had no objection to a condition for additional screening, advocated passage of the ordinance, and made herself available for questions. Colleen White, president of Spanish Oaks Condominium Board of Directors, expressed opposition to passage of the ordinance, noting that a parking structure would affect the residents' quality of life. Krista Maki proposed a number of ways in which the Hospital could address the parking issue. She advocated postponement of a decision in order to study the proposal for a different location of the parking gorge. Barring postponement, Ms. Maki suggested that the distance of a structure from residential be increased to 140 feet. lgal Bloch, on behalf of Spanish Oaks Condominium Association, expressed concerns with the negative effects of the ordinance. Michael Weiner, on behalf of Spanish Oaks Condominium, asserted that the proposed zoning changes should be considered a quasi-judicial matter because the changes proposed benefit only the Hospital. He advocated that the process start over again. Michelle Valle expressed opposition to the ordinance. Peter Gary commented on the current state of the Hospital, addressed the existing parking issue, and advocated passage of the ordinance. Andrew McLaughlin expressed opposition to the ordinance and advocated having a 250 foot setback. Malka Cabal expressed a number of concerns including safety and security, and stated her opposition to the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Singer proposed three amendments to the ordinance including increasing the distance of a parking structure from single family homes to 140 feet (page 3, line 25), new language specifying a standard for the fac;;ade to prevent light spillage for a parking structure (page 4, new section 28-925.c.), and signage to prevent non-official use of any access road (page 4, after line 10). In response to a question from Deputy Mayor Rodgers, Bonnie Miskel stated her client's agreement to the distance increase to 140 feet. Jim Bell then read into the record a revision to c.ii. on page 4 of the ordinance that would require a double of row of landscaping between a parking structure and single family homes. Council was provided with a handout containing the language. Members suggested that this revision should also apply to multi-family residential. Mr. Bell noted that staff had prepared a revision that would include multi-family residential buffering. This amendment would be a new subsection 28-925 d. Some discussion followed, after which Mr. Bell read the new language into the record. Mayor Haynie noted that five amendments had been proposed. The City Attorney suggested a brief recess to allow staff to organize and review the language suggested for the various amendments. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to recess the meeting. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The meeting recessed at approximately 8:15 pm and reconvened at approximately 8:24 pm. Acting City Manager George Brown reviewed the proposed amendments, identified where in the ordinance the new language would be inserted, and noted that the amendments had been reorganized with subsection d. now having three paragraphs requiring landscaping, fac;;ade, and access road signage that would be applicable to all residential, both single and multi family. Discussion ensued. Bonnie Miskel noted that there were no objections to most proposed amendments, but that the fac;;ade requirements should not be specific. The City Attorney noted that the design of any facade would be dealt with in a future site plan. However, Ms. Miskel stated that her client could not to agree to an amendment specifying fac;;ade design. Members discussed a possible change to the language addressing the fac;;ade requirements. The City Attorney addressed the objection to the legislative language. Mr. Brown suggested alternate language that eliminated the reference to 'shutters' and 'window-like' to which Ms. Miskel agreed. The City Attorney addressed at length Mr. Weiner's earlier comments with regard to legislative matters versus quasi-judicial matters, noting that the decision before Council is a policy decision, not one granting any development rights. When the Hospital submits a site plan, it will be considered at a quasi-judicial hearing. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Ordinance No. 5393 as amended. Members made final comments. Ms. O'Rourke posed several questions. Staff provided responses, in particular regarding height, location and employee parking. The City Attorney noted that this conversation is theoretical as there is no plan being considered at this time. All are questions that are appropriate when a site plan is before Council. Mr. Singer suggested that the rules be suspended and that the Hospital be allowed to respond. Ms. Miskel provided a response. Deputy Mayor Rodgers and Council Member Singer weighed in. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a wireless communicatiqn facilities site plan approval for a 98 foot tall stealth communication tower and compound area §1t the Broken Sound Old Golf Course, located at 1401 West Yamato Road: providing for repealer, providing an effective date (WCF-16-01 & SPA-16-12) · Resolution No. 47-2017 Mayor Haynie stated that Resolutions No. 67-2017 and 47-2017 would be heard cont6mporaneously and voted on separately. The City Attorney verified that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the request for a telecommunications tower and the appeal of the denial of a setback variance. Details of the stealth tower, its location and the site plan were provided. Mr. Schaad noted that the tower is compliant with City Code in all respects except the setback. The justifications for the tower location and the variance, as provided by the applicant, were reviewed. The Community Appearance Board review was discussed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommend approval of the tower but not the variance. Mr. Schaad then detailed the Zoning Board of Adjustments denial of the variance. In consideration of multiple factors, the Development Services staff recommends granting the variance and approval of the tower itself. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Deborah Martohue, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. She began by describing the proposed site for the tower and its compliance with the City Code. The reasons for the location of the tower were presented, as were other details of the project. It was noted that the project had the support of neighbors. In conclusion, Ms. Martohue asked for support of the variance and the site plan. Glenn Gromann offered support of both resolutions. John Crean, General Manager of Broken Sound Club, relayed that the Board of Governors and the Club membership fully endorsed granting the variance and approving the tower. Larry Kobren, First ViGe President of the Broken Sound Board of Governors, noted that residents do not have good cell service and they support the tower that will improve cell service. There was no cross examination. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 67-2017, reversing the decision of the Zoning Board of Adjustment and granting the appeal. Council Member Singer made final comments and made several suggestions with regard to the Zoning Board of Adjustment. Mayor Haynie noted her support of the appeal. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 47-2017. Motion carried unanimously on!a voice vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andre~ Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 75-2017 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the a~peal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying LexisNexis Risk Solutions'! requested building identity sign (Permit No. 17-1058) for a multiple story building located at :777 Yamato Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 75-2017 Mayor Haynie noted that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members rt,ade their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. I Tori Golden, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The property locatiJn was provided, as was the location of the requested building identity sign. The Community Appea~ance Board (CAB) reasons for denial, including letter and logo size, were reviewed. Examples of ~ther building signs mounted on glass were provided. Ms. Golden noted that staff determined that the sign is in compliance with the Sign Code and recommended that the decision of the CAB be reversed! and the appeal be granted. Upon concluding, Ms. Golden and Brandon Schaad, Director of Development Services, responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Patricia Ortiz, on behalf of the petitioner, noted that her company appeared before CAB a number of times, revising the sign in response to the Board'$ comments. It was noted that LexisNexis had agreed to store the glass panel so that it could be reinstalled should the company leave the location. Members asked that storage of the glass and that :the removal of the trademark symbol be conditions for granting the appeal. CAB member Jessica Dornblaser gave a PowerPoint presentation reviewing the reasons that the Board did not approve the sign, citing the supplemental criteria used by the Board. Details were provided. CAB member Joej Peterson provided further information, commented on staff's analysis and then responded to questions. Ms. Ortiz then made comments in rebuttal, provided a handout, and responded to questions. Eric Saida, LexisNexis, noted the company's commitment to Boca Raton and the importance of the sign to the company. Members asked further questions regarding the size and placement of the sign. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members offered comments and noted their position. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Resolution No. 75-2017 to grant the appeal with modifications. The City Attorney read language into the record outlining the modifications: the glass panel removed will be retained in storage and the registered trademark symbol will be removed from the sign. Deputy Mayor Rodgers accepted the amendments to the motion Motion carried 3 to 2; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying LexisNexis Risk Solutions' requested flat sign and freestanding sign (Permit No. 17-1078) proposed to be located at 6601 Park of Commerce Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 76-2017 Mayor Haynie stated that the same quasi-judicial procedures continued to govern this public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Tori Golden, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Details were provided on the property location and specifications of the proposed wall and monument signs. The CAB cited the size of the logo and the trademark symbols in their denial of the permit. Staff determined that both signs are in compliance with the Sign Code and recommended reversal of the CAB decision. U~on concluding, Ms. Golden made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Patricia Ortiz presented on behalf of LexisNexis Risk Solutions, providing details of the proposed signs and noting that the registered trademark symbols would be removed. She then responded to questions. Joe Peterson, CAB member, offered comments on the requests made of LexisNexis, principally the request for landscaping and the size of the logo. CAB member Jessica Dornblaser added her comments. Patricia Ortiz stated that they would be willing to provide landscaping that would not interfere with the sign. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney read amendments into the record. In section 3 of the resolution, the appeal would be granted with the trademark symbol be removed. In section 5, the same modification would apply to the monument sign as well as the requirement to install landscaping. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to adjourn Resolution No. 76-2017 to grant the appeal with modifications as r~ad into the record. Motion carried 3 to 2; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Resolution No. 80-2017 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board approving Luxury Travel Experts' requested flat sign (Permit No. 17-1197), with a condition regarding the size of the logo, propmped to be located at 1200 Yamato Road, Suite B2: providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 80-2017 Once again the Mayor noted that the quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Tori Golden, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the property and the sign were provided. The CAB cited the size of logo in their denial. Ms. Golden provided the measurements of elements of the sign. She stated that staff determined that the sign is in compliance with the Sign Code and reversing the CAB decision, allowing the sign as presented. Ms. Golden made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Susan Bogen, Signarama, read a statement from the franchisor regarding the sign, which included the claim that the sign was registered and therefore could not be changed. A handout was provided showing the location of the business storefront, noting that its distance from the road necessitates the size of the sign not being reduced. Ms. Bogen then responded to questions. Jose Arosemena, the Expedia CruiseShipCenters franchisee, addressed the appearance should the size be reduced. CAB member Jessica Dornblaser gave a PowerPoint presentation explaining the Board's reason for denying the sign permit and the conditions the Board proposed. She pointed out that there are multiple versions of the trademarked sign with various layouts and sizes and reviewed the comments made by the Board in their denial of the permit. Deputy Mayor Rodgers suggested that the appeal be granted with the conditions that the registered trademark symbol be removed and the logo size, excluding the points, be no larger than the letters. CAB member Joe Peterson commented. Discussion ensued. Susan Bogen made final comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney recommended that the decision of the CAB be affirmed with modified conditions reducing the height of the logo so that the circumference, excluding the points, is no higher or lower than the letters of the sign and that registered trademarks be removed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 80-2017affirming the decision of the Community Appearance Board with modifications as stated. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council· Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Selection of Florida League of Cities Conference Voting Delegate Memo Both Council Member Weinroth and Council Member Singer suggested that Mayor H$ynie be designated as the City's voting delegate, to which all members agreed. · I fL Biennial Review of Retirement and Disability Benefits - General Employees' Ptnsion Plan Memo : i I City Manager Leif Ahnell explained that the Code of Ordinances requires this review ~very two years. It is recommended that, due to a serious erosion of benefits, certain retirees receive a cdst of living increase and others receive a lump sum. He then responded to questions. Rodrigo Hidalgo, representing SEIU members, offered thanks for movement on this issue and emphasized that the increase in the cost of living for retirees. Retiree Anthony Bazant addressed the effects of the erosion of benefits. Steve Griffith commented on the fact that general employee retirees do not get a cost of living adjustment in their pensions and provided a handout with his recommendation. In general, Council members agreed to proceed with an RFP with alternatives for residential service only and for both residential and commercial service.

He then made himself available for questions. Members offered comments and positive feedback in support of Mr. Ahnell's job performance.

units.text: Executive Performance Review Review City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser highlighted the function of the City Attorney's Office and reviewed important issues that her staff has addressed in the last 12 to 18 months. Council members thanked Ms. Frieser and offered positive comments in support of her job performance.

units.text: Council Member Singer highlighted the upcoming Summer in the City events downtown. Deputy Mayor Rodgers pointed out comments in an online newsletter and noted that the City Attorney was incorrectly quoted. Ms. Frieser addressed the comments and offered corrections. Council Member O'Rourke commented on the possibility of readdressing the Pattern Book. Mayor Haynie offered final comments and wished all a Happy Fathers Day. Council Member Singer announced his next town hall.

units.text: Resolution No. 94-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton urging the Florida Legislature to enact legislation that would make texting while driving a primary offense; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 94-2017 Council Member Weinroth made introductory remarks on the resolution brought forward at his request. He then introduced Representative Emily Slosberg who gave a brief PowerPoint presentation in support of State legislation making texting while driving a primary offense and then responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Sheila Jaffe offered support of the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 94-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ellyn Okrent provided an update of the work being planned for and being done at the Children's Museum. She requested the City's help with renovations of the buildings at the Museum. Mohamed Abdalla, Habitat for Humanity, provided details of the work Habitat will be doing at the Museum. Margaret Fitzsimons gave a PowerPoint presentation on her recommendations for the downtown waterfront property and the planning for same to produce a design and planning program document. She requested an endorsement of this document. Council Members O'Rourke and Singer offered their thoughts. Jo Ann Landon offered support of Ms. Fitzsimons presentation, advocated connectivity to other waterfront parks and commented on other related topics. Steve Griffith commented on the COLA for general employees retirement benefit. The City Manager provided additional information. Aaron Fisher asked about the rental registration program, the Dixie Highway beautification, and adults approaching minor children. Mr. Ahnell provided information on the beautification and rental registration. Ms. Frieser provided information on the possibility of an ordinance regarding Mr. Fisher's last issue.

units.text: Council Member Weinroth thanked his colleagues for passage of the resolution regarding texting while driving. He then asked for consideration of a meeting change in October due to a conflict with a Florida League of Cities Fly-In. After a brief discussion, members agreed to check calendars and work on an accommodation. He then reported on the Office Depot Foundation donation of backpacks for children in need and the nine new police officers recently sworn in. Mayor Haynie commented on a request members have received to prohibit conversion therapy for children. She asked the City Attorney to review the City Code regarding protection of children. Council Member O'Rourke thanked the representatives of the Children's Museum. ll ADJOURNMENT: The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 8:00 pm. • ATTEST: Susan S. Saxton, City Clerk

units.text: Mayor Haynie announced that the public hearings on items A., B., and C. would be conducted contemporaneously and each petition would be voted on separately. She noted that Ordinance No. 5394 required four votes for adoption. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave a PowerPoint presentation on the ordinances and resolution, beginning with a brief review of the application that included a Future Land Use Map amendment, a rezoning and a site plan approval. The location, current land use and current zoning of the property were provided. Consistency, compatibility and concurrency of the Future Land Use amendment and rezoning with the Comprehensive Plan were discussed; concerns and inconsistency were pointed out. Mr. Schaad also noted a higher demand for emergency services and the costs related to same. The site plan resolution was then reviewed. Mr. Schaad noted that the Community Advisory Board reviewed the project and had a favorable view. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended denial of the application. Staff also recommends denial. Upon conclusion, Mr. Schaad responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, on behalf of petitioner Goray-Rosemurgy Senior Living, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He noted the mix of uses adjacent to the property and contended that the project meets or exceeds the requirements of the proposed zoning. Elevations and details of the complex were provided. Mr. Marshall argued that the use is not incompatible with adjacent zoning uses and that it is compatible and consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. The benefits of the project were listed. He then introduced Dan Sacco, Boca Raton Regional Hospital, who expressed support for this project that the Hospital finds essential. Jim Rosemurgy, petitioner, made several points in support of the project, touting the partnership with the Hospital's Marcus Neuroscience Institute and Florida Atlantic University College of Nursing. Gerry Goray, petitioner, addressed the emergency services issue and offered support of the project. Council members asked a number of questions of the petitioners. Mr. Schaad the read into the record a number of conditions of approval amending Section 2 of the site plan resolution, to which the petitioners agreed. The City Attorney added a condition related to the urgent care center. Mr. Marshall thanked Council and offered final comments. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments and stated their positions.
