Resolution No. 97-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1098{a), Code of Ordinances, to allow an eating and drinking establishment, not including curb service, in the General Industrial (M-2) zoning district for the property located at 4160 NW 1st Avenue Bay Numbers 19, 20 and 21; providing for repealer; providing an effective date {CA- 17-01) Resolution No. 97-2017 Drawings Mayor Haynie again noted that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She identified the location and zoning of the property and provided details of the project. The conditional use requested for the tasting room was explained. Details were provided, including traffic impacts. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval with a condition prohibiting on-site food preparation that has been added to the resolution. Staff recommends approval subject to the conditions in the resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to questions, in particular with regard to the condition prohibiting food trucks. The public hearing was opened. Ty Harris, GrayRobinson, on behalf of the applicant, addressed the restriction on food service and the hours of operation. He then made himself available for questions. Ken Gross, Prosperity Brewery, advocated for the ability to have food, both food trucks and delivered food. He also responded to questions. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, noted that the condition does not prohibit delivery of food. Members discussed allowing food trucks, their effect on parking, and an opening time of 5:30 pm. Discussion ensued. Mr. Harris provided further information. No one else came forward to speak. The City Attorney read into the record amendments allowing food trucks, having adequate trash disposal and a parking plan, and changing the opening time to 5:30 pm. The public hearing was then closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 97-2017 as revised and amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5396 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute a non­ exclusive Construction and Demolition (C&D) Debris Collection and Disposal Services Franchise Agreement with SABA Recycling, Inc., pursuant to Section 14-21, Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5396 Dan Grippo, Municipal Services Director, gave a brief presentation on the ordinance. He provided details of the City's Construction and Debris Collection and Disposal Services Franchise Program. He then responded to questions from Council members. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5396. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Ordinance No. 5397 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton discontinuing the City's policy of allowing private expressive installations in Sanborn Square; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5397 The City Attorney briefly summarized the ordinance, noting that first amendment speech is not affected by this ordinance. Ms. Frieser responded to a number of questions from Council, providing clarification, a history of how installations were first allowed in Sanborn Square, and the types of installations that the City itself could put in Sanborn Square. Ms. Frieser provided information on free speech areas in the City, noting that parks are traditional public forums. The public hearing was opened. Therese Brady, Laurie Colbert, Robin Hardy, Dr. Victoria Gylys-Morin, Charles Fix, Ron Sheldon, Ed Johnson, Brian Wood, Carol Steelman, Emmanuel Okwor, Cristina Escalante, Marlene Cowan, Janet Sheldon, Jerry Chua, Diane Kabbas, Dale Oliver, and Christine Roman expressed opposition to the ordinance. Many speakers stated that the government should not decide what can be displayed and that they do not want their religious traditions curtailed. Joe Manceri offered his opinion of the issues he sees as central to this ordinance. Joseph Kabbas expressed opposition and requested that no decision be made tonight. Rev. Andrew Sherman commented on the candlelight vigil that the interfaith council held the previous night and expressed concerns about giving up traditions and not allowing free expression. Sunny Lehman asked if there could be a vote on this ordinance by citizens. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council members offered comments and stated their positions, each noting that there would not be a vote on this ordinance tonight. There was no motion to adopt the ordinance, and no action was taken. The meeting was recessed at approximately 9:27 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:41 pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering an appeal by Outfront Media LLC of an administrative decision (on behalf of the Development Services Department) relating to Section 7.14 of the Unified Land Development Code (ULDC) resulting in a denial of Outfront Media's request to alter an existing billboard (off-premise sign) from a mechanically changeable sign face to an electronic, digital sign face (Permit No. 16-5912) located at 2471 Butts Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (BP16-00005912) The City Attorney reviewed the procedures that would be followed as this item is an administrative appeal under the County's ULDC. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He identified the location, land use and zoning of the property. The billboard was described as was the proposal for the change to an electronic face. Mr. Schaad noted that the County billboard settlement agreement has expired and, therefore, is no longer applicable. He continued to review his analysis of the situation, providing reasons why the sign is non-conforming and not allowable. Details were provided, including extensive references to the provisions of the ULDC. Mr. Schaad then reviewed the options before Council. Upon concluding he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. William McCormick, GrayRobinson on behalf of the appellant, provided a notebook to Council. He then began his presentation, referring to various sections in the book, refuting the assertions made in the staff presentation and making an extensive case for allowing the electronic billboard. Ty Harris, GrayRobinson, offered his perspective on the issue. The public hearing was then closed. The City Attorney began her comments by stating that Council should not rule in fear of a lawsuit. She then addressed a number of the points made by Mr. McCormick, providing counter points and explaining a number of the assertions made. At this time, Mayor Haynie noted that a motion was needed to extend the meeting beyond 11 pm. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to extend the meeting beyond 11 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The City Attorney referenced the extensive staff report and then pointed out the letter from the County Zoning Director which stated that electronic billboards are not now and never have been allowed in Palm Beach County. Mr. McCormick requested that the hearing be reopened. The Mayor stated that the public hearing was closed and his objection to that was noted for the record. Ms. Frieser reviewed further aspects of this administrative appeal. Motion was made by Council Member Singer, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Resolution No. 95-2017 to deny the appeal. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. 1§.:. CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS: George Brown, Deputy City Manager, summarized the procedures for the sale of western golf course included in the ordinance introduced earlier in the meeting. The timeline was reviewed . Members offered comments and discussed the timeframe. In general, members agreed to ask staff to compress the timeline. City Manager Leif Ahnell then discussed the RFP for sanitation services. He noted that staff suggests going forward with residential component now and , perhaps , go forward with the commercial component at a later date. He then responded to questions from Council.

units.section: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS
units.text: Proposed User Fee Schedule City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a PowerPoint presentation reviewing the proposed budget for the coming fiscal year. The goals and priorities set by Council during the May 2017 Strategic Planning Sessions were listed. Mr. Ahnell proposed a millage rate of 3.6788 for the 2017-18 fiscal year, which is a slight decrease from last year. He then reviewed proposed changes in various operating costs, as well as detailing new personnel and a new program for canal maintenance and refuse collection. There followed a number of charts and graphs illustrating a resident's tax bil;, assessed property values in Boca Raton; tax rate history; and favorable comparisons of Boca Raton to neighboring cities' tax rates, fire assessment, and water/sewer rates. The presentation was then turned over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2017/18-2022/23 Capital Improvement Program (CIP). Ms. McGuire noted the sources of revenue that will fund capital improvements and then reviewed, by department, the projects, vehicles and equipment included in the CIP for 2017-18 fiscal year. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire and Mr. Ahnell responded to questions from Council members. Jean-Michel Neault, Compliance Auditor, gave a PowerPoint presentation on the changes to the User Fee Schedule to become effective October 1, 2017. He reviewed the changes proposed for the coming year, and then responded to questions from Council members.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton imposing Fire Services Assessments against Assessed Property located within the City for the Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2017; approving the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Rate of Assessment; approving the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Assessment Roll; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 109-2017 Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation on the proposed increase in the fire services assessment. She noted that one letter was received objecting to the increase. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Council Member Weinroth suggested that the residential fee increase be cut in half. The public hearing was opened. Charlie Helton voiced opposition to the fire services assessment fee and advocated that it be eliminated. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. In response to Council Member Weinroth's comments, Mr. Ahnell addressed the method of calculating the fee and provided other information. Discussion ensued; members shared their positions. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 109-2017. Motion carried on a 3 to 2 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Mr. Ahnell announced that the Final Budget Hearing would be held on October 2, 2017. Members discussed the nonprofit funding. Council Member Weinroth addressed the hurricane related damages to the Tri-County Humane Society, stating that any grant for same should be treated as a separate item. Members provided final comments. Council Member O'Rourke commented on the recent passing of former Boca Raton Mayor Carol Hanson. Council Member Weinroth reported that the northbound entrance ramp of the new Spanish River Boulevard 1-95 interchange would be opening at 5:00 am on Tuesday morning.
units.full: Resolution No. 109-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton imposing Fire Services Assessments against Assessed Property located within the City for the Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2017; approving the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Rate of Assessment; approving the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Assessment Roll; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 109-2017 Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation on the proposed increase in the fire services assessment. She noted that one letter was received objecting to the increase. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Council Member Weinroth suggested that the residential fee increase be cut in half. The public hearing was opened. Charlie Helton voiced opposition to the fire services assessment fee and advocated that it be eliminated. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. In response to Council Member Weinroth's comments, Mr. Ahnell addressed the method of calculating the fee and provided other information. Discussion ensued; members shared their positions. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 109-2017. Motion carried on a 3 to 2 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Mr. Ahnell announced that the Final Budget Hearing would be held on October 2, 2017. Members discussed the nonprofit funding. Council Member Weinroth addressed the hurricane related damages to the Tri-County Humane Society, stating that any grant for same should be treated as a separate item. Members provided final comments. Council Member O'Rourke commented on the recent passing of former Boca Raton Mayor Carol Hanson. Council Member Weinroth reported that the northbound entrance ramp of the new Spanish River Boulevard 1-95 interchange would be opening at 5:00 am on Tuesday morning.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium 6500 Congress Avenue Monday, September 26, 2017 3:03 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Susan Haynie Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr., Chairman Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang Council Member Scott Singer Commissioner Erin Wright Council Member Robert S. Weinroth Commissioner Craig Ehrnst City Manager Leif J. Ahnell Arthur C. Koski, Attorney and Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser I. Welcome and Introductions - Mayor Susan Haynie and Chairman Bob Rollins Mayor Susan Haynie called the meeting to order at 3:03 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics A Ocean Breeze Golf Course Commissioner Robert Rollins, Chairman of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) provided brief comments referencing the report provided to the City and invited questions from Council. Mayor Haynie asked that Mr. Koski provide a high level overview of the documents provided to the City. before turning the meeting over to Executive Director Koski, which followed. Topics included, but were not limited to, the appraisal, the use and operation of the hotel property, improvements to the surrounding infrastructure, the cost of course development, and financing for acquisition. Mr. Koski then responded to Council members' questions. Mr. Koski noted that the intent is to rename the course Boca National Golf Club. Richard Singer and Ed Getherall, with the National Golf Foundation that did a feasibility study on behalf of the Beach and Park District, provided further information on income and development cost projections for the course. Mr. Koski then reviewed the appraisal and provided additional information on the potential uses for the 29 acres. District members then offered comments. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Larry Kobren, Harold Chaffee, Declan Murphy, Madeline Cuevas, Peggy Haupt, Dottie Provenzano, Robert DuKate, expressed their support of acquiring the Ocean Breeze course and the purchase price. Karl Dickey, Doug Coller, Angelo Sands, Cil Ciliberti, Glenn Gromann, Lenore Wachtel commented. Roger Kleinschmidt spoke in support of the Boca Municipal Golf Course. Judith Teller Kaye and Jay Slapp expressed concern with the cost of Ocean Breeze. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Chairman Rollins indicated that the District was looking for support from the Council to move forward. Members made final comments, voiced their concerns and stated their positions. The consensus of Council members was to support the District moving forward with the purchase of Ocean Breeze. Mayor Haynie then read into record the supportive comments of Jacob Jennings. Chairman Rollins acknowledged the support of the Council and stated that the District would move forward with the golf course purchase. IV. Adjournment The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 4:38 pm. ~tk~ stisans.saxton, City Clerk

Ordinance No. 5401 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article I, Section 28-7, "Reasonable Accommodation Procedures," Code of Ordinances, updating and amending the procedures and requirements for requests for reasonable accommodation, including the established legal standards with respect to eligibility and qualification for such requests: amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," Code of Ordinances, updating the definition of substance abuse treatment facility to delete the portion of the definition previously invalidated: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5401 City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser explained that this ordinance would update the City's procedures with regard to reasonable accommodation. She then highlighted various provisions of the ordinance and then noted that this would improve the City's procedures. Upon concluding, Ms. Frieser responded questions. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute a non­ exclusive Commercial Solid Waste Collection Services Franchise Agreement with Waste Pro of Florida, Inc. pursuant to Section 14-22, Code of Ordinances: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date Items 12.J. and 12.J.a. are related. Resolution No. 116-2017 will be heard immediately following consideration of Ordinance No. 5406. Should Ordinance No. 5406 not be adopted, Resolution No. 116-2017 will not be considered. Ordinance No. 5405 Once again, Dan Grippo gave a brief presentation, noting that this is agreement is with a new solid waste collection service provider. He stated the annual fee and then recommended approval of the ordinance The public hearing was opened. Tim Bowers, representing Waste Pro, provided information on his company. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5405. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. In response to a question, the City Manager provided information on the possibility of using the companies with which the City has franchise agreements to remove storm debris. Ordinance No. 5406 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 13-60, "Applicability," and creating Section 13-74, "Special Transactions," both in Article Ill, "Sale of City Property," Chapter 13, "Public Places," Code of Ordinances, to provide procedures for the sale of City property involving large transactions (and excluding such transactions from the remainder of Article Ill): providing procedures for the sale of the City-owned property known as the Municipal Golf Course West: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5406 .§.:. Resolution No. 116-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton requiring a non-refundable pre-selection deposit as a condition of eligibility for the potential purchase of the City's Municipal Golf Course West, in accordance with the procedures established by Ordinance No. 5406: authorizing the City Manager to execute a Pre-Selection Deposit Agreement and expend deposited funds delivered to the City by the selected finalist for such legal and professional services the City Manager deems appropriate in connection with the purchase and sale of the Municipal Golf Course West: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date Resolution No. 116-2017 George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation. The provisions of the ordinance were enumerated, including elements of an agreement for the sale of land greater than 150 acres, specific procedures for the potential sale of the Municipal Golf Course West, details of the process for Council's consideration of the purchase contracts, and the required form contract variables. Mr. Brown then briefly described the resolution that addresses the pre-selection deposit agreement. The public hearing was opened. Mitch Kirschner, attorney for Lennar, asked for consideration of including an outside by which the City would adopt the approving ordinance to sell the golf course. Mr. Brown acknowledged that such language could be crafted and suggested December 31 as the date. The City Attorney provided further information. Members weighed in and, in general, agreed the date should be April 2. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Brown then read into the record language to be inserted in Ordinance 5406 on page 7, sub-paragraph 10, end of line 6, that sets April, 2018 as the date after which, if the ordinance is not adopted, the contract with the selected purchaser is no longer binding and enforceable. The City Attorney suggested further language. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5406 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Resolution No. 116-2017. The City Attorney provided information on the selection deposits and refunds of same. Council Member Singer asked about the three finalists and the time table for the deposits, to which Mr. Brown responded. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Mr. Brown reviewed the schedule going forward. Mayor Haynie inquired as to the cone of silence. The City Attorney confirmed that it remains in effect.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute an amendment to the Agreement for Services with AshBritt, Inc.; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mike Woika, Assistant City Manager, gave a brief explanation of the resolution. He provided background information on the pre-positioned contract with Ashbritt, noting that the various hurricanes caused a unique situation with many cities issuing emergency contracts paying much higher rates. This resolution will raise the rate Boca pays so that we can keep the contractors here, picking up debris. It was noted that the up-charge to this higher rate may not be eligible for reimbursed by FEMA. Mr. Ahnell provided further information. Members offered comments in support of the resolution, noting that the debris needs to be picked up in the interests of safety. Comments were made about price gouging. Discussion ensued. Dan Grippo provided information on the current debris pick up. Mr. Ahnell elaborated. Mr. Woika also provided further information. Further discussion followed regarding FEMA. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 126-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Mayor Haynie opened the public hearing. Ellyn Okrent, CEO of Florence Fuller Child Development and the Children's Museum, requested additional funds to help cover roof damage on the Rickards Building due to Hurricane Irma. She responded to questions about the insurance implications and thanked the City for their support. Kari Oeltjen, Chief Development Officer of Habitat for Humanity, requested non-profit funding that will allow Habitat to continue to enhance their sustainability program. Dick Schmidt, Chairman of the Boca Raton Golf Charities, updated Council on the funding of the Boca Raton Regional Hospital Championship Golf Tournament, formerly the Allianz. Since speaking at the September 25 Workshop Meeting, Mr. Schmidt said that $500,000 had been secured from another source, so the request of the City was $656,500 for a one year commitment. He then provided further information on the benefits of a title sponsorship package. Edward Carbone, Tournament Director, echoed Mr. Schmidt's comments. They both responded to questions from Council members. Discussion ensued. City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information regarding advertising spots. Lisa McDulin, Director for Advancement at Place of Hope, requested non-profit funding for their programs. Sarah Pearson, Executive Vice President of the Boca Raton Chamber of Commerce, referencing previous comments, noted that the Chamber has supported the golf tournament in the past and supports keeping the event in Boca Raton.

units.text: Referring to Exhibit 3, the Mayor and Council members reviewed their requests for other funding changes. Council Member O'Rourke requested funding for a full time Resiliency/Sustainability Officer. Members discussed and offered their opinions. In response to questions, Mr. Ahnell provided information on contractors for canal cleaning, the overlap of an Innovation Officer and a Sustainability Officer, and the cost of a full time position. Members made final comments and, in general, agreed to inclusion of the Sustainability Officer position. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to amend the budget to include approximately $120,000 to fund a full time Resiliency/Sustainability Officer position. Deputy Mayor Rodgers inquired about the possibility of funding the position with a grant. The City Manager noted that this could be researched. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Weinroth requested $100,000 to assist in reconstruction of Tri-County Animal Rescue building destroyed by Hurricane Irma; Mayor Haynie requested $104,500. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to amend the budget to include $104,500 for reconstruction of the Tri-County Animal Rescue building. Responding to Council Member Singer's question, Sharon DiPietro, Tri County Animal Rescue, shared information regarding insurance coverage on the destroyed building. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Weinroth requested $180,000 in funding for reconstruction of the Children's Museum cottage damaged by Hurricane Irma and noted that it is a City building. Discussion ensued on the amount of funding and the possibility of FEMA reimbursement. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to amend the budget to include $100,000 in funding for the Children's Museum for building renovation. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Weinroth requested an additional $50,000 in funding for the Festival of the Arts. Mr. Weinroth noted the importance of the Festival to the City. Discussion ensued. Charles Siemon, Festival of the Arts Chair, responded to questions about the increase in Festival expenses. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to amend the budget to include an additional $50,000 in funding for the Festival of the Arts. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Weinroth requested one-time economic development funding of $656,000 for the Boca Raton Regional Hospital Championship Golf Tournament (f/k/a the Allianz Championship) to ensure that this event remained in Boca Raton. Mayor Haynie suggested $500,000 in light of the promise of funding from the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District and in the hope that the County would participate in funding as well. Discussion ensued. It was suggested to seek other funding partners and to leverage this contribution as best as possible. The City Manager noted that this funding will come back to the Council in a contract for approval. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances: amending Section 28-1326 to prohibit medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities in all zoning districts in the City, and clarifying the impact of a list of prohibited uses on authorized uses within zoning districts: amending Section 28-2 to provide a definition for medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facility; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-16-03) Ordinance No. 5415 Mayor Haynie noted that this is the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with background information on the past actions of the State, the City and the County. The proposed Code amendment was reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board did not recommend approval; Mr. Schaad detailed the objections of Board members. He noted that this ordinance does not prohibit anyone from obtaining medical marijuana through a licensed prescriber and then noted what other cities have done. The public hearing was opened. Eric Sevell, noting that he was the son of a Planning and Zoning Board member, stated his opposition to the ordinance. He gave a brief PowerPoint presentation reviewing the actions taken to date, making his case for allowing marijuana dispensaries. He cited studies that support allowing dispensaries and provided handouts of same. Cristina Escalante agreed with Mr. Sevell. She stated her support for having easy access to marijuana dispensaries. Seeing no o ne else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Haynie asked the City Attorney if the City has the power to regulate cameras, lighting and other security measures at dispensaries as suggested by Mr. Sevell. The City Attorney stated that the legislative framework is limited and this is an area of uncertainty. She noted that the ordinance addresses a zoning issue, not an assessment of the value of medical marijuana. Members asked further questions, to which Ms. Frieser responded, and made further comments. Mayor Haynie then announced the date of the second public Hearing Ordinance No. 5416 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 23 "Planning and Development", Code of Ordinances, relating to sidewalks and bikeways; amending Section 23-161 to modify and clarify the definitions, delete the definition for "pathway", and add a definition of "owner"; amending Section 23-162 to specify when sidewalks are required and their widths and excluding sidewalks on Yamato Road between Military Trail and Saint Andrews Boulevard from the 8 feet width requirement; amending Section 23-161(d), 23-162(2)(e), 23-162(3), 23-162(4), 23-163(1), 23-163(3), 23-164( 1) and 23-165 to replace "developer" with "owner", replace "touring courses" with "existing bikeways", and replace "obstructions" with "objects"; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-08) Ordinance No. 5416 Jim Bell, Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He provided background information on the genesis of this ordinance, and then reviewed the proposed amendment and the cross references in various sections of Chapter 23. Mr. Bell noted that the amendment is consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan, and then reviewed the staff analysis of the ordinance. The Planning & Zoning Board did not recommend approval. The Board members concerns and recommendations were detailed. Despite the Board's position, staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to Council members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Members commented and expressed their opinions. Staff responded to further questions. Extensive discussion ensued. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, stated that staff would soon bring forward a discussion of complete streets, which was a part of the initial discussion of the sidewalk size, and would offer a comprehensive solution to these issues. Members made further comments and further discussion ensued. The City Attorney confirmed that no Council member has a potential conflict due to their membership in a church or synagogue. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to postpone Ordinance No. 5416. Members made final comments and asked further questions. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton repealing Chapter 21, Code of Ordinances, "Flood Damage Prevention and Protection," in its entirety; adopting a new Chapter 21, Code of Ordinances, entitled "Flood Damage Prevention and Floodplain Management"; providing for definitions, applicability, and flood hazard areas; designating the City Manager as the Floodplain Administrator and providing duties and powers; providing for permit requirements and inspections; providing procedures for variances and appeals; affirming and providing for floodplain management in areas annexed pursuant to Ordinance Nos. 4717, 4718, 4719, 4734, 4795, and 4796; adopting regulations consistent with the 2014 Florida Building Code; adopting the Federal Emergency Management Agency's Flood Insurance Rate Maps and the Flood Insurance Study; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-05) Ordinance No. 5418 Keith Carney, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the purpose of the ordinance and then noted that a revised version of ordinance had been provided to the Council, as had the report of the Community Assistance Visit. Details of the new Code Chapter 21 were provided. It was noted that new FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps were included in the ordinance. Mr. Carney then provided information regarding the Community Rating System, an important aspect of floodplain management. Benefits of the ordinance were summarized and it was noted that the ordinance is consistent with the Comp Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended adoption. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Carney responded to questions from Council members. The City Attorney confirmed the intent of certain wording in the ordinance with regard to the role of the Environmental Advisory Board. The public hearing was opened. Jo-Ann Landon inquired as to the effect of removal of environmentally sensitive vegetation, to which Mr. Carney responded. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. In response to a question, Mr. Carney provided further information on the Community Rating System. The City Attorney clarified a section of the ordinance, suggesting inclusion of language on p. 25, sub­ paragraph h, line 7, addressing alteration of sand dunes and mangrove stands. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to adjourn Ordinance No. 5418 as revised and amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a Universal Conditional Amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of 2.03 acres, more or less, from Commercial (C) to Residential High (RH), located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard and 910 East Palmetto Park Road; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06/SC) Ordinance No. 5413 Ordinance No. 5414 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a Universal Conditional Rezoning, pursuant to Article VI, Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances, of property consisting of 2.03 acres, more or less, from the Community Business (B-2) zoning district to the Multi­ Family Residential (R-5-A) zoning district and of property consisting of 1.49 acres, more or less, from the Multi-Family (R-4) zoning district to the Multi-Family Residential (R-5-A) zoning district, located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard, 155 South Ocean Boulevard and 910 East Palmetto Park Road; providing for the appropriate revisions to the Zoning District Map: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06/ZC) Ordinance No. 5414 Resolution No. 119-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan, pursuant to a Universal Condition (UC) request, to construct a seven (7) story multi-family residential condominium building, approximately 324,400 square feet with 70 units, with a technical deviation from Section 23-190(j), Code of Ordinances, to allow for a reduction in inbound reservoir distance to a gated entrance for a residential development located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard, 155 South Ocean Boulevard and 910 East Palmetto Park Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06/SPA) Resolution No. 119-2017 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Items A., B., and C. would be conducted contemporaneously. A separate vote would be taken on each ordinance and resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the components of the petitioner's request. The location, future land use and zoning of the property were provided. Ms. Rahman provided details of staff's analysis of the project for consistency, compatibility and concurrency with the Comprehensive Plan, with particular emphasis on the property's location in a coastal high hazard area and flood zone. She then reviewed the rezoning, including the traffic analysis. The site plan was then described, including renderings and building elevations. The requested technical deviation for a reduction in reservoir length was supported by the City's Traffic Engineer. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with recommendations, which, it was noted, were included in the site plan by the developer. Staff recommended approval of the all petitions. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to a number of questions from Council members. In response to a question, Maria Tejara, City Traffic Engineer, emphasized that there was no objection to the reservoir length as the number of units does not justify the reservoir length required by City Code. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided information on the condition regarding hurricane evacuation. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the project. The application was reviewed. The differences in the original and revised proposals were pointed out, emphasizing the amount of green space. Jorge Garcia, project architect, narrated a video illustrating the project. Both Ms. Miskel and Mr. Garcia noted that they had worked with the neighbors to improve the project. Members asked a number of questions regarding landscaping, public access areas, setbacks, and public art. John Donaldson, JMD Engineering, responded to questions about hurricane evacuation times and trip generation analysis. Mark Simmons, Riviera Civic Association, noted the Association's support of the project. Carrie McGurk, vice president of the Marbella Condominium board, provided information on the relationship with the Ocean Palm developers. She requested that a decision be postponed until Marbella residents have returned and have an opportunity to voice their concerns. She expressed a number of her own concerns. Glenn Gromann offered support of the project, addressed the previous speaker's comments, and advocated approval of the project. No one else came forward to speak. Bonnie Miske! provided rebuttal, in particular of the comments made regarding the Marbella. She responded to a question about the shadow study. Jorge Garcia also addressed the Marbella comments. The public was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5413. Mayor Haynie noted that the ordinance required four votes for adoption. Members made final comments, offering their support for the project. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Ordinance No. 5414. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. The City Attorney confirmed that the conditions recommended by Planning and Zoning Board were included in the site plan and the resolution. Ms. Frieser then recommended language for two new conditions requested by Council member O'Rourke related to electric vehicle charging stations (page 9, subsection c, new viii) and location and approval of public art (page 12, subsection 6, new e). Mayor Haynie then called for a motion with these two conditions and two directives to staff regarding signage. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 119-2017 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; amending Section 28-1326 to prohibit medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities in all zoning districts in the City, and clarifying the impact of a list of prohibited uses on authorized uses within zoning districts; amending Section 28-2 to provide a definition for medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facility; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-03) Ordinance No. 5415 Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, recapped the presentation he made at the first public hearing on the ordinance. He noted the Planning and Zoning Board recommendation to deny passage of the ordinance. Staff recommends approval. Mr. Schaad then responded to a number of questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann offered his opinion regarding medical marijuana and problems with dispensaries. He stated his support of passage of the ordinance. Eric Sevell shared comments in response to an article he posted. He stated his opposition to the ordinance, which he claimed would restrict access to medical marijuana. Susan Pernell offered her support of medical marijuana and stated her opposition to the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Weinroth stated his position, noting that he will not support the ordinance. Council Member O'Rourke offered her opinion, noting that the people had voted in favor of medical marijuana and she would abide by that vote. Mr. Schaad responded to further questions from Council members. The City Attorney commented on the State Statute that addresses the regulation of medical marijuana dispensing facilities. She also responded to a number of questions. Members commented further and asked further questions. Council Member Singer stated his concerns and lamented the limited choices available. Deputy Mayor Rodgers proposed amendments to include the clarification of the Statute as a legislative priority and to revisit the ban in one year. Council Member O'Rourke asked about the timing of further clarification from the State. The City Attorney provided information. Ms. O'Rourke suggested that the ordinance be tabled. Council Member Weinroth noted that tabling the ordinance could stop any future ban. The City Attorney provided clarification. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Ordinance No. 5415 as amended by Mr. Rodgers. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no.

units.text: Resolution No. 130-2017 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton concluding the selection procedures specified in Section 3 of Ordinance No. 5406 in connection with the potential sale of the City's Municipal Golf Course West; selecting a purchaser of the City's Municipal Golf Course West and determining that selection to be in the best interests of the City; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date Memo Resolution No. 130-2017 Deputy City Manager George Brown gave the PowerPoint presentation on the potential sale of the City's western golf course. He noted that should a purchaser be selected and Resolution No. 130-2017 be adopted, then Ordinance No. 5410 authorizing the sale would be introduced. Background information on the process to date was reviewed, noting that all steps to date had been completed by the two finalists, GL Acquisitions Corporation (GL Homes) and Lennar Homes, LLC (Lennar). The procedures to be followed at the public hearing were also reviewed. Details of both offers to purchase were provided, including purchase price, deposits and refunds, remedies, title, inspection, insurance, environmental remediation, development approvals, assignment, current golf course operations and eminent domain. Each offer was then summarized. Finally, the fiscal impact of each offer was discussed. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown responded to questions. The City Attorney also provided responses. The public hearing was opened. As determined by a random drawing, GL Homes was the initial presenter. Larry Portnoy, Vice President, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He began with the justification for the decrease in purchase price and then provided a detailed comparison of the GL Homes and Lennar offers, noting the large number of contingencies in the Lennar contract. In closing, he contended that his company's offer was superior. Upon concluding, Mr. Portnoy responded to Council members' questions. Bruce Grundt, Vice President with Lennar, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of Lennar's offer. He noted that Lennar is a local company and had worked with City in the past on the land for the Downtown Library. He then reviewed details of Lennar's offer. Upon concluding, he responded to Council members' questions. Discussion of several issues ensued. As determined by a random drawing, Lennar was the first to offer a rebuttal. Bruce Grundt compared the price offers and contended that the City would be better off working with Lennar. In rebuttal for GL Homes, Senior Vice President Alan Fant explained the reasons for the reduced price offer, comparing the two offers with regard to risk and contingencies and making the case that the GL offer is superior. He proffered that GL would increase their offer to a $65 million minimum with the terms and conditions of the Lennar contract. Larry Portnoy responded to some of Mr. Grundt's comments during his rebuttal. Seeing no one else came forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council members began discussion and deliberation. At this time, Mayor Haynie noted that it was nearing 11 pm and a motion was needed to continue the meeting beyond that time. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to extend the meeting beyond 11 :00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Members continued with comments, stating their positions and posing a number of questions to the finalists and staff. The City Attorney provided an explanation of the contract process thus far and suggested to continue with the next step during which the finalists can adjust their offers. Mr. Brown and Ms. Frieser responded to further questions. Members continued to comment. The finalists were asked to present their best offer after a recess. The meeting went into recess at approximately 11: 15 pm. The meeting reconvened at approximately 11:30 pm. Mr. Brown received one price increase form from GL Homes raising the contract purchase price to $65 million and decreasing the non-refundable deposit amount. Mr. Portnoy provided clarification. The City Attorney noted that minor revisions would need to be made to the form contract. Council members offered comments in response to the amended offer. In response to several comments, Mr. Fant stated that the offer price was firm, but the non-refundable deposit could be increased to $2 million. The price increase form was then amended. Further discussion ensued. Mr. Fant reiterated that the $65 million offer price was final. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 130-2017 selecting GL Acquisitions Corporation as purchaser with the price amendment reflected on the price increase form. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Conditional Use approval pursuant to Section 28-1098(9), Code of Ordinances, to allow a family resource center (career training and counseling facility), in the General Industrial (M-2) zoning district for the property located at 1595 NW 1st Court; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-17-02) Resolution No. 125-2017 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the request and identified the location and zoning of the property and provided background information, including that a building permit for the facility had been issued by the City in error. Mr. Schaad then reviewed the reasons for the determination that the requested use would adversely affect the surrounding area. The applicant's justifications for the requested use of the building as a career training and counseling facility were listed. Mr. Schaad then detailed the numerous problems currently created by the existing facility, most notably parking, that would be exacerbated by approval of the application. The traffic analysis was provided and the actions of the Planning and Zoning Board were reviewed. Staff recommended denial of the request. Mr. Schaad noted that if Council decided to approve the conditional use, there were conditions in the resolution addressing the issues identified by staff. Upon concluding, he responded to Council members' questions, as did Transportation Planning Engineer Quan Yuan. Discussion of a number of issues ensued. The public hearing was opened. Christina Bilenki, Dunay Miske! Backman, on behalf of Boca Helping Hands, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Details of the services and programs of Boca Helping Hands were provided. It was noted that Boca Helping Hands has opened locations in West Boca Raton and Boynton Beach to serve residents in those areas. Information was provided on the job training programs offered at the main facility. It was noted that the building in question would provide an environment more conducive to learning for clients participating in the job training programs. Ms. Bilenki then reviewed the site plan, noting that the recommendations of the Planning and Zoning Board had been incorporated in same. She then responded to a number of assertions made in the City staff presentation, including the parking issue. In conclusion, she noted that Boca Helping Hands is working to continue to address these issues. She then introduced Gary Peters, Board President, who talked about the work of Boca Helping Hands and the numerous people who volunteer there. He requested approval of the application, and then responded to Council members' questions. Jack Webb, representing the family charitable trust that donated the building in question, offered support of the Boca Helping Hands and the job training programs that would take place in the facility. Bill Trinka commented on the conditional use approval initially granted to Boca Helping Hands. He presented a number of pictures illustrating the problems he asserts are caused by Boca Helping Hands that impact his neighboring property, including parking, loitering, and garbage. Susan Whiting supported the need for training people and also the need for parking safety. She asked that the outstanding issues be addressed before granting this request. Dr. Charles Tate offered support of Boca Helping Hands and the irreplaceable service it provides. He noted that the problems detailed are only getting worse because so many people need these services. Ms. Bilenki addressed the ways in which the problems detailed by the neighbors were being handled. Council Member O'Rourke asked for specifics, to which Ms. Bilenki responded. In response to Council Member Weinroth, Mr. Peters acknowledged that a condition to have personnel police the area was acceptable, and then responded to further questions. Deputy Mayor Rodgers asked that a condition be included to place garbage receptacles outside. Council Member Singer asked a number of questions about parking and other topics, to which Mr. Peters and Ms. Bilenki responded. During cross examination, Bill Trinka refuted a number of the previous comments. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 125-2017. Discussion of amendments and further conditions ensued. The City Attorney read language into the record addressing the reduction of disposable trash (new condition 4); supervision of pedestrian and vehicular traffic and loitering from 10 am to 1 pm (new condition 5); shared parking for the two Boca Helping Hands sites; and the location of employee and volunteer parking (replacement conditions 2). Some discussion followed. Council Member Singer suggested a recess. The meeting went into recess at approximately 8:05 pm. The meeting was reconvened at approximately 8: 13 pm. The City Attorney read language into the record revised language for replacement condition 2. The applicant acknowledged that the condition was acceptable. Mayor Haynie summarized the amendments as new conditions 4 and 5 and a revised replacement condition 2. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to amend Resolution No. 125-2017 as stated. Motion carried 4 to 1 on a voice vote; Council Member O'Rourke opposed. Members offered final comments, stating their opinions. On the main motion to approve Resolution No. 125-2017 as amended; motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. Ji. Resolution No. 136-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Conditional Use approval to provide for a restaurant with a customer service area in excess of 1.000 square feet in the Motel-Business {R­ B-1) zoning district. together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655. Code of Ordinances. to provide for a reduction in the number of required parking spaces and affirming a reduction in parking based on a shared parking study, for the property located at 1279-1401 West Palmetto Park Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-16-03) Resolution No. 136-2017 Drawings The Mayor noted that the same quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The site location and zoning were provided, as was the location of the cafe bay. Details of the conditional use were reviewed. The technical deviation for shared parking was explained, noting staff's support of the request. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimous approval was noted. Staff recommends approval of the conditional use. Mr. Schaad then responded to several questions. The public hearing was opened. Heather Allen, Dunay Miskel Backman, presented on behalf of the applicant, briefly reviewing the parking analysis. Ms. Allen thanked Mr, Schaad for his presentation and then made herself available for questions. Seeing no one come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 136-2017. Mayor Haynie asked if petitions such as this were good reasons for streamlining. Mr. Schaad agreed Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 138-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to a Conditional Use approval (Resolution No. 111-84, as amended) to reduce the amount of open space from approximately 39 percent to 35 percent to accommodate 18 additional parking spaces in the R-1-D Single Family Residential zoning district, for the St. Mark Greek Orthodox Church located at 2100 West Yamato Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-11-03R 1) Resolution No. 138-2017 Drawings The Mayor again noted that the same quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with a summary of the application. The location and zoning of the property were provided. The requested modification to the conditional use for additional parking spaces and a modification of the parking area was reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the petition. Staff also recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to members' questions. Mr. Schaad addressed a question about streamlining for situations such as this one. The public hearing was opened. Dale Meaux made brief remarks in support of the request and then made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council members offered final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 138-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 135-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Third Amendment to the Amended and Restated Campus Development Agreement between the Florida Atlantic University Board of Trustees and the City of Boca Raton; extending the term for two years ending December 31, 2019; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 135-2017 Mayor Haynie stated that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. Referring to a revised resolution and Third Amendment distributed to Council, he explained that, pursuant to Florida Statute, the term of the Campus Development Agreement (CDA) could be no longer than ten years, necessitating a revised Third Amendment end date of November 24, 2019. The FAU Campus Master Plan was then reviewed, as was the CDA. Mr. Brown stated that all fair share payments would continue and no other changes were made to the agreement. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown responded to Council members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Azita Dashtaki Dotiwala stated that FAU would be starting the process to update their Master Plan in the very near future. She then responded to questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Haynie announced the November 28, 2107 date of the second public hearing. !;L Ordinance No. 5410 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the sale of a parcel of City-owned land consisting of approximately 188.158 acres and located at 8111 Golf Course Road, Palm Beach County (known as the City's Municipal Golf Course West), pursuant to Section 13-74, Code of Ordinances, and the specific provisions and procedures of Ordinance No. 5406; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5410 George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with a review of the potential sale process to date, including Council's selection of G.L. Acquisitions Corporation (GL Homes) as purchaser of the golf course. There followed an explanation of revisions made to Exhibits A and C-1 of the purchase contract as of November 13, 2017. Exhibit A included an updated legal description and an increase in the total acreage, while Exhibit C-1 included a modification to the title and survey paragraph. Details of the contract were provided. In conclusion, Mr. Brown summarized the contract, noted the fiscal impact and the recommendation of staff to approve the ordinance. He then responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Larry Portnoy, GL Homes, made himself available for questions. Dr. Charles Tate asked that Council reconsider the sale of the Municipal Golf Course and offered comments in support of the Course. Zoe Delaney spoke in opposition to the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5410 as amended. The City Attorney reviewed the revisions to the exhibits to the ordinance. Members made final comments. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, relating to off-street parking provisions for electric vehicles; amending Section 28-1646 to provide for definitions related to electric vehicles; amending Sections 28-1648, 28-1649, 28-1650, 28-1653, and 28-1655 to provide for electric vehicle off-street parking provisions for multifamily residential, commercial, and industrial uses; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-03) Ordinance No. 5420 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The proposed code amendment was reviewed. Topics included, but were not limited to, electric vehicle (EV) and related definitions, requirements for charging stations when altering or redeveloping projects, EV parking space and charging station design standards, and off-street parking space provisions. Ms. Allen then explained the staff analysis of the proposed amendment. It was noted that Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval, as does staff. As a proponent of this ordinance, Council Member Weinroth addressed the increase in electric vehicles, showing a short video, followed by strong support of the ordinance. Members then posed numerous questions to staff. Lengthy discussion of provisions of the ordinance, principally the requirements to include EV parking spaces and charging stations for new or redeveloped structures, ensued. The public hearing was opened. Charlie Helton commented on the free use of City Hall charging stations, the City's parking problems and wasteful spending. Gene Folden gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the ordinance. James Hendrey suggested that there should be some changes to the ordinance so as not to impact the commercial community. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members commented at length, offering their opinions, expressing hesitancy, and suggesting the ordinance be refined and brought back at a later date. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to postpone Ordinance No. 5420; Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer voting yes; Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting no. Ordinance No. 5421 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, "Definitions," to modify the definition of "Established Grade" for the purpose of changing the calculation for determining "height of a building" and "established grade:" and repealing Section 28-62, Code of Ordinances, "Variances for Height of Single-Family Residences:" providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17- Qfil Ordinance No. 5421 Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation, briefly summarizing the proposed ordinance and noting that it was related to Ordinance 5422 which addresses changes to the Building Code. The proposed definition of established grade and height of structure were reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff also recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5421. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. In light of the hour, it was suggested to allow Public Requests at this time. There was no objection.

units.text: Gene Folden addressed previous comments regarding electric vehicle charging stations. Nancy Hendrey shared her concerns regarding the ethics discussion at yesterday's CRA meeting. Chris Scarpa commented on the number of students at Boca Raton High School, overcrowding and the need for a new high school. Mayor Haynie and Council Member O'Rourke commented. Jo-Ann Landon commented on residential developments in the City and the effect of such development. Kevin Wrenne, Executive Director of Banyan Place, addressed the ordinance requiring that assisted living facilities have generators. He asked that the introduction of the ordinance be postponed. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to extend the meeting beyond 11 :00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Tom Dowell, Administrator of Advent Square, continued his comments and advocated that the ordinance requiring that assisted living facilities have generators be postponed. Charlie Helton commented on the ordinances regarding electric vehicle charging stations and the Yamato Villas development.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5422 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 19 "Buildings and Building Regulations," Code of Ordinances: adopting local amendments to the Florida Building Code for the purposes of participating in the National Flood Insurance Program's Community Rating System; establishing the minimum elevation requirement for residential buildings and structures in flood hazard areas and non-flood hazard areas; establishing the minimum elevation requirement for commercial and multifamily buildings and structures in flood hazard areas and non-flood hazard areas: establishing elevation criteria related to the minimum elevation requirement for both residential and commercial buildings and structures in all flood zone areas; amending the definition of "substantial improvement" to require accumulation of costs of improvements and repairs of buildings, based on issued building permits, over a 3-year period for buildings and structures in flood hazard areas; deleting Section 19-32 relating to permit exemptions for single-family dwellings; amending Section19-67 relating to permit exemptions: amending Section 19-107 relating to construction documents to require additional plans and documents for building permits of residential and commercial buildings and structures in all flood zone areas; amending Section 19-139 relating to building permit valuations; and amending Sections 19-225 and 19-226 regarding variances relating to elevation requirements and flood plain management, and to marine structures and drainage, and clarifying the variance review responsibilities of the Builders' Board of Adjustment and Appeals; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-07) Ordinance No. 5422 John Cosmo, Building Official, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Cosmo began with brief background information and then reviewed the proposed Code amendments. He stated that the proposal was consistent with City's Comprehensive Plan, that the Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval, and that staff recommended approval as well. He then made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5422. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 141-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Fred J. and Jane L. Hengel, for a settlement and reduction of seven (7) Code Enforcement liens imposed against property located at 7200 North Dixie Highway; providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing an effective date Resolution No. 141-2017 Doug Sheedy, Code Compliance Manager, gave the presentation, noting that staff does not support the requested lien reduction. He provided information of the Code violations and seven liens dating back to 1998, as well as the current situation. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Mr. Sheedy responded to questions regarding the dates of the liens. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 141-2017 to deny the request for lien reduction. Council Member Singer made several suggestions for notice that might forestall such problems in the future. There was a brief discussion of the form of the resolution. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Council Member O'Rourke asked about Italian Fest and the possible closure of Federal Highway. Deputy Mayor Rodgers added his comments regarding Downtown events. Council Member Singer also commented on Italian Fest. Council Member Weinroth commented on having Public Requests earlier in the agenda when meetings run long. He then suggested that outside help be engaged to address the ethical questions discussed at the CRA meeting. Members weighed in. It was verified that staff was working on the suggestions made yesterday regarding best practices to address some of members' concerns. Lengthy discussion ensued regarding the current situation and what the next steps should be to address any future ethics situations that may be faced by Council members. In general, it was agreed to have staff research possible people with the experience and knowledge to conduct an ethics workshop for Council. Direction was also given to the City Manager to provide the Ethics Commission with the documents sent to the Palm Beach Post and ask that the Commission review same and provide clarification of their opinion. Mayor Haynie wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving.

units.text: October 19, 2017 Minutes Council Member O'Rourke requested that Resolution 158-2017, item 9.1., be removed from the Consent Agenda . Deputy Mayor Rodgers asked to remove Resolution 157-2017, item 9.H. Mayor Haynie noted that both resolutions would be considered immediately following the Consent Agenda. She then provided an opportunity for public input on any remaining Consent Agenda items. No one came forward to speak. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve the Consent Agenda as amended.
