units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering tentative plat approval for the proposed Yamato Villas Plat (a replat of all, or portions of, Lots 1 through 1O of Block 3 of the University Heights Plat), subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-03/SUB) Resolution No. 150-2017 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Items A., B., C., D., and E. would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related. A separate vote would be taken on each ordinance and resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation on the five petitions for Yamato Villas. The location and zoning of the property were provided. The site plan was reviewed; details were provided . Topics included, but were not limited to, site access, driveway length, parking, garages, various conditions of the development, elevations, and the tentative plat. The requested modifications to development parameters were listed . The traffic analysis was reviewed. The requested technical deviation for off-street vehicular circulation was explained. The proposed future land use change and rezoning were reviewed. The project's consistency with the Comprehensive Plan was reviewed . The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of all components of the application. Ms. Eassa pointed out the revision to the site plan resolution that was the result of an updated School Capacity Available Determination (SCAD) letter including a contribution to the School District. Staff recommended approval of the petition, subject to the conditions in the ordinances and resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to Council members' questions, as did Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director. Yajaira Moleiro, City Traffic Engineer, also responded to questions about trip generation. The public hearing was opened. Heather Allen, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the petition . She reviewed the application requests and then provided a history of the property and the type of development appropriate for the location. Details were provided on the land use change and rezoning. Ms. Allen then introduced the project architect, Juan Caycedo, who reviewed the design of the project, in particular the townhouse pods. Ms. Allen then detailed the requested technical deviation to allow on-street circulation and a one-way drive aisle. Other topics included open space and landscape buffers. In conclusion, Ms. Allen advocated approval and noted that the petitioner agreed to the contribution to the School District. Both Ms. Allen and Mr. Caycedo then responded to Council members' questions, as did staff. Mike Rentler provided copies of a petition signed by a number of neighbors and expressed opposition to the project. Citing a number of issues, Carol Rice also expressed opposition to the project. JoAnne Weise expressed her concerns and opposition to the project. Charlie Helton commented on the project, noting his concern should this property being developed as a commercial site and his support of keeping this a residential project. During rebuttal, JoAnn Weise addressed previous comments regarding commercial development. Ms. Allen then provided brief comments and then responded to further questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed . At the request of Council members, Deputy City Manager George Brown provided information on previous commercial proposals for the property and the impact of commercial development. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Ordinance No. 5428. Members commented, offering their thoughts and opinions. At Council Member Singer's request, the City Attorney read draft language to be added to a condition in the site plan resolution that would require the School District's SCAD voluntary contribution be spent on schools in Boca Raton. Lengthy discussion ensued on a number of issues, in particular changing the land use. The City Attorney reminded all that the site plan is an essential component of the Comp Plan amendment; therefore the Comp Plan amendment should not be approved if the site plan is not acceptable. Discussion continued. At the request of the Mayor, Juan Caycedo addressed the design of the townhouses and the number of parking spaces. Ms. Allen also responded to questions. Discussion continued, in particular with regard to school overcrowding and parking . It was suggested to continue the matter and also suggested that a School Board representative be invited to attend a future meeting to discuss the Board's plans for schools in Boca. In general, members agreed to invite a School Board representative to a future meeting and that a continuation of the matter was best. Deputy Rodgers withdrew his motion. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to continue Ordinance No. 5428 to January 23, 2018. In response to a question, the City Attorney provided information on concurrency with regard to school capacity and roadway infrastructure and the Council's ability to deny applications. Discussion followed. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to continue Ordinance No. 5429 to January 23, 2018 . Motion carried unanimously. units.full: Resolution No. 150-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering tentative plat approval for the proposed Yamato Villas Plat (a replat of all, or portions of, Lots 1 through 1O of Block 3 of the University Heights Plat), subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-03/SUB) Resolution No. 150-2017 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Items A., B., C., D., and E. would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related. A separate vote would be taken on each ordinance and resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation on the five petitions for Yamato Villas. The location and zoning of the property were provided. The site plan was reviewed; details were provided . Topics included, but were not limited to, site access, driveway length, parking, garages, various conditions of the development, elevations, and the tentative plat. The requested modifications to development parameters were listed . The traffic analysis was reviewed. The requested technical deviation for off-street vehicular circulation was explained. The proposed future land use change and rezoning were reviewed. The project's consistency with the Comprehensive Plan was reviewed . The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of all components of the application. Ms. Eassa pointed out the revision to the site plan resolution that was the result of an updated School Capacity Available Determination (SCAD) letter including a contribution to the School District. Staff recommended approval of the petition, subject to the conditions in the ordinances and resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to Council members' questions, as did Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director. Yajaira Moleiro, City Traffic Engineer, also responded to questions about trip generation. The public hearing was opened. Heather Allen, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the petition . She reviewed the application requests and then provided a history of the property and the type of development appropriate for the location. Details were provided on the land use change and rezoning. Ms. Allen then introduced the project architect, Juan Caycedo, who reviewed the design of the project, in particular the townhouse pods. Ms. Allen then detailed the requested technical deviation to allow on-street circulation and a one-way drive aisle. Other topics included open space and landscape buffers. In conclusion, Ms. Allen advocated approval and noted that the petitioner agreed to the contribution to the School District. Both Ms. Allen and Mr. Caycedo then responded to Council members' questions, as did staff. Mike Rentler provided copies of a petition signed by a number of neighbors and expressed opposition to the project. Citing a number of issues, Carol Rice also expressed opposition to the project. JoAnne Weise expressed her concerns and opposition to the project. Charlie Helton commented on the project, noting his concern should this property being developed as a commercial site and his support of keeping this a residential project. During rebuttal, JoAnn Weise addressed previous comments regarding commercial development. Ms. Allen then provided brief comments and then responded to further questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed . At the request of Council members, Deputy City Manager George Brown provided information on previous commercial proposals for the property and the impact of commercial development. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Ordinance No. 5428. Members commented, offering their thoughts and opinions. At Council Member Singer's request, the City Attorney read draft language to be added to a condition in the site plan resolution that would require the School District's SCAD voluntary contribution be spent on schools in Boca Raton. Lengthy discussion ensued on a number of issues, in particular changing the land use. The City Attorney reminded all that the site plan is an essential component of the Comp Plan amendment; therefore the Comp Plan amendment should not be approved if the site plan is not acceptable. Discussion continued. At the request of the Mayor, Juan Caycedo addressed the design of the townhouses and the number of parking spaces. Ms. Allen also responded to questions. Discussion continued, in particular with regard to school overcrowding and parking . It was suggested to continue the matter and also suggested that a School Board representative be invited to attend a future meeting to discuss the Board's plans for schools in Boca. In general, members agreed to invite a School Board representative to a future meeting and that a continuation of the matter was best. Deputy Rodgers withdrew his motion. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to continue Ordinance No. 5428 to January 23, 2018. In response to a question, the City Attorney provided information on concurrency with regard to school capacity and roadway infrastructure and the Council's ability to deny applications. Discussion followed. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. units.text: August 17, 2017 October 5, 2017 October 19, 2017 Minutes At the request of Council Member Weinroth, the City Manager provided information on Resolution 166-2017 regarding staffing of emergency shelters. units.text: Resolution No. 165-2017 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan to allow development of a 284-unit multifamily residential project generally located at 5201 Congress Avenue and 901 West Yamato Road: considering four (4) modifications of development parameters to eliminate required planted buffer areas in certain locations, eliminate a required buffer of a parking structure in a specific location, reduce a required building setback from Congress Avenue, and reduce a required sidewalk width: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-16-01) Resolution No. 165-2017 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Development Services Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with background information on planned mobility developments, and then provided the zoning, land use, size and current status of the subject site. Ms. Eassa then summarized the proposed project and master plan approval. Site access, parking and trip generation were detailed. It was noted that the Community Appearance Board reviewed the project but did not formally recommend approvals of elevations or landscaping as these are subject to change. Charts were provided illustrating the project's compliance with the PMD development requirements. Ms. Eassa then reviewed the four proposed modifications of the development parameters for planter and parking structure buffers, setbacks and sidewalk width, noting staffs approval of the modifications. It was also noted that the project is consistent with the PM land use. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the PMD Master Plan. Staff recommended approval as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa and Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, responded to Council members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Heather Allen, representing the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation. The property location and information were provided. Details of the proposed master plan were reviewed, noting its enhancement of the adjacent office buildings. Ms. Allen then addressed the requested PMD development parameter modifications. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen responded to questions. She also provided a handout with details of the analysis done to determine trip generation. In response to a question, the City Attorney noted that the master plan approval runs with the property. Discussion of shuttle service ensued. Glenn Gromann, speaking as a board member of the Park at Broken Sound, offered support of the project. Jo-Ann Landon expressed her concern with allowing residential units in this area of the City. Chris Scarpa asked about the school concurrency report. Mayor Haynie provided the requested information. There was no cross examination. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members offered their thoughts and opinions. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 165-2017. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5420 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, relating to off-street parking provisions for electric vehicles; amending Section 28-1646 to provide for definitions related to electric vehicles; amending Sections 28-1649, 28-1650. 28-1653, and 28-1655 to provide for electric vehicle off-street parking provisions for multifamily residential, commercial, and industrial uses; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-03) Ordinance No. 5420 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation highlighting the revisions made to the ordinance since its November 14 presentation. She then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Gene Folden gave a brief presentation in support of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann offered comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5420 as revised. Members made final comments and stated their opinions. It was noted that charging stations do have the capability to charge a fee in the future. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to questions. Motion carried on 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. Ordinance No. 5426 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, creating Section 28-1309 to require a permanent emergency generator to be located at any adult congregate living facility (ACLF), convalescent home or nursing home and allow the City Manager or designee to approve site plan modifications for the placement of such generator in certain circumstances; amending the following zoning districts to clarify the list of permitted and conditional uses with respect to ACLF's and similar or related uses: Section 28-538 (R-3-D District), Section 28-742 (R-B-1 District) and Section 28-922 (MC District); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17- M) Ordinance No. 5426 Mayor Haynie noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Susan Lesser, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with background information on the ordinance. She then reviewed the public input that had been received at the Planning and Zoning Board hearing and at the workshop held with facility operators. The proposed amendments to the ordinance were reviewed. Staffs analysis was provided, including the determination that the ordinance is consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. In conclusion, Ms. Lesser noted that staff recommended approval. She then made herself available for questions. The City Attorney provided clarification with regard to consistency of language in the ordinance. Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers noted that, due to a potential conflict, he would recuse himself and then left the dais. Assistant Fire Chief Matt Welhaf responded to questions about inspection of generators. The public hearing was opened. Kevin Wrenne, Banyan Place Executive Director, expressed his concerns with the ordinance, in particular the 100% power requirement. Mr. Wrenne then responded to Council members' questions. Glenn Gromann commented favorably on the ordinance. Tom Dowell, Advent Square Director, addressed the requirement to have 100% power provided by a generator. Taniel Shant addressed previous comments and offered support of the ordinance. Tom Thayer touted the upcoming Boat Parade and then suggested that the ordinance only apply to new facilities. Cristina Escalante commented on the ordinance and addressed the terminology used in the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members offered their comments and opinions. It was suggested that staff refine the ordinance to address some of the concerns expressed earlier. Mayor Haynie then announced the date of the second public hearing.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Code of Ordinances to establish two new zoning districts within Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Chapter 28, Zoning, Code of Ordinances, by creating a new Division 11, "City CG Commercial General," and Division 12, "City CHO Commercial High Office," which districts incorporate Palm Beach County's regulations (in effect on April 23, 2002) for the CG General Commercial District and CHO Commercial High Office District, respectively, except as specified, authorizing planned mobility development in those zoning districts and providing applicable development regulations, and specifying the maximum number of dwelling units that may be authorized pursuant to planned mobility development within those zoning districts; amending Article XVII, "Planned Development," Division 8, "Planned Mobility Development," Section 28-1854 Code of Ordinances, to clarify the aggregate maximum number of dwelling units that were previously authorized for lands pursuant to planned mobility development and to specify the maximum number for properties zoned R-B-1, POI, City CG Commercial General, and City CHO Commercial High Office: amending Section 28-301 (c), to include the new zoning districts, and Section 28-307(1 ), to specify building intensity for City CG Commercial General and City CHO Commercial High Office; providing for severability: providing for repealer, providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-16-12) Ordinance No. 5433 Council Member Weinroth introduced the ordinance. Ordinance No. 5434 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Division 3, "R-B-1 Motel-Business District" and Division 9, "POI Professional, Office and Institutional District," Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; creating sections entitled "Planned Mobility Development" for both the R-B-1 District and for the POI District to implement planned mobility development regulations for lands zoned R-B-1 and POI that are also designated "Planned Mobility" on the Future Land Use Map of the City's Comprehensive Plan; amending Article XVII, "Planned Development," Section 28-1854, "Maximum Number of Dwelling Units," Code of Ordinances, to clarify the aggregate maximum number of dwelling units that were previously authorized for lands pursuant to planned mobility development and to specify the maximum number for properties zoned R-B-1 and POI; amending Section 28-307(1) to provide the maximum building intensity for R-B-1 and POI pursuant to a planned mobility development approval; providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-16-11) Ordinance No. 5434 Deputy Mayor Rodgers introduced the ordinance.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of a decision of the Zoning Board of Adjustment (Resolution BA-17-02} denying Lot 69 Ibis Point Circle, LLC's request for a variance from Section 28-336, Code of Ordinances, with respect to the rear setback line (which setback, pursuant to a PUD authorized by Resolution No. 116-81, was previously reduced to 20 feet}, to allow a rear setback of ten (1 O} feet, in lieu of the required rear setback of twenty (20} feet, in order to construct a new single-family home on an approximately 0.63 acre single-family residential zoned property (R-1-NR-1-B/PUD) located at 4081 Ibis Point Circle; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (BA-17-02} Resolution No. 164-2017 Mayor Haynie noted that the quasi-judicial procedures reviewed earlier remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on the variance request and the Zoning Board of Adjustment (ZBOA) decision was provided. The code section related to rear and side setbacks was reviewed. The zoning, location and shape of the lot were identified. Information on the plot lines and definitions of same in relation to the proposed orientation of the house on the lot was discussed. Staff determined that the appellant's request for this variance was not unreasonable and recommended approval of the appeal of the decision of the ZBOA, thereby granting the variance. Ms. Eassa then responded to a number of Council members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Mitch Kirschner, attorney with GrayRobinson on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the side and rear setbacks of the lot. A comparison of the setback in question for the proposed and former homes on this lot was provided. Mr. Kirschner reviewed letters of support from neighboring homeowners. It was noted that the rear setback is generally assumed to be on the water. Staff's recommendation to approve the appeal and grant the variance was reviewed, Mr. Kirschner noting his agreement. He then addressed the objection letter filed by the Elsa Schack, owner of the neighboring lot. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Elsa Schack read her letter of objection into the record. She then reiterated that the petitioner should have to abide by the 20 foot rear setback requirement. Glenn Gromann contended that the variance should be granted. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. There was no cross examination. The petitioner waived rebuttal. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 164-2017 reversing the decision of the Zoning Board of Adjustment and granting the variance. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

J LECTIVE □ APPOINTIVE WHO MUST FILE FORM 88 This form is for use by any person serving at the county, city, or other local level of government on an appointed or elected board, council, commission, authority, or committee. It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a "relative" includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A "business associate" means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joint venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). · ELECTED OFFICERS: In addition to abstaining from voting in the situations described above, you must disclose the conflict: PRIOR TO THE VOTE BEING TAKEN by publicly stating to the assembly the nature of your interest in the measure on which you are abstaining from voting; and WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER THE VOTE OCCURS by completing and filing this form with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who should incorporate the form in the minutes. APPOINTED OFFICERS: Although you must abstain from voting in the situations described above, you are not prohibited by Section 112.3143 from otherwise participating in these matters. However, you must disclose the nature of the conflict before making any attempt to influence the decision, whether orally or in writing and whether made by you or at your direction. IF YOU INTEND TO MAKE ANY ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION PRIOR TO THE MEETING AT WHICH THE VOTE WILL BE TAKEN: • You must complete and file this form (before making any attempt to influence the decision) with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who will incorporate the form in the minutes. (Continued on page 2) CE FORM 8B - EFF. 11 /2013 PAGE 1 Adopted by reference in Rule 34-7.010(1)(f), FAG. APPOINTED OFFICERS (continued) • A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency. • The form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. IF YOU MAKE NO ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION EXCEPT BY DISCUSSION AT THE MEETING: • You must disclose orally the nature of your conflict in the measure before participating. • You must complete the form and file it within 15 days after the vote occurs with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who must incorporate the form in the minutes. A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency, and the form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Code of Ordinances to establish two new zoning districts within Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Chapter 28, Zoning, Code of Ordinances, by creating a new Division 11, "City CG Commercial General," and Division 12, "City CHO Commercial High Office," which districts incorporate Palm Beach County's regulations (in effect on April 23, 2002) for the CG General Commercial District and CHO Commercial High Office District, respectively, except as specified; authorizing planned mobility development in the City CG Commercial General and City CHO Commercial High Office zoning districts; providing applicable development regulations, including pre-conditions, for planned mobility development for properties zoned, R-B-1, POI, City CG Commercial General and City CHO Commercial High Office, and specifying the maximum number of dwelling units that may be authorized pursuant to planned mobility development within such zoning districts; amending Article XVII, "Planned Development," Division 8, "Planned Mobility Development," Section 28-1854 Code of Ordinances, to clarify the aggregate maximum number of dwelling units that were previously authorized for lands pursuant to planned mobility development and to specify the maximum number for properties zoned R-B-1, POI, City CG Commercial General, and City CHO Commercial High Office; amending Section 28-301 (c), to include the new zoning districts, and Section 28-307(1 ), to specify building intensity for City CG Commercial General and City CHO Commercial High Office; providing for severability; providing for repealer, providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-12) Ordinance No. 5433

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Division 3, "R-B-1 Motel-Business District" and Division 9, "POI Professional, Office and Institutional District," Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; creating sections entitled "Planned Mobility Development" for both the R-B-1 District and for the POI District to implement planned mobility development regulations for lands zoned R-B-1 and POI that are also designated "Planned Mobility" on the Future Land Use Map of the City's Comprehensive Plan; amending Section 28-307(1) to provide the maximum building intensity for R-B-1 and POI pursuant to a planned mobility development approval; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-11) Ordinance No. 5434 Ordinance No. 5435 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering rezoning property annexed into the City in 2003 (generally located south of Glades Road, east of St. Andrews Boulevard, north of the Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 and L-47 canals, and west of Interstate 95) consisting of (i) 215.02 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CG General Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CG Commercial General," (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith), and (ii) 26.90 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CHO Commercial High Office District (formerly Palm Beach County CS Specialized Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code) to "City CHO Commercial High Office" (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith): providing for revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for severability: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-16-01) Ordinance No. 5435 Mayor Haynie stated that the public hearings on Ordinances 5433, 5434, and 5435 would be conducted contemporaneously. She noted that, as this was the first of two public hearings on the ordinances, no vote would be taken. The City Attorney clarified that the ordinances are legislative rather than quasi­ judicial and the public hearing would be conducted accordingly. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation, beginning with background information on the Southwest Planning Area, commonly known as Midtown. Comprehensive Plan policies and objectives, including the Planned Mobility designation, applicable to this area were reviewed. It was noted that Land Development Regulations were required to implement the Planned Mobility designation. Further background information was provided. Mr. Schaad discussed in detail the changes to the use provisions as the County CG/CHO zoning is incorporated into the City Code. The proposed Planned Mobility Development (PMD) regulations were reviewed, noting that the underlying assumptions of a built and operational tri-rail station, functioning shuttle service and completed street infrastructure. Topics included, but were not limited to, dwelling unit size; street types and designs, including landscaping; sidewalks and crosswalks; bicycle lanes; building height and stepback; parking (on-street, structures, valet, surface lots); open space requirements; transit provisions other than Tri-rail; and the traffic analysis. Mr. Schaad addressed transit oriented development (TOD) and other planning considerations. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the ordinances with modifications, which Mr. Schaad reviewed. Staff also recommended approval. Upon concluding, he responded to numerous questions from members. Maria Tejara, Traffic Engineer, also responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, representing multiple property owners, generally offered support of the vision for the area but pointed out a number of ordinance provisions that are untenable. These provisions included the requirement for the tri-rail station, the timing of completion of the infrastructure, and building height requirements in the PMD overlay. He also discussed design elements, open space, enhanced shuttle service, and other requirements. Mr. Marshall then addressed the traffic analysis and the method for calculation of same. Bonnie Miskel, representing property owners west of Butts Road including Simon (the Mall), addressed three items in the ordinance: density, parking ratio, and allocation of rights. She pointed out that the transportation hub by the mall worked and, therefore, complete reliance on a tri-rail station was not necessary. In conclusion, Ms. Miskel asked that her client receive a minimum allocation of dwelling units, thanked the staff for their work on this matter and made herself available for questions. Kevin Plenzler, Fishkind & Associates, addressed the market study for residential development demand done by his firm, which was previously provided to the Council. Upon concluding, he responded to Council members' questions. Glenn Gromann, representing several property owners, addressed various elements of the ordinances including height, distance from single family residential, infrastructure vis-a-vis traffic, and TODs, among other topics. He suggested that property owners should be required to maintain the landscaping of medians. Seth Schneider expressed his concerns with the potential development that would be allowed should these ordinances be passed. He advocated having a master plan for the Midtown area. Gene Folden commented on the airport as it related to the Midtown area. He advocated that an avigation easement be a requirement of the Midtown development. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members discussed, asking further questions. Mr. Schaad provided responses. Topics included, but were not limited to, unit size, the need for a master plan and a market study, infrastructure, the number of units, and traffic. Lengthy discussion ensued. Mayor Haynie announced the date of the second public hearing.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5426 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, creating Section 28-1309 to require a permanent emergency generator to be located at any adult congregate living facility (ACLF), convalescent home or nursing home and allow the City Manager or designee to approve site plan modifications for the placement of such generator in certain circumstances; amending the following zoning districts to clarify the list of permitted and conditional uses with respect to ACLF's and similar or related uses: Section 28-538 (R-3-D District), Section 28-742 (R-B-1 District) and Section 28-922 (MC District); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17- Q1} Ordinance No. 5426 At this time, Deputy Mayor Rodgers left the dais, as he had recused himself from deliberation on this matter. Susan Lesser, Senior Planner, gave a very brief presentation, noting that this was the second public hearing and no changes had been made to the ordinance since the initial presentation. She offered to recap that presentation. Council Member Weinroth suggested that, as the Legislature may be considering a change to the current law, this item be postponed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to postpone Ordinance No. 5426. Members asked staff for their opinion on the Legislature's position and what they might do during session. The City Attorney addressed possible pre-emption by the Legislature. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Charles Siemon, representing Banyan Place, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation stating that the ordinance is supported with one exception: the requirement for the provision of 100% of normal electric power. He then reviewed the list of the essential electric service that should be required to be powered. He noted that his client is agreeable to wait to see what the Legislature will do. He then responded to questions. Staff also responded to Mr. Siemon's proposal. Andrew Hagen, Advent Life Ministries, addressed the situation at Advent Square that does have a generator that does not provide 100% power but does provide the necessary power during an emergency. Kevin Wrenne, ED of Banyan Place, offered support of the motion on the floor. He also addressed the 100% requirement. Staff will look at the suggestion made by Mr. Siemon. Bob Rollins addressed the 100% requirement as opposed to the provision of essential services. He then addressed the special meeting with the BPD that was suggested earlier and noted that he felt the timing would work. Tom Dowell, Advent Square, walked through the process they follow in an emergency. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

She offered to recap that presentation. Council Member Weinroth suggested that, as the Legislature may be considering a change to the current law, this item be postponed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to postpone Ordinance No. 5426. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering rezoning property annexed into the City in 2003 (generally located south of Glades Road, east of St. Andrews Boulevard, north of the Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 and L-47 canals, and west of Interstate 95) consisting of (i) 215.02 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CG General Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CG Commercial General," (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith), and (ii) 26.90 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CHO Commercial High Office District (formerly Palm Beach County CS Specialized Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code) to "City CHO Commercial High Office" (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith); providing for revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-16-01) Ordinance No. 5435 Mayor Haynie advised that the second public hearings public hearings on Items A., B., and C. would be conducted contemporaneously and separate votes would be taken on each ordinance. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation reviewing the eight issues discussed at the first public hearing. These included the need for a master plan; the submitted market study; building heights; the minimum unit size; the geographic allocation of units; an optional PMD overlay versus a new mandatory district; the perquisite of a train station; and, lastly, infrastructure and options for completion of same. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, GrayRobinson, speaking on behalf of several stakeholders, explained the overall idea behind Midtown as a mixed-use, walkable environment. He then pointed out elements in the ordinances that his clients believed were detrimental to creating this walkable environment, including unit allocation, Tri-Rail contingencies, street infrastructure requirement, building height, non-PMD parking, open space, unit size, setbacks, and shuttle requirements. Upon concluding, he responded to a number of questions from Council members. Extensive discussion followed. Topics included funding the infrastructure, the need for a master plan, the Tri-Rail station, and Military Trail concurrency. Brandon Schaad provided additional information. Angelo Bianco, Crocker Partners, addressed street infrastructure improvements and concurrency, and also provided further information on the planning process for their ten-year project. John Donaldson, traffic engineer, explained traffic concurrency as detailed for the Midtown area. Bonnie Miske!, Dunay Miskel Backman, speaking on behalf of Simon Properties, noted that her client has an interest in this item while not being part of the Midtown area. She commented on the ordinances that would create new zoning districts, the transit hub on Butts Road, and the allocation or units. Joseph Jaffe, on behalf of Fairfield of Boca, commented on the need for a plan leading to a vision, noting that one must start somewhere and work together. William Seenyshyn, president of Timbercreek Homeowners Association, requested that a master plan for the area be completed before moving ahead and stated his support of the Planning and Zoning Board recommendations. John Watts commented on the Tri-Rail station, the allowable number of units, traffic on Military Trail, and other topics. Stuart Melsez offered support of Midtown. Kathryn Sauers expressed her concerns and asked a number of questions about the availability of information. Adam Beighley, on behalf of Via Verde Homeowners Association, commented on the stakeholders' interaction with the Association. Lorraine Braile displayed a poster illustrating the location of the residential units and expressed other concerns. Tim Day expressed his opposition to the Midtown plan, stating that it will negatively impact his neighborhood and the City as a whole. Bobbye Miller agreed with the previous speaker and expressed her opposition to the Midtown plan. JoAnn Landon commented on the lack of mass transit, the increasing number of residential units, and asked that the Council not approve Midtown. Donna Mincuzzi expressed opposition to the Midtown project and the number of rental units. John Renne, Florida Atlantic University urban planning professor, commented on the purpose of the hearing, master planning, traffic congestion in walkable communities, and other related topics. He offered support of Midtown. Monica Mayotte commented on the need for a master plan and a market study for Midtown. She asked that no vote be taken. Diane Pingle commented on traffic on Military Trail and expressed opposition to Midtown. Jason Pellish expressed opposition to the residential units proposed to be built and the project as a whole. Lenore Wachtel commented on the need for a master plan and a special assessment as was done for the downtown community redevelopment area. Steve Utrecht expressed his concern with planned mobility and advocated having site specific plans before granting vested rights. Brian Stenberg commented on the advent of autonomous vehicles and the impacts on roadways, and other related topics. Carrie Gibbons expressed her opposition to the ordinances and any increase in residential units. Pauletta Moore commented on traffic on Military Trail and its effect on her neighborhood. Joe Pedalino expressed opposition to Midtown and advocated having a master plan and market study. Martina Shokey commented on traffic congestion and offered opposition to residential. Michael Marshall responded to a number of the previous comments. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members asked questions of staff. Brandon Schaad and the City Attorney provided information on traffic and school concurrency. Angelo Bianco responded to a question regarding the Tri-Rail station requirement, other aspects of the Midtown plan and establishment of regulations. He emphasized the need to work together. Mayor Haynie enumerated topics that needed to be addressed: information on the County's plan for Military Trail, a reduction in the number of units, timing or roadway infrastructure, the lack of setbacks and other concerns. She suggested that more time was needed before a decision could be made. Members weighed in and asked further questions. Mr. Bianco and Mr. Schaad provided information on funding for a shuttle, a transit oriented development, and the Tri-Rail requirement. Members made further lengthy comments. Discussion of the timing of a postponement, allowing time to work out the differences between the stakeholders and City, and the necessary planning for the area as it relates to the land development regulations, ensued. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levin O'Rourke, to extend the meeting beyond 11 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Discussion continued. Mr. Schaad addressed the planning process as he sees it going forward, and responded to a number of questions. Mr. Bianco expressed his desire to move forward. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to have a city-driven small area plan for this area. Prior to voting, the City Manager summarized the direction he heard during the discussion. The City Attorney addressed the planning process and what it is included in same. Discussion ensued. Topics included the definition of a small area plan, implementation of land development regulations, timing of a plan, the legalities involved, analyzing the roadway network. The City Attorney responded to some of the statements made. Members commented further. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Mayor Susan Haynie voting no. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to postpone Ordinance No. 5433, Ordinance No. 5434 and Ordinance No. 5435 to March 27, 2018. Motion failed 2 votes to 3; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting yes, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton, deleting, revising and/or restating portions of Chapter 2, "Administration," Chapter 13, "Public Places," and Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; assigning matters under the jurisdiction of the Zoning Board of Adjustment to the Planning and Zoning Board; abolishing the Zoning Board of Adjustment and deleting provisions relating to such board; consolidating various provisions regarding variances into one article and amending provisions for the processing of variances, including amending the appeal provisions and considering the minimum vote requirement to grant a variance; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-09) Ordinance No. 5437 Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this ordinance was part of the streamlining process. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5437 as amended as stated. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 22-2018 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board approving Rose Paving LLC's request to remove trees (Permit No. 17-6127}, with a condition that five such trees remain, at The Atrium of Boca Raton located at 1080 NW 15th Street; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 22-2018 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Nora Fosman, Senior Environmental Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The staff recommendation to reverse the decision of the Community Appearance Board (CAB) was explained. Various pictures illustrated the justification for removal of the trees and that the trees did not mature properly due to where they were planted. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chair, explained that the applicant had been offered the opportunity to reconfigure the parking lot islands in exchange for allowing the removal of the trees. He noted that he is not opposed to removing the trees. Debra Hernandez, on behalf of the Atrium, provided a handout to the Council, and stated that the request to remove the trees was due to the fact that the roots were causing a public safety issue. She noted that a reconfiguration of the parking lot would result in the owner having to submit for a site plan modification rather than simply removing the trees, replacing them with properly scaled vegetation, and repaving and restriping the lot. Upon concluding, she responded to questions. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, addressed the possibility of a site plan change as suggested by CAB. Mr. Jacobsen weighed in. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. At the request of the Council, the City Attorney read language into the record reflecting the approval of removing six trees and the requirement to change the configuration of the parking lot islands. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 22-2018 affirming the decision of the Community Appearance Board with conditions as stated. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5436 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, authorizing restaurants as permitted uses in certain business and commercial zoning districts; amending the lists of permitted and conditional uses in the following zoning districts to provide for such restaurant uses: Sections 28-742 and 28-743 (R-B-1 Motel-Business District}, Section 28-777 and 28-778 (B-1 Local Business District), Sections 28-797 and 28-798 (B-2 Community Business District), Sections 28-822 and 28-823 (B-3 Central Business District), Sections 28-847 and 28-848 (B-4 General Business District), Sections 28-872 and 28-873 (C-1 Commercial District), and Sections 28-893 and 28-894 (POI Professional, Office and Institutional District); amending Section 28-745, Code of Ordinances, to provide for consistent treatment of restaurant uses in the R-B-1 Motel Business District; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-10) The public hearings on items B., C. and D. will be conducted contemporaneously. A separate vote will be taken on each item. Ordinance No. 5436 Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, noted that this was the second of two public hearings and that no changes had been made to the ordinance. She then briefly reviewed the purpose and benefits of the ordinance before making herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5436. Members made final comments Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. ~ Ordinance No. 5441 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the fiscal year 2017-2018 budget through the Ocean Breeze Budget Amendment; revising revenues and expenditures in certain budgeted funds; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5441 Ordinance No. 5442 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton, Florida authorizing the issuance of a revenue bond by the City in an amount not exceeding $20,000,000 for the purpose of providing funds to the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (the 'District') to acquire the Ocean Breeze property for development of recreational and related facilities for the benefit of the residents of the City and the District; providing for a supplemental resolution setting forth the details of said Bond; authorizing specified City employees to negotiate with financial institutions for purchase of the Bond; authorizing the City Manager or designee to enter into a rate lock agreement; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5442 Resolution No. 15-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, authorizing the issuance of a Revenue Bond of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $20,000,000 for the purpose of providing funds to the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (the "District") to acquire the Ocean Breeze property for development of recreational and related facilities for the benefit of the residents of the City and the District, and paying costs of issuance of the bond; awarding the sale of the bond to Raymond James Capital Funding, Inc.; providing for security for the bond; providing other provisions relating to the bond; making certain covenants and agreements in connection therewith; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 15-2018 Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on items B, C and D would be conducted contemporaneously as they are related. A separate vote would be taken on each. Council Member O'Rourke explained the reasons that, in an abundance of caution, she would recuse herself from discussion of and voting on these items. She then left the dais. Sharon McGuire, Budget Director, briefly reviewed the revenue and expenditures contained in Ordinance 5441. She made herself available for questions upon concluding. Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, reviewed the bond Ordinance 5442 and Resolution 15-2018, noting that, of the institutions that bid on the bond, Raymond James offered the most favorable rate and thus was chosen to issue the bond. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Steve Haar urged a yes vote on the ordinances and resolution. Craig Ernst thanked the Council and staff for their work on these items and the partnership of the City and District. Doug Coller offered support of the bond issue. Robert DuKate thanked Council for their support of the recent Boca Raton Championship and urged passage of the bond ordinance and resolution. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments and shared their thoughts. Motion was made by Council Member S, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve to approve Ordinance No. 5441. Motion carried 3 votes to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5442. Motion carried 3 votes to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, to approve Resolution No. 15-2018. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Council Member O'Rourke returned to the dais. s Ordinance No. 5443 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Boca Raton Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order to allow roof overhangs, eaves, gutters, balconies and decorative architectural features to encroach into required setbacks of buildings from rights­ of-way lines; affirming that the amendments do not require the filing of a Notice of Proposed Change to the DORI; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (AM-18-01) Ordinance No. 5443 Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He noted that allowing encroachments of design elements would result in better architecture. Several graphics were presented to illustrate details of encroachments. The staff recommendations were reviewed, including the amendment suggested by the Downtown Advisory Committee. Mr. Schaad then responded to questions for members. Members offered comments in support of the ordinance. The public hearing was opened. Juan Caycedo commented on the ordinance and offered his support. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney pointed out the revisions to the ordinance which she read into the record. It was again noted that staff recommends approval of the ordinance as revised. She provided further information, as did Mr. Schaad. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5443 as amended. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, FS., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a "relative" includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A "business associate" means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joint venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). ELECTED OFFICERS: In addition to abstaining from voting in the situations described above, you must disclose the conflict: PRIOR TO THE VOTE BEING TAKEN by publicly stating to the assembly the nature of your interest in the measure on which you are abstaining from voting; and WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER THE VOTE OCCURS by completing and filing this form with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who should incorporate the form in the minutes. * * APPOINTED OFFICERS: Although you must abstain from voting in the situations described above, you are not prohibited by Section 112.3143 from otherwise participating in these matters. However, you must disclose the nature of the conflict before making any attempt to influence the decision, whether orally or in writing and whether made by you or at your direction. IF YOU INTEND TO MAKE ANY ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION PRIOR TO THE MEETING AT WHICH THE VOTE WILL BE TAKEN: • You must complete and file this form (before making any attempt to influence the decision) with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who will incorporate the form in the minutes. (Continued on page 2) CE FORM 8B - EFF 11/2013 PAGE 1 Adopted by reference in Rule 34-7.010(1)(f), FAC. APPOINTED OFFICERS (continued) • A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency. • The form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. IF YOU MAKE NO ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION EXCEPT BY DISCUSSION AT THE MEETING: • You must disclose orally the nature of your conflict in the measure before participating. • You must complete the form and file it within 15 days after the vote occurs with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who must incorporate the form in the minutes. A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency, and the form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. units.text: Resolution No. 39-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton encouraging the United States Congress and Florida Legislature to enact measures to protect school children and our communities from gun violence, and to develop effective strategies to address, support, and provide resources for persons suffering from mental health issues, which may include enacting reasonable firearms regulations, providing resources to address mental health issues, and implementing enhanced security measures for public schools and other community institutions: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date Resolution No. 39-2018 Mayor Haynie stated that this resolution was brought forward by Council Member O'Rourke. Ms. O'Rourke made an opening statement expressing her feelings and advocating action to keep school children safe. Council Member Singer commented on the steps currently being taken by the City. Council Member Weinroth commented on the restrictions on local governments with regard to gun control. Mayor Haynie invited Joseph Majhess, student at Boca Raton High School, to the podium. He shared the letter he wrote to district leaders and elected government officials regarding protecting schools and providing a safe environment for students and staff alike. He offered a number of suggestions to address the issue of school safety, including specific suggestions for the City to implement. Maltec Sera, a student at Boca Raton Middle School, offered a number of suggestions to address her concerns with state gun laws, background checks, age limits to purchase a gun, and other related topics. Frank Barbieri, District 5 School Board member, thanked the City for help that was provided to the District in the wake of the Parkland tragedy. He then reported on what is being done at the District level to address school safety in Boca Raton, read a portion of a letter to parent from the Superintendent that identified specific steps being taken to improve school safety, and provided additional information. The upcoming day of action on March 14 was addressed. Mental health counselor Lisa Gold offered her suggestions on how to help children with behavioral issues. Luke Sherlock, whose niece was a victim of the Parkland shooting, commented on the lack of security at local schools and the need for gun reform. He urged support of Boca's students. Kim Bremer commented on the school shooting and offered her suggestion to establish an Education Safety Task Force, provided details and addressed the audience of the need to get involved. Glenn Gromann offered his support of the ideas floated this evening and touted his military security background. He commented on the openness of the local school and university campuses in the City. Jon Carter commented on the openness of the Boca High campus and suggested the need to address this issue. JoAnn Landon commented on the lack of state funding for schools and the need to stop selling guns. Charlie Helton noted that schools are soft targets and commented on the history of gun laws in the state and other topics. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Resolution No. 39-2018 as revised. Members made final comments in support of the resolution. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Mayor Haynie noted that the public hearings on Items A., B., C., D., and E. would be conducted contemporaneously and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures. A separate vote would taken on each ordinance and resolution. Ordinance No. 5428 would require four votes for passage. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak.. Elizabeth Eassa, Development Services Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The changes to the project since it was first presented to City Council were reviewed. Topics included, but were not limited to, the site plan, trip generation, and the modified condition related to a voluntary contribution to the School District as detailed in the school capacity availability determination (SCAD) letter. Ms. Eassa stated staff's recommendation for approval, subject to the conditions in the ordinances and resolutions. The public hearing was opened. Heather Allen, on behalf of the applicant, summarized the revised project and provided a history of the property. She addressed the project's consistency with the City's Comprehensive Plan, the rezoning, and the project's trip generation. The revised site plan was then reviewed, noting the decrease in number of units and the number of parking spaces along the access road. The technical deviation regarding on-street circulation was addressed and the latest school concurrency letter was reviewed. In conclusion, Ms. Allen advocated approval of the project and then responded to questions. She noted that her client agreed that the condition that the voluntary contribution to the School District be held by the City was acceptable. Susan Rentler expressed concern with the amount of traffic that the project will generate and noted her opposition to the rezoning and the height of the buildings. Maria Tejara, City Traffic Engineer, addressed the possibility of channeling to reduce some of the traffic concerns. Mike Rentler expressed his concerns with traffic, the lack of parking, and the height of the townhomes among other issues. He stated his opposition to the project. Glenn Gromann addressed some of the concerns expressed previously as well as school concurrency. He advocated approval. Charlie Helton offered support of the project. Joanne Wise, after being sworn in, advocated that the land remain vacant or that the number of units be decreased. She expressed opposition to the project. There was no cross examination. In rebuttal, Ms. Allen responded to some of the previous comments, including traffic through the neighborhood. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Ordinance No. 5428 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a universal conditional amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 1.744 acres, located at 300, 316, 382 and 398 West Yamato Road, and 5001, 5033 and 5067 Northwest 3rd Avenue, from Residential Low (RL) to Residential High (RH), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-03/SC) Yamato Villas Update for Items A-E Ordinance No. 5428 Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Mayor Susan Haynie, to approve Ordinance. No. 5428 as revised and amended. The City Attorney clarified and read into the record the two repeated conditions in the site plan and the development orders that have the site plan as an attachment. Revised condition 3.k. was related to the City holding and expending the voluntary contribution suggested in the School District SCAD letter. A new condition in Section 3. sub 3.d.vi. addressed the channelization of the exit from NW 4th Avenue to Yamato Road allowing right turn movement only. After a brief discussion, Ms. Allen and Ms. Tejara agreed as to the location of the channelization. Members then made final comments and expressed their support or lack thereof. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. ~ Ordinance No. 5429 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a universal conditional rezoning, pursuant to Article VI, Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances, of property consisting of approximately 1.744 acres, more or less, located at 300, 316, 382 and 398 West Yamato Road, and 5001, 5033 and 5067 Northwest 3rd Avenue, from Single-Family Residential (R-1-D) to Multi-Family Residential (R-3- C); subject to conditions; providing for the appropriate revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-03/ZC) Ordinance No. 5429 Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5429 as revised. Council Member Weinroth made final comments. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: Resolution No. 34-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from Section 24-77(b), Code of Ordinances, to allow two (2) freestanding signs (where only one (1) freestanding sign is permitted), for a place of worship and school in a single-family residential zoning district, for Temple Beth El of Boca Raton, located at 333 SW 4th Avenue; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SCV-17-02) NOTE: The appellant has requested a continuance of the following matter to the March 27, 2018 Council meeting without objection. Resolution No. 34-2018 Tori Golden, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the property was described and the proposed location of the second sign was provided. Ms. Golden explained that the proposed sign would identify the entrance to the Somerset Academy Boca that is located on the property. Details of the sign were provided. Staff recommends approval subject to conditions related to landscaping. Ms. Golden noted that the Community Appearance Board recommended approval with the condition to landscape the base of the sign. Upon concluding, Ms. Golden made herself available for questions. At this time, Mayor Haynie asked the City Attorney to confirm that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect, which she did. Members had no ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Ms. Golden affirmed that her testimony was true and correct. The public hearing was then opened. Steve Kaufman, Executive Director of Temple Beth El, responded to questions re landscaping. Daniel Shourds, principal of Somerset Academy Boca, addressed the need for a sign to identify the location of the school. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 34-2018 granting the variance. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Council Member O'Rourke commented on the outreach meeting regarding boat ramps at Lake Wyman and Rutherford Park and the community's opposition to same. She asked that Round the Town, a downtown ride service, be on the next agenda. She also advocated creation of a school safety task force. Deputy Mayor Rodgers also addressed the Lake Wyman/Rutherford Park plans, as well as plans for Silver Palm Park. Council Member Singer added his thoughts regarding the outreach meeting and suggested that further outreach take place regarding the location of boat ramps. He also addressed the suggestion of an education safety task force. Council Member Weinroth suggested a comprehensive review of potential stops for Round the Town and a bike share system. He also asked that the Council join Weston regarding changing a state law related to gun control. The City Attorney provided information and noted that she will follow up and report back. Members weighed in. Mayor Haynie announced the ribbon cutting for the 1-95 Spanish River interchange.
