units.text: Resolution No. 43-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Conditional Use and Conditional Commercial Node Master Plan approval (Resolution No. 55-2011) for the Shoppes at Blue Lake, located at 1200 West Yamato Road, to increase the maximum restaurant square footage from 25,000 square feet to 26,287 square feet, and decrease the maximum retail square footage from 25,000 square feet to 23,713 square feet: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-03-06R5) The public hearings on items B. and C. will be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related. A separate vote will be taken on each resolution. Resolution No. 43-2018 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Development Services Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the subject property was identified, a history of prior approvals was detailed, and the requested changes were presented. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval. Staff found no adverse impacts and recommended approval as well. Ms. Eassa then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Richard Brooks, on behalf of the petitioner, made brief comments in support of the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 43-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Resolution No. 44-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a modification to the approved Woodfield Country Club Planned Unit Development (PUD) Master Plan (Resolution No. 15-2015) to authorize expansion of the recreational facilities (and accessory uses to support such facilities) for the Woodfield Country Club Recreation Parcel generally located on approximately 23.45 acres at 3600 and 3650 Club Place; subject to conditions: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (PUD-85-08R3) Resolution No. 44-2018 Drawings Resolution No. 45-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering tentative plat approval for the Woodfield Country Club Recreation Parcel replat (a replat of all of Parcel P, a portion of Tracts L-10-A and T-5 of Woodfield Country Club, and portions of Golf Course Parcel A and Lake Parcel C of The Enclave at Woodfield Country Club), generally located at 3600 and 3650 Club Place: subject to conditions: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SUB-17-02) Resolution No. 45-2018 Drawings Mayor Haynie noted that items B and C would be heard together and that a separate vote would be taken on each resolution. The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa again gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location and size of the property were identified and brief background information was provided. Details of the site plan and master plan were reviewed. The need for a tentative plat was explained. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval, as does staff. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, on behalf of the applicant, advocated approval and then responded to questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 44-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Robert S. Weinroth, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 45-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Scott Singer, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 35-2018 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of a decision of the Builders' Board of Adjustment and Appeals (Resolution BBAA-17-92600001) approving variances from the following sections of the City's Code of Ordinances: Section 22-62(2), to allow a finger pier width of eight (8) feet in lieu of the maximum allowable width of six (6) feet; Section 22-62(6) to allow a finger pier to encroach 27.4 feet beyond the maximum encroachment of 45.6 feet (fifteen percent (15%) of the width of the waterway but not exceeding sixty (60) feet) into a waterway; Section 22-62(7) to allow a finger pier side setback of forty (40) feet in lieu of the required side setback equal to the distance the finger pier extends out into the waterway (73 feet); and Section 22-63(1) to allow a boat lift to encroach fifty-three (53) feet into a waterway in lieu of the maximum encroachment of twenty (20) feet, for the property located at 600 Northeast Fifth Avenue; subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (BBAA-17-92600001) Resolution No. 35-2018 Appellant Submission The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Keith Carney, Senior Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The property that is the subject of the matter was identified and background information was provided. Details of the variances requested were provided, as were details of the prior and proposed dock and boat lift. The Marine Advisory Board recommended approval with conditions regarding the boat lift and a pumpout facility. The Builders' Board of Adjustment and Appeals (BBAA) granted the variances with conditions. Staff recommended approval of the variances. Upon concluding, Mr. Carney responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Howard DuBoser, on behalf of the appellant Paul Rosenberg, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He outlined his argument in support of granting the appeal and denying the variances. Mr. DuBosar noted that the main objection was that the dock will extend 73 feet into the lntracoastal, emphasizing that the literal interpretation of the City's Code should prohibit granting the variance. He stated that the proposed dock length would impact the Rosenberg's view. Mr. Rosenberg then made a statement regarding the Fowler's decision to build a new dock and expressing his concerns. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the Fowlers, gave a PowerPoint presentation, reviewing the variance criteria. Charlie Isiminger, Isiminger & Stubbs Engineering, continued the presentation, reviewing the special and unique situations that exist in support of the variance. Ms. Miskel addressed the way in which the Fowlers would be deprived of rights commonly enjoyed by owners of properties in the same area. Drew Campbell, Environmental & Marine Consulting Services, then addressed the design and location of the dock and lift. Matt Butler, Isiminger & Stubbs Engineering, refuted the right to a view and navigation impacts as discussed by Mr. DuBosar. Ms. Miske! then concluded the presentation. There was no cross examination. During rebuttal, Michael Moskowitz, on behalf of the Fowlers, provided handouts and responded to points made by Mr. DuBosar including how the City interprets its Code and the violation of the Rosenberg's riparian rights. He concluded that the variances should be granted and the appeal denied. Mr. DuBosar rebutted various points, including the age and condition of the old dock, new testimony, interpretation of the City's Code, obstruction of views, and other topics. The City Attorney provided her analysis of the City Code as it applies to this matter. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, also addressed the limitation of the length of finger piers. Mr. Carney, Ms. Miske! and Mr. DuBosar responded to Council members' questions. The public hearing was closed. The City Attorney clarified that, on appeals, the Council can rely on the record and new testimony when making a decision. Motion was made by Mayor Susan Haynie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 35-2018 affirming the decision of the BBAA and granting the variances. Members made final comments and expressed their opinions. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Robert S. Weinroth voting yes; Council Member Scott Singer voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 23 "Planning and Development," Article IV, Division 5, Section 23-190, "Driveways and Off-Street Parking Facilities other than Single-Family and Duplex," Code of Ordinances, amending provisions relating to required vehicle reservoirs for gated developments: clarifying that Section 23-190 does not apply to single-family and duplex residential plots; providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-13) Ordinance No. 5450 Andrew Capra, GIS Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information was provided. A handout showing suggested changes to the proposed amended language was distributed. Staff recommends approval of the amendment. Mr. Capra noted that the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with a minor change. In response to a question regarding communities with more than one entry, Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided a handout containing additional language that addressed that circumstance and explained same. Maria Tejera, Traffic Engineer, responded to questions as well. The public hearing was opened. JoAnn Landon inquired about gated communities with two-lane entries. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. For clarity, the City Attorney suggested adding additional language to the table outlining the requirements for reservoir length. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5450 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting yes. Ordinance No. 5451 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 25, "Streets and Sidewalks," Article II, "Vacation and Abandonment of Streets and Easements," Code of Ordinances, amending and updating procedures for the vacation and abandonment of rights-of-way and special purpose easements, by deleting, revising and/or restating portions of Sections 25-31-25-40, and by creating Sections 25-41 and 25-42, Code of Ordinances: providing procedures for the vacation and abandonment of required rights-of-way and special purpose easements in conjunction with a site plan approval; providing procedures for the administrative abandonment of non-required rights-of-way and special purpose easements: and providing procedures for the vacation and abandonment of rights-of-way and special purpose easements pursuant to a replat: providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-16- Ql) Ordinance No. 5451 Lynn Bodor, Property Specialist Appraiser, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this was a streamlining effort. Background information was provided, including the meaning of paper easements. The changes to the methods of abandonment were summarized. Ms. Bodor provided details of a number of past abandonments that would have been done administratively had this code change been in place. She then responded questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5451. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting yes. units.text: Ordinance No. 5444 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to the transportation element of the City's Comprehensive Plan: amending an objective and policy to establish an alternative transportation concurrency standard (ATCS) for the Boca Royale Planned Unit Development (PUD) to satisfy traffic concurrency along Northwest 2nd Avenue/East Country Club Boulevard north of Yamato Road, subject to certain mitigation measures and conditions, and authorizing execution of a mitigation agreement: deleting references to the Ocean Breeze Development, an expired project; deleting obsolete statutory references: reaffirming that an ATCS may only be authorized by the City Council through an amendment to the Comprehensive Plan; considering a universal conditional amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 55.12 acres, generally located at 7601 East Country Club Boulevard, from Recreation and Open Space (PR) to Residential Low (RL), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for severability: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-17-09) Ordinance 5444 Drawings Council Member Rodgers introduced the ordinance. Ordinance No. 5453 An Ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Article V, "Qualifications and Elections," Section 5.03, "Qualifications," of the Charter of the City of Boca Raton to modify the requirements to qualify as a candidate for City Council, including the office of Mayor, by: (i) extending the length of the residency requirement, establishing certain requirements for residency, and requiring proof of such residency (to be prescribed by Ordinance), and (ii) eliminating the $25 qualifying fee and instead requiring the verified signatures of a specified number of registered voters of the City, and providing for procedures for collection, submission, and verification of such signatures (to be prescribed by Ordinance); providing for a special election regarding the proposed Charter amendments to be held on August 28, 2018 (the date of the primary election); amending Chapter 6 1 "Elections," of the Code of Ordinances to create (subject to approval of one, or both, of the above Charter amendments) a new Section 6-16, "Proof of Residency," prescribing procedures for establishing residency, and a new Section 6-17, "Filing of Petition," prescribing procedures for the collection, submission, and verification of signatures; providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing for revisions to the City Charter and codification in the City Code, respectively; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5453 Council Member O'Rourke introduced the ordinance.

units.text: Resolution No. 60-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the City of Boca Raton (and its elected officials, at their discretion) to join in litigation filed by the City of Weston, Florida (and other municipalities), seeking a declaration that provisions in Section 790.33, Florida Statutes, that punish elected officials (and their municipalities) for enacting or enforcing regulations relating to firearms and ammunition, are invalid; authorizing the City Attorney to execute a retainer agreement; providing an effective date Resolution No. 60-2018 The City Attorney gave a brief explanation of the resolution and provided her reasoning for recommending adoption. She then responded to a number of questions posed by Council members. The Mayor commented on the pre-emption of home rule. The public hearing was opened. JoAnn Landon offered her support of the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 60-2018. Deputy Mayor Singer suggested two changes to the resolution, which the City Attorney read in to the record. The amendments were accepted by the motion maker and seconder. Members made final comments. Motion on Resolution No. 60-2018 as amended carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Susan Haynie, Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes; Council member Jeremy Rodgers voting no.

units.text: Resolution No. 55-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1396, Code of Ordinances, to authorize construction of a convenience store in excess of 750 square feet. and a carwash facility at a service station for the property located at 1255 West Palmetto Park Road; providing for repealer, providing an effective date (CA-17-03) Resolution No. 55-2018 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the petitioner's request. The location and zoning of the subject property were identified. Details of the proposed project were provided. The site plan was reviewed, noting that the addition of the car wash required the conditional use approval. Staffs analysis of the conditional use showed that the request met the requirements of the Code. Technical deviations related to driveways and egress were also approved by staff. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the conditional use and approved the site plan. Staff recommended approval of the conditional use with the conditions included in the resolution. The public hearing was opened. Jamie Crowley, Gunster Law Firm on behalf of the petitioner, gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of the application. He addressed various aspects of the proposal and provided details of the project, noting that they had been working with staff to address the site constraints. Concerns expressed in an email from the neighboring property owner were addressed. Mr. Crowley then turned the presentation over to Danny Alonso, architect for the project. Mr. Alonso reviewed the site plan and provided details of the design of the facility. Information on the operation of the car wash was provided. He then responded to Council members' questions. Seeing no one else came forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 55-2018. The City Attorney referenced page 6 of the Planning and Zoning Board resolution, Exhibit 1 to Resolution 55-2018, which lists the conditions of approval. She suggested that condition 3 in Section 7 would more appropriately be designated as "h", with a, band c renamed 1, 2 and 3. Conditions 4 and 5 would then be renumbered 3 and 4. Both Ms. O'Rourke and Ms. Mayotte agreed to incorporate the changes into their motion. Motion on Resolution No. 55-2018 as amended carried on a 3 to 0 vote; Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to the transportation element of the City's Comprehensive Plan; amending an objective and policy to establish an alternative transportation concurrency standard (ATCS) for the Boca Royale Planned Unit Development (PUD} to satisfy traffic concurrency along Northwest 2nd Avenue/East Country Club Boulevard north of Yamato Road, subject to certain mitigation measures and conditions, and authorizing execution of a mitigation agreement; deleting references to the Ocean Breeze Development, an expired project; deleting obsolete statutory references; reaffirming that an ATCS may only be authorized by the City Council through an amendment to the Comprehensive Plan; considering a universal conditional amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 55.12 acres, generally located at 7601 East Country Club Boulevard, from Recreation and Open Space (PR) to Residential Low (RL), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-17-09) Ordinance No. 5444 Drawings Deputy Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing and if the ordinance was not transmitted, Ordinance 5445, the rezoning, would not be considered for introduction. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He noted that Council would only be considering transmitting the Comprehensive Plan Amendments to the State Department of Economic Opportunity. The applicant's overall request that included a rezoning, master plan approval, tentative plat approval and site plan approval, was reviewed and the project was described, including location, zoning and number of units proposed. Details were provided. Mr. Bell then provided staffs analysis of the projects compatibility with the Comp Plan. Topics included the future land use change; concurrency of water/sewer, drainage, public schools, and transportation. The traffic analysis was reviewed. While the project was noted to be consistent with some policies and objectives in the Comp Plan, it was inconsistent with the elements related to recreation and open space as well as nd transportation, in particular the failure of NW 2 Avenue despite the applicant's proposal of a payment in mitigation agreement and establishment of an ATCS. These inconsistencies were the reasons to recommend denial of the Comp Plan Amendments. The specific language of the proposed amendments was presented. Mr. Bell then discussed the Comp Plan objective related to coastal high hazard areas and flood zones as related to the construction of homes on the property. The Planning and Zoning Board voted to deny recommendation. Staff did not recommend approval of nor transmittal of the Comp Plan Amendment. Deputy Mayor Singer noted that he had expressed concerns with the project. He then opened the public hearing. Michael Marshall, Gunster Law Firm on behalf of the petitioner, began by requesting a continuance. He then reviewed the benefits of the project. Mr. Marshall addressed the review criteria for consistency with the Comp Plan, the transportation element, existing deficient roadways, the coastal high hazard zone and related topics. The developer's offer to provide bike paths and open space access was noted. Mr. Marshall countered a number of statements made in the staff presentation. Staff provided information. The City Attorney also provided information regarding the City's flood maps and updating of same. A brief discussion of open space followed. Rob Berthiaume offered his opinion that the project was a bad fit for the area. He thanked the Council and staff for their openness and willingness to talk with residents. He then supported recreational space, noting that residents are not opposed to any development of the property. Bob Boggs, vice president of the Hidden Lake Property Owners Association, agreed with the previous speaker and then addressed points made with regard to traffic and schools. Deputy Mayor Singer provided information on schools. Rosie Service provided a map handout and stated her opposition to building more residences and giving up recreation space. Angelo Sands thanked the residents in his community who spoke up about this proposed development. Ray Smolenski asked that the way in which traffic affects emergency services be taken into account. Jack McWalter commented on the school capacity letters and school overcrowding. Harold Chaffee advocated keeping the property as open space. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney provided information on the procedure for considering an amendment to the Comprehensive Plan and the transmittal of same. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, not to transmit Ordinance No. 5444 to the appropriate state agencies. Members made final comments. Motion carried on 3 to 0 vote; Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. The City Attorney suggested to amend the agenda to remove Ordinance No. 5445, item 15.A., from Introductions of Ordinances. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to remove Ordinance No. 5445, item 15.A., from the agenda. Motion carried on a 3 to 0 vote; Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. Prior to proceeding with the agenda and as requested by Council Member O'Rourke, Deputy Mayor Singer reported the breaking news that Mayor Haynie had been booked on criminal charges, noting the troubling nature of this news. He then made comments regarding the situation, stating that public trust is important and the Council will continue to work on behalf of the residents. Council Member O'Rourke expressed her deep disappointment and commented further on the situation. Discussion followed as to the next steps for the Council. The City Manager and City Attorney provided information. Council Member Mayotte shared her thoughts and disappointment. The Deputy Mayor made final comments and then resumed the agenda.

units.text: An Ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Article V, "Qualifications and Elections," Section 5.03, "Qualifications," of the Charter of the City of Boca Raton to modify the requirements to qualify as a candidate for City Council, including the office of Mayor, by: (i) extending the length of the residency requirement, establishing certain requirements for residency, and requiring proof of such residency (to be prescribed by Ordinance), and (ii) eliminating the $25 qualifying fee and instead requiring the verified signatures of a specified number of registered voters of the City, and providing for procedures for collection, submission, and verification of such signatures (to be prescribed by Ordinance); providing for a special election regarding the proposed Charter amendments to be held on August 28, 2018 (the date of the primary election); amending Chapter 6, "Elections," of the Code of Ordinances to create (subject to approval of one, or both, of the above Charter amendments) a new Section 6-16, "Proof of Residency," prescribing procedures for establishing residency, and a new Section 6-17, "Filing of Petition," prescribing procedures for the collection, submission, and verification of signatures; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revisions to the City Charter and codification in the City Code, respectively; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5453 City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser briefly explained the ordinance brought forward at the direction of the Council, noting that the Charter amendments would be placed on the August 28, 2018 primary election ballot. Deputy Mayor Singer offered Council Member Mayotte, as the newly-elected member, the opportunity to weigh in on the ordinance. Discussion followed on the ordinance and a continuance of the public hearing to a date certain. The City Attorney addressed the possibility of a continuance and the deadline for submitting ballot question language. The public hearing was opened. Frank Chapman asked how proof of residency would be determined. The City Attorney provided information. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to continue Ordinance No. 5453 to May 8, 2018. Motion carried on a 3 to 0 vote; Deputy Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: An Ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Article V, "Qualifications and Elections," Section 5.03, "Qualifications," of the Charter of the City of Boca Raton to modify the requirements to qualify as a candidate for City Council, including the office of Mayor, by: (i) extending the length of the residency requirement, establishing certain requirements for residency, and requiring proof of such residency (to be prescribed by Ordinance), and (ii) eliminating the $25 qualifying fee and instead requiring the verified signatures of a specified number of registered voters of the City, and providing for procedures for collection, submission, and verification of such signatures (to be prescribed by Ordinance); providing for a special election regarding the proposed Charter amendments to be held on August 28, 2018 (the date of the primary election); amending Chapter 6, "Elections," of the Code of Ordinances to create (subject to approval of one, or both, of the above Charter amendments) a new Section 6-16, "Proof of Residency," prescribing procedures for establishing residency, and a new Section 6-17, "Filing of Petition," prescribing procedures for the collection, submission, and verification of signatures; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revisions to the City Charter and codification in the City Code, respectively; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5453 The City Manager briefly explained the substance of the ordinance. Members commented and asked questions. Information on the form of petitions was discussed. Mayor Singer suggested that the proposed ballot questions should be on the November ballot rather than the August ballot in order to avoid voter confusion. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Tamara McKee voiced her concerns and asked that the ordinance not be adopted. Jason Pellish reported on the results of a Boca Watch website poll on possible changes to residency requirements for candidates running for City Council. Kathy Cottrell offered support of the increased residency requirements. David Sergi expressed his concerns with the proposal to gather 200 signatures rather than pay a fee. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Members commented further. The City Attorney provided information on the effect of possible changes to the title should consideration of the ordinance be postponed to a date certain. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, to postpone Ordinance No. 5453 to the Council meeting of July 24, 2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting yes. Ordinance No. 5454 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute a non­ exclusive Construction and Demolition (C&D) Debris Collection and Disposal Services Franchise Agreement with Coastal Waste & Recycling, Inc. pursuant to Section 14-21, Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5454 Dan Grippo, Municipal Services Director, gave a brief presentation on the ordinance, providing information on revenues received from C&D franchise agreements. He then made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5454. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Jeremy Rodgers voting yes.

units.text: Stephen Walsh noted his appearance at a prior meeting and asked if there was a response to his question regarding the height of single family homes. The City Manager noted that the ban will be reconsidered in October. Council Member O'Rourke addressed the considerations the Council made when debating the ban.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS Boca Raton Community Center, Royal Palm Room Wednesday, May 9, 2018 5:30 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. , Chairman Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang City Manager Leif J. Ahnell Commissioner Erin Wright City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser I. Welcome and Introductions - Mayor Scott Singer and Chairman Bob Rollins Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm . The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics A. Ocean Breeze Golf Course Update Commissioner Robert Rollins, Chairman of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) reviewed the District's interview process for consultants/architects being considered for the Ocean Breeze Golf Course. Details were provided. After narrowing the proposers to a short list of five consultants, Nick Price/Tom Fazio II was selected. He noted that the next step was to draft a consulting agreement and then reviewed the anticipated design and permit timeline. Discussion followed; members of both bodies offered comments. Chairman Rollins confirmed that several public input meetings would be scheduled prior to finalizing the golf course design. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Kevin Wrenne inquired whether any of the proceeds from the sale of the Municipal Golf Course West would go towards the development of the Ocean Breeze golf course property. Joel Buoy, on behalf of the Boca Golf Association, thanked the District for their work in choosing the golf course architect and for listening to the Association's input. Robert DuKate and Harold Chafee offered their thanks for the District's acquisition of the golf course while expressing concerns with the effects a hotel would have on the Boca Teeca neighborhood, increased traffic, and the profitability of the course. Michelle Grau asked about the construction costs and costs of RFP process. Chairman Rollins provided information. David Sergi commented on the profitability of the Red Reef Golf Course. Both Chairman Rollins and City Manager Leif Ahnell provided responses. other members commented. Barry Tetrault asked whether the City Council would agree to help fund the construction of the course. Jessica Gray asked about the possibility of acquiring the properties located at 2500 and 2600 N. Ocean Boulevard. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Chairman Rollins provided further information on the financing of acquisition and development of the golf course. City Manager Ahnell, Commissioner Rollins and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information on the 2500 and 2600 N. Ocean Boulevard properties. Rollins, Jr. , Chairman Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang City Manager Leif J. Ahnell Commissioner Erin Wright City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser I. Welcome and Introductions - Mayor Scott Singer and Chairman Bob Rollins Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm . The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics A. Ocean Breeze Golf Course Update Commissioner Robert Rollins, Chairman of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) reviewed the District's interview process for consultants/architects being considered for the Ocean Breeze Golf Course. Details were provided. After narrowing the proposers to a short list of five consultants, Nick Price/Tom Fazio II was selected. He noted that the next step was to draft a consulting agreement and then reviewed the anticipated design and permit timeline. Discussion followed; members of both bodies offered comments. Chairman Rollins confirmed that several public input meetings would be scheduled prior to finalizing the golf course design. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Kevin Wrenne inquired whether any of the proceeds from the sale of the Municipal Golf Course West would go towards the development of the Ocean Breeze golf course property. Joel Buoy, on behalf of the Boca Golf Association, thanked the District for their work in choosing the golf course architect and for listening to the Association's input. Robert DuKate and Harold Chafee offered their thanks for the District's acquisition of the golf course while expressing concerns with the effects a hotel would have on the Boca Teeca neighborhood, increased traffic, and the profitability of the course. Michelle Grau asked about the construction costs and costs of RFP process. Chairman Rollins provided information. David Sergi commented on the profitability of the Red Reef Golf Course. Both Chairman Rollins and City Manager Leif Ahnell provided responses. other members commented. Barry Tetrault asked whether the City Council would agree to help fund the construction of the course. Jessica Gray asked about the possibility of acquiring the properties located at 2500 and 2600 N. Ocean Boulevard. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Chairman Rollins provided further information on the financing of acquisition and development of the golf course. City Manager Ahnell, Commissioner Rollins and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information on the 2500 and 2600 N. Ocean Boulevard properties. Discussion ensued on a number of topics including , but not limited to, financing , current and future projects, a master interlocal agreement, and the need for more regular joint meetings. Chairman Rollins thanked the members of Boca Golf Association and residents of Boca Teeca for their support and input. IV. Adjournment Mayor Singer thanked everyone for their input. The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 6:42 pm. K thleen Maxwell, Recorder Susan S. Saxton, City Clerk

units.text: Ordinance No. 5455 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton repealing Chapter 19, Code of Ordinances, in its entirety; adopting an updated Chapter 19, Code of Ordinances, entitled "Building Regulations"; adopting the Florida Building Code 6th Edition (2017), and local amendments to the administrative provisions of the Florida Building Code relating to its administration, interpretation, application and enforcement; providing for definitions and applicability; establishing the Code Compliance Division as the Department of Building Safety; providing for the powers and duties of the building official; providing for regulations relating to permit and plan submittal and review, permit issuance, fees, and inspections; providing for regulations relating to occupancy, completion and utility service connections; providing for regulations relating to violations and appeals; providing for the Builders' Board of Adjustment and Appeals; providing for regulations relating to unsafe structures and equipment; adopting local technical amendments relating to flood-resistant design requirements; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-14) Ordinance No. 5455 Chapter 19 - Showing Revisions John Cosmo, Building Official, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Cosmo began with historical information and then reviewed the content of the building code. Information on the permit process was provided. Topics included, but were not limited to, permit application submission, plan review and building inspections, and improved Insurance Service Office rating based on the City's enforcement of the building code. The significant updates in Chapter 19 were highlighted. Mr. Cosmo explained the revision to the table detailing the elevation for buildings. He then made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann complimented the City's building department and commented on insurance rates and residential building height. Kathy Cottrell asked that historical buildings be included. Brandon Schaad addressed the comment about measurement of the height of a home. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer reviewed the revision to the table on page 59 provided by Mr. Cosmo. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5455 as amended. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. Ordinance No. 5456 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 28-1308, Code of Ordinances, to confirm that, in addition to accessory uses, the City may continue to use or place, and to authorize the use and placement of, utilities and infrastructure in city-owned lands adjacent to the intracoastal waterway; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification in the Code of Ordinances; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5456 The City Attorney briefly reviewed the ordinance and then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5456. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: April 4, 2018 Minutes Council Member O'Rourke requested that item 9.H. be removed from the Consent Agenda for consideration separately. units.text: Resolution No. 77-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan amendment to authorize an expansion of the existing outdoor seating area {from approximately 1,157 square feet to approximately 2,140 square feet) for the Grand Lux Cafe, together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655, Code of Ordinances, so that additional parking spaces resulting from the expansion will not be required, for the Town Center at Boca Raton Mall located at 6000 Glades Road: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SC-09-05R2) Resolution No. 77-2018 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the property was provided and relevant background information was reviewed. The site plan showing the proposed outdoor seating area was displayed. Information on the parking requirements resulting from the increased service area was detailed. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval of the site plan. Staff recommended approval of the site plan modifications and the technical deviation related to the number of parking spaces, subject to conditions in the resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to questions from Council members. The public hearing was opened. Bradley Miller, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. He noted that the request would double the amount of outdoor seating and then adressed the technical deviation for parking spaces. Upon concluding, Mr. Miller made himself available for questions. The floor was opened for public input. Seeing no one come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 77-2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: Henry Handler, representing several property owners in the Midtown area, addressed 'glitch bill zoning' and his clients' feelings that such zoning would lead to piecemeal zoning and would drive the parties farther apart. Ed Lepselter commented on the poor exterior condition of the building at 1000 Spanish River Road and noted that he had not heard from the City regarding this situation. He provided pictures for the Council to review. Members commented and asked questions. It was noted that the City Manager would look into the situation. The City Attorney responded to several issues raised by Mr. Handler. She pointed out that the ordinances he referred to would be introduced at this meeting and that two public hearings would follow at which there would be time for public input. She provided further information on the Council's ability to act with regard to legislative matters and addressed glitch zoning.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton expressing concern regarding the Lake Worth Drainage District's proposed L-49 canal clearing project adjacent to the north shore of Sabal Palm Lake in Boca Raton and stating the City's intent to initiate the conflict resolution procedures of Chapter 164, Florida Statutes; specifying the issues of conflict with the District; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Deputy City Manager George Brown presented, noting that this resolution is the result of the discussion at yesterday's Workshop. He reviewed the resolution's content and stated that the resolution would allow further discussion with the District. Details were provided. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown responded to members' questions. He related that the City is not able to tell the District what to do, but is taking this step to facilitate dialog on behalf of the homeowners in their dealings with the District. Mr. Brown and Ms. Frieser provided information on how the process would conclude should the situation be resolved. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Jim Wolf expressed gratitude to the Council and staff for their active participation in this situation. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 84-2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 75-2018 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, to authorize a handicap access ramp approximately 10.6 feet seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL), for a multifamily residential (R-5-A) zoned property located at 750 South Ocean Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-17-10) Resolution No. 75-2018 The City Attorney noted that the quasi judicial rules continued to apply. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The City Code provision regarding the Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) was highlighted and the applicant's request reviewed. It was noted that the handicap ramp was built without a permit. A map of the property was provided, as were the size, zoning and land use. The location of both the CCCL and the handicap ramp on the property were identified. Aerial shots of the property before and after construction of the new ramp were shown. The staff analysis concluded that the new ramp does not impact the beach dune of to sea turtles. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously approved the variance. Staff recommended approval as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Charley Putman, on behalf of the applicant, reviewed the request and referred to an aerial photo to identify the CCCL and the old and new access ramps. He noted that a grade change necessitated the ramp. He invited Michael Hawkins, the contractor, to explain how the permitted installation occurred prior to getting the variance. Mr. Putman then discussed the justification for approval of the ramp, which is required for ADA compliance. It was noted that the ramp empties on to a previously disturbed area. He distributed a letter from the manager of the Sabal Ridge Condominium regarding the importance of the ramp. Upon concluding, Mr. Putman responded to questions. Seeing no one else came forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 75-2018. Members asked several questions of staff and made final comments. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Ingrid Allen provided information. Motion carried on a 3 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no. Code of Ordinances. to allow a freestanding sign approximately 31 feet. four inches in width (where a freestanding sign is limited to a maximum width of 18 feet). and a variance from Section 24-96(b)(3), Code of Ordinances. to allow two (2) flat signs (where only one (1) flat sign is permitted) in the Community Redevelopment Area. for the Boca Raton Museum of Art. located at 501 Plaza Real: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SCV-17-03) Resolution No. 76-2018 The City Attorney confirmed that quasi judicial procedures would continue to govern the hearing. Ms. Golden then explained each variance, providing graphics of the signs and photos identifying their proposed locations. The Community Appearance Board recommended approval of the variances with a condition related to the thickness of a sign cabinet. Staff recommends approval of the variances and supports the applicant's proposed sign cabinet thickness. Ms. Golden provided further justification for the signage requested and then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Margi Nothard with Glavovic Studio and Andy DeVries with Jones Sign, both on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation identifying the need for, location of and details of the proposed signs for the Museum. Ms. Nothard then responded to questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 76-2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

Mr. Putman then discussed the justification for approval of the ramp, which is required for ADA compliance. It was noted that the ramp empties on to a previously disturbed area. He distributed a letter from the manager of the Sabal Ridge Condominium regarding the importance of the ramp. Upon concluding, Mr. Putman responded to questions. Seeing no one else came forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 75-2018. Members asked several questions of staff and made final comments. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Ingrid Allen provided information. Motion carried on a 3 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no. Resolution No. 76-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from Section 24-96(c)(1 ). Code of Ordinances. to allow a freestanding sign approximately 31 feet. four inches in width (where a freestanding sign is limited to a maximum width of 18 feet). and a variance from Section 24-96(b)(3), Code of Ordinances. to allow two (2) flat signs (where only one (1) flat sign is permitted) in the Community Redevelopment Area. for the Boca Raton Museum of Art. located at 501 Plaza Real: providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SCV-17-03) Resolution No. 76-2018 The City Attorney confirmed that quasi judicial procedures would continue to govern the hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Golden, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The variance requests of the Boca Raton Museum of Art were reviewed, and the Code allowances for signage were noted. Ms. Golden then explained each variance, providing graphics of the signs and photos identifying their proposed locations. The Community Appearance Board recommended approval of the variances with a condition related to the thickness of a sign cabinet. Staff recommends approval of the variances and supports the applicant's proposed sign cabinet thickness. Ms. Golden provided further justification for the signage requested and then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Margi Nothard with Glavovic Studio and Andy DeVries with Jones Sign, both on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation identifying the need for, location of and details of the proposed signs for the Museum. Ms. Nothard then responded to questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 76-2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS Boca Raton Community Center, Royal Palm Room Monday, July 23, 2018 5:30 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr., Chairman Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang City Manager Leif J. Ahnell Commissioner Erin Wright City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser Arthur C. Koski, Executive Director Sam Goren, Attorney and Special Counsel I. Welcome and Introductions - Mayor Scott Singer and Chairman Bob Rollins Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:33 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics A. Recreation Needs Assessment Commissioner Robert Rollins, Chairman of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) reviewed the District's proposal to do a recreation needs assessment and hoped the City would share in the cost of the report estimated at $100,000. Michael Kalvort, Recreation Services Director, provided additional information on having a community-wide needs assessment survey, noting that the last time an assessment was performed was in 1987. Discussion followed; members of both bodies offered comments. Mr. Kalvort reviewed the timeline for the process, subject to budget approval. The possibility of piggy-backing on another contract to shorten the RFP process will be researched. B. Golf Course Update Executive Director Art Koski provided background information on the interview process to select a golf course architect. The District hopes to sign a consulting agreement with Price/Fazio at their meeting later tonight. Upon receipt of the agreement, the consultants will begin preparation of a master plan and preliminary designs for the golf course. They hope to begin bidding of the work and commence construction in October of 2018, with anticipated completion of the golf course only in March of 2019. Other amenities would be completed in phases. There will be a minimum of three public hearings to discuss the architect's plans prior to implementation of the final design. Discussion followed; members of both bodies offered comments. C. Gumbo Limbo Master Plan Chairman Rollins noted there was an estimated $200,000 design fee for the master plan. There will be a presentation and discussion on the scope of the plan at the District's August 6, 2018 meeting. City Manager Leif Ahnell added that a summary of the results of the Waterfront Master Plan study conducted by the City's outside consultant was provided to the District. Chair Rollins said their budget was recently amended to complete the renovation of the boardwalk and tower. Lengthy discussion ensued on additional monies needed to complete construction for both Gumbo Limbo and the golf course, and whether the City may be willing to help with the funding or if the District would secure another loan. Discussion returned to the golf course. Topics included, but were not limited to, additional funds needed to complete the construction of the course; the use of the hotel parcel; possible revenue generated by a clubhouse; a partnership with the City to share in the additional costs by contributing proceeds from the City's sale of the western golf course; constrained roadways and traffic concerns; the possible abandonment of Jeffrey Street east of Second Avenue versus the connection of Clint Moore Road and Jeffrey Street; and the redevelopment of the Boca Teeca area. The City Manager noted that the City could begin to plan for further financing for the District. It was agreed to have further discussions on financing when plans are completed and more tangible construction costs for both Gumbo Limbo and the golf course are received. D. Non-resident Fees Chair Rollins began the discussion regarding the definition of non-resident, noting the current non-resident fee of $65 per child per sport and the contribution of non-residents to the sports culture. Other commissioners weighed in. In response to a question, the City Manager stated that the City only recovers a small percentage of the total cost of recreation programs from the fees. Discussion ensued on the definition of non-resident and the equitability of fees. District staff has been directed to meet with City staff to work on standardizing rental fees across the different recreational facilities. There was further discussion of residents versus non-residents on sports teams, a fee cap or a reduced rate for families with multiple children or children playing multiple sports, and some consideration for events for employees of local businesses. Michael Kalvort provided additional information and confirmed that the rate for non-residents was approximately 25% above the resident fee and that residents felt that the fee schedule was very convoluted. After continued discussion, it was agreed to have staff from both bodies review all the recreation fees, both City and District, and bring back a recommendation that would standardize them .. Ill. Public Comment The public comment period was opened. Michelle Peel, on behalf of Friends of Gumbo Limbo, spoke in support of the Gumbo Limbo Master Plan. Robert DuKate thanked everyone for their support of the golf course and offered support of the investment of funds at Gumbo Limbo, wider sidewalks and having a recreational facility as opposed to a hotel at the golf course. Susan Caruso spoke in support of Gumbo Limbo. Julian Louvet commented on the vegetation clearing along the L-48 canal and hoped for beautification projects along that corridor. Mayor Singer responded that the Lake Worth Drainage District has suspended further clearing on the canals within the City. Linda Sturdy supported the City and the District working together to benefit Gumbo Limbo. Earl Starkoff provided his thoughts on the non-resident fees. Darlene Ward supported allocating funds to update and improve Gumbo Limbo. Doug Coller spoke against having a hotel at the golf course and extending Jeffrey Street. Lenore Wachtel felt monies from the sale of the western golf course should go towards funding the golf course and enhancing Gumbo Limbo. Harold Chaffee asked the City to provide a portion of the funds to the District for construction of the golf course. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Members discussed a future joint meeting and asked staff to check for a date in September. Topics also nd included the beautification of the entrance to Boca Teeca along NW 2 Avenue, the design fee for phase 2 of the Spanish River/DeHoernle project to commence in 2021, an agreement between the City and the Friends of Gumbo Limbo to allow the opportunity for naming rights in some form and a master local agreement. IV. Adjournment Mayor Singer thanked everyone for their input. The meeting was adjourned without objection at ly 8:11 pm. Joint Meeting Minutes July 23, 2018 Page 2

units.text: April 26, 2018 April 26, 2018 Disability May 24, 2018 Minutes Mayor Singer provided an opportunity for public input on any Consent Agenda item. He then called attention to consent item 9.P., Resolution 98-2018 concerning the dispute resolution procedures with the Lake Worth Drainage District and asked that it be removed from the Consent Agenda as Comment Cards had been submitted to speak on this item. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to remove item 9.P., Resolution No. 98-2018 from the Consent Agenda as amended. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member O'Rourke pointed out items 9.K., L.,M.,N.,O., resolutions concerning reimbursement to the City for beach renourishment. As there was a request for public comment on item 9.Q., Mayor Singer suggested it be removed from the Consent Agenda. removed from consent JR and MM seconded, unanimous voice vote Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to remove item 9.Q., Resolution No. 99-2018 from the Consent Agenda as amended. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve the Consent Agenda as amended. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Resolution No. 98-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton expressing concern regarding the Lake Worth Drainage District's proposed L-48, L-49, and L-50 canal clearing projects in Boca Raton; stating the City's intent to initiate the conflict resolution procedures of Chapter 164, Florida Statutes: specifying the issues of conflict with the District; incorporating the provisions of Resolution No. 84-2018 (adopted June 12, 2018} and establishing the effective date of this resolution as controlling for procedural purposes; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 98-2018 The public hearing was opened. Mike Jurus commented on the function of the Lake Worth Drainage District and posed several questions. Jane Jurus thanked the Mayor for his outreach and made further comments. Sherri Croyle commented on the function of the District and provided a handout with several pictures. She contended that the L-50 canal should be dealt with differently and should not be a part of this resolution. Linda Slate spoke about Sabal Palm Lake, the L-49 canal, and the District's ownership of easements on same. John McPhail commented on the District's claim of a cloud on the title to his property and asked for assistance dealing with the District. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 98-2018. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes. Resolution No. 99-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the City Manager to execute Work Order No. 2 with Applied Technology and Management, Inc. for the purpose of developing detailed design documents, and for the development and submittal of State and Federal Permit applications associated with the Rutherford Park and Lake Wyman Park Restoration Project; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 99-2018 The City Manager briefly reviewed the resolution. The public hearing was opened. Frank Duemmler commented on a canal bordering his property and Lake Wyman Park. He requested clarification of tasks in the work order. The City Manager provided information. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 99-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Master Plan (Resolution No. 37-88. as amended by Resolution No. 164-2005) for Hillsboro El Rio Park. located at 400 Southwest 18th Street to add and remove certain park features and amenities: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SC-18-04) Resolution No. 88-2018 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on the park, as well as the location, land use and zoning of the site were provided. Ms. Allen reviewed the proposed master plan noting elements being removed, such as a fishing pier and boardwalk, and new items being added, including sports courts and a non-motorized boat launch. Ms. Allen stated the Parks and Recreation Board unanimously approved the proposed master plan; Staff recommends approval as well. Upon concluding, she responded to questions about a submerged barge in the canal. Ms. Allen advised that the barge was within the jurisdiction of the Lake Worth Drainage District. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 88-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 109-2018 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Blue Martini Boca LLC for a settlement and reduction of two (2) code enforcement liens imposed against property located at 6000 Glades Rd #C1380; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 109-2018 Doug Sheedy, Code Compliance Manager, gave a brief presentation, providing background information on the code violations and circumstances to date, noting that Staff does not support the lien reduction. He then made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Scott Topolski, attorney on behalf of Blue Martini, provided details of the nine alleged violations and liens imposed by the Special Magistrate, noting that Blue Martini has an appeal pending on this matter before the Palm Beach County Circuit Court and making his case for the reduction. Mr. Topolski then responded to Council members' questions, as did Staff. Bob Ziegler, a resident of Via Verde, reviewed the violations and the effect of the loud noise on nearby neighborhoods over a number of years. He thanked the City Council and City Staff for their assistance throughout this issue. In conclusion, he requested that the fines not be reduced. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to adopt Resolution No. 109-2018 to deny the lien reduction request. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5461 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Code of Ordinances to establish two new zoning districts within Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Chapter 28, Zoning, Code of Ordinances, by creating a new Division 11, "City CG Commercial General." and Division 12. "City CHO Commercial High Office," which districts incorporate Palm Beach County's regulations (in effect on April 23, 2002) for the CG General Commercial district and CHO Commercial High Office district, respectively, except as specified, and expressly providing a list of permitted and conditional uses for the new districts; amending Section 28-301(c), to include the new districts; amending Section 28-307(1 ), to specify the building intensity; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-1£) Ordinance No. 5461 ~ Ordinance No. 5462 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering rezoning property annexed into the City in 2003 (generally located south of Glades Road. east of St. Andrews Boulevard, north of the Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 and L-47 Canals, and west of Interstate 95) consisting of (i) 215.02 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CG General Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CG Commercial General," (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith), and (ii) 26.90 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CHO Commercial High Office District (formerly Palm Beach County CS Specialized Commercial District) pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CHO Commercial High Office" (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith); providing for revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-16-01) Ordinance No. 5462 Mayor Singer noted that this first of two public hearings on items A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the ordinances were related. No vote would be taken on either ordinance. Development Services Planner Elizabeth Eassa gave the PowerPoint presentation on the City-initiated ordinances that would create two new zoning districts and rezone certain annexed land in the southwest planning area into these new zoning districts. Background information was provided. Ms. Eassa went on to outline the provisions of the ordinances. Modifications regarding outdoor restaurant seating and proximity of establishments to residential properties were also covered. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended approval. Staff recommends approval of both ordinances. Upon concluding, Ms. Eassa responded to members' questions, as did Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director. The public hearing was opened. Henry Handler, attorney representing several property owners in the Midtown area, noted his clients' opposition to the ordinances. Referring to the lawsuits his clients had filed against the City, Mr. Handler offered his opinion that the lack of comprehensive planning for Midtown had adversely affected his clients. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer again noted that no vote would be taken at this meeting and that the second public hearing would be on September 12. In response to a request from Deputy Mayor Rodgers, the City Attorney responded to a number of Mr. Handler's comments. Ms. Frieser noted that the proposed ordinance takes existing zoning and makes it part of the City's zoning code. She then addressed several other comments made by Mr. Handler. Council members made final comments.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering rezoning property annexed into the City in 2003 (generally located south of Glades Road, east of St. Andrews Boulevard, north of the Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 and L-47 Canals, and west of Interstate 95) consisting of (i) 215.02 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CG General Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CG Commercial General," (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith), and (ii) 26.90 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CHO Commercial High Office District (formerly Palm Beach County CS Specialized Commercial District) pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CHO Commercial High Office" (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith); providing for revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-16-01) Ordinance No. 5462 Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the ordinances were related and that this second of two public hearings and a separate vote would be taken on each ordinance. After the Clerk read the titles of the ordinances, Mayor Singer pointed out that several stakeholders in the Midtown area had requested a postponement of the public hearing in order to work out parking issues. He then provided an opportunity for those people who had submitted a public comment card. Stuart Miesel noted that his presentation could also be postponed. Council members briefly discussed a postponement to which there was no objection. Mayor Singer then gave a brief overview of the situation and provided an opportunity for any other public input. No one else came forward to speak. In light of a postponement, there was no staff presentation. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, stated that a postponement to October 23 would provide ample time to address the issues. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to postpone the public hearings on Ordinance No. 5461 and Ordinance No. 5462 to the meeting of October 23, 2018. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. units.text: Mayor Scott Singer Deputy Jeremy Rodgers Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Council Member Monica Mayotte Council Member Andy Thomson PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: City Manager Leif Ahnell gave PowerPoint presentations on the proposed budget and millage rate as well as the proposed Capital Improvements Program.· The City's guiding principles - Financially Sound City, World Class Municipal Services, Strong Partnership with Community, and Vibrant and Sustainable City - were reviewed, noting the policy priorities associated with these principles. Changes to the general fund operating costs for the 2018-19 fiscal year were highlighted, as were new personnel and programs. Various charts and tables were presented illustrating year-over-year millage rates and assessed property valuations; allocation of operating expenses; and comparison of Boca Raton to other cities' fire assessment fee, property tax rates, and water/sewer rates. The presentation was then turned over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2018-19 portion of the six-year Capital Improvements Program. Highlights of various infrastructure, vehicles, technology updates and renovations requested by City departments were provided. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire responded to several questions, as did the City Manager.

City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a PowerPoint presentation on the 2018-19 budget. He provided an overview of change in millage rates and assessed property valuations and the identified the increase in general operating expenses and new personnel and programs proposed for the coming year. Various charts and graphs were presented illustrating favorable comparisons of Boca Raton to other city's fire assessment fees, property tax rates and water/sewer rates. The breakdown of the general fund program budget and the tax rate history were also discussed. Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, then reviewed the operating and capital improvement rebudgeted items, listed in Exhibit 1, which did not happen this year and will be carried over to the 2018-19 fiscal year budget. units.header: City Council shall amend the adopted tentative budget as it sees fit
units.text: Mayor Singer commented on the Non-Profit Funding Requests process. Members discussed changes to the funding list that each member had proposed. Individual asks were reviewed and changes were proposed. Working from the Mayor's list, changes were agreed to, resulting in an increase of $8,500 to the total amount of non-profit funding amount proposed by the Mayor. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to amend the budget to include the FY2019 Non-Profit Organization Funding Requests as stated. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member ORourke asked for an amount to be dedicated to the Art in Public Places, which would fund special events and continue the enthusiasm for this initiative. Discussion ensued. City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Meimber Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend the budget to include $25,000 in funding to continue the Art in Public Places initiative (Exhibit 2). Motion carried on a voice vote. In response to Council Member Mayotte's questions, the City Manager provided information about funding for the Beach and Park District, the FAU Research Park and the Tech Runway. Council members briefly discussed funding for needed upgrades to Town Hall that will be requested by the Historical Society.
