units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton creating Article X, Chapter 17, Code of Ordinances; establishing fertilizer use regulations pursuant to the requirements of Florida Statutes; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ordinance No. 5469 Mo Morel, City Civil Engineer, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Morel discussed impacts of excessive nutrients on bodies of water and the resulting requirement of local governments to adopt a fertilizer ordinance. The provisions of the ordinance were outlined, including regulating the proper use of fertilizer, training and licensing requirements, and establishing fertilizer free zones. Mr. Morel responded to questions and comments by members. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5469. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. il: REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS: There was no business to consider.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to a Planned Unit Development (PUD) with a master plan (previously approved by Resolution No. 77-2006) for the Lago Mar PUD located at 945-965 Lago Mar Lane, to eliminate a condition requiring a six (6) foot solid wall on the west property line north of Lago Mar Lane; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PUD-05-03R1) Resolution No. 137-2018 Drawings The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the petitioner's request. The location, zoning and future land use of the property were identified. The current site plan and approved master plan were reviewed, as were resultant changes to the property due to the wall's removal. Comments of a neighbor opposing the change were noted. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the petition. Staff also recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Derek Vander Ploeg, architect for the petitioner, provided background information on the property. The proposed changes were reviewed, and it was noted that if the home were sold in the future, the owner agreed to restore the wall. He then made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 137-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal by the Carlton Condominium Association of the decision of the Community Appearance Board approving, with conditions, the exterior painting of the building located at 901 East Camino Real; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 140-2018 The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Acting Deputy Director of Development Services, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Bell briefly reviewed the appeal, showing pictures and examples of proposed paint colors. He presented the appellant's argument and advised that the Community Appearance Board (CAB) was operating within its purview. Mr. Bell reviewed the options before Council and stated that staff recommended the CAB's decision be upheld and the appeal denied. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Ellyn Bogdanoff, on behalf of the appellant, provided pictures and paint color chips for the Council to review. Upon concluding, she responded to questions. Mark Jacobson, CAB chair, provided information on the Board's decision and responded to questions from members, clarifying the location of the banding on the building. Nicky Siegel, resident of the Carlton, commented on the color choices. There was no cross examination. Ms. Bogdanoff made comments in rebuttal. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 140-2018 to grant the appeal. Members asked several questions of staff and made final comments. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Code of Ordinances to establish two new zoning districts within Article XI, Business and Commercial Districts, Chapter 28, Zoning, Code of Ordinances, by creating a new Division 11, "City CG Commercial General," and Division 12, "City CHO Commercial High Office," which districts incorporate Palm Beach County's regulations (in effect on April 23. 2002) for the CG General Commercial district and CHO Commercial High Office district, respectively. except as specified, and expressly providing a list of permitted and conditional uses for the new districts; amending Section 28-301 (c), to include the new districts; amending Section 28-307(1 ), to specify the building intensity; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-16-11) Ordinance No. 5461 Ordinance No. 5462 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering rezoning property annexed into the City in 2003 (generally located south of Glades Road. east of St. Andrews Boulevard, north of the Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 and L-47 Canals, and west of Interstate 95) consisting of (i) 215.02 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CG General Commercial District pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CG Commercial General." (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith), and (ii) 26.90 acres (more or less) of property to be rezoned from CHO Commercial High Office District (formerly Palm Beach County CS Specialized Commercial District) pursuant to the Palm Beach County Code to "City CHO Commercial High Office" (a new City zoning district being considered contemporaneously herewith); providing for revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-16-01) Ordinance No. 5462 Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items A and B would be conducted contemporaneously as the ordinances are related. A separate vote would be taken on each ordinance. Elizabeth Eassa, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that the ordinances are not part of the Midtown Small Area Plan. Provisions of the ordinances were discussed, including creation of the CG and CHO zoning districts and corresponding regulations. Permitted and conditional uses were reviewed, as well as regulations for mall parking, which include a three-step process for calculating the parking rate. Building height and additional changes were covered. Staff recommended approval. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann, representing property owners in the affected area, relayed concerns with components of the proposed ordinances, including parking, the County ULDC and the original annexation agreements. Mayor Singer asked staff to clarify points mentioned by Mr. Gromann. Deputy City Manager George Brown provided information regarding zoning designations, specifically CGSE (Commercial General Special Exception). Bonnie Miskell commented on behalf of the Simon Group, thanking staff for their work and requesting two changes regarding parking. Michael Marshall, Gunster Law Firm, suggested additional clarification to language in the ordinances. Mr. Brown and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided information. Discussion ensued. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. The meeting was recessed at approximately 7:38 pm and reconvened at approximately 7:49 pm. The City Attorney read new language into the record, identifying pages and line numbers in Ordinance No. 5461, which addressed the concerns expressed related to parking. She then addressed previous comments regarding the annexation agreements. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5461 as revised and amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5462. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute an agreement with the Mizner Park Cultural Arts Association, Inc. for the purpose of providing funding assistance for theater and gallery upgrades and replacement of equipment; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 157-2018 City Manager Leif Ahnell reviewed the budget amendment ordinance and the resolution requesting a grant to cover the costs of repairs and equipment at the Cultural Arts Center. The public hearing was opened. David Sergi commented on amount of money being requested. At the request of Mayor Singer, Mizner Park Cultural Arts Association (MPCAA) Board Member Peg Anderson provided information regarding scheduled events, use of space and the needed renovations. In response to members' questions, Mr. Ahnell provided a brief history of the MPCAA. Discussion ensued. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5472. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Members made final comments regarding the MPCAA Board and expressed a desire for more open communication. The City Attorney suggested that a letter could be written to the Board outlining the Councils' concerns. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No.157-2018. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. ll:_ REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS: There was no business to consider.

units.text: Resolution No. 150-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a variance from Section 24-78(a), Code of Ordinances, to allow a 60 square foot flat sign in lieu of the maximum allowed area of a flat sign of 32 square feet for the Islamic Center of Boca Raton, located at 3480 Northwest 5th Avenue: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SCV-17-01} Resolution No. 150-2018 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Golden, Land Development Coordinator, gave a PowerPoint presentation . She provided background information, noting that the sign had been installed without a permit. A description of the sign, its dimensions, and location on the property were provided. The Community Appearance Board (CAB) denied the application. Staff recommended approval of the variance. Ms. Golden then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Rim Maclaren presented on behalf of the petitioner and provided the history of how the sign came to be installed without a permit. Mark Jacobsen, speaking on behalf of the CAB, reviewed the reasons why the board denied the variance. Mr. Jacobsen made himself available for questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Mr. Maclaren made final comments, addressed the reasons his client was asking for the variance, and requested approval. The public hearing was closed. Members made final comments. There was discussion of the necessity of the applicant going back to CAB for approval of the permit. Ms. Frieser noted that in Section 2 of the resolution, the second condition would be removed so that it would not be required for the applicant to get CAB approval of the permit. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 150-2018 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes . .1!. CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS: The City Manager had no reports. ~ CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS: The City Attorney had no reports.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing a Fifth Amendment to the Agreement for Purchase and Sale dated November 27, 2017, by and between the City of Boca Raton and G.L. Acquisitions Corporation for the purchase and sale of the City of Boca Raton Municipal Golf Course West, as authorized by Ordinance No. 541 O; authorizing a fifth extension of the inspection period; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The public hearings on Ordinance No. 5474 and Resolution No. 163-2018 will be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related. Ordinance No. 5473 George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation. A brief history of the sale of the property was provided. Details of the retention and construction of cell towers were reviewed. Potential modifications to the contract were presented. Staff recommended approval of the extension. Mr. Brown and Mr. Ahnell responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Larry Portnoy, speaking on behalf of GL Homes, emphasized that GL Homes was prepared to close on the sale. He noted that the inspection date extensions allowed for resolution of issues that have come up and assured the Council that GL Homes will work with the City on continuity of golf in Boca Raton. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5473. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Ordinance No. 5474 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Section 9-60, "Supplemental Code Enforcement Procedures," Article IV, Chapter 9, Code of Ordinances, to provide for the enforcement of the Code of Ordinances by issuance of citations by code enforcement officers directly to individual violators; providing for procedures for the issuance of such citations; providing procedures to contest citations; setting forth minimum and maximum civil penalties for violations enforced pursuant to such citations, including contested citations; providing for severability; providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-18- .@ Ordinance No. 5474 1 Resolution No. 163-2018 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering adoption of a Schedule of Minimum Civil Penalties applicable to violations of the Code of Ordinances enforced by the issuance of citations directly to individuals pursuant to Section 9-60, "Supplemental Code Enforcement Procedures," Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 163-2018 Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave a PowerPoint presentation. An overview of the ordinance was provided, including options for violators. The necessity for direct citations was discussed, as was the types of violations that would be enforced by this ordinance. Mr. Schaad then made himself available for questions. Doug Sheedy, Code Compliance Manager, provided information. The public hearing was opened. Robert Eisen expressed doubt that direct ticketing would work within the City and questioned several line items within the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Schaad and Diane Grub Frieser, City Attorney, responded to previous comments and provided additional information. A brief discussion followed. Mayor Singer requested that a fine for littering on waterways be added to the schedule of fines in Resolution No. 163-2018. Ms. Frieser read language into the record to address a fine for littering on canals, lakes and bodies of water. Ordinance No. 5473 George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation. A brief history of the sale of the property was provided. Details of the retention and construction of cell towers were reviewed. Potential modifications to the contract were presented. Staff recommended approval of the extension. Mr. Brown and Mr. Ahnell responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Larry Portnoy, speaking on behalf of GL Homes, emphasized that GL Homes was prepared to close on the sale. He noted that the inspection date extensions allowed for resolution of issues that have come up and assured the Council that GL Homes will work with the City on continuity of golf in Boca Raton. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5473. It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a "relative" includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A "business associate" means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joint venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). ELECTED OFFICERS: In addition to abstaining from voting in the situations described above, you must disclose the conflict: PRIOR TO THE VOTE BEING TAKEN by publicly stating to the assembly the nature of your interest in the measure on which you are abstaining from voting; and WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER THE VOTE OCCURS by completing and filing this form with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who should incorporate the form in the minutes. APPOINTED OFFICERS: Although you must abstain from voting in the situations described above, you are not prohibited by Section 112.3143 from otherwise participating in these matters. However, you must disclose the nature of the conflict before making any attempt to influence the decision, whether orally or in writing and whether made by you or at your direction. IF YOU INTEND TO MAKE ANY ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION PRIOR TO THE MEETING AT WHICH THE VOTE WILL BE TAKEN: • You must complete and file this form (before making any attempt to influence the decision) with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who will incorporate the form in the minutes. APPOINTED OFFICERS (continued) • A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency. • The form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. IF YOU MAKE NO ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION EXCEPT BY DISCUSSION AT THE MEETING • You must disclose orally the nature of your conflict in the measure before participating. • You must complete the form and file it within 15 days after the vote occurs with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who must incorporate the form in the minutes. A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the agency, and the form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. Ele Zachariades, on the behalf of the applicant, noted that she did not need to make a presentation. Seeing no one else came forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, authorizing Planned Mobility Development in the City CG Commercial General, City CHO Commercial High Office, R-B-1 Motel-Business and POI Professional, Office and Institutional zoning districts: providing applicable development regulations for Planned Mobility Development: amending Section 28-307(1 ), to specify a maximum floor area ratio of 0.50 for Planned Mobility Developments in certain districts: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-18-08) Ordinance No. 5476 Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The southwest planning area that would be affected by the implementation of the planned mobility regulations was identified. Comprehensive Plan objectives and policies that are applicable to this area were reviewed. Background information on staffs work to date related to the southwest planned mobility area was presented. Mr. Schaad discussed the small area plan, noting that the proposed ordinance reflects many of the concepts identified during the planning process for the plan. The PMD regulations were reviewed and explained. Topics included, but were not limited to, street types and designs, building setbacks and height, building step-backs, glazing requirements, valet and street parking, surface parking lots, open space, and transit. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval as well. Mr. Schaad noted that the Planning and Zoning Board asked that staff provide information on a funding mechanism for infrastructure improvements. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, speaking on behalf of Cypress Realty, addressed the ordinance's consistency, or lack thereof, with the Comprehensive Plan. He stated his belief that the southwest area needs to have a mixed use in order to support a walkable environment. Gene Folden commented on the width of type A roadways and asked that roads not be narrowed and that parking spaces not be made smaller. Seeing no one else came forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Schaad responded to previous comments and emphasized that the ordinance is intended to promote a pedestrian friendly area. He then responded to members' questions. The City Attorney responded to comments made by Mr. Marshall, disagreeing with his assertions with regard to the Comprehensive Plan. She provided additional information. Members asked further questions of Mr. Schaad. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5476. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Resolution No. 8-2019 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the conditional use approval for the Jog Road Center, approved by Resolution No. 50-92 to increase the maximum restaurant square footage from 3,000 square feet to approximately 5,160 square feet, to authorize approximately 4,230 square feet of professional office space and approximately 3,000 square feet of personal services space, and to decrease the maximum retail square footage from 20,304 square feet to approximately 11,710 square feet; for the Jog Road Center located at 2901 and 2911 Clint Moore Road; providing for repealer, providing an effective date {CA-91-13R1) Resolution No. 8-2019 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman, Senior Planner, gave a PowerPoint presentation beginning with a review of the petition and the location and zoning of the property. Background information was provided and the site plan was reviewed. Parking and traffic impacts were discussed. The Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval as well. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Craig McDonald, Corporate Property Services on behalf of the petitioner, made very brief remarks in support of the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 8-2019. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte announced the dates for the Oasis Championship and commented on the mural art at Red Reef Park. She then commented on a resident's email regarding the Lake Worth Drainage District. The City Manager provided information. Mayor Singer weighed in with regard to the Lake Worth Drainage District. Council Member O'Rourke provided information on the art murals and tunnels at Spanish River Park that will be painted. She then highlighted upcoming events Downtown Mayor Singer commented on the retirement of Deputy City Clerk Diane King and highlighted the Wings of Freedom program. He also announced an upcoming town hall that he will host. th Mayor Singer then gave a presentation on his attendance at the Mayors' Institute on City Design at which the 20 Street and University district area was chosen for review by other mayors and professionals who shared their input based on their experiences. Recommendations were made to enhance the public realm by creating a walkable, attractive street. There were also recommendations for the FAU gateway and the private parcels along the corridor. Members weighed in. Discussion followed with regard to next steps. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, responded to questions and provided information. The City Manager noted that timing of moving ahead may be affected by FAU's master planning. Discussion continued. In general, members seemed to th be in favor of a complete streets approach along 20 Street.

units.text: Resolution No. 9-2019 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton acknowledging an existing business/technical school as an established conditional use pursuant to Section 28-719, Code of Ordinances, and considering modifications to an existing conditional use for the property located at 414 Northwest 35th Street; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-18-04) Resolution No. 9-2019 The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Development Services Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed the application, identified the location and zoning of the property, and provided details of the history of the use of the property. The proposed project was described in detail. Mr. Bell then presented staff's analysis of the proposed conditional use. There followed diagrams illustrating the survey of the property, floor plan of the building, the location of the alley abandonment, and the site plan. It was noted that there were no impacts to traffic the parking requirements were met. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with conditions. Staff recommended approval as well. The public hearing was opened. Gilbert Hyppolite and Tia Phillips, Techni-Pro Institute Campus Director, offered support of the project. Delilah Bartocome, consultant for dialysis center, assured Council that the center would be in compliance. Belzoria White, Techni-Pro clinical coordinator, offered her support of the project and addressed traffic concerns. No one else came forward. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. The public hearing was closed Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 9-2019. Members made final comments. The City Attorney reminded members that the resolution contained the Planning and Zoning Board conditions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Gaddis Properties LLC for a settlement and reduction of one code enforcement lien imposed against property located at 200 East Boca Raton Road; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 1-2019 Doug Sheedy, Code Compliance Manager, gave a brief presentation. He explained the request of the owner for a reduction of the lien and noted that staff does not support a reduction of the lien. Hans Huang, chief legal officer for Kaufman Lynn Construction, tenant of the property, noted that he was appearing on behalf of a number of entities involved in this matter. He asked that the City assist in getting the Gaddis property converted into a parking lot. Michael Doyle, Kaufman Lynn project manager for Tower 155, noted the company's cooperation at every step of the process for using the property as a parking lot and addressed the lengthy time for a hearing on their request. He stated his objection to the imposition of back-dated fines and stressed the fact that the site had been restored quickly. Mr. Doyle asked for a reduction based on this timing. Mr. Huang provided a handout of an email exchange and further information on the lengthy process. Derek Vander Ploeg provided background information on the lease of the property for use by Tower 155 as a parking lot. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. In response to questions, Doug Sheedy gave further details of the timeframe for imposition of the fines. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information on the timing. Mr. Huang responded to a previous comment on scheduling of a hearing regarding the lot, and answered further questions about timing, as did Mr. Schaad. Members began a discussion of the request. Deputy Mayor Rodgers suggested a reduction, perhaps to $20,000. Council Member Thomson suggested a reduction of the fine to $10,000. Mayor Singer suggested a fine of $49,000. Further discussion ensued. Members agreed that the lien should be reduced by $21,220 to $40,000 to be paid within 15 days. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 1-2019 reducing the lien as stated. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying Modernizing Medicine lnc.'s requested wall sign (Permit No. 18-9195) located at 4850 Network Way; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Resolution No. 21-2019 Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the property was identified and information on the signage and location of same was provided. Mr. Schaad discussed the Community Appearance Board (CAB) review and denial of the sign permit and the appellant's argument for granting the appeal. He then presented staff's analysis that addressed compliance of the sign with the Code, historical precedent, and CAB's authority. Staff recommended reversing the decision of CAB and approving the sign permit as submitted. Upon concluding, he responded to questions. Jennifer Ronneburger and Kathleen Bocek, Senior Vice President of Modernizing Medicine, noted that the petitioner agreed with the staff presentation. Mark Jacobsen, CAB chair, offered in detail CAB's rationale for the denial of this sign which was to be placed on a building that is architecturally significant. He then responded to questions from members. Doug Mummaw provided a handout and commented on the significance of the building on which the sign is proposed to be placed. He suggested that the sign should be iconic and detached from the building. Danielle Vennett, BRIC General Manager, addressed the concerns expressed about the building. She commented on the importance of Modernizing Medicine and its importance to the City. She asked that all this be taken into consideration. During cross examination, Mark Jacobsen questioned Doug Mummaw, suggesting that a sign could be free standing. Ms. Vennett also questioned Mr. Mummaw on his suggestion regarding a free standing sign. Mr. Mummaw responded. Jennifer Ronneburger offered rebuttal on behalf of the petitioner. She addressed the attachment of the sign to the building as well as other points made by Mr. Jacobsen. Kathleen Bocek addressed the historic value of the building and the need for a business sign, noting that Modernizing Medicine wants to be a good corporate citizen. She asked that the Council allow them to put up the sign. Brandon Schaad responded to Council members' questions. Members commented on the petition and offered their opinions. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 21-2019 to reverse the decision of the Community Appearance Board granting the appeal. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a tentative plat for Royal Palm Polo Plat Four (a replat of: a portion of Royal Palm Polo Plat Two, all of Lots 64-123, together with all of Tract R2 and Tract W4, as recorded in Plat Book 122, pages 105 through 111; together with Lots 94 through 98 of Block 2 and a portion of Tract R, Royal Palm Polo, as recorded in Plat Book 117, pages 194 through 200), generally located at 6300 Old Clint Moore Road; subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-13-02R2/SUB) Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items A, B, C, and D would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related, and a separate vote would be taken on the ordinance and each resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Elizabeth Eassa, Development Services Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The request was reviewed, the location of the property was identified, and background information was provided. Topics included, but were not limited to, the site plan amendment, the PUD modification, the tentative plat approval, and traffic impacts. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the application. Staff also recommended approval. Ms. Eassa noted that a new condition related to the school concurrency (SCAD) voluntary contribution was included in Resolution No. 17-2019, the site amendment. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Jeff Brophy, WGI, advocated for approval of the petitions on behalf of the applicant. He noted that the applicant was in agreement with the condition regarding the school concurrency voluntary contribution. He then responded to questions from Council members. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5479. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.text: Resolution No. 22-2019 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a four-story, approximately 49 feet tall, 14,270 square foot duplex residence seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance). for a residential (R-3-F) zoned property located at 2600 North Ocean Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-16-08) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The Code provisions related to the CCCL were reviewed. The location of the subject site was provided as were renderings and other details of the proposed building. Mr. Schaad then reviewed the major environmental issues associated with this proposed project. Topics included, but were not limited to, sea turtle nesting data, dune vegetation impacts, and potential issues from storms and flooding. An evaluation of the applicant's response to variance criteria was outlined. Staff recommends denial of the request for this variance. It was noted that the EAB recommended denial as well. Mr. Schaad then responded to several comments made by the applicant at the EAB meeting. The public hearing was opened. Robert Sweetapple, on behalf of the petitioner, offered a number of emails and a video to illustrate his claim that certain members should refrain from voting on the variance request. He then asked that three members recuse themselves. Mayor Singer, Council Members O'Rourke and Mayotte responded to Mr. Sweetapple's comments and declined to recuse themselves. Mr. Sweetapple then made his opening statement. He responded to several of Mr. Schaad's contentions. Topics included the FDEP permit, maps of natural lands within the City, response number of the statements made in staff's report, the City's beach lighting code, the building size, and Dr. Kirt Rusenko's expertise on sea turtles. Mr. Sweetapple asked that Dr. Rusenko be cross examined. The City Attorney reviewed the cross-examination procedures. Mr. Sweetapple asked Dr. Rusenko a number of questions centering on the lighting at the beach and its effect on turtle hatchlings. Mr. Sweetapple then introduced Juan Caycedo, architect of the project. Mr. Caycedo gave a brief PowerPoint, discussing the design of the building and its location on the lot. The project engineer, Bill Stoddard, then addressed the work done with the FDEP to establish the building footprint and the resulting design restraints. Bonnie Miskel, attorney on behalf of the applicant, addressed the requested variance from the CCCL and her contention that the criteria for said variance have been met. Historical information was provided. After a brief discussion regarding additional time, Ms. Miskel continued her presentation. Tom Tomasello, attorney, asserted his familiarity with the CCCL variance process with FDEP and the need for the City to issue a letter. He presented into evidence an email from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission regarding the site's effects on turtles. Emily Gentile, Jan Grennell, Kevin Meaney, David Ofstein, Mark Mannix, Faith Goldstein, Robert Denman, Joe Graubart, Tricia Krefetz, Susie Cox, Richard Rose, Ryan Abrams, Jessica Gray, Michael Lazio, Stewart Byrne, Dinath Rose, and Sue Merril all spoke in opposition to the project and in favor of preserving the beaches. Mr. Sweetapple requested to cross examine Tricia Krefetz with regard to her testimony. Mr. Michael Lazio asked to cross examine Mr. Sweetapple about his client's knowledge of the CCCL. There was no rebuttal. The public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer stated his opinion and moved to adopt the resolution to deny the variance. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 22-2019 to deny granting the variance. The City Attorney addressed a number of the comments made regarding the CCCL, quasi-judicial procedures vs. judicial procedures, and evidence presented during the hearing. Members made final comments and stated their positions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: There was no business to consider. jb REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS: Ordinance No. 5481 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1. Section 28-1302, "Car Agencies," Code of Ordinances, to delete the requirement that a car agency be enclosed by a six foot high masonry wall; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-18-07) Elizabeth Eassa, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background information on the code was reviewed and analysis of the amendment was provided. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval as well. Ms. Eassa responded to Council members' questions, as did Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, and Diana Grub Frieser, City Attorney. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw spoke on behalf of the applicant and suggested postponement due to new information. Mr. Mummaw addressed the original zoning regulation from 1965 and how needs have changed, and explained the rationale behind the request to eliminate the wall requirement. He advised that boutique dealers operating within the City would be impacted by the Code change. He then responded to questions. Mr. Schaad and Ms. Frieser provided additional information. Jim Wood inquired about enforcement of this Code change. Mr. Schaad, Ms. Frieser and City Manager Leif Ahnell provided information regarding enforcement. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued . Mr. Schaad and Ms. Frieser addressed property buffers and allowable variances permitted under the Code and provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to continue Ordinance No. 5481 to the meeting of April 23, 2019. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote: Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. 13. REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS:. There was no business to consider. 14. PUBLIC REQUESTS:. Briann Harms, Interim Director for the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District, commented on the desire of the District to collaborate with the City on upcoming projects. She then responded to Council members' questions.

There was no objection. Mayor Singer then provided an opportunity for public input on any other Consent Agenda item. No one came forward to speak. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve the Consent Agenda as amended. Horticultural Products; Requested by Recreation Services; Diamond R. Fertilizer Co. Inc., Helena Agri-Enterprises LLC; (formerly known as Helena Chemical Company); SiteOne Landscape Supply; $235,918 Council Member Mayotte thanked Recreation Services staff for their efforts to reduce the use of pesticides in City parks and encouraged continued action. Council Member O'Rourke asked for additional information from staff. Recreation Services Director Michael Kalvort updated members regarding staff efforts such as manual hoeing. He also noted that the steam machine vendor has thus far not accommodated the request for testing. Mayor Singer shared that City staff had made inquiries to other cities as to how they are addressing the issue. Mr. Kalvort added that he recently attended a state conference where the concerns were addressed, noting that few alternatives were presented. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve item 9.A.2. Council Members made final comments. City Manager Leif Ahnell and Mr. Kalvort provided information regarding the difficulty of hiring part-time staff, the use of organics and the caution used when treating parks and playground areas. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote: Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5482 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton modifying and expanding the scope of the Green Living Advisory Board and changing the name of the Green Living Advisory Board to the Sustainability Advisory Board; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date This is the first of two public hearings on Ordinance No. 5483. No vote will be taken. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5482. Mayor Singer and Council Member Mayotte suggested the Board research the issue of using organics for weed control. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. !!:, Ordinance No. 5483 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article XII "Industrial Districts," Division 2, "Light Industrial and Research Park (LIRP) Zoning District," Section 28-981, "Conditional Commercial Nodes Uses Allowed," to authorize car and truck rentals and package stores selling alcoholic beverages (subject to certain restrictions and requirements), as part of a conditional commercial node master plan approval in the LIRP zoning district, by amending the list of allowable and prohibited uses; amending Section 28-979, "Prohibited Uses," to affirm that a package store selling alcoholic beverages is an allowable use in a Conditional Commercial Node: providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-18-11) Mayor Singer stated that this was the first of two public hearings. Jim Bell, Development Services Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The objective of the text amendment was presented, as well as the history of the current code. Mr. Bell reviewed the locations of the LIRP commercial nodes and benefits of the inclusion of the vehicle rental use in the zoning district. The features of the text amendment allowing package stores to sell alcoholic beverages were then presented. Mr. Bell noted that the proposed uses were consistent with the zoning and the proposed changes would fall within the limits of City's Comprehensive Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board recommendations and approval were discussed. Staff recommended approval of the proposed text amendment following the second hearing. Mr. Bell then made himself available for questions. Members asked questions regarding vehicle rental businesses, types of package stores affected by the text amendment and the parking and storage of rental vehicles. Mr. Bell and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Mayor Singer noted that the second public hearing would be on April 23. ll:, REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS: There was no business to consider.

units.text: Boca Raton Historical Society Renovation of Town Hall Council Member Mayotte spoke on behalf of the need to support and preserve Town Hall, home to the Boca Raton Historical Society and Museum. She shared the results of recent fundraising efforts of the Historical Society and noted the planned new exhibits. Mary Csar, Executive Director of the Historical Society, gave a brief presentation on the repairs needed at Town Hall. Derek Vander Ploeg, the project architect, provided additional information. Ms. Csar and Mr. Vander Ploeg responded to questions. Hank Jahari, president of the Historical Society, asked the Council for their support. Board Member Denise Allman spoke about the need to preserve the history of the building. Members commented and expressed support for a contract with the Society. The City Manager noted that a contract and budget amendment would be brought before Council for approval. Deputy Mayor Rodgers reported on his attendance at the recent meeting of the Business Development Board of Palm Beach County and commented on the City's availability of Class A office space. Council Member O'Rourke commented on available office space in the Downtown and the City's upcoming Strategic Planning Workshop. Mayor Singer provided details about the upcoming Strategic Planning Workshop. He reported on his attendance at the Florida League of Mayors meeting and commented on staff efforts to meet ADA website requirements. ll:. units.text: Ordinance No. 5481 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, Section 28-1302, "Car Agencies," Code of Ordinances, to delete the requirement that a car agency be enclosed by a six foot high masonry wall: providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-18-07) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this public hearing was continued from the March 26, 2019 City Council Meeting. Questions raised at the prior hearing were reviewed and responses provided. Topics included, but were not limited to, setbacks, impact on residential zoning and anticipated locations of future car agencies. Staff recommended approval of the ordinance as originally presented. Mr. Schaad presented further amendment options for Council consideration. He then made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of Investments Limited, made brief comments in support of the amendment as originally presented. Les Wilson from Boca First expressed support of the ordinance. Cristina Escalante came forward to inquire about medical marijuana dispensaries. Mayor Singer clarified the public hearing was regarding this ordinance only, and her question would be addressed during the public requests. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5481. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. fl Ordinance No. 5483 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article XII "Industrial Districts," Division 2, "Light Industrial and Research Park (LIRP) Zoning District," Section 28-981, "Conditional Commercial Nodes Uses Allowed," to authorize car and truck rentals and package stores selling alcoholic beverages (subject to certain restrictions and requirements), as part of a conditional commercial node master plan approval in the LIRP zoning district, by amending the list of allowable and prohibited uses: amending Section 28-979, "Prohibited Uses," to affirm that a package store selling alcoholic beverages is an allowable use in a Conditional Commercial Node: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing for codification: providing an effective date (AM-18-11) Jim Bell, Development Services Long Range Project Manager, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation, noting that this was the second of two public hearing. The purpose of the amendment was discussed, and it was noted that the changes were consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with an amendment to remove truck and non-habitable trailer rentals. Staff recommended approval as modified. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell then responded to Council members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Martin Heise, owner of affected property, expressed support of the amendment. He questioned parking and site plan review once the Code amendment was approved. Mr. Bell responded. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer asked Mr. Bell if an amendment could be added to address Mr. Heise's concern. Mr. Bell and Mr. Schaad advised they had language prepared. In order to allow the City Attorney time to review the language with staff, it was decided, without objection, to postpone a vote to later in the meeting and move on to Public Requests.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium Tuesday, May 28, 2019 5:30 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang, Chair Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. Council Member Andy Thomson Commissioner Erin Wright Deputy City Manager George Brown Briann Harms, Interim Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser Samuel Goren, Attorney and Special Counsel Arthur C. Koski I. Welcome - Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Susan Vogelgesang Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:34 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topic A. Boca National Golf Course Update Commissioner Robert Rollins and Arthur Koski of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) provided a summary of the project thus far and stated, with Council's approval, they were ready to proceed to the RFP. Council Members asked several questions regarding the timeline and clarification as to the cost. Lengthy discussion ensued. District Commissioners stated that, at this time, they were only seeking approval for the Phase I design concept. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser requested a list of the Phase I details in order to prepare a resolution. Further discussion ensued. District Chair Susan Vogelgesang, course designers Tom Fazio and Nick Price and traffic engineer John Donaldson responded to Members' questions. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Anthony Ciliberti, Andrea Steckloff, Dorothy Provenzano, Charles Possenriede, Andrew Dickson, Richard Close, Tom Vassel, Tom Lambert, Rob Berthiaume Robert Dukate, Lenore Wachtelk and Mr. I. Rubinov expressed concerns regarding funding of the golf course. Gil Linder asked several questions regarding the design of the course; Mr. Rollins and Mr. Fazio responded. Harold Chaffee shared his view of the project. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Merv Timberlake, financial consultant for the Beach and Park District, commented on the District's ability to fund the course. Following additional discussion, the District Commissioners advised they would review funding and design options at their next meeting and present the findings at the June 10th City Council Workshop. Mayor Singer and Chair Vogelgesang thanked everyone for their participation. IV. Adjournment The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 8:29 pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan and Site Plan to authorize demolition of an approximately 98,000 square foot office building and construction of a 297-unit multifamily residential project generally located at 5400 Broken Sound Boulevard and incorporation of an existing, approximately 59,800 square foot office building at 5300 Broken Sound Boulevard; considering three (3) modifications of development parameters, pursuant to Section 28-1843 and Section 28-1720 (1), Code of Ordinances, to eliminate required planted buffers along sidewalks and to eliminate required street trees within planted buffers: (i) along sidewalks at a maximum distance of 35 feet on center, and (ii) along portions of roadways internal to the property; considering the abandonment of a portion of a platted public utility easement; considering a waiver of plat requirements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-18-02) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Elements of the existing Master Plan and the proposed modifications were presented. The Community Appearance Board recommended approval. It was noted that the project meets the mobility objectives of the Comprehensive Plan. The applicant's requests to waive platting requirements and abandon a platted utility easement were discussed. Recent updates to FPL setback guidelines necessitated modifications to landscape plans LP-01, LP-02, LP-03 and LP-09, and Ms. Rahman stated that staff supported the revisions. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. City staff recommended approval with the accompanying conditions of approval and modified landscape plans. She then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Juan Caycedo, architect of the project, gave a brief presentation highlighting architectural features of the proposed project. No one else came forward . There was no cross examination or rebuttal. The public hearing was closed. John Donaldson, traffic engineer, Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, and Maria Tejera, Traffic Engineer, responded to members' questions. Council Member Thomson moved , and Deputy Mayor Rodgers seconded, approval of the resolution. The City Attorney provided clarification regarding inclusion of replacement landscape sheets LP-01, LP-02, LP-03 and LP-09 as an amendment to the resolution, to which both members agreed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 64-2019 as amended. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member O'Rourke commented on the tunnel mural project at Spanish River Park and noted that some local businesses had stopped providing plastic straws. She then highlighted upcoming events in Mizner Park. Council Member Thomson also commented on the Spanish River Park tunnel mural project. Mayor Singer complimented local businesses on their transitioning from providing straws. He offered several suggestions for wording changes to the Strategic Planning goals and priorities. Mayor Singer then asked members for their input regarding the Boca National Golf Course. Discussion ensued. Mr. Brown advised that the City would need to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the District's updated proposal and he reminded members that there is currently an agreement with the District for their agency to develop the property. Ms. Freiser clarified the differences in governance and responsibilities between the two bodies. Further discussion ensued. Mayor Singer expressed the Council's desire to work with the District. The Strategic Planning priorities were reviewed, and members top priorities tallied . Discussion ensued. Deputy Mayor Rodgers suggested the results be summarized with three top priorities and five medium priorities. The Deputy City Manager noted that items not designated as top priorities would still be worked on by City staff; he advised that a report with the revised set of priorities would be presented at the next meeting.

units.text: April 25, 2019 Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers requested that item 9.G., Resolution No. 75-2019 be removed from the Consent Agenda. Mayor Singer noted that the item would be considered separately immediately following the vote on the remaining Consent items. The Mayor then provided an opportunity for public input. No one came forward to speak. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve the Consent Agenda as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. 9.G. Resolution No. 75-2019 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute an interlocal agreement with Palm Beach County for the purpose of developing, constructing, and managing a public safety communications tower on City-owned property that will support public safety communications systems for the City, the County and other authorized public safety users; authorizing the expenditure of funds in an amount not to exceed 3 million dollars ($3,000,000) for the construction of the tower; authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute additional documents necessary to facilitate the development, construction, and management of the communications tower and to make nonmaterial changes to the interlocal agreement as may be acceptable to the City Manager; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Acting City Manager George Brown gave a brief overview of the agreement details. The ownership and responsibility of the tower were discussed. The Palm Beach County Zoning Board recommended approval to the County Commission. Mr. Brown responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades presented a brief PowerPoint outlining her client's opposition to the tower. Alan Feinberg, Dan Cohen, Jeffrey Greenhaut, George Corso, Constance Weaver, Shannon Otto, Sue Trombino, and Sothro Sok spoke against construction of the tower. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Brown responded to questions. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to postpone Resolution No. 75-2019 to the meeting of July 23, 2019. Motion failed 2 votes to 3; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. Further discussion ensued. Mr. Brown and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 75-2019. Motion carried 3 votes to 2; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Council; Member Andy Thomson voting no.

units.text: Ordinance No. 5487 (Second of two public hearings.) An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, with regard to assisted living facilities (ALFs), nursing homes and hospitals, to provide for the consistent use of terminology, delete obsolete terms, and affirm that such uses are regulated by beds per acre (BPA) and have a maximum of 75 beds per acre; deleting the obsolete term "orphanage" as a use; amending Chapter 28, Article I, Section 28-3, "Intent, Purposes, Methods," Code of Ordinances, to affirm, generally, that Chapter 28 is interpreted and applied in accordance with Federal and State law; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-17-12) Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman briefly reviewed the proposed amendment and noted that the changes were consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval, as well. Ms. Rahman then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Cristina Escalante commented. Ms. Rahman, the Acting City Manager, and the City Attorney provided additional information. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5487. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. fL Ordinance No. 5490 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering the adoption of amendments to the Boca Raton Comprehensive Plan and its goals, objectives, and policies in accordance with the statutory requirement to conduct an evaluation and appraisal of the Comprehensive Plan; amending the Community Profile, Future Land Use Element. Transportation Element. Housing Element. Infrastructure Element. Coastal Management Element, Conservation Element. Recreation and Open Space Element. Intergovernmental Coordination Element, Historic Preservation Element. Capital Improvements Element and the Map Series, and deleting the Public School Facilities Element; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-18-06) Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman reviewed the components of the amendments that included, but were not limited to, future land use, transportation, housing, and infrastructure. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with amendments. Staff recommends approval. Ms. Rahman, Maria Tejera, Traffic Engineer, and Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, responded to member's questions. The public hearing was opened. Seeing no one come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to transmit Ordinance No. 5490 to the appropriate agency. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. ll.: REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS: There was no business to discuss.

units.text: Resolution No. 78-2019 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a four-story, approximately 48 feet tall, 8,666 square foot single family residence seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance), for a residential (R-3-F) zoned property located at 2500 North Ocean Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-12-06) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the proceedings. Members made ex-parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. City Code provisions and variance criteria were reviewed. Elevations of the proposed building and site plan were presented. A summary of environmental issues was discussed, and analysis of the applicant's response to variance criteria was provided. Mr. Schaad noted that the project is inconsistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. Staff recommends denial of the request for variance. The Environmental Advisory Board (EAB) recommended denial. Mr. Schaad then reviewed staff's responses to the applicant's presentation at the April 10, 2019 EAB meeting. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Neil Schiller made a PowerPoint presentation on behalf of the applicant. Mr. Schiller requested that three members recuse themselves from voting on the agenda item. Mayor Singer, Council Members O'Rourke and Mayotte responded to Mr. Schiller's comments and declined to recuse themselves. Mr. Schiller then asked that the portion of Mr. Schaad's presentation regarding sea turtles be stricken from the record. Jane Herndon, former Deputy Director of the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, testified as to the department's permitting process. Bob Tuthill, architect of the project, reviewed the design of the proposed building, as well as changes that had been made to the original plans. Don Richardson, owner of Ecological Consultants, commented on the position of the house in respect to the vegetation, dunes and sea turtle nesting habitat. Mr. Richardson also addressed lighting, window coverings and reflectivity. Mr. Schiller commented on statements made by staff and consultants. Variance criteria were reviewed. Mike Jenkins from ATM consulting, consulting counsel Nancy Stroud, and Brandon Schaad responded to statements made by the applicant. Michael Laszlo, Helen Kaye, Gil Vizner, Lisa Salvati, Tom Slazinski, Bruce Diller Verstandig, Jessica Gray and David Sergi spoke in opposition to the resolution. Richard DeWitt, on behalf of the applicant, cross examined Mr. Jenkins regarding his report. Mr. Schiller offered his rebuttal to comments made by the public. Seeing no one else coming forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 78-2019 to deny granting the variance. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, ANO CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: City Manager Leif Ahnell gave the PowerPoint presentations on the proposed budget and millage rate as well as the proposed Capital Improvements Program. The City's guiding principles - Financially Sound City, World-Class Municipal Services, Strong Partnership with Community and Vibrant and Sustainable City - were reviewed, noting the policy priorities associated with these principles. Changes to the general fund operating costs for the 2019-2020 fiscal year were highlighted, as were new personnel and programs. Various charts and tables were presented illustrating year-over-year millage rates and assessed property valuations; allocation of property taxes; and comparison of Boca Raton to other cities' fire assessment fees, property tax rates, and water/sewer rates. The presentation was then turned over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2019-2020 portion of the six-year Capital Improvements Program. Highlights of various infrastructure, vehicles and equipment, technology updates and renovations requested by City departments were provided. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire responded to questions, as did the City Manager.

Ordinance No. 5497 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a corrective universal conditional (UC) rezoning, pursuant to Article VI, Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances, to affirm that Ordinance No. 5287 (UC-13-05) incorporated the approval, and conditions as appropriate, set forth in Ordinance No. 3798 (UC-89-05), and that the conditions imposed by Ordinance No. 3798 were repealed by Ordinance No. 5287, for the property located at 331-351 East Yamato Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-13-05R1/ZC) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Development Services Long Range Planning Director, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Details of the request for corrective rezoning were reviewed, including the rezoning, conditional use approval and site plan amendment approval. The current and proposed site plan were displayed. Results of the traffic study were provided, and staff analysis of the proposed changes was discussed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval. Upon conclusion, Mr. Bell responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. The existing site plan was reviewed along with photographs of the existing storefronts. Requested zoning changes were discussed, as well as the applicants proposed enhancements to landscaping. Mr. Mummaw responded to members' questions and comments. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5497. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. ~- Ordinance No. 5498 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a universal conditional (UC) rezoning, pursuant to Article VI, Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances. for an approximately 3.65 acre property located at 331 and 351 East Yamato Road, from the Motel-Business (R-B-1) zoning district to the General Business (B-4) zoning district, subject to conditions; providing for the appropriate revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-19-01/ZC) Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5498. units.text: Resolution No. 103-2019 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton imposing Fire Services Assessments against assessed property (residential, commercial, and industrial) located within the City for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2019; approving the fiscal year 2019-2020 rate of assessment; approving the fiscal year 2019-2020 assessment roll (based on the rate of assessment); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Sharon McGuire, Office of the Management and Budget Director, gave a brief explanation of the resolution. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Deputy Mayor Rodgers requested clarification of the fee. City Manager provided additional information. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Robin Newman, on behalf of Jamie Danburg, Tania Hajjar on behalf of the Monterey Investment Group LLC and Troy McClellan on behalf of the Boca Raton Chamber of Commerce questioned the assessment rates and how the amounts were decided. Ms. McGuire and the City Manager responded. Charlie Helton and Shannon Otto expressed their opposition to the resolution. David Eddinger, President of Firefighters and Paramedics of Boca Raton Local 1560, commented on the fees and their contribution to public safety. Glenn Gromann commented in support of Fire Services and encouraged restructuring the fee assessment. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 103-2019. Members made final comments. Ms. McGuire and Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Motion passed on a 4 to 1 vote: Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. ~- Ordinance No. 5496 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the General Employees' Pension Plan; providing for a one-time lump sum payment or an increase in the benefits paid for certain retired or disabled general employees; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Sharon McGuire, Office of the Management and Budget Director, provided a brief explanation of the ordinance.
