units.text: 6- Resolution No. 107-2019 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying Bauman Medical Group's requested wall sign (Permit No. 19-4545) located at 1450 South Dixie Highway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Wanda Sanders, Zoning Officer, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Background information of the appeal was provided, including photographs of the proposed signs. The Community Appearance Board (CAB) decision was reviewed, and the appellants argument was presented. Analysis of CAB design criteria was discussed. She then made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Matthew Boone presented on behalf of the applicant. Photos of the building with renderings of the proposed sign were provided. Landscaping considerations were mentioned. Dr. Alan Bauman addressed the council and asked that the appeal be granted. Glenn Gromann commented in support of the applicant. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. The public hearing was closed. Members made additional comments. Discussion ensued. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to members' questions and provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to reverse the decision of the Community Appearance Board and approve Resolution No. 107-2019 to grant the appeal with modifications. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium Thursday, September 12, 2019 5:00 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang, Chair Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. Council Member Andy Thomson Commissioner Erin Wright City Manager Leif Ahnell Briann Harms, Interim Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser David Tolces, Attorney and Special Counsel Arthur C. Koski, Consultant I. Welcome - Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Susan Vogelgesang Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:00 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topic A. Golf Course and Funding Options Chair Susan Vogelgesang of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) began by asking for approval of the Price-Fazio design concept for the Ocean Breeze Golf Course. Mayor Scott Singer inquired if the District had examined alternative design options provided by the Council. Chair Vogelgesang stated that there had been changes made to the design in order to lower costs and invited Wayne Branthwaite, on behalf of Price-Fazio, to review modifications that had been made to the course design since the May 28, 2019 Joint Meeting. Design changes and related costs were discussed, including components of the project that would be deferred to a later date, such as the clubhouse, tunnel and halfway house. Council Members asked a number of questions regarding elements of the design and the estimated expense. Lengthy discussion ensued. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Rick Heard, Richard Laman, Sue Daddino, Andrea Stekloff, Bruce DillerVerstandig, Lynn Glover, and Robert Dukate expressed concerns regarding funding and design of the golf course. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton adopting a final budget and appropriating funds for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2019 and ending September 30, 2020; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The City Clerk read Ordinance No. 5501 in full and the title of Ordinance No. 5502. City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a PowerPoint presentation on the 2019-2020 budget. Topics included, but were not limited to, a review of the City's mission, vision, and guiding principles; the policy agenda priorities for2019-20; millage and property tax comparison with 2018-19; and assessed property valuations over the last 10 years. He then identified the increases or decreases in general operating expenses and reviewed the new personnel and programs proposed for the coming year. Various charts and graphs were presented illustrating favorable comparisons of Boca Raton to other cities' fire assessment fees, property tax rates and water/sewer rates. The increase in the City's sanitation fees was noted. Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, then briefly discussed the Capital Improvements Program after which she reviewed Exhibits 1-3 identifying the rebudgeted items that will be carried over to the 2019-20 fiscal year budget. Discussion ensued regarding projects that were not approved for funding by the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (BPD). Upon conclusion, Ms. McGuire responded to questions. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Jean-Michel Neault, Compliance Auditor, gave a PowerPoint presentation with a brief overview of the proposed changes to the user fee schedule for the coming year (Resolution No. 113-2019). Upon conclusion, he made himself available for questions.

units.text: Referring to Exhibit 4, Deputy Mayor Rodgers asked for an amount to be dedicated to the FAU Research Park for the next one to two years and thought it should be allocated from the economic development fund. Council Member Mayotte concurred. Mr. Ahnell provided information. Council members commented. Andrew Duffel, FAU Research Park, responded to Council members' questions. There was consensus to include a $100,000 increase. Council Member O'Rourke discussed the amount she requested for the 'Turtle' Project. There was consensus to approve the proposed amount. She then asked for funding for the Flamingo Comedy Festival, which would fund the beginning of this proposed annual event. The City Manager provided additional information on Economic Development funding. Lengthy discussion ensued. Generally, Council members expressed concern with the large amount of funding for a for-profit company. It was suggested that the City become a sponsor or underwrite a specific portion. Mr. Leis provided additional information and responded to questions. Deputy Mayor Rodgers recommended deferring the request until after the inaugural Festival in order to make a better determination in 2020. Members agreed. Mayor Singer commented on the Non-Profit Funding Requests process. Working from the Mayor's list, individual requests were discussed, and changes were agreed to. Discussion ensued on reviewing the process going forward. The City Manager recapped the adjustments that were made resulting in an increase of $13,000 to the total amount of non-profit funding proposed by the Mayor. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to amend the budget to include the FY2019 Non-Profit Organization Funding Requests and the additions to Exhibit 4 as stated. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. The City Manager suggested voting first on Exhibit 1 as amended. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend Exhibit 1, Amendments to the FY 2019-20 Proposed Operating Budget, to include $185,000 for park restroom renovations eliminated from the BPD budget. Discussion ensued regarding the City absorbing costs for projects previously committed to by the BPD but eliminated from their budget. Final Budge Hearing 2 September 23, 2019 Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Jose Gonzalez and Brian Kronberg gave a presentation on behalf of Brightline/ Virgin Trains USA, LLC (VTUSA). Mr. Gonzalez noted that representatives of VTUSA had met with a number of resident groups, including the Junior League of Boca Raton, residents of Library Commons and Friends of the Library. An aerial photo of the property outlined the proposed train station and garage. Topics covered included, but were not limited to, the design and function of the parking garage, relocation of the Community Garden and an elevated pedestrian bridge. Upon conclusion, they responded to a number of questions. Discussion ensued. The floor was opened for public comment. Jackie Reeves, on behalf of the Greater Boca Raton Chamber of Commerce, read a letter in support of the proposed train station. Jo-Ann Landon spoke about the need for trees and landscaping, and potential future complications regarding the library as a polling location during elections. Susan Reilly, Manjunath Pendakur, Cyndi Bloom, and Krista Maki shared their thoughts on behalf of the Downtown Library and its patrons. Charles Bennardini, Bill Gellen, John Poletto, Terri Waitzer and Carol Wishnov, residents of Library Commons, related their concerns with the garage's proximity to their neighborhood. Alexandra Rosenzweig shared her environmental concerns regarding the train and security issues of the proposed garage. Bruce Diller Verstandig remarked on the train station's effect on local traffic and the cost to taxpayers. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was clm~ed. Mr. Gonzalez and Mr. Kronberg responded to comments and questions made by previous speakers. Further discussion ensued. There was consensus among members to direct the City Manager to continue working with Brightline/ VTUSA.

units.text: A resolution of the City Boca Raton considering a site plan, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) rezoning request, to authorize the construction of a 6,634 square foot multi-tenant retail building and a 121,019 square foot self-storage facility (interior storage unit access) and office, together with four (4) technical deviations from Section 23-190, Code of Ordinances, to eliminate a required driveway egress lane and eliminate a required driveway median separator for a driveway on North Dixie Highway, to eliminate a required median separator for a driveway on North Federal Highway, and reduce a required driveway reservoir distance on North Federal Highway, on an approximately 3.546 acre vacant lot generally located at 7021 and 7101 North Federal Highway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-17-02/SPA) Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items A, B, and C would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related, and a separate vote would be taken on the ordinance and each resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osney Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Components of the petitioners request were reviewed, along with aerial photos of the property outlining the proposed site plan and elevations. Traffic considerations and technical deviations from City code were discussed. The proposal is consistent with Comprehensive Plan. Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation and made herself available for questions. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5503. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 108-2019. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 109-2019. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rpurke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an Interim Campus Development Agreement between the Florida Atlantic University Board of Trustees and the City of Boca Raton for the period ending no later than December 31, 2024; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mayor Singer noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Deputy City Manager George Brown gave a PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Brown explained that the original Campus Development Agreement (CDA) expires on November 24, 2019. As the Florida Atlantic University (FAU) new Campus Master Plan is not yet finalized, the proposed Interim CDA was prepared in order to offset impacts until the Plan's completion. Minor adjustments to the Plan present no added impact to the City, and no additional development is authorized beyond the 2009 CDA. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown responded to questions. The public hearing was opened. Constance Scott, on behalf of FAU, expressed gratitude for the working relationship with the City of Boca Raton and Mr. Brown, in particular. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer noted the second public hearing on this item would be on November 13, 2019.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the alteration of an existing outdoor deck and pool area seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance}, for a multifamily residential (R­ S-A) zoned property located at 1400-1500 South Ocean Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-19-01) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Ingrid Allen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The applicant's request for variance was reviewed. Aerial photos of the property, existing elevations and proposed changes were displayed. Ms. Allen noted all variance criteria had been met. The Environmental Advisory Board and Planning and Zoning Board recommend approval. Development Services staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Allen made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Fichera, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief presentation. He noted that the proposed renovations are restricted to the existing hardscape and roof replacement of the underground parking garage. Upon concluding, Mr. Fichera responded to members' questions. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Members made final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers to approve Resolution No. 134-2019. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes ~ CITY MANAGER RECOMMENDATIONS AND REPORTS: The City Manager commented on recent events at Town Center Mall and Police and Fire Department responses. ~ CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS: The City Attorney had no report.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium Tuesday, November 12, 2019 5:30 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang, Chair Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. Council Member Andy Thomson Commissioner Erin Wright City Manager Leif Ahnell Briann Harms, Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser Samuel Goren, Attorney and Special Counsel I. Welcome - Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Susan Vogelgesang Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm. II. Discussion Topic A. Ocean Breeze Golf Course Mayor Scott Singer began by briefly reviewing the outcome of the prior Joint Meeting. Chair Susan Vogelgesang of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) invited Commissioners to discuss the options for golf course operation. Wayne Branthwaite, on behalf of Price-Fazio, reviewed the reduced scope of work within the proposed project. Lengthy discussion ensued regarding the scale of the project and whether or not the City would issue an RFP for alternate course designs. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Greg Galanis, Bruce Diller Verstandig, Rick Heard, Jim Sumislaski, Angelo Sands, Richard Close, Robert DuKate, Cil Gilberti, and Harold Chaffee commented on the design and cost of the proposed course, and the desire to see the golf course built quickly. Mr. Branthwaite offered to meet with City staff to provide additional background on the Price-Fazio design. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued. Topics included, but were not limited to, the extent of the District's approval of the City's course design, responsibility for operating expenses, and the prospect of shared profits and losses. City Manager Leif Ahnell advised staff will create an updated interlocal agreement before the end of the year. Council Members and Commissioners made final comments. There was consensus to schedule the next joint meeting on Monday, January 13 at 6:00 pm. IV. Adjournment The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 8: 18 pm. , Recorder on behalf of ton, City Clerk

units.text: Meghan Shea, on behalf of Junior League of Boca Raton, expressed support for the proposed train station and commented on relocation of the Community Garden. Susan Reilly, on behalf of the Library Board, provided a summary of recommendations regarding safety concerns. Krista Maki shared her support for the proposed station and relayed concerns regarding construction impacts. Don Kolodz, on behalf of Discover the Palm Beaches, Wendy Poe, lmran Siddiqui, and Ryan Reiter spoke in support of the proposed train station. Susan Sozin commented in support of a covered walkway and expressed concerns regarding safety. Christopher Marcello stated his opposition to the proposed station and additional traffic. Manju Pendakur and Michael Kohner relayed concerns with the proposed VTUSA lease. Seeing no one else come forward, the public request period was closed. Mayor Singer provided a review of the VTUSA presentation from the previous day. Brian Kronberg and Jose Gonzalez, on behalf of VTUSA, responded to a number of members' questions. The City Attorney provided information regarding provisions of the proposed lease. Deputy City Manager George Brown and City Manager Leif Ahnell responded to questions about city vehicle parking. Discussion ensued. Topics discussed included, but were not limited to, parking garage heights, public space within the proposed station, security and the opening of a crossing at Jeffrey Street. The Mayor provided additional clarification on the proposed lease and thanked Mr. Gonzalez and Mr. Kronberg for their time.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Tentative Plat entitled "Mainstreet 40" (a replat of Parcel U, Arvida Park of Commerce Plat No. 5, and a portion of Sections 1 and 12, Township 47 South, Range 42 East and a portion of Sections 6 and 7, Township 47 South, Range 43 East), for the property generally located at 5201 North Congress Avenue and 901 West Yamato Road, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-19-01) The public hearings on items C. through H. will be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related. A separate vote will be taken on the ordinance and each resolution. Mayor Singer advised the public hearings on items A and B would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related. A separate vote would be taken on each resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osny Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Components of the applicant's request and amendments to the master plan were reviewed. Contributions to the City's transit program were outlined. Modifications of development parameters were discussed, and aerial maps of the property were displayed, along with the site plan and building elevations. The traffic study was reviewed. Public concerns and opposition to the project were addressed. The proposed PMD is consistent with the City's comprehensive Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation and reviewed the requested modifications Juan Caycedo, project architect, reviewed illustrations of the proposed buildings. John Donaldson, Traffic Engineer, discussed the traffic study and how the proposed projects affects mobility. Upon concluding, Ms. Zachariades made herself available for questions. Ms. Zachariades, Mr. Caycedo and Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided additional information on several topics. John Fumero, on behalf of Infinity Sales Group, spoke in opposition to the project. Mr. Fumero listed concerns his client had with the proposed PMD, including parking, entitlements, and the mobility analysis. Michael Sexton, professional engineer, spoke on behalf of Infinity Sales Group. He reviewed a number of topics including, but not limited to, parking, mobility and matrix points. Mayor Singer asked staff to address concerns raised by Mr. Fumero and Mr. Sexton. Quan Yuan, Transportation Planning Engineer, John Donaldson, traffic engineer and Brandon Schaad responded to members' questions. Jonathon Ounjian spoke in opposition to the project and expressed concerns with the PMD. There was no cross examination. Ele Zachariades offered final comments on behalf of the petitioner. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 141-2019. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 142-2019. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a tentative plat for Broken Sound P.U.D. Parcel 24 replat (a replat of Parcels A, B, C and D of Broken Sound Parcel 24, according to the plat thereof, as recorded in Plat Book 74, Pages 199 and 200), generally located at 1905 and 1907 Clint Moore Road, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-18-01) Mayor Singer advised the public hearings on items C, D, E, F, G and H would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related. A separate vote would be taken on each resolution and the ordinance. The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures would continue to govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Attorney administered the oath to those who wished to speak. James Bell, Long Range Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Bell began with an overview of the request components, displaying aerial photos of the subject property. Analysis of the master plan and conditional use amendments were discussed, as well as evaluation of the proposed rezoning and conditional use. Conditions pertaining to operational aspects of the assisted living facility were reviewed. Technical deviations and traffic considerations were shown. Mr. Bell discussed waivers allowed for Community Appearance Board (CAB) criteria and noted CAB's approval. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Bradley Miller, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Matt Griffin, on behalf of Griffin Living ALF, provided an overview of the operations and amenities to be offered at the facility. Modifications to the current property layout and review of the requested technical deviations were discussed. On concluding, Mr. Miller responded to members' questions. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, responded to the amendments to conditions requested by the applicant. Lindsey Nieratka, Sustainability Manager, commented on the condition for structural soil use. Deputy Mayor Rodgers asked the applicant if they would consider postponing a decision if they could not come to agreement regarding conditions. Bebbe Reed, on behalf of the applicant, commented on the condition requiring a medical director be on staff or on call at all times. There was no rebuttal or cross-examination. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer noted the time and asked for a motion to extend the meeting. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to extend the meeting beyond 11:00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The City Attorney provided additional clarification regarding the condition for a medical director. Rod Sheldon spoke on behalf of the applicant. Further discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson suggested language to amend the condition regarding a medical director. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 136-2019. Motion was made by Mayor Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to lay the prior motion on the table. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 139-2019. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to amend Section 5, page 10. The City Attorney noted that condition 8.c. would be deleted and the applicant's language would become the new condition 8.c. Discussion ensued with regard to the medical director requirement. Motion on the amendment to Resolution No. 139-2019 passed 3 to 2; Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Mayor Scott Singer and Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers voting no. Motion was made by Mayor Singer, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to further amend Resolution No. 139-2019 regarding the condition for structural soil. The City Attorney read amended language into the record regarding the conditions for structural soil requirement in Section 5, pages 6 and 9 of the resolution. Motion on the second amendment to Resolution No. 139-2019 carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Members made final comments. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 139-2019 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 136-2019. units.text: Council Member O'Rourke commented positively on the new program to encourage beach cleanup. She also asked to review plans for the Wildflower property at the next Workshop and inquired about a resolution to address the Jeffery Street crossing. Mayor Singer asked Council Member O'Rourke to expound on her questions regarding the proposed plans for the Wildflower property; Ms. O'Rourke provided clarification regarding her concerns. Council Member Mayotte thanked members for their support in persuading the Public Service Commission to keep the 2014 energy goals in place. She also reported on the Discovery of the Palm Beaches tourism round table, a home rule resolution regarding plastic bags and styrofoam, and commented on the City's Veterans Day ceremony. Deputy Mayor Rodgers expressed his support for the Coastal Clean Up program and commented on the Joint Meeting with the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District). He asked members for ideas to go forward. Members weighed in regarding the golf course. Mr. Ahnell and Mr. Woika provided information regarding the RFP process. Discussion ensued. There was consensus that the updated interlocal agreement be completed before additional action be taken. Mr. Rodgers then addressed some of the comments made during Public Requests. Mayor Singer suggested that Ms. Mayotte's goal regarding home rule preemption be included in the legislative priorities and thanked all those involved with the Veterans Day festivities. Regarding the funding request from the Boca Raton High School Band, Mayor Singer suggested that parameters be discussed with regard to future funding requests. Members commented. The Mayor shared information regarding the Lake Worth Drainage District work within Broken Sound. Lastly, Mayor Singer suggested a date change for the January Joint Meeting with the District due to a schedule conflict with Palm Beach County Days in Tallahassee. Members agreed to propose the Joint Meeting be moved to January 27, 2019 following the City Council Workshop.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of 600 SW 3 LLC, for a settlement and reduction of one (1) Code Enforcement lien imposed against property located at 600 SW 3rd Street; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Doug Sheedy, Code Compliance Manager, gave a brief overview and provided background information on the code violations, noting that staff does not support the lien reduction. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Paul Carnrick, applicant, described circumstances leading to the code violations on the property. He explained that expired permits had since been closed out and the property had recently been sold. Upon concluding, Mr. Carnrick responded to members' questions, as did staff. The public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to reduce the fine by half, to $3,307.50. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend the motion on the floor to reduce the fine to $5,000. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The City Attorney clarified that the lien would be reduced by $1,615 to a total amount of $5,000 and that payment in full was to be made within 30 days. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 148-2019 reducing the lien to $5,000. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a long-term lease agreement with Virgin Trains USA LLC (VTUSA), pursuant to Chapter 13, Article Ill, "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances, for a portion of the City-owned property located at 400 Northwest 2nd Avenue (generally in the northeast of the parcel}, for the purpose of construction, maintenance, and operation of a passenger train station and a parking garage, pursuant to terms and conditions of the Agreement; determining, in accordance with Chapter 13, that the Agreement and the purposes served by the Agreement are of significant economic benefit to the City: authorizing temporary easements for parking and construction purposes, and providing for the relocation of the "Community Garden": authorizing a right of first refusal with respect to the leasehold lands and additional lands, as described in the Agreement; and authorizing the expenditure of funds in connection with the construction of the parking garage, as provided in the Agreement: providing for severability: providing for repealer: providing an effective date (SC-19-06) George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a PowerPoint presentation on the updated lease agreement with Virgin Trains USA, LLC (VTUSA). Mr. Brown began with a comparison of elements between the initial lease request and current proposed lease. Location and design elements of the proposed train station and parking garage were displayed. Aspects of garage operations and a general construction timeline were presented. Terms of the lease were discussed, including, but not limited to, relocation of the Community Garden, construction parking and coordination with the Library Commons residential neighborhood. Environmental considerations were also reviewed. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser then reviewed changes in the updated redline version of the lease, noting that many changes involved cleanup to the lease language while others were substantive changes that better benefitted the City. Among the changes were clarification of garage revenues, provisions for a City-declared state of emergency, and bankruptcy protection provisions. Mr. Brown and Ms. Frieser responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Jose Gonzalez and Brian Kronberg, on behalf of VTUSA, thanked City staff for their work on the proposed lease and made themselves available for questions. Cristy Stewart Harfmann, on behalf of the Junior League of Boca Raton, Troy McClellan on behalf of the Greater Boca Raton Chamber of Commerce, Meghan Shay, Debbie Abrams, Irvin Lippman, John Tolbert on behalf of the Boca Raton Resort & Club, Jorge Pesquera on behalf of Discover the Palm Beaches, Michael Daszkel, Mary Beth Tate, Jackie Reeves, Melissa Roberts, Peter Arts on behalf of Plastridge Insurance, Lila Newman, Anne Grigsby, Amanda O'Brien, Matthew Mandel, Sal Saldana on behalf of Town Center at Boca Raton, Carol Hicks, Steven Deutsch, Jennifer Graham, Michelle McGovern on behalf of Boca Raton Regional Hospital/ Baptist Health South Florida, Roberta Kjelgaard, Matthew Lane on behalf of Waterstone Resort, Alexandra Blye Abrahamy, Alan Feinberg Jr., Andrea Virgin, Patricia Ramudo, and Ryan Reiter expressed their support for the proposed train station. Charles Fix, Sue White, Dylan Reingold, City Attorney for Indian River County, Manju Pendjukar, Brian White, Charles Bennardini, Sonia Dehesa, Dr. Mary Aruda, John Hrycyk, Cheryl Sands Marcello, Martha Parker, Deborah Cusick, Silvia Hall, Nora Greenberg, Martha Parker, Pedro Voyer, Bill Gellin, Shannon Otto, Charlie Helton, Alexandra Rosenzweig, and Dr Nada Boskovic expressed their opposition to the proposed lease and train station. Terry Waitzer, Jack McWalter, Peter Lynch, JoAnn Landon, Cyndi Bloom, Veronica Risko, Robin Friedman, Alfred Treppeda, Krista Maki, Michael Kohner, Suzanne Vied, Susan Sosin, Robert Dukate, Jeffrey Odgis, Harold Chaffe and Herb Archibold stated their concerns and posed several questions relating to the proposed train station. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Brown addressed several points raised during the comment period. Topics included, but were not limited to, designated equipment areas, additional uses of the garage, and reserved library parking spaces. Mr. Gonzalez, Mr. Kronberg and Jeff Swiatek of VTUSA provided additional information. Discussion ensued. City Manager Leif Ahnell and Mr. Brown responded to members' questions, which included inquiries about buffer areas between the parking garage and adjacent neighborhood, shade trees, construction time periods and future development of the property. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5509. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Mayor Singer noted the time and asked for a motion to extend the meeting. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Monica Mayotte, to extend the meeting beyond 11:00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Mayor Singer thanked residents for their involvement and addressed additional comments made during the public comment period. Members made final remarks. The meeting recessed at approximately 11 :39 pm and reconvened at approximately 12:01 am.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved planned mobility development (PMD) site plan (Resolution No. 57-2014, as amended by Resolution No. 91-2016), to authorize the construction of a 124-room hotel in Phase II of the 900 Broken Sound PMD Site Plan; modifying conditions of approval for Phase I and Phase II of the site plan; together with a technical deviation from Section 23-190(b), Code of Ordinances, to increase the allowable length of five (5) parking rows from 250 feet to lengths ranging from 280 feet to 330 feet; and abandonment of a portion of a platted public utility easement; for the property generally located at 850 and 900 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway, and 900 Northwest Broken Sound Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-13-01R3/SPA) The Mayor advised the public hearings on Items 11 A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on each resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the request and description of the property. Mr. Bell outlined the amendments to the master plan and phases of the project development. Modifications to development parameters were summarized. The Community Appearance Board recommended approval 3-1, with 3 conditions. Results of the traffic study were provided. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. The proposed amended PMD project is consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. Staff recommends approval of the resolutions with a date correction. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. She provided the history of the original approval and described the conditions being contested. Ms. Miskel asked that her client's contributions to the City's Beautification Program be split into two payments, that Condition 6 be stricken, and lastly, that there be an alternative to the transit fee conditions. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Discussion ensued. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided further information regarding the petitioner's request and discrepancy regarding project phases. The City Attorney provided additional clarification. Paul Kilgallon, on behalf of the applicant, supplied additional background regarding the history of the site plan and development phases. Mr. Schaad and Ms. Frieser responded to comments made by the applicant. Further discussion ensued. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to amend Resolution Nos. 156-2019 and 157-2019 to revise language, to be finalized by staff, regarding the transit fee; change to the exhibit for the Planned Mobility Matrices; and to strike the median beautification contribution for Phase 1 in Resolution No. 157-2019. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to amend Resolution Nos. 156-2019 and 157-2019 to split the Phase 2 median beautification contribution into Phase 2 and 3 contributions. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Further discussion ensued. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 156-2019 as amended. Motion carried unanimously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. For clarity, the City Attorney provided language regarding the motion. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 157-2019 as amended with revisions previously stated. Motion carried unanimously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan to authorize the construction of an approximately 22,500 square foot restaurant building, together with a technical deviation from the 2002 Palm Beach County Unified Land Development Code Table 7.2-1 to reduce the number of required parking spaces, and a technical deviation from the 2002 Palm Beach County Unified Land Development Code Section 7.2.D.6 to reduce the required length of a loading space, for the Plaza located at 5355 Town Center Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-18-09) The City Attorney reviewed the Quasi-Judicial procedures. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Deputy City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman, Chief Planner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. The location of the project was identified, and elements of the site design were provided. Landscape buffers and traffic considerations were discussed. Technical deviations related to parking spaces and loading zone dimensions were reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with conditions. Development Services staff recommended approval with conditions included in the resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman made herself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall, on behalf of the applicant, asked for clarification of the proposed conditions regarding reservation of parking spaces. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information. Mr. Marshall responded to statements made by staff. Discussion ensued. The meeting was recessed at approximately 6:25 pm and reconvened at 6:28 pm. Mr. Marshall stated he had resolved the question regarding parking. He highlighted several components of the project, including pedestrian connections and the addition of new sidewalks, and asked Council to support the resolution. Mr. Marshall then responded to Council members' questions. Glenn Gromann spoke in support of the project. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 1-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. 1b REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS: There was no business to consider. ll: REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS/SETTLEMENTS: There was no business to consider.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium Monday, January 27, 2020, 6:00 PM Participants: City: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang, Chair Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. Council Member Andy Thomson Commissioner Erin Wright City Manager Leif Ahnell Briann Harms, Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser Jacob Horowitz, Attorney and Special Counsel I. Welcome - Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Susan Vogelgesang Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. Council Members and Commissioners introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topic A Ocean Breeze Golf Course Mayor Singer briefly recapped events since the last Joint Meeting. Chair Susan Vogelgesang of the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) asked Council for approval of the Price-Fazio golf course design, as the District had unanimously voted to take over the building of the course. District Executive Director Briann Harms and City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information regarding recent communication between the two entities. Members and Commissioners debated a number of topics, including, but not limited to, renegotiation of the interlocal agreement (ILA), potential budget impacts and construction timeframe of the proposed golf course. Discussion ensued. B. Other Topics There was no business to discuss. Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Glenn Gromann, Greg Galanis, Jim Ciliberti, Tom Lambert, Rick Heard, Fred Romanin, Jim Utterback, John Carter, Alan Feinberg, Pat Simpson, Regina Ecklund, Harold Chaffee, Christopher Carr, Roy Jones, Barry Tetrault, Robert Dukate, and Angelo Sands commented on their desire to have a golf course built and for both entities to work together. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued. The City Manager and City Attorney commented on the City's amended ILA and advised they would review information recently received by the District. Council Members and Commissioners made final comments. There was consensus to have staff schedule the next joint meeting. IV. Adjournment The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 8:44 pm. Ma Si ns, Recorder on behalf of Susan S. Saxton, City Clerk

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, with regard to pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities; to amend the term "neighborhood serving retail" to clarify that pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities may be permitted in "Neighborhood Serving Retail" and to define the term "Pharmacies"; to amend the following zoning districts to allow pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities as a permitted use: Local Business (B-1) District, Community Business (B-2) District, Central Business (B-3) District, General Business (B-4) District, Commercial (C-1) District, City General Commercial (CG) District, City Commercial High Office (CHO) District, Light Industrial Research Park (LIRP) District, Manufacturing Industrial (M-3) District, Medical Center (MC) District, Motel-Business (R-B-1) District, Village Center (VC) District, Professional, Office and Institutional (POI) District; to amend the following zoning districts to allow pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities as a conditional use: Neighborhood Convenience Business (NCBD) District, Warehouse (W-1) District and within commercial nodes of residential planned unit developments; to provide zoning regulations for pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities; to amend the prohibited uses in all zoning districts section to remove "medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities" as a prohibited use; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-19-08) Mayor Singer noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman began with an overview of revisions to the agenda item to reflect the final ordinance. She then provided a brief background of the legislation and a map of existing dispensaries in municipalities surrounding the City limits. A list of zoning districts within the City that currently allow pharmacies was reviewed. The proposed changes to City regulations were discussed. The Planning and Zoning Board vote on the ordinance was 2 to 2. Ms. Rahman noted that staff recommends denial of the ordinance due to uncertainty in regard to medical marijuana legislation and case law, as well as current state law that inhibits the ability of municipalities to limit or manage such facilities. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Eric Seville expressed his general support of the ordinance and proposed several changes to the language. Robert Eisen, on behalf of Investments Limited, expressed concern with the 5,000 square foot size requirement. Charles Felix spoke in support of the ordinance. Lauren Niehaus, on behalf of Harvest Health and Recreation, Inc., asked Council to approve the ordinance. Daniel Sparks, on behalf of Truelieve, commented in support of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann remarked on the current medical marijuana industry and expressed his opposition to the ordinance. Mark Wigder discussed potential conflicts with federal and state law regarding marijuana dispensaries and stated that he opposed the ordinance. Jason Ibarra spoke in support of the ordinance. Seth Penalver commented in support of the ordinance. Cristina Escalante, in support of the ordinance, remarked that although there were nearby dispensaries in neighboring cities, the locations were not convenient for those using public transportation. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer noted that the second public hearing on this item would be on February 11, 2020.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte commented on members' trip to represent the City at Palm Beach County days in Tallahassee, as well as her recent visit to Boca Elementary to read to students. Deputy Mayor Rodgers echoed Ms. Mayotte's positive remarks on their trip to Tallahassee and asked the City Attorney about the Ocean Breeze land acquisition. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser reviewed points of the original interlocal agreement with the Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District (District) and provided information about the City's financial obligation regarding the golf course. Council Member O'Rourke commented on her visit to Boca Elementary to read to students. She also remarked on successful meetings with City lobbyists during the members' time in Tallahassee and promoted upcoming City events. Council Member Thomson expressed concerns regarding the District's ability to both fund the proposed golf course and continue to meet other financial obligations with the City. Mayor Singer reported on his trip to Washington for the Conference of Mayors, noting that topics covered included innovation, infrastructure, and safety. The Mayor then initiated a conversation among members regarding the proposed ordinance on medical marijuana. Discussion ensued. Members asked questions on a number of points, among them, required square footage, potential legal ramifications and how other municipalities had handled the same issue. Staff members responded. The Mayor concluded his comments by encouraging residents to take part in the 2020 Census and announcing upcoming City events.

units.text: (B-4) District, Commercial (C-1) District, City General Commercial (CG) District, City Commercial High Office (CHO) District, Light Industrial Research Park (LIRP) District, Manufacturing Industrial (M-3) District, Medical Center (MC) District, Motel-Business (R-B-1) District, Village Center (VC) District, Professional, Office and Institutional (POI) District, and Neighborhood Convenience Business (NCBD) District; authorizing pharmacies and medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities as conditional uses in commercial nodes of residential planned unit developments; providing regulations for pharmacies, medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facilities and businesses with marijuana-derived products; amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," by amending the definitions of "medical marijuana treatment center dispensing facility" and "neighborhood serving retail", and creating a definition for the term "pharmacies"; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-19-08) Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation, and noted that this was the second of two public hearings. Ms. Rahman began by reviewing the changes made to the ordinance since the first public hearing. A summary of the proposed regulations was provided. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Robert Eisen, on behalf of Investments Limited, relayed his concerns regarding the square footage requirement. Shari Kaplan Stellino, on behalf of Cannectd Wellness, shared her son's experience with medical marijuana and her desire to see the ordinance passed. Eric Sevell, Seth Penalver, Jason Iberra, Cristina Escalante, Charles Felix, Marko Andrioff, and Emily Hartoa spoke in support of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann, Alan Feinberg, and Terri Murru expressed their opposition to the proposed ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. The City Attorney reviewed revisions made to the ordinance, noting that a number of changes involved cleanup to the language, while others were more substantive. Mr. Schaad responded to a remark made during the public comment period regarding the LIRP zoning district. An amendment to the ordinance was suggested by Council Member Thomson, to reduce the minimum square footage requirement from 5,000 to 2,500. Council Member Mayotte agreed, and proposed a limit of allowable distances between dispensaries and existing pharmacies. Staff displayed maps illustrating a restriction of 4,000-foot proximity to existing pharmacies. Discussion ensued. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser read proposed language into the record regarding distance separation. Deputy Mayor Rodgers expressed concerns regarding the proposed distance amendment and suggested language that would postpone the effective date of the ordinance, as well as require conditional use approval. Members expressed doubts that an additional delay would yield action by the State legislature. The City Attorney, noting the motions applied to the 2/11/2020 revision of the ordinance, identified the pages and sections that would amend the minimum gross floor area to 2,500 square feet and add language setting a distance separation of 4,000 feet from existing pharmacies. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend Ordinance No. 5513 to lower the minimum required square footage from 5,000 to 2,500. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend Ordinance No. 5513 establishing a distance separation of 4,000 feet from existing pharmacies. Ms. Frieser provided additional clarification regarding the distance separation maps developed by staff. Members commented. Motion carried on a 3 to 2 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers and Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to amend Ordinance No. 5513 to postpone the effective date to June 1, 2021. The City Attorney read the new language into the record. Further discussion ensued. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers and Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes, Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5513 as amended. Members offered final comments and stated their positions. Motion carried on a 3 to 2 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers and Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing the Downtown Advisory Board; providing for the membership, appointment, term, quorum, officers, powers and duties; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ruby Childers, Downtown Manager, briefly reviewed the ordinance and responded to members' questions. Mayor Singer and Council Member O'Rourke inquired about the intended goals of the proposed board. Members expressed concerns regarding board member requirements. Mayor Singer suggested the ordinance be refined and reconsidered at a later date. The public hearing was opened. Derek VanderPloeg commented in support of the proposed ordinance, citing the need to address goals not yet been met by the Downtown Advisory Committee. Robert Eisen suggested the creation of a task force to identify the duties and goals of the proposed board. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council Member O'Rourke inquired about board member qualifications. Ms. Childers responded, and discussion ensued. The City Attorney suggested the scope of the board be determined prior to its creation. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to postpone consideration of Ordinance No. 5516 to the regular meeting of April 14, 2020. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute an easement deed to Florida Power & Light over certain lands at the City-owned parking lot located at 190 Northeast 2nd Street; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-19-07) Jonathan Peservich, Property Specialist, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Peservich provided background of the Tower 155 development that led to the transformer installation. Details of the easement location were reviewed. Upon concluding, he responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Derek VanderPloeg, on behalf of Tower 155, responded to questions from Council Member O'Rourke. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Members requested additional information regarding beautification of the area. Mr. Peservich and City Manager Leif Ahnell responded. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser requested clarification concerning the subject of landscaping. Mr. VanderPloeg and Mr. Schaad responded. Discussion ensued. Ms. Frieser advised members that a condition to the approval of the easement could be added, which stated that prior to the issuance of Tower 155's certificate of completion, landscaping plans of the easement area will be submitted to staff for approval. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 19-2020 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a wireless communication facilities site plan approval for a 140 foot tall stealth communication tower and compound area at a City-owned property, Alamanda Park, located at 1700 Southwest 18th Street; considering one (1) modification of development parameters, pursuant to Section 28-1628(17), Code of Ordinances, to authorize a telecommunication tower taller than 100 feet in a residential zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (WCF-18-01/SPA-18-01) The Mayor advised the public hearings on items 11 A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on the Ordinance and Resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Deputy City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman began with a review of the applicant's request. An aerial view of the property was presented and existing use of the site was described. Terms of the proposed lease were summarized including, but not limited to, yearly rent payments, construction costs and the option for the City to utilize the tower at no expense. Photos that displayed renderings of the proposed tower were displayed. The Community Appearance Board recommended denial by a vote of 3 to 2. The applicants request for additional tower height was discussed. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services Staff recommended approval with no conditions. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Hahn, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He began by outlining the wireless coverage area affected by the proposed tower and reviewed the applicant's justification for additional tower height. Mr. Hahn displayed photographs comparing the proposed tower to existing tower designs. Forecasted revenue and tenant projections were provided. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Council Member Thomson advocated the addition of an American flag to the tower. Mayor Singer requested clarification regarding the potential improvement to wireless coverage and the proposed tower height. Thomas Ward shared his support for the project and questioned the cost for small business to rent space on the tower. Frederick Pfister inquired if the proposed tower would have lighting on the top for air traffic. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Members made final comments. There was not consensus among members to add a flag to the tower, owing to the amount of maintenance the flag would require, as well as the desire to maintain minimal visual impact. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5519. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.full: Resolution No. 27-2020 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a wireless communication facilities site plan approval for a 140 foot tall stealth communication tower and compound area at a City-owned property, Alamanda Park, located at 1700 Southwest 18th Street; considering one (1) modification of development parameters, pursuant to Section 28-1628(17), Code of Ordinances, to authorize a telecommunication tower taller than 100 feet in a residential zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (WCF-18-01/SPA-18-01) The Mayor advised the public hearings on items 11 A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on the Ordinance and Resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Deputy City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman began with a review of the applicant's request. An aerial view of the property was presented and existing use of the site was described. Terms of the proposed lease were summarized including, but not limited to, yearly rent payments, construction costs and the option for the City to utilize the tower at no expense. Photos that displayed renderings of the proposed tower were displayed. The Community Appearance Board recommended denial by a vote of 3 to 2. The applicants request for additional tower height was discussed. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services Staff recommended approval with no conditions. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Hahn, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He began by outlining the wireless coverage area affected by the proposed tower and reviewed the applicant's justification for additional tower height. Mr. Hahn displayed photographs comparing the proposed tower to existing tower designs. Forecasted revenue and tenant projections were provided. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Council Member Thomson advocated the addition of an American flag to the tower. Mayor Singer requested clarification regarding the potential improvement to wireless coverage and the proposed tower height. Thomas Ward shared his support for the project and questioned the cost for small business to rent space on the tower. Frederick Pfister inquired if the proposed tower would have lighting on the top for air traffic. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Members made final comments. There was not consensus among members to add a flag to the tower, owing to the amount of maintenance the flag would require, as well as the desire to maintain minimal visual impact. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5519. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.text: Council Member Thomson began a discussion regarding reopening the boat ramp for use by commercial fishermen only. Council Member O'Rourke expressed concerns regarding the safety of staff and potential overcrowding by large numbers of the public. City Manager Leif Ahnell advised additional staff would be needed to review commercial fishing licenses and provide admittance to the ramp. Discussion ensued. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information and clarification. There was general consensus to direct staff to research the topic and report back at the next Council meeting. Lastly, Mr. Thomson noted that local company SA Company would be having a free facemask giveaway at their Boca Raton location. Council Member O'Rourke asked if staff had considered the idea of pro-rating or extending the expiration dates of parks and facilities permits. The City Manager remarked on the many factors that would need to be taken into consideration. Ms. O'Rourke then commented on the work of Hospitality Helping Hands (H3) and asked how the City could contribute. Deputy Mayor Rodgers suggested the Financial Advisory Board research the possibility of pro-rating existing permits. He also thanked H3 for their work in the community and suggested staff research ways to offer support. Members weighed in on the options for assisting H3; there was general agreement to direct staff to research a financial contribution. The City Attorney noted the Council could consider providing for public comment prior to taking a vote. Motion was made by Deputy Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to direct staff to provide a one-time grant of $10,000 to Hospitality Helping Hands for use within the City of Boca Raton. Mayor Singer then provided an opportunity for public input. Anthony Barber, owner of Troy's BBQ, shared his approval for the City's donation and noted that free meals are also being distributed from his restaurant in conjunction with H3. Alan Feinberg Jr., Glenn Gromann, Dee Lawrence and Leo Denlea expressed their support for the City's proposed contribution. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public comment period was closed. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Deputy Mayor Rodgers suggested the Council consider meeting more frequently to discuss timely issues. The City Manager and City Attorney provided additional information, noting procedural requirements for Council meetings. Discussion ensued. There was consensus to schedule a Special Workshop Meeting on Tuesday, April 21. Mr. Rodgers then advised he was in favor of reopening the golf course, noting that the closure was enacted to comply with County orders. Lastly, he expressed his commitment to preserving citizen's individual liberties. Council Member Mayotte stated the water bond referendum she had mentioned at a previous meeting was on hold and expressed her gratitude to essential workers. Mayor Singer conveyed his thanks to both the public and private sectors working to support the community.

Mikhail Guseynov submitted a question regarding the reopening of beaches and community pools. City Manager Ahnell provided information on the County order lifting restrictions on community pools. Rachel Eade stressed that appropriate preparations should be made by the City in anticipation of the repeal of State and County emergency orders. The City Clerk read the following comment into the record: Kris Mortenson expressed his concerns regarding the shallowness of the inlet and how this might affect boating now that restrictions were being lifted. The City Manager advised that the dredge was currently being repaired and would be put back into service once operational. Rene Stern requested that her business be identified as essential. It was noted that stricter guidelines concerning the designation of essential businesses was established under County guidelines. 3 April 28, 2020 Regular Minutes Josie Machovec asked for clarification of Palm Beach County guidelines and noted the difficulty she encountered in reaching County commissioners. The City Attorney and City Manager provided additional information regarding City enforcement of emergency orders.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton regarding the intent of the City Council to transfer title of a parcel of real property, owned by the City and located near the Don Estridge Middle School, to the School Board of Palm Beach County to be used for the construction and operation of a new elementary school; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Deputy City Manager Mike Woika gave a brief PowerPoint presentation, beginning with the background of the school reconstruction project. The public comment period was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Resolution No. 60-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Thomson advised he was able to confirm with the County that parks under the jurisdiction of homeowners and other associations may be opened. Council Member O'Rourke commented on the financial assistance program proposed by the Chamber of Commerce. The City Manager provided information. Members weighed in. Topics included, but were not limited to, the need to retain existing businesses, criteria for applicants, and the possibility of additional funding from federal programs. There was consensus among Council members to have staff research the issue and report back at the next Special Workshop Meeting scheduled for the following Tuesday. Council Member O'Rourke concluded her remarks by highlighting local charities and encouraged residents to get involved. Deputy Mayor Rodgers inquired about communication received by the public. The City Clerk advised email and voicemail related to the Council meetings had been made available to Council members prior to the meeting. Mr. Rodgers thanked City staff for their work and urged County officials to hold a public meeting. He also referred to a letter he is composing to the federal government regarding the tax code. Council Member Mayotte commented on the need for additional Covid-19 testing sites in south Palm Beach County. Mayor Singer assured residents that City officials and staff were advocating on their behalf and reminded residents to enjoy the parks safely and responsibly.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1098(d), Code of Ordinances, to authorize the expansion of office use in an existing building with a General Industrial (M-2) zoning district, for the property located at 4010 Oak Circle; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-19-01) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. Drew Capra, GIS Planner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. A description of the project location and history of the property development was provided. Mr. Capra reviewed the proposed change of use to incorporate office space and outlined the alterations to the parking areas. The traffic analysis was presented. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Capra responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Charles Putman, on behalf of the applicant, reviewed the site plan and the modifications proposed to accommodate office use. Landscaping alterations within the project were discussed. Upon concluding, Mr. Putman made himself available for questions. There was no cross examination. Seeing no one else indicate that they wished to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 33-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. ll,, REGULAR PUBLIC HEARINGS:

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved site plan (Planning and Zoning Resolution No. 83-33R), pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) rezoning request, to authorize the construction of an additional 16,296 square feet of office space, on an approximately 4.984 acre property generally located at 1489 and 1499 West Palmetto Park Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-19-02/SPA) The Mayor advised the public hearings on items 11. A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the virtual public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osny Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the petitioner's request and a description of the property. Elements of the proposed rezoning and site plan amendment were discussed. Drawings of the pedestrian connection requested by the Planning and Zoning Board were displayed. Mr. Jean presented results of the traffic study, followed by an explanation of the parking agreement condition with a neighboring business. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Matthew Scott gave a presentation on behalf of the applicant. Photographs of the existing property were compared with renderings of the proposed alterations. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Glenn Gromann expressed his support for the proposed project. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Mr. Scott made final comments. Seeing no one else indicate that they wished to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, to approve Ordinance No. 5523 as revised. For clarity, the City Attorney provided language regarding the motion. 3 May 27, 2020 Regular Minutes Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 63-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.
