units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton amending the Boca Raton Municipal Facilities and Services User Fee Schedule to set forth fees for new application processes included in the adoption of a new Chapter 24, "Signs," Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The Mayor advised the public hearings on items 12. A., B., and C. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an overview of the amendments, citing changes in case law and issues with the existing sign regulations that necessitated the need for updates to the sign code. The results of a 2017 Community Appearance Board roundtable were discussed. Topics included, but were not limited to, streamlining of the approval process, greater design flexibility and the use of logos for brand consistency. Other significant issues included banners, temporary real estate signs, and temporary residential election campaign signs. Proposed changes regarding flags and flag poles were also discussed. Mr. Schaad highlighted a recommended revision to the proposed flag ordinance regarding allowable flagpole height in relation to building height. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the Sign Code ordinance by a vote of 3 ~o 1 and approved the companion ordinance by a vote of 4 to 0. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to members' questions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarification. 4 May 27, 2020 Regular Minutes Mayor Singer inquired about extending the length of time for temporary election signs due to the expansion of early voting and proliferation of mail-in ballots. Discussion ensued. There was consensus among members to expand the time allowed for temporary election signs from 30 to 45 days. Deputy Mayor Rodgers inquired about the length of time permitted for temporary promotional signs. Mr. Schaad, Ms. Frieser, and Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mum maw commented in support of the proposed changes. Glenn Gromann also expressed his approval. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5517 as amended. The City Attorney provided clarification of the proposed revision regarding noncommercial temporary signs. Council members thanked staff and community members for their collaboration on the updated regulations. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Levine Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5518 as revised. units.text: Council Member Mayotte read a letter she had prepared that was addressed to Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, citing his recent public comments and social media posts regarding Covid-1_9 related restric~ions. She shared her concern that his remarks could be misinterpreted by some to be representative of the Council as a whole. 3 June 9, 2020 Regular Minutes Deputy Mayor Rodgers thanked Ms. Mayotte for her remarks and acknowledged their differing views on the current state of emergency. He asserted that he had been speaking solely on behalf of himself and his constituents in the instances cited and would continue to do so. Council Member O'Rourke expressed her agreement with Ms. Mayotte and shared her apprehension that Mr. Rodgers' position about Covid-19 issues could be mistakenly attributed to the Council. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member O'Rourke responded to communication she received from residents asking the City to require the wearing of facial coverings in public. She noted the impracticality of enforcing such a mandate and asked residents to be mindful of others. She also commented positively on the March for Unity. Council Member Thomson thanked his fellow Council members for working together and relayed a conversation he had with neighboring elected officials about the participation rate of the 2020 Census. Mr. Thomson suggested additional strategies to encourage residents to complete the Census. Members expressed their support. Mayor Scott Singer reiterated the importance of completing the Census, stressing the impact of the results on the amount of Federal funding received. He remarked positively regarding the peaceful protests within the City and the previous weekend's March for Unity.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering approval of a use and development in the Public Land (PL) zoning district pursuant to Section 28-1238(b)(1), Code of Ordinances, to authorize the development of Wildflower Park, and the redevelopment of Silver Palm Park, for properties generally located at 551 and 600 East Palmetto Park Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-20-01) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures . At the Mayor's request, the City Attorney provided clarification regarding ex parte disclosures where the applicant is the City. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation . He began with a review of the locations and condition of each site. Pictures that showed multiple vantage points of both parks were displayed. Mr. Lindgren provided a brief description of the Conditional Use Approval and noted that the site plan was approved by the Parks and Recreation Board in March . Drawings of the approved site plan were shown, as well as the revised site plan that reflected revisions made to accommodate the approved budget. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened . Kona Gray, consultant with EDSA, provided additional information . He answered questions about the alterations made to the plan in order to reduce costs. Jennifer Bistyga, Coastal Program Manager, informed Council members of her attempts to contact the owner of the adjacent property. Discussion ensued. Ms. Bistyga, Mr. Gray, and City Manager Leif Ahnell responded to questions and provided information about the project timeline. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 80-2020. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Jeremy Rodgers, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Presentation on Upcoming Elections - Wendy Sartory Link, Supervisor of Elections Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link made the presentation. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton establishing a Parking Meter Zone consisting of two hundred and forty three (243) on-street parking spaces within a portion of the Downtown Community Redevelopment Area, generally bounded by West Royal Palm Road/East Palmetto Park Road on the south, Northeast 5th Avenue/Northeast Mizner Boulevard on the east, Northeast 8th Street on the north, and North Dixie Highway/Northwest 2nd Avenue on the west, which Parking Meter Zone also includes Northwest 4th Street generally adjacent to the Downtown Library (outside of the Downtown Community Redevelopment Area); authorizing the City Manager to implement the Parking Meter Zone; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a brief presentation. He provided a timeline of actions leading to the Resolution and advised that the only locations where parking meters would be implemented at this time were around Tower 155. He then reviewed the future parking meter locations included in the resolution. Upon concluding, Mr. Ahnell responded to members' questions. Council Member Mayotte suggested the meters to be placed by the Post Office be free of charge for the first 30 minutes. Mayor Singer and Council Member O'Rourke commented on the timing of the installations and the need to provide on­ street parking to high-traffic business areas. Council Member Thomson expressed his support based on assurances that the only parking meters to be installed now would be those surrounding Tower 155. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann shared his support for the resolution and noted additional areas in the downtown that he believed could benefit from parking meters. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Thomson commented on the budget allocated for meter installation. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 99-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering the adoption of amendments to the Boca Raton Comprehensive Plan and its goals, objectives, and policies in accordance with the statutory requirement to conduct an evaluation and appraisal of the Comprehensive Plan; amending the Community Profile, Future Land Use Element, Transportation Element, Housing Element, Infrastructure Element, Coastal Management Element, Conservation Element, Recreation and Open Space Element, Intergovernmental Coordination Element, Historic Preservation Element, Capital Improvements Element and the Map Series, and deleting the Public School Facilities Element; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-18-06) Tamashbeen Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Rahman provided an overview of the elements and purpose of the Comprehensive Plan. She discussed the Department of' Economic Opportunity's objections, recommendation, and comments, and provided staff's responses. Revisions included, but were not limited to, a revision to the Coastal Management Element, strengthened language and updated maps. Ms. Rahman noted that the proposed amendments meet State statutory requirements. Development Services recommended approval of the amended plan. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman made herself available for members' questions. Council Member Mayotte shared concerns regarding climate-related issues. Ms. Rahman and the City Manager responded. The public hearing was opened, and seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Mayor Singer noted that the Ordinance required four votes for adoption. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5490. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide for large-scale indoor commercial recreation uses and define such uses; amending Article XII, Division 8, "M-3 Manufacturing Industrial District," to add large-scale indoor commercial recreation as a conditional use, and establish a 50-foot height limit; amending Article XV, Division 1, "Supplementary District Regulations," to establish regulations for such uses; amending Article XVI, Section 28-1655, "Required Off-Street Parking," to provide parking standards; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-19-06) Mayor Singer noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. She began with a review of the applicant's request and summarized elements of the text amendment. Components of the application included, but were not limited to, an allowance for large-scale indoor commercial recreation, a height limitation, and required off-street parking for the conditional use. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval. The proposed amendment is consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan. Upon concluding, Ms. Hansen made herself available for questions The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Miskel provided background information of the project that led to the proposed new use category. She commented on the residential neighborhood to the north of the subject area and described steps taken to alleviate the residents' concerns. Upon concluding, she made herself available to answer members' questions. Glenn Gromann and Malcolm Butters expressed their support of the proposed project. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Council Member O'Rourke expressed her support. Mayor Singer noted the second public hearing on this item would be on August 25, 2020.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying Gift of Life Marrow Registry, lnc.'s requested wall sign (Permit No. 20-1916) located at 5901 Broken Sound Parkway Northwest; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The City Attorney noted that quasi-judicial procedures still applied. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex-parte disclosures Austin Budazewski, Zoning Officer, gave the PowerPoint presentation. An aerial view of the property was provided, as well as a description and illustration of the proposed sign. The decision of the Community Appearance Board's (CAB) denial was reviewed. Staff analysis concluded that while the CAB may restrict design aspects of a sign, they may not deny placement of a sign where the Code otherwise allows it. Staff recommends that the CAB decision be reversed, with conditions that the location and size of the sign be altered. The applicant agrees to the changes. Upon concluding, Mr. Budazewski made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Buttress, on behalf of the appellant, stated he had nothing further to add and thanked Mr. Budaszewski for his presentation. Jay Feinberg, also on behalf of the appellant, provided additional information and responded to members' questions. Glenn Gromann expressed his support. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Motion was made by Council Member Thomson, seconded by Council Member Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 100-2020 reversing the decision of the Community Appearance Board and granting the appeal with the recommended conditions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member O'Rourke commented on the current qualifications to run for City Council and suggested proof of residency as well as a one-year residency requirement. Mayor Singer expressed his support for clarified residency and recommended an additional requirement of signatures. Ms. O'Rourke recommended City staff research naming opportunities for City Parks, especially Wildflower/Silver Palm Park. Mayor Singer commented on the complexities of such a project. Council Member Mayotte spoke about the rebuilding of Addison Mizner Elementary and asked if Council could advocate to the Palm Beach County School Board for enhanced filtration systems in the school. Mayor Singer and Council Member O'Rourke weighed in. Ms. O'Rourke noted that it is not within the City's jurisdiction to direct the School Board. Council Member Thomson congratulated Ms. O'Rourke and Ms. Mayotte on their new Council positions. Mayor Singer reminded residents of the importance of preparedness during hurricane season and prompted listeners to complete their 2020 Census forms.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1124, Code of Ordinances, to authorize a large-scale indoor commercial recreation facility for the property located at 900 Peninsula Corporate Circle; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-19-03) The public hearings on items D, E and F will be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedure as required by items E and F. A separate vote will be taken on each ordinance and the resolution. Should item D not be approved, items E and F will not be considered. The Mayor noted the public hearings on items 11. A., B., and C. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. He noted that this was the second of two public hearings for Ordinance No. 5524. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. A summary of the proposed text amendment was reviewed, and potential impacts were discussed. Ms. Hansen noted that the proposed amendment is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan, and approval was recommended by both the Planning & Zoning Board and Development Services staff. A brief history of the Peninsula Corporate Center ORI was provided and the amendment was summarized. The site plan was displayed, and components of the plan were outlined. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize construction of an approximately 3,000 square foot professional office building with covered and surface parking, for an approximately 0.334 acre property generally located at 3101 Northwest 2nd Avenue, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-18-02/SPA) The Mayor noted the public hearings on items 11. G., H., I., and J. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. Ordinance No. 5528 would require four votes for passage. The City Attorney confirmed that the same quasi-judicial procedures would continue to govern the public hearing. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex-parte disclosures Tamashbeen Rahman, Chief Planner, made the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a summary of the applicant's request. Ms. Rahman reviewed the proposed Future Land Use Map amendment and advised that it was consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. It was noted that rezoning of the property from Single-Family Residential (R-1-O) to Local Business (B-1) would keep development consistent with that of the existing area. Components of the site plan were examined. A rendering of the proposed building was displayed, and the traffic analysis was discussed. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, gave the presentation. Ms. Zachariades reiterated the need to rezone the property in order for proposed development to be compatible with the surrounding area. She described the outreach of the applicant to the adjacent residential neighborhood and highlighted structural and landscaping elements that would provide a buffer. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the Builders' Board of Adjustment and Appeals; amending portions of Chapter 2, "Administration," Chapter 19, "Building Regulations," Chapter 21, "Flood Damage Prevention and Floodplain Management," Chapter 22, "Marine Structures," Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," and Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; renaming the Board as the "Permitting and Construction Review Board"; reducing the number of members from nine (9) to five (5), and revising the qualifications for membership; requiring a super­ majority vote in connection with building code administrative appeals; transferring jurisdiction over variances from Chapter 22, "Marine Structures," to the Planning and Zoning Board, and providing for the Marine Advisory Board to make recommendations in connection with such variances; transferring jurisdiction over appeals of certain sidewalk requirement determinations to the Planning and Zoning Board; deleting the process to appeal certain development parameter standards and criteria determinations (under Chapter 28, Article XVII, "Planned Development") to the board; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-02) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The historical background of the board was presented, and the infrequency of board meetings noted. Proposed changes of the board name, membership, and member qualification were discussed. Mr. Schaad outlined the proposed process for appeals, the transfer of marine code variances and formalization of Marine Advisory Board recommendations. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval, with the suggested modification that reversal of an administrative decision be decided by a percentage of the board members present, rather than 4 affirmative votes. Development Services staff did not recommend inclusion of the condition. Development Services staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, he responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened, and seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5525. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton equalizing the assessments; levying the same as assessments against benefited properties within the Downtown Special Assessment District, City of Boca Raton, Florida; directing the City Clerk to record assessments in the Improvement Lien Book; establishing priority of lien and payment of principal and interest; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Stephen Timberlake, Special Projects Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The method of calculating the assessment rate was explained and various charts and graphs were presented. He noted that no objection letters were received, and one inquiry received regarding how the special assessment worked. Upon concluding, Mr. Timberlake made himself available for questions. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 133-2020; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson, and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting yes.

units.section: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: City Manager Leif Ahnell gave PowerPoint presentations on the proposed budget and millage rate. He began by observing that, although the annual Goal Setting sessions were not held due to the Coronavirus pandemic, staff was continuing to work on 2020 objectives and new goals had been added. Mr. Ahnell reviewed the City's guiding principles - Financially Sound City, World Class Municipal Services, Strong Partnership with Community, and Vibrant and Sustainable City - and noted policy priorities associated with these principles. Tables and charts were presented illustrating millage rates and assessed property valuations, and allocation of operating expenses. Mr. Ahnell reviewed the City flyer that explains residents' property tax bill. He highlighted comparisons of Boca Raton to other cities' fire assessment fee, property tax rates, and water and sewer rates. No increase in the fire assessment fee was proposed, and water and sewer rates will remain unchanged. A small increase in sanitation rates was proposed to account for additional staff and capital equipment. The presentation was then turned over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2020-21 portion of the six-year Capital Improvements Program. Ms. McGuire highlighted requests of City departments for various infrastructure projects, vehicles and equipment, technology updates, and renovations. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire responded to questions, as did the City Manager.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize construction of an approximately 6,399 square foot, 25 foot tall professional office building with covered and surface parking, together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1653(1 ), Code of Ordinances, to reduce required dimensions of parking spaces, for the Yamato Office Park generally located at 276 and 298 West Yamato Road, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-14-02/SPA) Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on Items 11. A., B., C., and D. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. A separate vote would taken on each ordinance and resolution, and Ordinance No. 5535 would require four votes for passage. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Long Range Project Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the request components, which included a proposed future land use change, a request for rezoning, the tentative plat and proposed site plan. An aerial view of the subject property was shown. Mr. Bell discussed staff concerns over the proposed future land use change and cited issues presented by the adjacent orphaned parcel and backout driveway access. Staff did not support the future land use change, as it was inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan. The proposed rezoning was not complementary to the remaining parcels. He then outlined details of the site plan. It was noted that the applicant requested one technical deviation regarding parking space size, which staff supported. The application complied with land development regulations for the proposed office building. Development Services staff does not support the application in its current form. Mr. Bell advised Council that should they approve the project, staff would then encourage approval of the additional ordinance and two resolutions that would provide conditions. Upon concluding, he responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Juan Caycedo, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He began with an aerial view of the property and an illustration of the proposed site plan. Mr. Caycedo proposed options for the entrance and exit of the adjacent vacant lot. Upon concluding, Mr. Caycedo made himself available for members' questions. Rochelle Lecavalier, one of the owners of the subject property, explained her outreach to the owner of the adjacent parcel. Alan Klasfeld, representing the owners of the adjacent property, commented on past contact with the applicant and expressed his opposition to the project. Glenn Gromann shared his support of staff's assessment of the project but conveyed his desire to see the property developed in some way. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Ms. Lecavalier and Mr. Caycedo offered final comments. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer to approve Ordinance No. 5535. Jim Bell and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. Discussion ensued. Both property owners indicated their desire to communicate about the project. Mayor Singer asked City staff for direction regarding continuance of the of the items. Mr. Schaad, the City Manager and City Attorney provided information. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson to amend the main motion to continue the public hearings for Ordinance Nos. 5535 and 5536, and Resolution Nos. 118-2020 and 119-2020 to the October 27, 2020 Council Meeting. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amended and restated conditional use approval incorporating the conditional use approvals granted by Resolution Nos. 195-87, 145-88, 193-90, 201-96 and 112-97, and authorizing, pursuant to Sections 28-340(2) and 28-340(4 }, Code of Ordinances, an increase in the number of preschool students from 176 to 183 (an increase of seven (7) students), an increase in the number of daycare students from 368 to 428 (an increase of 60 students), and an increase in the number of staff from 70 to 80 (an increase of ten (10) staff) in a Single-Family Residential (R-1-D) zoning district for the Congregation B'nai Israel located at 2200 West Yamato Road; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-96-05R2) The City Attorney confirmed the quasi-judicial procedures would continue to govern this public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex parte disclosures. Drew Capra, GIS Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. A brief history of the property was provided, accompanied by a description of the existing location and its current uses. The site plan was displayed, as were maps illustrating the proposed guardhouse and new landscaping. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with a condition regarding the sidewalk along the front of the subject property. Development Services Staff recommends approval subject to the conditions set forth in the resolution. Upon concluding, Mr. Capra made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Neil Schiller, on behalf of the applicant, made the presentation. He began with aerial photos of the property and outlined the conditional use approval. Components of the proposed site plan were discussed, and a drawing of the traffic movement plan was shown. Upon concluding, he responded to members' questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 125-2020. Members made additional comments, and Mr. Schaad, Mr. Ahnell and Ms. Frieser responded to questions. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-340(4), Code of Ordinances, to authorize a new public school for students from Pre­ Kindergarten through 8th grade in a Single-Family Residential (R-1-D) zoning district for the Addison Mizner School generally located at 199 Southwest 12th Avenue; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-20-02) Mayor Singer advised the same quasi-judicial procedures would apply to this public hearing. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex parte disclosures. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Lindgren began with a description of the subject property and provided an overview of the project. The site plan was displayed, and components of the property described. The landscape plan and illustrations of the proposed school were shown. Elements of the interlocal agreement were reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Mr. Lindgren noted that the project is consistent with the comprehensive plan, and Development Services staff recommended approval with the conditions listed in the resolution. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Council Member Mayotte inquired about updates to SW 12th Avenue and lengthening the school zone. The City Manager provided additional information. Zach Bihr, Municipal Services Director, gave a short PowerPoint presentation highlighting the City's planned updates to SW 12 Avenue and Royal Palm Road. Upon concluding he responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Kari Botek, on behalf of the Palm Beach County School Board, made the presentation. Upon concluding, she made herself available to respond to member's comments. The public comment period was opened. Glenn Gromann noted that the Palm Beach County School Board is not required to comply with City landscape requirements and asked if they had to comply with the City's sign code. Mr. Lindgren, the City Manager and City Attorney provided additional information. Ms. Botek confirmed that fencing around the perimeter of the school would be supplemented with landscaping. Seeing no one else indicated their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 126-2020. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," Article IV, Division 4, "Sidewalks and Bikeways," Section 23-162, "Sidewalk Policy," Code of Ordinances, to clarify the requirement to construct new sidewalks and/or expand existing sidewalks as part of a redevelopment; and to exclude the south side of Yamato Road (between Military Trail and Saint Andrews Boulevard only) from the eight foot minimum sidewalk width requirement; amending Sections 23-161 through 23-165 to update terminology and to delete, revise and/or restate certain definitions and terms; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-04) Osny Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Background of similar text amendments brought before prior Councils were reviewed. Mr. Jean then provided a summary of the changes to the code language in the proposed amendment. Aerial views were displayed of locations in the City where 8' sidewalks had been installed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The City Manager provided clarification and additional information. Discussion ensued. Mr. Jean, Mr. Ahnell and Mr. Schaad responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Neil Schiller, on behalf of B'nai Israel, gave a short PowerPoint presentation in support of the ordinance. Glenn Gromann noted that while the sidewalk requirements may inversely impact non-profit organizations, creating special dispensations for a limited group of property owners may create a liability for the City. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Thomson, Seconded by Mayor Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5532. Council Member Thomson expressed his support for the ordinance. He noted the low amount of pedestrian traffic in the area and shared his concern that the requirement places a burden on religious non-profit institutions. Council Member Mayotte stated her opposition to the ordinance, as did Deputy Mayor O'Rourke, citing their desire to meet walkability goals and enhance pedestrian safety. City Manager Ahnell clarified the cost estimate provided by staff for sidewalk extension. Mr. Ahnell advised that, should the City undertake the replacement of the sidewalks, ownership of the sidewalk would need to be transferred to the City from affected property owners. The City Attorney and City Manager provided additional information. Discussion ensued. The City Attorney confirmed that any construction within the City was required to meet code requirements. She then read new language into the record to delete the exclusion of the Yamato area from the 8' sidewalk requirement. The changes were confirmed by Mr. Schaad. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend the motion on the floor to remove the language excluding the south side of Yamato Road from the sidewalk requirement. Motion carried on a 3 to 1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte voting yes; Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5532 as amended. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for proposed Charter amendments to be considered at the regular election on March 9, 2021, to amend Article V, "Qualifications and Elections," Section 5.03, "Qualifications," of the City Charter to modify the qualification requirements for candidates for City Council, including the office of Mayor, by: (i) extending the length of the residency requirement, establishing certain requirements for residency, and requiring proof of residency (with procedures adopted by ordinance), and (ii) eliminating the qualifying fee and requiring signatures of registered voters (with procedures adopted by ordinance); if the Charter amendment(s) are approved, amending Chapter 6, "Elections," of the Code of Ordinances to create Section 6-16, "Proof of Residency," prescribing procedures for proving proposed amendment, and Section 6-17, "Filing of Petition," prescribing procedures for collection, submission, and verification of signatures of voters; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for revisions to the City Charter and codification in the City Code, respectively; providing an effective date City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided a brief overview of the amendment, noting that the ordinance had been revised to delete provisions for proof of residency as that issue was being addressed by a separate ordinance. Upon concluding, she made herself available for member's questions. Mayor Singer commented on the proposed requirement for signatures in lieu of a qualifying fee, pointing out similar requirements in other Florida municipalities. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann expressed concern regarding proof of residency requirements and privacy issues related to public record exemptions in Florida Statute 119. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Ms. Frieser provided clarification. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5539. Ms. Frieser clarified that the motion to approve was regarding the revised version of the ordinance, dated September 9, 2020, which included deletion of language from the title relating to section 6-16 of the Code. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a PowerPoint presentation on the 2020-2021 budget. Mr. Ahnell reviewed the mission, vision, and guiding principles of the City and discussed the priorities under each . Significant challenges and opportunities were outlined . Mr. Ahnell advised that the millage rate would be marginally lower than that of the previous year and noted that the City's assessed property values continued to rise . Changes to the general fund operating costs from the previous year were highlighted. Mr. Ahnell then reviewed the tax bill flyer and emphasized the comparison to other cities, noting that the City's property tax rate continues to be below that of surrounding municipalities. The fire assessment fee and water and sewer rates remain unchanged, and sanitation rates would go up slightly due to keeping those services in-house. Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, reviewed the operating re-budgets. Ms. McGuire explained that these were due to projects across multiple City departments that had not reached completion within the previous fiscal year. Upon concluding, Mr. Ahnell and Ms. McGuire responded to members' questions.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Code of Ordinances pertaining to mobile food dispensing vehicles; deleting Chapter 16, Article Ill, Section 16-58, "Operating Food-Service Vehicles Near Schools," Code of Ordinances, to delete a prohibition on operating a mobile food dispensing vehicle near a school; amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide a definition and specify zoning districts where mobile food dispensing vehicles shall be an allowed accessory use; to create Article XV, Division 1, Section 28-1315, "Mobile Food Dispensing Vehicles," to set forth regulations; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-06) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this was the second of two public hearings. A brief summary of the ordinance was provided. The Planning and Zoning Board unanimously recommended against adoption of the ordinance, primarily due to concerns regarding food-service vehicle owners operating in residential neighborhoods. Development Services staff recommends approval and advises the concerns of the Planning and Zoning Board be addressed in a separate follow-up ordinance. Upon concluding, he responded to members' questions. The City Attorney provided additional information. The public hearing was opened, and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5540. Members expressed concerns regarding the proposed ordinance. At the Mayor's request, City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser expounded on recent State statute and advised members that they may consider amending the parameters in a future ordinance. Discussion ensued . The City Manager provided additional information. Ms. Frieser noted that the proposed ordinance expands the permissions currently available. Members made final comments. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering tentative plat approval for Boca Haven (a replat of Lots 4 and 5 and a portion of Lot 3, Block 1, Bible Conference Estates) for an approximately 1.5 acre property generally located west of Northwest 6th Avenue and north and south of Northwest 6th Street extended; subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB- 19-02) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Golden, Land Development Coordinator, gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location of the proposed development was displayed, and the applicant's request was reviewed. Dimensions of the three subject lots were outlined. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Golden made herself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Noel Barnett, on behalf of the applicant, thanked City staff for the presentation and made himself available for members' questions. Steven Utrecht expressed his support for the project based on an amendment clarifying that there would be no filling of the lake to enlarge a lot. John Holland gave a PowerPoint presentation and shared his apprehension regarding the proposed development of the subject lot and highlighted potential impacts to his adjacent property. Kenneth Green referred to a letter he submitted to Council Members regarding his concerns about the proposed project. Noel Barnett responded to Mr. Holland's concerns regarding construction on the lot and potential drainage issues. Stephen Eigles, owner of the subject property, confirmed that he had no plans to fill the lake, as well as his desire to preserve existing landscaping. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information regarding the conditions of approval. The City Attorney asked for clarification of the language to be added to the resolution. Mr. Schaad and Tori Golden read language into the record regarding the proposed conditions. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 146-2020 as amended. Members made final comments. Motion passed 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan to authorize development of a 277-unit multifamily residential project and modify one (1) development parameter, pursuant to Sections 28-1720(1) and 28-1843, Code of Ordinances, to eliminate a required sidewalk in a specific location, for the property generally located at 6401, 6405, 6409, 6413 and 6421 Congress Avenue; considering a waiver of a plat requirement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-18-01) The Mayor confirmed the same quasi-judicial procedures previously read by the City Attorney would apply. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by noting that a site plan approval was not included in this proposal and would require a separate application, and if approved, the project would meet the residential unit capacity for the northwest planning area. Ms. Rahman provided an overview of the existing property, as well as a history of the location site plan approvals, noting that the proposed plan met all building setback requirements and requested no technical deviations. Ms. Rahman pointed out that there is no traffic signal at the existing driveway, but if warranted, installation would be funded by the property owner. Traffic flow and parking details were outlined, and the requirement for the applicant to install additional or enlarged sidewalks was discussed. A modification to development parameters that was supported by staff involved a decision to not install sidewalks in one particular area in order to preserve existing trees. Ms. Rahman explained the applicant's request for a waiver of platting requirements and variations from engineering design standards manual regarding parking space size. Both were supported by staff. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Ms. Rahman noted the rescheduling and re-advertisement of the item from the originally scheduled date. She advised the proposed project meets the intent of PMD and is consistent with the City's comprehensive plan. Staff recommends approval with the accompanying conditions included in the resolution. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, gave the presentation. Ms. Zachariades reviewed the deviations requested and noted the project met the City's planned mobility parameters. The existing site plan was shown and compared to the proposed master plan, highlighting the existing and proposed sidewalk and noted the improvements being made on 65th street by the applicant. Ingress and egress from the property were reviewed. Pedestrian connectivity and variations or surface parking spaces were discussed. An elevation of the proposed building was shown. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Ms. Zachariades confirmed there would be 25 electric car charging spaces throughout the property. John Donaldson, traffic engineer for the project, provided additional information. Jonathan Ounjian expressed his opposition to the project, citing his concerns with the project's density and resulting traffic. David Sergii conveyed his displeasure with a comment made by the representative of the applicant. Judy Farmer shared her concerns about project construction and how it would affect nearby businesses. During cross-examination, Mr. Ounjian asked for clarification about the determination of distance for intended uses. Ms. Zachariades responded. Mr. Schaad provided clarification regarding how the PMD matrix is utilized for evaluations and confirmed that staff has consistently applied the rules. He also noted that, per code, on-site notice was not required to be posted for this project. Ms. Zachariades made final comments. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 137-2020. Members made final comments. Mr. Schaad and Maria Tejera, City Traffic Engineer, responded to questions. Motion passed 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the acceptance of a donation of property located at 17751 Boca Club Boulevard (consisting of approximately 167.17 acres and known as the Boca Golf & Tennis Country Club) pursuant to the terms and conditions of a donation agreement (including a joint defense agreement); authorizing, after donation, a lease of the property to the donor for up to one year (to provide a transition period); authorizing a waiver of procurement for an assumption of a lease of electric golf carts; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Deputy Mayor Michael Woika gave the PowerPoint presentation. The location and amenities of the property were reviewed. The history of the course and current ownership were discussed. The donation agreement, joint defense agreement, and ground lease were reviewed, and points of each were highlighted. The City Clerk read a letter into the record from the owners of the Boca Raton Hotel and Club. Mr. Woika noted that during the 11-month transition period, City staff would meet with neighbors to address their concerns. He advised there would be no debt associated with taking over the golf course and that staff would assess the potential fees and rates for play. Upon concluding, Mr. Woika made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Ron Klein, Ann Averso, Frank Reiss, Herb Levy, Peter Pinter, Robert Trinchetto, Kenneth Denslow, expressed concerns about how the golf course donation would affect the security, traffic and property values of existing country club members and asked for a postponement of the vote. The Mayor read a letter into the record from Greg Galanis that stated his general support of the course donation and encouraged recreational development of the Ocean Breeze property. Jordan Serlin and Fred Weinberg shared concerns regarding jurisdiction issues for law enforcement and fire rescue responses. Craig Ehrnst expressed his support for the golf course donation. Shari and Sally Friedman, Jared Hershkowitz, Marilyn Soto, Kenneth Landau and Jeffry Chase conveyed their concerns about the course donation and possible affects to the surrounding residential neighborhood. The City Clerk read a comment submitted by Howard Markovitz asking for additional information about the donation. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 163-2020. Deputy City Manager Mike Woika responded to several of the comments made by the public. He stated there were no known environmental concerns and that some needed improvements had been identified. Fees would be assessed and determined at a later time. Mr. Woika noted that it was not the City's intention to operate the western golf course at the same time as the new course. City Manager Leif Ahnell addressed several additional questions, including, but not limited to, traffic concerns, golf course, pool, and tennis court maintenance, and security. Mr. Ahnell also advised that the current owners of the golf course would not be receiving tax breaks from the City in exchange for the donation. Discussion ensued. Members expressed their support and shared their commitment to the recreational development of the Ocean Breeze property. Motion passed on a 4 to 0 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: City Manager Leif Ahnell asked the City Clerk to read a letter from Council Member Jeremy Rodgers into the record. He then asked the Council for direction and advised the City Attorney could provide additional information. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser advised that, with respect to performing military service, elected officials may take a leave of absence which creates a 'temporarily unoccupied position'. Ms. Frieser explained that the remaining members of the body may elect an individual to fill the seat until either the elected official returns, or their term of office concludes. Discussion ensued. Additional information was provided by the City Attorney. Members thanked Council Member Rodgers for his service and Amanda Rodgers for her willingness to serve. Council Member Mayotte and Deputy Mayor O'Rourke suggested applicants be interviewed in order to fill the vacancy. There was consensus to direct staff to proceed with advertising of the temporary vacancy, and for applications to be due by 5:00 pm on October 22, 2020. Mayor Singer noted the time and asked for a motion to extend the meeting. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to extend the meeting beyond 11 :00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a site plan, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize construction of an approximately 6,399 square foot, 25 foot tall professional office building with covered and surface parking, together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1653(1 ), Code of Ordinances, to reduce required dimensions of parking spaces, for the Yamato Office Park generally located at 276 and 298 West Yamato Road, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-14-02/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11. A., B., C., and D. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. Ordinance No. 5535 would require four votes for passage. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Schaad began by providing a brief review of the application components. He explained that staff recommended denial based on the compatibility of the proposed future land use and zoning given the parcel configuration and surrounding land use. It was noted that if Council approved the land use amendment, however, the remaining elements of the application met code standards for approval. If the application was approved, Mr. Schaad remarked that approval would not restrict or limit use of the adjacent property in any way under its current land use and zoning designations. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Rochelle Lecavalier, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. The cross-access easement with the adjoining property owner was highlighted. Drawings of the exterior elevations were presented, and considerations to the residential neighborhood were emphasized. Ms. Lecavalier discussed her efforts to come to an agreement with the adjacent property owner and asked Council to support the project application. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Mitchell Kirschner, on behalf of the adjoining landowner, expressed agreement with staffs recommendation of denial and suggested alternative development that was consistent and compatible with the existing residential use land designation. Robert Sweetapple, also speaking on behalf of the adjoining landowner, urged Council to follow staffs recommendation and deny the application, and stated that the rezoning of the properties should be considered under one consolidated application. Juan Caycedo, architect of the proposed project, provided additional information and asked for Council's approval. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5535. Council Member Mayotte asked the City Attorney to clarify potential issues regarding the proposed land use change. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information regarding the current application and clarification of the term 'spot zoning'. Mr. Schaad confirmed that the adjoining property owner would have the same rights offered to them as the current applicant and provided clarification of application processing timelines. Members made final comments and expressed their support for the project. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a temporary appointment to fill Council Member Rodgers' seat (temporarily unoccupied due to military leave of absence); providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Manager Leif Ahnell briefly reviewed the options available to fill the temporarily vacant council seat. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke commented on similar situations that the current and prior City Councils had encountered in the past. The public comment period was opened. Alan Feinberg expressed his disappointment that candidates who are running in March would not be disqualified from filling the temporarily unoccupied seat. Seeing no one else indicated their desire to speak, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 165-2020. Members reiterated their gratitude to all of the applicants. Council Member Thomson commented on the option to leave the seat open. Members weighed in, and discussion ensued. There was general agreement to fill the temporarily vacant seat. Council Member Monica Mayotte nominated Yvette Drucker. Council Member Thomson nominated Amanda Rodgers, Julie Vianale, and Kerry Koen. Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke nominated Yvette Drucker. Members made final comments and there was unanimous consent to close the nominations. In the voting, Ms. Drucker received three votes, Ms. Rodgers received one vote. Therefore, Ms. Drucker was appointed to fill the temporary unoccupied City Council vacancy. City Attorney Frieser provided additional information regarding the swearing-in and onset of Ms. Drucker's service. Ms. Frieser then noted that Ms. Drucker's name would be added to the Resolution and suggested additional language regarding the swearing-in and commencement. Motion was made by Mayor Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to amend Resolution No. 165-2020, to include the language as provided by the City Attorney. Motion carried 4 to Oona voice vote. Motion to approve Resolution No. 165-2020 as amended. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1396, Code of Ordinances, to authorize construction of a convenience store in excess of 750 square feet and accessory to a service station in the R-B-1 zoning district for the property generally located at 5899 North Federal Highway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-18-01) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex parte disclosures. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by providing a description of the property location. Mr. Lindgren reviewed components of the application and noted that it complied with conditional use approval criteria and was consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren responded to members' questions regarding generator installation and buffers between the subject property and adjacent residential homes. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information regarding conditional use approval requirements. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, thanked staff for their presentation. She confirmed that proposed plans included a generator that would power the whole site and that a wall and additional landscaping would be added to the west side of the property. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. There was no cross-examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 150-2020. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the request of the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District for an exemption from the annual tax increment payment due to the Boca Raton Community Redevelopment Agency pursuant to Section 163.387(2)(d), Florida Statutes and City Resolution No. 9-2020; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Michael Woika, Deputy City Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Woika began by providing background and history of the Tax Increment Program. He reviewed Resolution No. 9-2020 and outlined the procedure for a special district to request exemption from the tax increment payments. Estimated payments of the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (BPD) for the next five years were displayed. Mr. Woika reviewed the application factors for exemption including, but not limited to, fiscal and operational impact of the exemption to both the CRA and BPD, the benefit to the specific purpose for which the BPD was created, and the benefit of the BPD's activities to the City's area of operation. City staff recommended denial of the application. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Jacob Horowitz, attorney, spoke on behalf of the BPD. He began with a review of the debt payment history. Mr. Horowitz suggested that, as past payments had been applied to the debt service at Mizner Park and that debt was satisfied, the funds might be better redirected through the BPD to other projects within the community. Briann Harms, Executive Director of the BPD, reiterated points made by Mr. Horowitz and, citing the importance of the City's parks and beaches, asked members for their support. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 177-2020 to deny the exemption. Members commented and requested clarification from City staff. City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information and advised that, if the request were granted, there would be a significant shortfall in CRA revenues. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser noted that the criteria for exemption comes from State statute. Discussion ensued. Mr. Ahnell further clarified that the only individuals paying into the CRA and the Downtown are Downtown property owners. Mr. Horowitz and Ms. Harms responded to points made. Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, confirmed the information relayed by the City Manager. Members expressed their positions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved conditional use and master plan (Resolution No. 1-93, as amended by Resolution Nos. 14-2001, 160-2010 and 70-2019), to amend conditions of approval by eliminating a requirement to extend a left turn lane on North Military Trail, and changing the timing of a required extension of a southbound right turn lane on North Military Trail, for Lynn University located at 3601 North Military Trail; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-10-04R2) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Members made their ex parte disclosures. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Lindgren highlighted the subject location and provided a brief overview of the application. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. It was noted that the proposed amendment is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren made himself available for members questions. The public hearing was opened. Lauren Odom, on behalf of the applicant, asked members for their approval and made herself available for questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 180-2020. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to the infrastructure element of the City's Comprehensive Plan to update the City's 10-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan, incorporate alternative water supply projects identified in the South Florida Water Management District's Regional Water Supply Plan, and revise potable water level of service standards; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-20-03) Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Hansen began by describing the transmittal process and requirements of the State guidelines. Updated elements of the 2016 Water Supply Facilities Work Plan were reviewed, including but not limited to, population projections, potable water distribution and storage figures, and City water/reclaimed water commodity rates. Ms. Hansen noted that the amendments were consistent with Comprehensive Plan. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to transmit Ordinance No. 5551. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a Universal Conditional (UC) amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 12.08 acres, generally located at 2600 Northwest 5th Avenue and 2500 Northwest 5th Avenue, from Residential Low (RL) to Residential High (RH), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-17-03/SC) Mayor Singer advised this was a transmittal hearing. Tamashbeen Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by explaining that the only element of the application currently under consideration was the transmittal of the large-scaled Future Land Use Map (FLUM). Ms. Rahman then reviewed the steps for consideration of the FLUM amendment request. The location and future land use designation of the subject property were discussed. Staff evaluation was provided regarding the project's consistency with both the Comprehensive Plan and City Code, compatibility with surrounding land use and development, and concurrency with available public services. The traffic impact study was reviewed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Development Services staff recommended denial, noting that the proposed change to the property's zoning designation was incompatible and inconsistent with surrounding future land uses. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman made herself available for members' questions. Council Member Mayotte inquired what a typical land use transition would encompass and asked if the transmittal were approved, what additional planning would be involved. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke asked if there were plans for future work on N.W. 5th Avenue. Ms. Rahman and Marie Tejera, City Traffic Engineer, provided additional information. Mayor Singer inquired about other Residential High (RH) zoning designated areas within the City. Ms. Rahman and City Manager Ahnell responded. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by describing the location of the proposed development and highlighted features of the surrounding areas. John Clifford, speaking on behalf of the property management of the proposed project, provided additional information regarding community design and safety features for future student residents. Ms. Miskel highlighted components of the application request, including the Future Land Use Map amendment and the rezoning justification, and noted the City's need for additional student housing. She stated that the application was consistent with the City's Comprehensive Plan and provided results from a poll of the community regarding student housing. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Mayor Singer asked Ms. Miskel if the project had received endorsement from FAU. Ms. Miskel advised that the University had approved the concept but could not endorse private entities. She was asked to expound on the proposed pedestrian bridge over the El Rio canal. Ms. Miskel responded to additional questions from Council Members Mayotte and Drucker. Mr. Ahnell provided information. The public comment period was opened. Renata Pawlowski, a board member of the Windwood community, expressed concerns about traffic impacts of the proposed development. Carol Campion, Kathleen MacDonald, Marcus Wood, Patricia Fyke expressed their opposition to the project. Hailey Berman, Nhu Nguyen, Alan Feinberg, Kevin Buchanon, Malcolm Butters, and Paul Kilgallon spoke in support of the project. Ryan Bowersox suggested Windwood expand onto the subject property. Sally Celano cited traffic and security as her main concerns in opposition to the project. Steve Edwards stated he was in support of additional student housing but felt the proposed density was incompatible with the area. Lorena Villegas and Margarita Pazmino spoke in opposition to the rezoning. Joseph Graubart commented that he did not feel the project served the community. The City Clerk read comments submitted by Neal Temple who stated that the City was not responsible to supply student housing, and by Peggy Lowenberg, who inquired if the size of the property could be cut in half. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public comment period was closed. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the applicant, responded to comments made during the public comment period. She remarked that existing traffic issues would be improved by the project and commented on zoning issues. Council Members asked additional questions regarding the proposed project's pedestrian connection to the FAU campus and future widening of N.W. 5th Avenue. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, and City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to transmit Ordinance No. 5537. Members shared their final thoughts and their positions on the project. Motion carried 3 votes to 2; Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Mayor Scott Singer and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. Mr. Schaad provided information about the transmittal process.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, by amending Article XI, Division 10, "MC Medical Center District," Section 28-927, "Yards," Code of Ordinances, to modify the minimum yard (setback) requirements of buildings over 25 feet in height, and by amending Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1653, "Design," Code of Ordinances, to reduce the minimum parking stall dimension requirements for surface parking lots accessory to a hospital in the MC Medical Center zoning district; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-07) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by reviewing the setback provisions of the amendment. Revisions of the proposed amendment were highlighted, including changes to parking stall dimensions and differences regarding setbacks of property abutting both residential and non-residential properties. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for members' questions. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke remarked on the change to parking space size and asked if this should be addressed in City streamlining priorities. Mr. Schaad and the Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miske!, on behalf of the applicant, thanked Development Services staff for their work on the project. She described the applicant's outreach to nearby residential property owners and made herself available for members' questions. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5552. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. The meeting was recessed at approximately 9:10 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:16 pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the Spanish River Presbyterian Church located at 2400 West Yamato Road: (i) an amended and restated conditional use approval consolidating conditional use Resolution Nos. 1-82, 108-85, 36-94 and 203-94, and (ii) an amendment to the approved conditional use approval (Resolution No. 1-82, as amended) to authorize demolition of the existing outdoor pavilion cafeteria, and construction of an approximately 24,410 square foot cafetorium, classroom and office building, and a 1,144 square foot covered walkway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-20-03) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hansen, senior planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by describing the existing property and reviewed components of the applicant's request. A site plan of the property and drawings of the proposed building were displayed, and an abandonment of a utility easement was discussed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Ms. Hansen then reviewed a request by the applicant to revise condition of approval #9 for the amended site plan, concerning a management plan for an existing one acre preserve. Proposed revisions to the site plan resolution were shown. Development Services staff recommended approval of both the conditional use and the proposed amendment to site plan condition #9. The public hearing was opened. Lindsay Libes and David Ofstein, on behalf of the applicant, thanked Development Services staff for their work and made themselves available for members' questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 1-2021 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.
