units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the conveyance of City-owned land consisting of approximately 15 acres (generally located east of Military Trail, south of Spanish River Boulevard, and southeast of Don Estridge High Tech Middle School) to the School District of Palm Beach County, pursuant to Chapter 13, Article Ill, "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances, for construction of a new public elementary school, pursuant to the terms and conditions of a Donation Agreement, and subject to the retention (or receipt) of certain public utility easements; and authorizing the execution of: an interlocal agreement for the joint use of a parking lot, an easement over certain lands adjacent to the donated property for stormwater drainage purposes, and such other instruments to effectuate the conveyance; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Michael Woika, Deputy City Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by reviewing the background of the City's relationship with the School Board concerning the property. An aerial map of the land was displayed and the location of the property to be donated was shown. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Mr. Woika briefly reviewed the documentation associated with the donation of the City property and discussed the changes made to specific documents since the Ordinance had been introduced in November. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Mayor Singer lauded School Board and City staff for their work on the project. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke inquired about the process for deciding on a school name. Council Member Mayotte expressed her support for the new school. The public hearing was opened. Kristin Garrison, on behalf of the PBC School Board, thanked staff for their presentation and explained the School Board's policy for naming of schools. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5554. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; amending the lists of permitted and conditional uses in all zoning districts regarding governmental uses and facilities; amending Chapter 28, Article XIII, Division 5, "PL Public Land District," Section 28-1238, "Development Parameters," and Article XV, Section 28-1305, "City and beach and parks district parks facilities; City water, sewer, reclaimed water, and stormwater facilities; City buildings, facilities and uses; and City police and fire stations," Code of Ordinances, to: (i) specify whether the Planning and Zoning Board, the Parks and Recreation Board, or the City Council has the authority to review and approve site plan applications for certain City and other Governmental uses; (ii) provide for setback and landscape buffer requirements (for certain City and other governmental uses in nonresidential zoning districts) to be determined as part of a site plan review and approval (except where abutting a residential zoning district); and (iii) delete obsolete language and redundant requirements with respect to such City and other Governmental uses; amending Article XIII, Division 2, "LB Civic Center and Limited Business District," Section 28-1173, "Uses Permitted," and creating Section 28-1173.1, "Conditional Uses," to require conditional use approval for certain uses that already require City Council approval; reformatting and restating various provisions for clarity; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-19-01) The Mayor noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, made the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a summary of the ordinance, noting that it was primarily a streamlining measure. He stated that the amendment would correct inconsistencies in provisions for a number of sections in the current code, and he briefly reviewed the affected sections. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for members' questions. Council Member Mayotte asked Mr. Bell about the concerns of the Planning and Zoning Board, specifically in relation to the O5C school. Mr. Bell provided additional information. The public comment period was opened, and seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Mayor Singer advised the second public hearing on this item would be on January 26, 2021.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," Article IV, Division 4, "Sidewalks and Bikeways," Section 23-162, "Sidewalk Policy," Code of Ordinances, to exclude the south side of Yamato Road (between Military Trail and Saint Andrews Boulevard only) from the eight foot minimum sidewalk width requirement; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-10) Jean Osny, Senior Planner, made the PowerPoint presentation. He began by reviewing the proposed amendment and existing sidewalk policy. Mr. Jean provided an analysis of the amendment, including a "special corridor" sidewalk standard due to the existing uses in the area. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the ordinance by a vote of 5 to 1. The public hearing was opened. Neil Schiller, on behalf of B'Nai Israel, commented in support of the ordinance, citing the financial hardship that the requirement would cause to the affected non-profit properties. David Ofstein and Ronald Tobias, on behalf of Spanish River Church, also expressed their support of the ordinance, citing low pedestrian traffic on that specific stretch of road and the economic impact to the religious organizations. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public comment period was closed. Council Member Thomson expressed his support of the ordinance, noting the low amount of pedestrian traffic of the subject area. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke and Council Member Mayotte shared their opposition to the item, citing their commitment to walkability and safety. Mayor Singer commented in support of the ordinance. Council Member Drucker questioned if voting in favor of the ordinance would be setting a precedent for future sidewalk exemption requests. Discussion ensued. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5556. Motion failed on a 2 to 3 vote; Mayor Scott Singer and Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, and Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a plat entitled "101 Pine Circle" (a replat of Lot 1, Block 7, Boca Raton Hills Section One), pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, generally located at 101 Pine Circle; authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-13-03R1/SUB) Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items A., B., C., and D. would be conducted contemporaneously, and a separate vote would be taken for each Ordinance and Resolution. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osny Jean, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by noting that the application was comprised of a PUD master plan amendment, a site plan amendment, and a plat approval. Mr. Jean displayed an aerial map of the site and provided background of previously granted approvals for the property. Analysis of the PUD master plan and site plan amendments were reviewed. Rooftop amenities areas were discussed, and privacy measures such as rooftop screenings were highlighted. Revisions to the approved tentative plat were noted and drawings of the proposed elevations were shown. The site plan traffic analysis was presented. Mr. Jean advised that if this application were denied, the property could still be developed in accordance with the previously granted approval. At the Dec. 3, 2020 Planning and Zoning (P&Z) Board meeting, concerns regarding traffic, density, rooftop amenities areas and parking were discussed. Development Services staff and the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with the conditions included in the ordinance and resolutions. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean responded to members' questions regarding fencing and parking space locations on the property. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided additional information related to fence height limitations in residential areas. The public hearing was opened. Fabio Pereira, on behalf of the applicant, briefly reviewed the changes to the application since the prior approval. Mr. Pereira noted the potential for the project to alleviate existing drainage issues and stated that neighbors' questions about privacy had been addressed. He then made himself available for members' questions. Andrew Evanch expressed misgivings about the size of the project. Aaron Markoff conveyed his opposition to the project and shared slides that displayed past traffic incidents in the area. Council Member Thomson asked Mr. Markoff to clarify one of his comments regarding legal issues involving the former Mayor. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke asked staff for the Council vote from the previously approved application; Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, stated that the vote had been 5 to 1 in approval. Blanca Salcedo, Kathleen Spaulding, Michael Kohner and Susanna Cox expressed their opposition to the project, citing concerns regarding privacy, traffic, and the impact of construction on neighborhood streets. Frank Jonas, speaking on behalf of Renai Jonas, commented on a court case involving the former Mayor and shared concerns about the rooftop fence, drainage issues and existing setbacks. City Clerk Susan Saxton read a comment from Vittoria Charneco who opposed the density of the project. Sonia Olson relayed doubts that the existing soil could support the proposed structures. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Osny Jean responded to comments and questions submitted during the public hearing. Concerns related to traffic issues were addressed, and a condition of the previous development approval was highlighted which directed the property owner to plan and maintain street calming improvements, as well as add a five-foot sidewalk and additional street trees. In response to questions about privacy, Mr. Jean advised the rooftop trellis and landscaping had been added at the request of staff. Mr. Schaad explained that rooftop amenities were permitted, providing the rooftop was structurally sufficient and all required safety measures were followed. Zach Bihr, Municipal Services Director, stated that his department would review any flooding concerns related to the site during the planning review process. Mr. Bihr also explained that geotechnical and structural engineers would address concerns about stability of the land during the building process. In response to comments regarding the 2015 City Council vote on the original approval, the City Attorney advised that she was not aware of any issues which would impact the effectiveness of the original development orders. Mr. Jean responded to additional questions about fencing on the property and confirmed that the development was required to have a HOA declaration. Mr. Pereira, on behalf of the applicant, stated that there would be additional landscaping to supplement the fencing, and that any items added to the roof would be approved by HOA Mr. Pereira also responded to objections regarding traffic and parking. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5560. Members requested that language be amended to address fencing. Mr. Jean provided clarifying language prepared by staff regarding condition No. 1 of the amended site plan, Resolution No. 4-2021. Mr. Schaad proposed additional wording be added to read" ... and the fence shall be completely opaque". Maria Tejera, Traffic Engineer, provided information regarding traffic issues and informed members that the applicant could be required to install traffic calming features ranging from signage to speed bumps. Council Members thanked residents for their participation and made final comments, noting the number of changes being made from the prior development approval. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 3-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 4-2021 with the amendments previously read into the record concerning fencing. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Concerns related to traffic issues were addressed, and a condition of the previous development approval was highlighted which directed the property owner to plan and maintain street calming improvements, as well as add a five-foot sidewalk and additional street trees. In response to questions about privacy, Mr. Jean advised the rooftop trellis and landscaping had been added at the request of staff. Mr. Schaad explained that rooftop amenities were permitted, providing the rooftop was structurally sufficient and all required safety measures were followed. Zach Bihr, Municipal Services Director, stated that his department would review any flooding concerns related to the site during the planning review process. Mr. Bihr also explained that geotechnical and structural engineers would address concerns about stability of the land during the building process. In response to comments regarding the 2015 City Council vote on the original approval, the City Attorney advised that she was not aware of any issues which would impact the effectiveness of the original development orders. Mr. Jean responded to additional questions about fencing on the property and confirmed that the development was required to have a HOA declaration. Mr. Pereira, on behalf of the applicant, stated that there would be additional landscaping to supplement the fencing, and that any items added to the roof would be approved by HOA Mr. Pereira also responded to objections regarding traffic and parking. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5560. Members requested that language be amended to address fencing. Mr. Jean provided clarifying language prepared by staff regarding condition No. 1 of the amended site plan, Resolution No. 4-2021. Mr. Schaad proposed additional wording be added to read" ... and the fence shall be completely opaque". Maria Tejera, Traffic Engineer, provided information regarding traffic issues and informed members that the applicant could be required to install traffic calming features ranging from signage to speed bumps. Council Members thanked residents for their participation and made final comments, noting the number of changes being made from the prior development approval. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Code of Ordinances; amending the lists of permitted and conditional uses in all zoning districts regarding governmental uses and facilities; amending Chapter 28, Article XIII, Division 5, "PL Public Land District," Section 28-1238, "Development Parameters," and Article XV, Section 28-1305, "City and beach and parks district parks facilities; City water, sewer, reclaimed water, and stormwater facilities; City buildings, facilities and uses; and City police and fire stations," Code of Ordinances, to: (i) specify whether the Planning and Zoning Board, the Parks and Recreation Board, or the City Council has the authority to review and approve site plan applications for certain City and other Governmental uses; (ii) provide for setback and landscape buffer requirements (for certain City and other governmental uses in nonresidential zoning districts) to be determined as part of a site plan review and approval (except where abutting a residential zoning district); and (iii) delete obsolete language and redundant requirements with respect to such City and other Governmental uses; amending Article XIII, Division 2, "LB Civic Center and Limited Business District," Section 28-1173, "Uses Permitted," and creating Section 28-1173.1, "Conditional Uses," to require conditional use approval for certain uses that already require City Council approval; reformatting and restating various provisions for clarity; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-19-01) Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation and advised this was the second of two public hearings for this ordinance. He noted that the proposed text amendment deleted obsolete language, redundant requirements, and would make City Code more logical and accessible. A summary of the amendments was provided. Staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5555. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke noted that this ordinance was created in response to population growth within the City and the resulting need for additional services. Mayor Singer thanked staff for their streamlining efforts. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide for athletic training facility uses and define such uses; amending Article XII, "Industrial Districts," to provide for an "Athletic Training Facility" as a permitted use in the M-1 Light Industrial and M-3 Manufacturing Industrial Districts; amending Article XV, Division 1, "Supplementary District Regulations," Section 28-1316, "Athletic Training Facilities," to establish regulations for such uses and establish a 15,000 square footage limit; amending Article XVI, Section 28-1655, "Required Off­ Street Parking," to provide parking standards for athletic training facilities; amending Article XII, Division 6, "M-1 Light Industrial District," Section 28-1097, "Permitted Uses," to provide consistency in terminology and formatting with respect to athletic training facilities; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-01) Mayor Singer noted that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. Regulations and limitations addressed by the amendment were discussed and parking rules were reviewed. Regulations for competitive events were also discussed. Development Services staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell responded to questions and provided clarification. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. The Mayor announced the date of the second hearing would be February 9, 2021.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Police and Firefighters' Retirement System; amending Section 12-134, "Administration" and Section 12-151, "Retirement Dates and Benefits; Optional Provisions for Firefighters" of Article IV, "Pension Plan for Police and Firefighters' of Chapter 12, "Pensions and Retirement," Code of Ordinances, effectuating the pension related provisions of the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the City and the IAFF (Firefighters Union); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Michael Woika, Deputy City Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Woika noted that the most noticeable change to the plan was the extension of the deferred retirement option plan (DROP) period. It was noted that changes to the pension plan were associated with firefighters only and not police officers, as the only negotiations completed so far had been with the firefighters' union. Mr. Woika reviewed the modifications made to the ordinance. Comments submitted by Bob Sugarman, attorney for the Police and Firefighters' Pension Board, were read into the record. Mr. Woika then shared responses to the comments and addressed questions about administration, delay, postponement, "undropping" and revisions. The actuarial impact statement reflected a contribution increase of $167,707. Staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The City Attorney offered additional clarification of revisions to the ordinance that were not readily apparent due to the lightness of the shading. In response to Mr. Sugarman's comments regarding DROP participation, Ms. Frieser and Mr. Woika provided additional clarification concerning section 5. The public hearing was opened. David Eddinger, President of Firefighters of Boca Raton Local 1560, expressed his support of the ordinance. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5561. Mayor Singer suggested additional language be added to provide clarification to the end of Section 5, page 6, line 3, " ... at which point the member's employment shall terminate." Ms. Frieser noted that while the proposed wording did reflect what the section provides, the existing language had already been bargained and negotiated with the union. Ms. Frieser also noted that the City's pension lawyer had suggested the language be kept as is. The Mayor inquired the wording could be added to the meeting minutes, to which Ms. Frieser agreed, and she reiterated that the language of the plan clearly provides that the end of the DROP period and the end of member's employment is coterminous. There was consensus among members to have the language added to the minutes. Mayor Singer noted that his vote to approve the ordinance would be predicated on its inclusion. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke pointed out that the communication from Pension Board trustee John Girard was not received until just prior to the meeting. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 12, "Pensions and Retirement," Article Ill, "General Employees' Pensions," Section 12-105, "Deferred Retirement Option Plan," Code of Ordinances, to modify the maximum DROP participation period; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Michael Woika, Deputy City Manager, reviewed the ordinance. Mr. Woika stated that the changes primarily reflected the extension of the DROP period from 60 to 84 months and the associated provisions. There were no comments received from the General Employee Pension Board. The Police and Firefighter Pension Board did submit comments, and the resulting revisions were reflected on page 2 of the ordinance. The actuarial impact statement reflected a zero additional contribution as a result of this change. Upon concluding, Mr. Woika made himself available for members' questions. The City Attorney noted that the changes referred to by Mr. Woika were on page 2, subsection C. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. units.text: Council Member Drucker advised that staff from Water Utility billing was working with residents to create payment plans for those financially impacted by the pandemic. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide for athletic training facility uses and define such uses; amending Article XII, "Industrial Districts," to provide for an "Athletic Training Facility" as a permitted use in the M-1 Light Industrial and M-3 Manufacturing Industrial Districts; amending Article XV, Division 1, "Supplementary District Regulations," Section 28-1316, "Athletic Training Facilities," to establish regulations for such uses and establish a 15,000 square footage limit; amending Article XVI, Section 28-1655, "Required Off­ Street Parking," to provide parking standards for athletic training facilities; amending Article XII, Division 6, "M-1 Light Industrial District," Section 28-1097, "Permitted Uses," to provide consistency in terminology and formatting with respect to athletic training facilities; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-01) Jim Bell, Long Range Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Bell noted that this was the second public hearing for this item. He began with a brief overview of the ordinance and discussed the clarifications and changes being proposed by the amendment. He explained that the amendment addressed problems in the City Code related to athletic training facilities. Mr. Bell stated the ordinance would make zoning districts M-1, M-2, and M-3 consistent and also provide needed definitions, specific regulations, and parking requirements. He affirmed that the proposed regulations and limitations would help to address potential future loss of industrial space in the City. Staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5558. Motion carried 4 to 0; Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 22, "Marine Structures," Article Ill, "Docks and Other Mooring Facilities," Code of Ordinances, by creating Section 22-69, "Marine Structures in the Hillsboro and C-15 Canals," to provide that certain size requirements for dolphins, finger piers and boat lifts in the Hillsboro and C-15 Canals shall not be applicable so long as a valid permit for such improvements has been issued by the South Florida Water Management District, and by amending Section 22-58, "Docks," to eliminate a duplicative provision; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-08) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Schaad began by explaining that this item was created to streamline the code. He explained that the City defers to South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) requirements for size and location requirements of docks, dolphin pilings, finger piers, and boatlifts. A map was shown that displayed the jurisdiction of the Hillsboro and C-15 canals within the City. Mr. Schaad noted the frequency of variance requests due to the shallow depth of the Hillsboro Canal near its shore and C-15 canal limitations. He reassured members that all marine structures would remain subject to building permit requirements. The Marine Advisory Board recommended approval 6-1 and the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval 7-0. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. units.full: Ordinance No. 5566 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 22, "Marine Structures," Article Ill, "Docks and Other Mooring Facilities," Code of Ordinances, by creating Section 22-69, "Marine Structures in the Hillsboro and C-15 Canals," to provide that certain size requirements for dolphins, finger piers and boat lifts in the Hillsboro and C-15 Canals shall not be applicable so long as a valid permit for such improvements has been issued by the South Florida Water Management District, and by amending Section 22-58, "Docks," to eliminate a duplicative provision; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-08) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Schaad began by explaining that this item was created to streamline the code. He explained that the City defers to South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) requirements for size and location requirements of docks, dolphin pilings, finger piers, and boatlifts. A map was shown that displayed the jurisdiction of the Hillsboro and C-15 canals within the City. Mr. Schaad noted the frequency of variance requests due to the shallow depth of the Hillsboro Canal near its shore and C-15 canal limitations. He reassured members that all marine structures would remain subject to building permit requirements. The Marine Advisory Board recommended approval 6-1 and the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval 7-0. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5566. Motion carried 4 to 0; Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: (Second and final public hearing. Four votes required for adoption.) An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering amendments to the Infrastructure Element of the City's Comprehensive Plan to update the City's 10-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan, incorporate alternative water supply projects identified in the South Florida Water Management District's Regional Water Supply Plan, and revise potable water level of service standards; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-20-03) Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Noting that this was the second public hearing, Ms. Hansen explained that the amendments had been transmitted in November 2020 for review by the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO), the South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD), and others. She identified the key elements of the Water Supply Facilities Work Plan that had been updated since its last approval in 2016. It was pointed out that comments submitted by Water Management District staff had been addressed and revisions had been included in the ordinance before Council. The DEO and SFWMD support the amendments and updated work plan, and City staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Hansen made herself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5551. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 14, "Solid Waste," Section 14-20, "Prohibited Activities," Code of Ordinances, to provide for enhanced minimum civil penalties for various littering offenses, including littering of personal protective equipment used to prevent disease transmission; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Council Member Thomson shared a slide presentation and explained the motivation for the ordinance. Council Member Drucker inquired if the Governor's mandate against fines for Covid-related offenses would impact the enforcement. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarification, noting that this ordinance created a sub-category in the City's existing code enforcement structure. Council Member Mayotte and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke expressed their support. The public hearing was opened. Jessica Gray Patterson commented in support of the ordinance. Ray Dobrota expressed general support but shared his concern that the scope of the ordinance was too narrow and would ultimately make it difficult to implement. The City Clerk read a comment from Michael Path man, who shared his opinion that the best way to end mask littering was to stop making masks mandatory. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5568. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. 1. The public hearing was opened. Cristina Escalante asked for additional information. Council Member Andy Thomson provided clarification. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 28-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Drucker reported on the recent Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) meeting. She noted the rate of pedestrian/ bicyclist fatalities in the City and asked residents to be aware of cyclists and pedestrians when driving. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke congratulated the newly re-elected members of Council. She noted the high level of vaccines available and reminded residents to not discard of PPE in the street. She also noted the Organizational Meeting and upcoming Goal Setting sessions. Council Member Thomson reported on the TPA meeting and the legislative policy visions, specifically the Vision Zero program, the purpose of which is to eliminate traffic fatalities. Council Member Mayotte commented on the importance of Home Rule and provided a report on the threat to municipal government created by current bills coming before the State Senate. Ms. Mayotte thanked Senator Tina Polsky's staff for their assistance and encouraged residents to reach out to their state representatives regarding legislation. Among the bills she referenced were those that propose to limit local control of vacation rentals, preempt local government from adopting design regulations for single- and two-family dwellings, and restrict municipalities from making decisions in times of emergency. Ms. Mayotte concluded by welcoming new businesses to the City. Mayor Singer referred to Vision Zero and noted that traffic enforcement in the downtown had doubled. He closed by noting the retirement of City Clerk Susan Saxton and thanked her for her service.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 25, "Streets and Sidewalks," Article II, Section 25-39, "Abandonment of Required Rights-of-Way or Required Special Purpose Easements Pursuant to a Site Plan," Code of Ordinances, authorizing the Community Redevelopment Agency to abandon rights-of-way and easements contemporaneously with an individual development approval, and confirming the delegation of authority to act upon an application for an abandonment; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-12) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He referred to Ordinance No. 5451 which delegated authority for easements and right-of-way abandonments to occur as part of the site plan approval but did not specifically grant the CRA the same authority regarding abandonments as part of Individual Development Approvals (IDA) in the Downtown. Mr. Schaad noted that the amendment also included minor, non-substantive adjustments to language in the current Code. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval, as did staff. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5571. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.header: Ordinance No. 5572 (First of two public hearings. No vote will be taken)
units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 "Zoning," Article XI, Division 3, "R­ B-1 Motel-Business District," Section 28-742, "Permitted Uses," Code of Ordinances, to authorize business, trade, technical, or secretarial schools as permitted uses in the Motel-Business (R-B-1) zoning district; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-09) Jim Bell, Long Range Project Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He noted that the amendment had been considered by the Planning and Zoning Board in the past and was once again being brought forward in light of the occupancy of a technical school operating within the City on North Federal Highway. After analysis, staff determined that "business, trade or technical schools" should be reinstated as permitted uses in the R-B-1 zoning district. Mr. Bell referred to historical precedents, citing more than a dozen business, trade, and technical schools that had operated under the "educational institutions" provisions. The existing Professional, Office and Institutional (POI) restriction which limits enrollment to persons 18 years of age or older would be removed. He stated that the corrective amendment would reflect the purpose and intent of the R-B-1 district by providing appropriate educational uses for community services. Staff recommended approval. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended unanimous approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one indicate their desire to speak, closed. Mayor Singer advised that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken. He noted that the second public heating would take place on April 27, 2021.

units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS HELD VIRTUALLY Monday, April 26, 2021 6:00 PM Participants: City of Boca Raton: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang, Chair Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Yvette Drucker Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Monica Mayotte Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr. Council Member Andy Thomson Commissioner Erin Wright City Manager Leif Ahnell Briann Harms, Executive Director City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser Samuel Goren, Attorney and Special Counsel I. Welcome Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Susan Vogelgesang Mayor Scott Singer called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. The participants introduced themselves. II. Discussion A. Recreation Needs Assessment Presentation Recreation Services Director Michael Kalvort provided opening comments and introduced the consultants. Neelay Bhatt, accompanied by Brayton McClure from Pros Consulting, Inc., gave the PowerPoint presentation. A review of the strategic plan process was provided, and a number of topics were covered, including, but not limited to, a demographics analysis, a recreation trends analysis, community input summary, survey methodology, and a priority investment rating. Maps of neighborhood parks, ball fields, and tennis courts were also shown. The visioning process was discussed. Mr. Bhatt stated that the next step was to conduct a system-wide comprehensive master plant to implement the Needs Assessment findings. Discussion ensued on the level of service priorities, how COVID had affected activities and the survey projections, and the need for additional marketing of recreation offerings. Mr. Kalvort provided additional information regarding the municipal golf course, the addition of the Boca Raton Country Club golf course, and how the results of the Needs Assessment will help Recreation Services. B. Gumbo Limbo Nature Center This item was added to the agenda at the request of the BPD in consideration of recent conversations regarding the piping project. Commissioner Craig Ehrnst began by noting the 1984 agreement with the City and stated that they are committed to Gumbo Limbo, the volunteers, and the City, and recognized their obligations. He expressed concern with the Friends of Gumbo Limbo (Friends) and their lack of participation in helping to fund the project. He felt the District or the City should have some type of agreement with the Friends which would include financial transparency and a contribution to projects at Gumbo Limbo. Discussion ensued. There was consensus among the members of both parties that there should be an agreement to formalize the relationship. City Manager Ahnell advised he would direct staff to work with the Friends to formalize an agreement and report back in the next few months to both parties. Ill. Public Comment Bruce Diller Verstandig commented on the opening of Ocean Strand, FAU, Gumbo Limbo and Ocean Breeze. Greg Galanis commented on the condition of the golf course at the Boca Country Club and suggested developing Boca Teeca as an executive golf course and practice area. Earl Starkoff remarked on golf operations in Boca, the need for additional pickleball courts and athletic fields, and SABR. Steve Rose stated that there should be more pickleball courts in Boca. Raul Travieso, President of the Boca Raton Pickleball Club, also spoke in support of building a premier indoor/outdoor pickleball complex at either Ocean Breeze or Boca Raton Country Club locations. Cil Ciliberti commented on emails he sent to Council members regarding Ocean Breeze and pickleball courts. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke commented on whether a pickleball facility could be constructed at the Boca Country Club or Ocean Breeze. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. She then inquired whether the District could lease property to an outside entity to run a pickleball facility. Mr. Goren, District Council, responded that they would research the option. Discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to, the District's ability to transfer property, constructing a pickleball complex, some type of golf or walking trails at Ocean Breeze, and the District's RFI for recreational needs at Ocean Breeze. Mr. Ahnell suggesting getting someone onboard to look at both the Boca Country Club and Ocean Breeze sites for a pickleball complex and to bring back options by the end of summer. Council members and District commissioners provided their final comments and there was consensus to move forward. IV. Adjournment The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 7: 10 pm. ath Maxwell, Recorder on Mary Siddons, City Clerk Joint Meeting Minutes April 26, 2021 Page2

units.text: Council Member Mayotte commented on the Boca Bash and expressed concern about the number of resources being utilized to ensure the safety of those attending this non-permitted event. She then highlighted three sets of legislative bills that, if signed by the Governor, would preempt local government action regarding renewable energy. In conclusion, Ms. Mayotte noted an upcoming virtual meeting of the TPA and confirmed that one of the members would be attending. Council Member Drucker cautioned drivers to be aware of pedestrians and cyclists sharing the road and encouraged all to follow the rules of the road, particularly in school zones. Ms. Drucker then expressed her commitment to the topic of mental health, noting that May is Mental Health Awareness Month. She expressed her desire for some form of community engagement and outreach regarding this topic. As a final point, Ms. Drucker stated that she had received her second dose of the COVI D-19 vaccine. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke began by thanking Councill Member Mayotte for her update on the legislative bills and expressed her support for Ms. Mayotte's position. Ms. O'Rourke also shared her concerns about the Boca Bash and inquired if there was an option for the City to annex Lake Boca and obtain jurisdiction over the area. She shared information about a new YMCA meeting place for teenagers recently opened in Town Center Mall and noted the groundbreaking for Boca Ice. Ms. O'Rourke noted the updated CDC guidelines about wearing masks outside. In conclusion, she asked the City Manager what the next steps would be in regard to the recreational needs assessment. City Manager Leif Ahnell advised that staff would begin to form a master plan and would report back to Council in August. Mayor Singer commented further on the Boca Bash, noting that he had contacted all participating agencies and thanked them for their assistance. He agreed that a request for additional authority over Lake Boca should be added to the City's priorities for the fall legislative session. Mayor Singer then addressed Ms. Drucker's comments regarding mental health, noting that the City had partnered with non-profit centers to provide mental health counseling at local high schools. He also highlighted the mental health outreach provided by Boca Raton Police Department. He shared that he had also received his second vaccine and urged residents to continue to follow CDC guidelines regarding Covid-19.

IF THE POTENTIAL DISPOSITION IS FOR LESS THAN FAIR VALUE, CONSIDERATION OF PROPOSALS FOR THE POTENTIAL DISPOSITION AND REDEVELOPMENT OF PROPERTY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY: City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser gave a brief overview of the procedures, noting that Council would need to consider the use of the Mizner Park Amphitheater land which would fall under the City's Code of Ordinances as sale of City property, and to also give direction to staff to proceed with negotiations in the connection of City property. Ms. Frieser then responded to question regarding fair market value. She added that Members were only providing directing to staff at this time. A. If the disposition is for less than fair value, consideration of proposals: Potential disposition and redevelopment of property owned by the Community Redevelopment Agency in accordance with Section 163.380, Florida Statutes, the "Performance Venue Parcel" (City Council authorization is required in the event the disposition is for less than fair value), which redevelopment shall include a performance venue (and may also include the potential "sale" of adjacent land owned by the City of Boca Raton and operated as the Mizner Park Amphitheater, the "Amphitheater Parcel"). Notice of this public hearing has been provided pursuant to the requirements of Section 163.380, Florida Statutes (see below). Consideration of potential "sale" of City property: Potential "sale" of the "Amphitheater Parcel" in connection with the potential disposition and redevelopment of the "Performance Venue Parcel." Questions to proposers: Questions to proposers from members of the Council Members and discussion by the City Council. Public comment. Andrea Virgin, President of BRADEC, accompanied by attorney Michael Marshall, thanked everyone for their comments and stated that she looked forward to working with the City on this project. Michael Marshall, on behalf of Gunster Law Firm, requested clarification for the record that the decision was unanimous to proceed with BRADEC's proposal. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser responded that no decision was made by City Council but clarified that this was a process to direct staff to proceed with negotiations with BRADEC. She stated that this was not a binding decision, but a direction to proceed with negotiations and, hopefully, bring back a set of transaction documents to present to the CRA and City Council at a noticed hearing for their consideration. Discussion ensued. City Manager Leif Ahnell affirmed that he was clear on the direction for staff to begin negotiations with only BRADEC. Discussion/Deliberation/Direction by the City Council: The Council may discuss the proposal selected by the CRA and the potential "sale" of City property. The Council may direct City staff to enter into negotiations regarding the potential "sale" of City property, may request additional information, may take any other action(s) deemed to be in the public interest, or may take no action. If a proposal is selected for negotiations, any proposed transaction(s) will be considered pursuant to all applicable requirements of law and will be subject to final approval by the City at a future hearing. Council members agreed that staff was directed to conduct negotiations with only BRADEC. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke inquired about the cone of silence, and the City Attorney Frieser responded that the cone of silence was in place until an award was made.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, Article Ill, "Boards, Committees, Commissions and Special Magistrates," Division 4, "Community Appearance Board," Section 2-132, "Appeals," Code of Ordinances, to provide that the time period for filing an appeal to the City Council of a decision of the Community Appearance Board shall begin upon the rendition of the decision, and to affirm that the City Council shall consider the appeal upon the expiration of the appeal period and the effectuation of public notice; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-21-03) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. units.text: Deputy Mayor O'Rourke continued the discussion of permitting virtual attendance by the public at City Council meetings. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Members weighed in. Ms. O'Rourke then noted a virtual presentation regarding a tree canopy assessment workshop. She concluded by noting the groundbreaking for the relocated Community Garden and the upcoming Strategic Planning Workshop. Council Member Drucker inquired when City boards would resume in-person meetings. Mr. Ahnell advised that the Community Appearance Board and the Planning and Zoning Board would resume in-person meetings in June, and that staff was currently analyzing space requirements for the other boards. Ms. Drucker then highlighted the return of City-sponsored outdoor camps and commented on the recycling tips Council Member Mayotte had provided at a previous meeting. Council Member Mayotte inquired when Gumbo Limbo Nature Center would re-open. Mr. Ahnell stated that while some portions of Gumbo Limbo were already opened, the interior portions were mostly operated by volunteers and were not fully staffed at this time. He noted that the recruitment and processing of volunteers were under way. Mayor Singer commented on the groundbreaking for the newly relocated and expanded Community Garden. He then recognized National Law Enforcement Officer's Week and the City's virtual tribute for Police Officer Memorial Day. Mr. Singer reviewed the schedule for the Strategic Planning Workshops and highlighted the public comment times. In conclusion, he noted the broad availability of Covid-19 vaccines and encouraged all to stay safe.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved site plan (Planning and Zoning Resolution No. 81-71 ), pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize revisions to the parking and drainage layout, together with a technical deviation from Section 23-1900), Code of Ordinances, to reduce a required minimum inbound reservoir distance to a site entrance, for the Connected Life Christian Church located at 2500 Northwest 5th Avenue, subject to conditions; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date (UC-17-03/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11. A., B., C., D., E., F., and G. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and Ordinance No. 5537 would require four votes for passage. A separate vote would be taken on each item if the prior item were approved. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex­ parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a review of the applicant's request, including, but not limited to, a proposed amendment to the Future Land Use Map, a request for rezoning, a conditional use approval and a site plan amendment. Aerial maps were displayed, and information about the proposed future land use designation was provided. Analysis of the rezoning component was examined, and the traffic study results were presented. Ms. Rahman then explained that Staff considered the proposed land use designation to be unreasonable, and the proposed rezoning was determined to be incompatible with the City's Comprehensive Plan. The proposed master plan and site plan were discussed next, which included suggested improvements and site design components by the applicant. Staff did not support the proposed master plan. There were no staff objections to the proposed modifications to development parameters, as the relocation of the building closer to the street would be expected to promote pedestrian activity. Staff's response to components of the applicant's presentation at the December 8, 2020 transmittal hearing was provided. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with two revisions, which were agreed to by the applicant and incorporated into the site plan. Ms. Rahman concluded by reviewing Staff's recommendation of denial due to the proposed change of the land use designation, the inconsistency of the proposed rezoning with the City's Comprehensive Plan, and objections to the Master Plan and technical deviation requests. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. She began by displaying an aerial map of the subject property, noting the existing condition of the subject parcels and the surrounding neighborhoods. Ms. Miskel shared a chart and quotes from local news sources to demonstrate the need for additional housing for FAU students. A map of student housing developments within the City was shown, and a map outlining RH land use designations within the City was presented. John Donaldson, Traffic Engineer for the project, provided additional information for the justification of the future land use map amendment and rezoning proposals. Ms. Miskel then pointed out components added to the proposed site plan by the designers and landscape architects. Drawings of the proposed building elevations were shown, as were results of a poll administered by the applicant to City residents which showed community support for additional campus-adjacent housing for FAU students. Ms. Miskel concluded by outlining commitments to the community, which included a pedestrian bridge to campus, 24/7 security and shuttle service. Upon concluding, she responded to members' comments. The public hearing was opened. Charman Postel, Chris Krebs, Jon Carter, Michael Cairo, Nicholas Bamberg, Ryan Rossi, Tykeem McCord, Antonia Frenot, Brian Norton, Briana Moffatt, Kevin Buchanan, Felipe Mora, Joseph Justice, Andrea Virgin, Glenn Gromann, Maxwell Simonson, Alan Feinberg, Jr., Michael McGovern, and Brad Busscher expressed their support for the proposed project, citing the need for student housing close to the University campus. Sally Celano, property manager of the Windwood community, expressed concerns with the proposed rezoning from low to high residential. Kathleen MacDonald, Lorena Villegas, Margarita Pazmino, Xianyu Wu, and Renata Pawlowska also shared their opposition to proposed rezoning of the property. Cristina Escalante inquired whether the units would be available only to student residents. The City Clerk read comments submitted by William Dickey, Marcus Wood, and William Giffin, expressing their concerns with the proposed development. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, both online and in-person, the public hearing was closed. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, provided additional information in response to questions posed during the public comments and by Council Members. On behalf of the applicant, Bonnie Miskel responded to concerns expressed during the public comment period. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5537. Council Member Thomson addressed concerns expressed by residents during the public hearing, citing the provisions being offered by the applicant to alleviate traffic concerns and the need for additional student housing. Council Member Mayotte thanked all those that communicated their positions to Council and commented on the demand for student housing, noting that the proposed project could alleviate the lack of available single-family homes which were currently occupied by students during school semesters. Council Member Drucker echoed comments made by Council Members Thomson and Mayotte, noting that FAU was no longer a commuter college and that she recognized concerns about security and increased traffic. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke introduced the subject of the 20 th Street Corridor and asked for member's input. Discussion ensued. Ms. O'Rourke thanked everyone from the public who commented and expressed her desire to see additional student housing with lower density than the proposed project. Further discussion ensued. Mayor Singer thanked the developer for their efforts to address concerns that had been raised and encouraged FAU to continue to build additional on-campus housing. He concurred with members that the 20th Street Corridor would need to be made a priority. Motion failed on a 3 to 2 vote: Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Mayor Scott Singer and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Police and Firefighters' Retirement System; amending Section 12-126, "Definitions"; Section 12-134 "Administration"; and Section 12-153, "Retirement Dates and Benefits; Optional Provisions for Police Officers" of Article IV, "Pension Plan for Police and Firefighters" of Chapter 12, "Pensions and Retirement," Code of Ordinances, effectuating the pension related provisions of the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the City and the FOP (Police Officers Union); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, briefly explained the ordinance. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Ms. Davidson provided additional information regarding the financial impact outlined in the actuarial statement. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one online or in-person indicate their desire to speak, closed. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the Pine Crest School located at 2700 Saint Andrews Boulevard: (i) an amended and restated conditional use approval, consolidating previously-issued conditional use approvals, (ii) an amendment to conditional use Resolution No. 67-2008 to approve a Master Plan and authorize the addition of an approximately 5,808 square foot two (2)-story Learning Commons Building, which includes a Student Union and flex space classrooms, and certain minor future improvements (tennis pavilion, maintenance building expansion, fine arts building expansion, swimming pool, concessions building, bleachers, scoreboard, and running track); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-07-17R1) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by reviewing the applicant's request, which included a proposed amended and restated conditional use approval, and site plan approval for an additional building. It was noted that the master plan reaffirms the improvements approved in 2008. A map and aerial photo of the subject area were shown, and Ms. Hanson provided a brief explanation of the both the amended conditions of approval and seven additional conditions that had been added to the 2008 resolution. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval of the amended and restated conditional use resolution, subject to the proposed conditions. Laura Odom, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. She began by providing an overview of the existing property. Ms. Odom reiterated that the only new approval in the application was for the proposed Learning Commons building and noted that the master plan conditional use approval would restate the previously approved master plan from 2008. Existing conditions of the subject location and intended use of the proposed buildings were explained. Stephan Claren, architect for the proposed project, provided additional details of the structure and displayed slides showing renderings of the buildings, results of a line-of-site study with the adjacent neighborhood, and drawings of the landscape plan. Upon concluding, Ms. Odom and Mr. Claren made themselves available for members' questions. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 63-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 9, Code of Ordinances, "Miscellaneous Offenses," by creating Article VII, "Waste Reduction," to prohibit polystyrene foam products, balloons, and confetti in City facilities, on City property, and in City rights of way (as more particularly provided); amending Section 9-60, "Supplemental Code Enforcement Procedures," to provide for enforcement; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Council Member Mayotte presented the item and began by thanking City staff for their work on the ordinance. She highlighted the point that, because the State preempts municipalities from regulating many kinds of single-use plastics, the proposed measure would only prohibit use of the specified products on City property. Ms. Mayotte explained that the measure would ensure that vendors at special events would be prohibited from selling or distributing items packed in polystyrene, and outdoor pavilion rental contracts would include a prohibition on balloons and confetti. Ms. Mayotte illustrated the need to cut down on waste by sharing photographs she had recently taken of litter in City parks, including pictures of discarded balloons and polystyrene plates. She advised she had recently spoken at the May 7th Beach and Park District meeting, and 5 of 7 commissioners supported the ordinance. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarification of revisions made to the ordinance since its introduction. The public hearing was opened. Karen Leader, Alana Daniel, Rory Fielding, Erica Allen, and Jessica Gray expressed their support of the ordinance. Guillermo Asca commented on the need to provide education to the public and asked that the ordinance be amended. Glenn Gromann conveyed his approval and suggested change to the language. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5580 as revised. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke expressed her support of the ordinance and thanked Council Member Mayotte and members of the audience for their work on behalf of the environment. Council Member Drucker also shared her approval and her commitment to taking care of our City. Mayor Singer thanked Ms. Mayotte for her willingness to address concerns regarding enforcement of the ordinance and indicated his support for the item. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Boca Raton Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order to reflect established planning principles, guidelines, goals and requirements included within the DORI and the Amended Downtown Plan as specific criteria to be reviewed in connection with applications for individual development approval; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (AM-21-04) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by providing the background of Ordinance No. 4035. He noted that the proposed ordinance would incorporate objectives such as urban design, walkability and connectivity into the DORI Development Order, and provide ease of reference for staff and property owners. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke advised that she proposed the ordinance to further enhance the walkability of the Downtown area and to make the process more concise for applicants and staff. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward to speak, closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5581. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Drucker expressed her desire to see the Education Task Force reinstated, urged residents to continue to be vigilant regarding Covid-19, and reminded all to be mindful of school zones while driving. Council Member Mayotte reviewed the resolutions that she would be voting on at the upcoming Florida League of Cities conference; members expressed unanimous support of the resolutions. She then commented on the increase in COVID-19 cases and encouraged everyone to get vaccinated. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke urged all who are eligible to get the Covid-19 vaccine. She then asked Council Member Drucker what the assigned task would be for the Education Task Force. Ms. Drucker responded, and brief discussion ensued. Ms. O'Rourke then commented on the Brightline train station site plan and inquired about the walkability of the project. Mr. Ahnell responded. She then addressed the proposed building recertification ordinance and thanked everyone who came forward to speak on the issue. She encouraged residents to email Council members with specific ideas or suggestions on the topic. Mayor Singer commented on the suggestion to reinstate the Education Task Force and proposed surveying current City board members for feedback. Council Members weighed in. He then commented on the Covid- 19 vaccination rate. Mayor Singer concluded by highlighted the Back-to-School Tax Holiday and encouraged all to be prepared for hurricane season.

units.text: Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte to withdraw item 17.B., Resolution No. 108-2021, from the agenda. Mayor Singer asked Ms. Mayotte if her intent was to withdraw or postpone the item, to which she replied that her goal was to remove the resolution from consideration. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser suggested additional language to provide clarification to the motion. Motion was amended by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to remove item 17.B., Resolution No. 108-2021, from the agenda, and to have Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 2021-008 become the final resolution. Ms. Mayotte expressed her view that the appeal was unwarranted and that there are code enforcement regulations in place to address any future issues that may occur with the operation of the subject property. Council Member Thomson shared his support for the removal of the item and the finalization of the Planning and Zoning resolution. Council Member Drucker also conveyed her concerns with the proposed resolution and stated that she supported the motion. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke commented that she did not agree with the removal of the item from the agenda and felt that it was the obligation of Council to review components of development that staff believe warrant attention. Mayor Singer expressed his opinion that there were elements of the appeal that warranted discussion and encouraged members to consider the item. Further discussion ensued. Motion passed 3 votes to 2; Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Mayor Scott Singer and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

Resolution No. 106-2021 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the Brightline Train Station and parking structure located at 400 Northwest 2nd Avenue, 101 Northwest 4th Street, and 151 Northwest 4th Street, a modification of a condition of a Universal Conditional (UC) Approval (Ordinance No. 5206), to amend the approved site plan for the City's Downtown Public Library (Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 12-07), to authorize the construction of a one-story, approximately 9,035 square foot passenger train station and a 4.5-story, approximately 171,050 square foot parking structure, along with surface parking lot modifications, together with four (4) technical deviations from Section 23-190(d), Code of Ordinances, to reduce the width of an ingress lane, reduce the number of egress lanes, eliminate a required median, and reduce the required reservoir distance for a new driveway connecting to Northwest 4th Street; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-11-05R1/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11. A, B., C., and C.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures as required by items C. and C.1. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each of the ordinances and resolutions. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave a brief presentation for the First Amendment to the Ground Lease. He noted that the amendment was proposed due to a grant awarded from the Federal Railroad Administration, which resulted in a $1.5 million reduction of cost for the construction of the Brightline Train Station parking garage. Mr. Brown also presented Resolution No. 116-2021, and explained that the Council, acting as landlord, was required to make a determination whether or not the Brightline Train Station site plan was consistent with the conceptual site plan originally approved by the lease. Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, began by reviewing the request for the Universal Conditional Approval of the train station and parking garage. An aerial photograph of the location was shown, and components of the proposed site plan were reviewed. Mr. Bell advised that the site plan was consistent with the lease. A breakdown of proposed parking for both the Downtown Library and the Train Station was provided, and drawings of the Station and Garage were displayed. Staff determined that the project is consistent with mobility goals of the Comprehensive Plan. Results of the site plan traffic analysis were shown, and technical deviations were discussed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval 5-1. Staff supports the technical deviation requests and recommends approval of the universal Conditional amendment and the site plan amendment. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members questions. The public hearing was opened. Susan White, president of the Library Commons HOA, expressed concerns regarding potential damage from construction and traffic issues. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Brown and Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided additional information and responded to members' questions. Mr. Brown and Mayor Singer thanked Brightline for their collaboration and the congressional delegation for their support. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5587. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 116-2021, with the finding that the site plan is substantially consistent with the sketches attached to the lease. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5588.
