units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 19, "Buildings and Building Regulations," Code of Ordinances, to establish a building recertification inspection program based on, primarily, building age, and including timeframes for the recertification of such buildings, the process and requirements for recertification, timeframes for repairs or modifications found to be necessary resulting from recertification inspections, providing for remedies based on failure to either submit a recertification inspection report or make repairs/modifications of buildings, and establishing penalties for noncompliance with the recertification inspection program; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-21-05) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, began the presentation by defining the types of buildings that would be subject to the proposed ordinance. Those that are 30 years and older and those defined as Threshold Buildings, excluding single-family homes and duplexes, would be required to complete the building recertification inspection. The process would include, but is not limited to, a notice of inspection to be mailed 365 days prior to coming due, the submission of an engineering/inspection report, identification of deficiencies and the actions needed to address them, and a repair plan, if necessary. Mr. Schaad then outlined actions that could result in Code Enforcement action or fines. He noted that staff had identified 242 buildings within the city that are immediately subject to recertification, and proposed a four-year schedule based on geographic zones to address this backlog. A map of the proposed zones, prioritized from east to west, was displayed. A table was shown that compared the City's ordinance to a proposal of the League of Cities. Staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Mr. Schaad noted that this was a new program being implemented from scratch and advised that there may be revisions in the future. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. Mayor Singer began by thanking staff for their hard work on the ordinance. He suggested that the words "threshold building" be replaced with the actual description used in State statute. Council Member Mayotte asked if staff would provide a suggested format for the required report and requested additional information on the timeframe for the repair plan and schedule. Council Member Thomson highlighted the importance of transparency in the process and questioned if there had been changes made to the ordinance to address it. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke requested clarification regarding who the 'owners' were that would be receiving notification and commented on the availability of structural engineers to complete the assessments. Council Member Drucker shared that, ideally, she hoped staff would have more time to craft the ordinance before being put forward for a vote and she inquired what the impact of the program would be to staff levels and budgets. Mr. Schaad and Mr. Ahnell responded to members' questions and provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Steven Wallach encouraged Council to wait before adopting the ordinance and stated that the cause of the Surfside Condominium collapse still was not known. Richard Zimmer provided a handout with information included in Broward County's program for their building recertification, and he addressed specific portions of the proposed ordinance that he felt needed to be changed. Peter Sachs spoke in support of the ordinance and encouraged staff to move ahead with the program. Paula McClure commented that the 'owner' of a building is sometimes a board and noted the issues that could present when it came to notifying unit owners. Charlie Helton suggested that the city add additional engineers to staff to assist with the implementation of the program. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5589. Members weighed in and suggested additions or changes to refine the language. Further discussion ensued. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson to amend Ordinance No. 5589 to include language suggested by Council Members. The City Attorney reviewed amended language into the record. Included were corrections to page 5, lines 9 and 19, the inclusion of the definition of "threshold buildings", inclusion of language on page 9, line 12, to address a timing issue prior to issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy or Completion, addition of the word "structural" on page 6, line 26, addition of a new subsection "F" on page 4, and a provision for additional notices on page 4, line 20. Motion to amend Ordinance No. 5589 as stated carried unanimously on a voice vote. Members made final comments. Motion to approve Ordinance No. 5589 as amended carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: John Martin expressed concerns that Dixie Manor residents might be displaced if the historical integrity of the neighborhood is not preserved. Holli Sutton commented on development proposed for 2 SW 12th Avenue and submitted petitions to keep the current zoning in place. Danielle Iverson echoed Mr. Martin's comments and asked how the City plans to support affordable workplace housing and not displace current residents. Cynthia Briggs conveyed her support for the neighborhood surrounding the property at 2 SW 12th Avenue and advocated for the current zoning to be left unchanged.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the Beresford Condominium located at 350 South Ocean Boulevard, a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the alteration of an existing pool, spa, deck and walkway area seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance), and other site changes including the replacement of some herbaceous vegetation east of the bulkhead wall on the upper beach, and the removal of all seagrapes on the dune, to be replaced with herbaceous dune mix vegetation; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-19-03) The City Attorney confirmed that quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Components of the application were reviewed, and aerial photos of the subject property were shown. A site plan was displayed that outlined proposed modifications, as well as those previously completed without a permit. It was noted that the applicant wished to rectify the situation through the current variance process. Mr. Lindgren pointed out that the condominium was originally built prior to the establishment of the CCCL, and that the proposed hardscape and vegetative changes would have either a minimal, or advantageous impact to the health of the dune. Both the Environmental Advisory Board and the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval subject to the conditions set forth in the resolution. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren and Mr. Schaad responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, thanked City staff for their presentation and repeated that the applicant desires to rectify the issue of prior work being completed without a permit. She made herself available for members' questions. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 107-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte inquired how staff was making the determination to continue with in-person meetings versus returning to a virtual format. Mr. Ahnell advised that staff is monitoring a number of elements on a daily basis, such as Fire Rescue transports and Covid-19 numbers at local hospitals. Ms. Mayotte reported on her attendance at the Florida League of Cities conference and noted that the resolutions she shared at a prior meeting were all adopted. Council Member Drucker encouraged everyone to get vaccinated and to take whatever steps they could to mitigate the transmission of Covid-19. She commented about her attendance at the Florida League of Cities conference and expressed her thankfulness that the Council Members share a positive and professional relationship with each other. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke congratulated Mayor Singer on being elected President of the Florida League of Mayors. She noted that the Downtown Business Alliance was starting to meet again and encouraged business owners to get involved. Council Member Thomson echoed Ms. Drucker's comments regarding the relationship of the current Council Members and expressed his appreciation to his fellow members. Mayor Singer repeated Ms. Drucker and Mr. Thomson's comments, and noted the Council's respect and cordiality with each other. units.section: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: City Manager Leif Ahnell gave PowerPoint presentations on the proposed budget and millage rate. He began by reviewing the City's guiding principles - a Financially Sound City, World Class Municipal Services, Strong Partnership with Community, and Vibrant and Sustainable City - and noted policy priorities associated with these principles. Tables and charts were presented illustrating millage rates and assessed property valuations, and allocation of operating expenses. New items proposed for FY 2021-22 included, but were not limited to, projects, personnel, and programs. Mr. Ahnell reviewed the City flyer that explains residents' property tax bill. He highlighted comparisons of Boca Raton to nearby cities' fire assessment fees, property tax rates, and water and sewer rates. He reported a small increase in water, sewer, and sanitation rates. The presentation was then turned over to Sharon McGuire, Office of Management and Budget Director, who reviewed the 2021-22 portion of the six-year Capital Improvements Program. Upon concluding, Ms. McGuire responded to questions, as did the City Manager.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 24, "Signs," Article I, Section 24-6, "Unlawful Signs, Sign Structures," and Article Ill, Division 2, "Sign Regulation By Zoning District," Section 24-81, Code of Ordinances, to allow painted wall signs in commercial, industrial and similar zoning districts, where the painted wall sign is internally-focused and not visible from grade from adjacent properties and rights-of-way (and therefore no sign permit is required); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-21-08) Brandon Schaad, Director of Development Services, gave the presentation. He began with a brief background of the Sign Code and proceeded to review the proposed amendment. Mr. Schaad noted that since the introduction of the ordinance, clarifying language had been added. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Goodwin provided a handout and spoke in support of the ordinance. Robert Eisen, representing Investments Limited, also expressed approval of the ordinance. Glen Weldon shared his support and suggested that the parameters outlined in the proposed ordinance be expanded. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5590 as revised. Council Member Mayotte stated that she felt the proposed ordinance was too restrictive and questioned if the Mizner Amphitheater stage door mural conflicted with the ordinance. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke remarked that more art in public places should be permitted, and suggested changes be made to expand the parameters of what would be allowed. Council Member Drucker conveyed her approval and noted that other cities she had visited incorporated a lot of art into their public spaces. Council Member Thomson inquired how staff had arrived at the proposed standards. Mr. Schaad provided additional information on the maximum size of the mural allowed. Discussion ensued. Ms. O'Rourke suggested amending the maximum allowable size. Members inquired as to the regulation of content. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information. Ms. Frieser then clarified where in the ordinance the language could be modified to raise the allowable height from 12 to 15 feet. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to amend Ordinance No. 5590 as revised, to raise the height limit from 12 feet to 15 feet. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion to approve Ordinance No. 5590 as revised and amended carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, Article Ill, Boards, Committees, Commissions and Special Magistrates, Code of Ordinances, for the purpose of abolishing the Art in Public Places Advisory Board; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Ruby Childers, Downtown Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She outlined the history of the Board and the art projects undertaken. Staff recommends approval of the ordinance. Upon concluding, Ms. Childers responded to members' questions. Both Mayor Singer and Ms. Childers confirmed that some of the board members had relayed the frustration they felt due to the the constraints related to being under the Sunshine Law. Members expressed their desire to see the momentum of public art installations to continue. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Glen Weldon commented favorably on the Community Appearance Board and suggested that board already provided the mechanism to review proposed public art. Cristina Escalante expressed disappointment that the board would be abolished and suggested language to change the ordinance. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5591. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke advised that she would be requesting additional funding for art at the upcoming Budget Hearing, Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Mayor Singer opened the discussion of the Non-Profit Funding requests and provided background of the increases to the non-profit items. Council Member Thomson suggested that those line items that received a majority of members' support be approved, and that discussion should be reserved for those items that did not receive a majority of members' votes. Discussion ensued. Council Member Mayotte noted that she transposed two numbers on her list and made the correction. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke suggested that the applications should be reviewed more in depth to determine if the funds granted were used in our community. Ms. O'Rourke noted that she inadvertently missed the Boca Raton Historical Society on her list and agreed to members' suggested amount of $12,000. After discussion, there was consensus to agree to the amounts that received at least 4 out of 5 votes for the same amounts. Members considered changes to the funding of those remaining non-profits. Working from the Mayor's list, changes were agreed to, resulting in an increase of approximately $10,000 to the budget. Referring to Exhibit 4 regarding requests for funding/changes, Mayor Singer discussed his request regarding initiatives resulting from the Harvard Bloomberg Innovation Track discussion. Members weighed in. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke gave a PowerPoint presentation in support of additional funds for an Art in Public Places program. She reviewed examples of art projects in other cities and request for additional funds to hire a consultant, draft a master plan and hire dedicated staff to manage. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Ms. O'Rourke then discussed her request for additional funds for the Boca Raton Museum of Art. Mr. Ahnell noted that the City currently provides an annual $100,000 grant to the museum. Discussion ensued and there was consensus to include $25,000 to continue the Art in Public Places initiative. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to amend Exhibit 4 to include $25,000 in funding to continue the Art in Public Places initiative. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to amend the budget to include the FY2022 Non-Profit Organization Funding Requests as amended. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering waivers from certain standards and guidelines for marquee signs set forth in the lnterlocal Agreement dated March 18, 2009, between the School Board of Palm Beach County and the City, to authorize marquee signs at specified elementary and K-8 schools and waive certain provisions limiting marquee sign width, scrolling text and use of pictures and logos, for the following schools: (i) Verde K-8 School located at 6590 Verde Trail, (ii) Addison Mizner K-8 School located at 199 Southwest 12th Avenue, and (iii) 05-C Boca Area Elementary School located at 1000 Northwest Spanish River Boulevard; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-21-05) John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He briefly reviewed the elements of the waivers requested from the Verde K-8 School, the Addison Mizner K-8 School, and the 05-C Elementary School. Among the requests were the installations of the marquee signs themselves, consent for photos and logos to be on the signs, and the use of scrolling text. Mr. Lindgren outlined proposed additional conditions that addressed the allowed brightness of the illuminated signs and hours of use. He advised that representatives of the School District had agreed to the conditions. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 135-2021 as amended. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for property consisting of approximately 1.6 acres, located at 690 and 698 Jeffery Street, and 651 and 699 Kingsbridge Street, a Universal Conditional (UC) rezoning, pursuant to Article VI, Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances, from the R-2 and R-3 Multifamily Residential zoning districts to the R-1-G Single-Family Residential zoning Regular Agenda 5 September 28, 2021 district, subject to conditions, to authorize the future development of ten (10) single-family homes on existing platted lots, and associated improvements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-21-02/ZC) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by reviewing the application and displayed aerial photos of the subject property. The proposed plan and lot detail were shown, and sidewalk and pedestrian improvements were outlined. Mr. Lindgren advised that the proposed rezoning was compatible with existing future land use designation. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval subject to modifications to the conditions of approval. Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Bradley Miller, on behalf of the applicant, made brief comments and thanked staff for their presentation. Marie Thomson spoke in support of the ordinance but expressed concerns about traffic from new development. Mr. Miller responded to Ms. Thomson's comments. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5596. Zack Bihr, Municipal Services Director, provided information about traffic calming policies, how problem areas are identified and how the traffic study process is implemented. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Christine Lyons, Lanie Gospavic, Brian Clinton, Laura Sweeney, Brendon Brennon, Amy Lang, Sheila Mahon, Sara Marieno, and Shari Ochrimenko expressed concerns regarding an application for an assisted living facility (ALF) proposed to be built on NW 12th Avenue. Barbara Caccavale-Hodges also shared her opposition to the proposed ALF and provided resident petitions regarding the same. Jennifer Thompson, the new CEO of Habitat for Humanity for South Palm Beach County, introduced herself to the Mayor and Council. Denise Sheffler, Roberta Lee, Beverly Sammit, and Gail Borsh off remarked on the City's acquisition of the golf course at the Boca Raton Golf and Racquet Club and shared their disappointment that the City would not be keeping their Country Club's pool open. Mr. Ahnell responded to comments and questions regarding the Boca Raton Golf & Racquet Club. He listed a number of projects planned to improve the golf course, tennis courts and associated buildings, and address security and traffic concerns. He outlined the cost of keeping the pool running, and explained that if kept open, it would need to be available to all City residents. Mr. Ahnell explained that City staff had been communicating with the Master Association on dozens of issues and had conducted a community outreach Zoom meeting in August. Members weighed in. The City Manager then addressed comments regarding the proposed ALF and explained that the project was very early in the application process. Mr. Schaad provided additional information and advised that the timeline for a proposed project to go from application to a public hearing can take anywhere from several months to years.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Gwendolyn and Lestan Quintanilla for a settlement and reduction of code enforcement liens imposed against property located at 450 NE 37th Street; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, reviewed the resolution. He provided the history of the property and reviewed Code Enforcement violations that had accrued over approximately one and a half years. It was noted that the Special Magistrate had issued an order of Enforcement requiring the applicant to fix the violations and comply with City code. Due to cancellation of Special Magistrate meetings because of Covid-19, however, the Magistrate had reduced the fines due. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to Members' questions. Regular Agenda 7 September 28, 2021 The public hearing was opened. Spencer Siegal, representing Mr. and Mrs. Quintanilla, gave a brief presentation. He noted that two of the Code issues pre-dated his clients' ownership of the property and had now been corrected. Mr. Siegal stated that the owners did not live at the property, but that it was being used by a relative during the time of the Code infractions. He advised that the Code infractions had been corrected and the property had since been sold. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to deny the request for lien reduction. Mr. Siegal explained that his clients were under the impression that if the Code Enforcement violations were corrected, that the lien would be reduced. Mr. Schaad advised that staff had been clear that staff would only be making a recommendation to Council, and that would not bind the Council Members in any way. Members weighed in. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 22, "Marine Structures," Article Ill, "Docks and Other Mooring Facilities," Section 22-63, "Boat Lifts," Code of Ordinances, to provide that certain restrictions on the distance that a boat lift may extend into a waterway shall not be applicable to a boat lift connected or adjacent to a finger pier or dolphin (provided the boat lift does not extend further into the waterway than the finger pier or dolphin); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM- 21-06) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an analysis of the current code. Mr. Schaad explained that finger piers or dolphin pilings are currently permitted to extend into a waterway further than a boat lift, and staff could determine no reason that a boatlift should not extend the same distance. It was also noted that staff received continuous variance requests of this kind, and that passage of the proposed amendment would not only save staff time and streamline the code, but would be beneficial to residents, as well. All marine structures would still be required to comply with all other City requirements. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Allan Elfassy and Jay Schneider expressed support for the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5598. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

Council Member Drucker highlighted Hispanic Heritage Month and the 50-year anniversary of the Junior League. She concluded by commenting on the opening of the Machu Picchu exhibit at the Boca Raton Museum of Art. Council Member Mayotte thanked everyone for their condolences. She commented on the Boca Raton Innovation Campus presentation from the prior day's Workshop and expressed her support. She noted that she wanted to be sure the cultural aspect was collaborative, not competitive, with the art initiative at Mizner Park. Mayor Singer highlighted the opening of the Boca Raton Community Garden and the Butterfly Garden, and commented on the City's Arbor Day program that provides a tree to City residents. He concluded by encouraging everyone to stay safe, stay strong, and stay positive.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.546 acre vacant property located at 7021 and 7101 North Federal Highway, an amendment to Exhibit "1" (setting forth the site plan) to revise the approved architectural elevations and authorize phasing of the project, for a universal conditional (UC) rezoning (Ordinance No. 5503); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-17-02R1/ZC) 1. Resolution No. 139-2021 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.546 acre vacant property located at 7021 and 7101 North Federal Highway, an amendment to a conditional use approval for a self-storage facility (interior storage unit access) (Resolution No. 108-2019) to revise the approved architectural elevations and authorize phasing of the project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC- 17-02R 1/CA) 2. Resolution No. 140-2021 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.546 acre vacant property located at 7021 and 7101 North Federal Highway, an amendment to an approved universal conditional (UC) site plan (Resolution No. 109-2019) to: (i) revise the approved architectural elevations, (ii) authorize phasing of the project, (iii) revise a condition of approval to provide for a dedication of right-of-way for North Dixie Highway to Palm Beach County rather than to the City, and (iv) abandon a utility easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-17-02R 1/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11.A., 11.A.1., and 11.A.2. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osny Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the request, which included phasing of the development, revision of approved architectural elements, amendment of a condition of approval regarding a right-of way, and an abandonment of a utility easement. A map of the parcel was displayed, and a history of the past zoning approvals was provided. Drawings of the proposed architectural changes were shown. Mr. Jean then explained the request for the right-of-way dedication and the abandonment of a City utility easement along the property's western driveway. Components of the phasing request were discussed, and Mr. Jean noted that while staff recommended approval of the proposed architectural revisions, easement abandonment, and right­ of-way dedication, staff recommended denial of the phasing portion of the application. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of all components of the application, as well as amendments to conditions 3.h. and 7 in the site plan resolution. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to members' questions. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, thanked staff for their presentation. She provided clarification regarding the request for phasing and explained how the driveway permit and right-of­ way dedication are connected. She relayed the applicant's desire to move ahead with the permit and expressed their desire to work with the City. Alex Rosemurgy, property owner, asked for Council to approve the phasing request so that there would be time to obtain the desired tenants and configure the footprint to their specifications. Ms. Zachariades then made herself available for members' questions. At the Mayor's request, Diana Grub Frieser, City Attorney, briefly reviewed a proposed alternative to condition 3.h. and ?(iii) of Resolution No. 140-2021 that she had discussed with Ms. Zachariades. She read language into the record and explained that it would allow the applicant to go forward with the building permit process, but that building would be limited pending the applicant's completion of the right-of-way dedication and driveway permit through Palm Beach County. If the County processes would not be completed within 6 months, the building permit would be considered null and void. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. The Mayor suggested a brief recess to allow staff and representatives for the applicant to review the proposed amendment to Resolution No. 140-2021. The meeting recessed at approximately 6:43 pm and reconvened at approximately 7:00 pm. Ele Zachariades advised that her client was amenable to the compromise reached with staff, but asked that the building permit be suspended rather than terminated if the process with the County were not completed within the allowable time frame. The City Attorney provided additional information and members weighed in. There was consensus to allow the requested phasing, the architectural changes, and to extend the time frame for the applicant to secure the necessary project components from the County. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5599. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 139-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Resolution No. 140-2021 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 1.4 acres, generally located at 644 Park of Commerce Way, from Planned Mobility (PM) to Conservation (N); providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-21-02) John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a description of the subject location and the project site plan. He noted that because the site plan had been approved to include the preserve, City code required that the Future Land Use designation be changed from Planned Mobility to Conservation. During staff analysis of the submitted application, it was determined that the subject area would be effective at providing native plant species and wildlife habitat that would support the preservation of the environmental area. The Environmental Advisory Board and Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren made himself available for members' questions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to public hearing notice requirements for various development-related applications; amending portions of Chapter 19, "Building Regulations," Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," Chapter 24, "Signs," Chapter 25, "Streets and Sidewalks," Chapter 26, "Subdivision Regulations," and Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to consolidate various public hearing notice requirements, and to: (i) amend and standardize the notice requirements and procedures; (ii) update the type(s) of notice (published, mailed and posted) required for different applications; and (iii) update the requirements (including timing) for each type; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-20-13) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, presented the PowerPoint presentation. He began by outlining the need to streamline and make consistent the City's requirements for public hearing notices. The benefits of standardizing to a 10-day notification timeframe were described. Mr. Schaad explained that the proposed amendment would focus more on the use of mailed and posted notices, rather than newspaper advertising, although all three methods would still be utilized for the most significant applications. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with a modification of 14-day advertising timeframe, but staff recommended against the proposed modification. Upon concluding, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5600. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Deputy Mayor O'Rourke suggested inviting the Director and Chair of the Boca Raton Housing Authority to give a short presentation at a City Council Workshop. Members agreed. She then commented on Chair Mayotte's presentation at the prior day's CRA meeting regarding economic development. Ms. O'Rourke offered to repeat her Goal Setting presentation of a proposed redesign of Palmetto Park Road and the Downtown in order to create better connectivity and walkability. Members weighed in and discussion ensued. Lastly, she congratulated Deputy City Manager George Brown on his induction into the Walk of Recognition by the Boca Raton Historical Society and noted his 44 years of service to the City. Mayor Singer congratulated Mr. Brown and acknowledged Robert Rollins on his induction into the Historical Society's Walk of Recognition. Council Member Drucker wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and let all those listening know that she hears their concerns and appreciates their communication on important issues. Council Member Mayotte commented on the popularity of the course at the Boca Raton Golf & Racquet Club and wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving. Mayor Singer remarked on recent dialogue he had with interested parties regarding the Dixie Manor community and encouraged additional public conversation to get the facts out to residents. He thanked congregations from B'nai Israel and Ebenezer Baptist Church for their food distribution in advance of the holidays and commented on the success of the tree lighting ceremony at Mizner Park. The Mayor highlighted upcoming events and thanked both Municipal Services and Police Services staff for the extra measures taken to keep event attendees safe. He concluded by wishing all a Happy Thanksgiving and Happy Hanukkah.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton making findings of fact and conclusions of law pertaining to the Boca Raton Technology Center Development of Regional Impact (ORI); considering an amendment to the DRI Development Order to reflect a proposed new parking structure and revise tabular data in connection with the parking structure; modifying Exhibit 'D' (Master Plan Map H-1) of the ORI; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC- 21-04) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Osny Jean, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a summary of the applicant's request and displayed an aerial map of the subject location. The history of the property and the proposed site plan amendment were reviewed. Renderings of the planned parking structure were shown. Mr. Jean summarized the amendment by displaying a map that reflected the proposed parking structure, highlighted the revised data table to include updated parking numbers and corrected scrivener's errors from previous DRI amendments. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services Department recommend approval with the conditions included in the resolution. Upon concluding, Mr. Jean responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, thanked staff for their presentation and asked for a revision to language in the resolution. She read language into the record proposed for inclusion on page four, section 16, regarding subsequent DRI amendments, and noted that Development Services staff had given their approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Glenn Gromann expressed his support. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 168-2021 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering accepting and approving the final plat known as Boca Haven (a replat of Lots 4 and 5 and a portion of Lot 3, Block 1, Bible Conference Estates) for an approximately 1.5 acre property generally located west of Northwest 6th Avenue and north and south of Northwest 6th Street Extended, authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the Plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-19-02) The Mayor confirmed that the public hearing would be conducted pursuant to the same quasi-judicial procedures as previously stated. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Boone, Land Development Coordinator, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by displaying an aerial photo of the subject property and reviewed components of the applicant's request. A table outlining the lot area and density was shown. The tentative plat was approved by both the Planning and Zoning Board and City Council in 2020. Ms. Boone advised that the final plat was consistent with the tentative plat and met all other platting requirements. Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Lynn Yurosco, Mark Rosenthal, Eugene Lehenbauer, Candace Lehenbauer, and Veronica Risko expressed their opposition to the proposed resolution, citing concerns regarding the preservation of the lake, local wildlife and the requested setbacks. Mayor Singer inquired about the lake and the area being referred to as wetlands. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, noted that there was a notation on the plat that specifically prohibited filling in the lake. Steve Utrecht, speaking on behalf of his client who owned a nearby property, stated that he had no objection to the project as long as the contours of the lake were not changed. Dr. Steven Eigles, petitioner, addressed concerns raised by previous speakers and made himself available for members' questions. Glenn Gromann expressed his support for the project and complimented Ms. Boone on her presentation. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Dr. Eigles reiterated that there was no intent to alter the lake in any way and advised that the development of the property would begin as quickly as possible upon approval. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Schaad responded to members' questions regarding environmentally sensitive lands, mailed and published notices, and setback requirements. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 169-2021. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-340(1), Code of Ordinances, to authorize a place of worship (Yagdil Torah Mikvah) in the R-1-D zoning district for the property located at 460 Northwest Spanish River Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-20-04) The Mayor confirmed that the quasi-judicial procedures reviewed earlier remained in effect. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Hansen began with a description of the subject property and a review of the applicant's request. She explained the differences between a Mikvah and traditional synagogues or churches that led to the two technical deviations and two variance requests. A site plan of the current subject property was shown alongside the proposed alterations to the existing home. A rendering of the elevation was displayed. Ms. Hansen noted the Planning and Zoning Board requested the parking spaces be reduced in size to allow a larger landscape buffer along Spanish River Boulevard. The applicant revised the site and landscape plans as requested. The Board voted 4-2 to approve the conditional use, the site plan and variances. Objections from the public were relayed. Staff recommends approval of the application with conditions. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. Ms. Hansen provided additional information regarding hours of use, parking, and zoning. The public hearing was opened. Kristin Nowicki, Senior Project Planner for WGI, presented on behalf of the applicant. She began by providing additional information about the use of the Mikvah, noting that use will be by appointment only. Ms. Nowicki noted the compatibility with surrounding building uses and highlighted the proposed modifications to the existing structure. It was pointed out that the project is expected to result in fewer traffic trips than a single-family home. Rabbi Light provided the history of Mikvah use and asked the Council for their support. The following expressed their approval of the project: Diana Barr, Julie Weiss, Deon Nathan, Judith Nathan, Leela Mahn, Adina Shayowitz, Charissa Hurd, Valeria Palmer, Abraham Meth, Shraga Greenbaum, Shraga Greenbaum, Chaim Morgan, Annette Ben-Habib, Deidre Zussman, Simona Roth, Nechama Feder, Deanna Casper, Yaffa Stransfeld, Tzipporah Nechama Zwiren, Batsheva Wasser, Aliza Sloan, Nechama Turk, Ayelet Rabinowitz, Suzanne Zigun, Kerrie Greenwald, Abby Brody, Zvi Bach, and Luly Horovitz, citing the private nature of the Mikvah's use and the fact that most individuals who will use the facility would be travelling there on foot. The following individuals expressed their opposition to the proposed Mikvah, citing traffic and crowd concerns and use of the property: Phil Liberty, Ekaterini Alexopoulus, Steve Duke, Dana Lynch, Keith Gamarra, and Charlie Helton. Rabbi Light, on behalf of the applicant, made final statements. He relayed his distress at certain comments made during the public hearing, and affirmed that, as Rabbi for the affected community, he encouraged a broader discussion of acceptance between those of different faiths. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 170-2021. Council Members thanked all those who spoke during the public hearing, addressed the concerns of residents opposing the project, and shared their reasons for supporting the application. The Mayor and Council Members also expressed their deep disappointment with remarks directed at members of the Orthodox community and encouraged residents to be tolerant and accepting of others. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the City's Comprehensive Plan to create a property rights element; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-21-06) Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing for the ordinance and the first of two public hearings. Tamash Rahman, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a brief description of the Comprehensive Plan and the elements included within it. Ms. Rahman explained that House Bill 59 requires all local governments to update their Comprehensive Plan to incorporate a property rights element that ensures private property rights are considered in local decision­ making. The proposed amendment meets the Florida Statutory requirement. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Charlie Helton commented on the ordinance and the effect on his personal property rights. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to transmit Ordinance No. 5604. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 19, "Building Regulations," Article VI, Division 3, "Permitting and Construction Review Board," Section 19-216, "Membership," Code of Ordinances, to require at least one member of the board hold a state license or certification as a professional engineer with experience in electrical engineering; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-21-11) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, briefly reviewed the ordinance. He explained that the recertification ordinance adopted earlier in the year requires submittal of reports from both a structural and an electrical engineer. Mr. Schaad noted that the Permitting and Construction Review Board is designated to review appeals of the recertification program, and the makeup of the board currently requires an architect and a structural engineer, with the remaining seats to be filled by any of a number of professions. The proposed ordinance would require that an electrical engineer fill one of the remaining seats. Staff recommends approval. Upon conclusion, he made himself available for members' questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5605. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. The meeting was recessed at approximately 9:23 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:33 pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the Three Thousand South Condominium located at 3000 South Ocean Boulevard, a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a new seawall, and replacement of a pool, pool deck with associated fence, pool equipment and outdoor shower, and beach stairs, (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-21-03) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Lindgren began by reviewing components of the applicant's request. Aerial photographs were shown of the subject site in relation to the CCCL. Pictures of the deteriorating condition of the existing seawall were presented. Mr. Lindgren then reviewed the proposed site plan and outlined the justification for rebuilding the seawall in the new location. It was noted that the existing pool was in a similar state of disrepair and would also be rebuilt. The plan to replace the existing vegetation was summarized. It was emphasized that the existing condominium was built prior to establishment of the CCCL and the application met all criteria for granting a variance. The Environmental Advisory Board recommended approval with conditions regarding the protection of sea turtle nesting activity. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. The required notices had been mailed and property signage posted in accordance with the applicable statutes. Staff recommends approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren responded to members' questions. Greg Polidora, Senior Environmental Officer, provided additional information about the required sea turtle nesting plan. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, thanked staff for their presentation and advised Council that all parties would meet prior to commencement of the building to review the sea turtle nesting plans. Ms. Zachariades reiterated that the original construction of the seawall was integrated with the structure of the parking garage, necessitating the applicant's request to build a new seawall in front of the existing structure. Dr. Don Richardson, environmental consultant for the project, was sworn in and provided additional information regarding the vegetation and impact to sea life. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 2-2022. Members made final comments and shared their position. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a conditional use approval pursuant to Section 28-1238(8), Code of Ordinances, to authorize the development of a passive park (Ocean Strand Park) on the portion of an approximately 14.8-acre property located at 2300 North Ocean Boulevard that is west of North Ocean Boulevard; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-21-02) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. John Lindgren, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the applicant's request and displayed aerial photographs of the subject location. The site plan of the property was shown, and proposed park features were identified. Mr. Lindgren explained the aspects of the archeological site on the land and presented a photograph that outlined the principal archaeological area that would be avoided. Staff analysis showed that the existing infrastructure and proposed amenities were appropriate to the site, that the proposed use is compatible with adjacent uses, and that archaeological concerns had been addressed. The required notices and posting on the property had been completed. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the site plan and conditional use. Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Lindgren responded to members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Carol Perez, landscape architect from AGT Land, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a description of the current state of the subject property. Details of the proposed features of the park were discussed. A site plan identifying signage and park elements was displayed. Upon concluding, she provided additional information regarding bike racks and recycle bins. Mayor Singer inquired about the prospect of vehicle parking. Erin Wright, newly elected Chair of the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (BPD), told members that she was looking forward to developing the relationship between the City and the BPD. Ms. Wright provided a brief history of the land and asked for the City's approval. She explained the reasons for not including parking on the site, including, but not limited to, parking meter installation, lack of staffing and environmental concerns. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Sean Swartz, on behalf of the applicant, noted that it was only the conditional use request that was before Council for their consideration, and not the site plan. Gabriel Banfi, a resident of a neighboring condominium, expressed his support for the park as proposed. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Regular Agenda 2 January 25, 2022 Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 1-2022. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke communicated her approval for the proposed resolution and her belief that it should remain a passive park and not include parking. Council Member Mayotte also relayed her endorsement for the park as proposed and noted that there may be other components to the park that could be added in a later phase, such as recycle bins, water fountains and a bicycle maintenance station. It was noted that the site plan approved by the Planning and Zoning Board was contingent on the Council approval of the proposed conditional use approval. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Boca Raton Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order to add provisions allowing for and regulations governing space efficient mechanical and automated parking systems; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (AM-20-12) Mayor Singer briefly summarized the prior day's CRA discussion regarding the continuation of this public hearing to a future meeting date. The City Manager and the City Attorney provided clarification regarding the staff presentation and future meeting dates. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to continue the public hearing on Ordinance No 5607 to February 8, 2022. Deputy City Manager O'Rourke asked if continuing the matter to the next meeting would provide enough time for staff to conduct the research requested. City Manager Leif Ahnell advised that the narrow timeframe could limit the amount of information staff would be able to collect. Discussion ensued. Members examined the need for clearer communication and clarification of expectations between Council and staff. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser asked if the direction of the body was for staff to give input on the ordinance as it was written, or if staff was to conduct a discretionary review. There was consensus from members to have staff give a thorough appraisal of the ordinance and come forward with any concerns that might exist. Discussion continued regarding the timeframe of the next hearing and the role of staff input on Council Member initiated legislation. Motion carried 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no. Members made final comments.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Boca Raton Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order to add provisions allowing for and regulations governing space efficient mechanical and automated parking systems; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (AM-20-12) Deputy City Manager George Brown made the presentation. He noted that the CRA had discussed the proposed ordinance at length, and recommended approval once several amendments had been made. Mr. Brown briefly reviewed the revisions which included, but not limited to, language clarification and formatting, the requirement of a full-time valet or attendant, and OSHA requirements. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Joe Graubart asked a number of questions, including whether a maintenance log would be required, if there would be annual inspections, and if 24/7 attendants would be required. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Brown advised that the proposed ordinance required a maintenance plan and inspections of the systems. He also noted that an attendant would be required at all times unless the applicant could demonstrate that the garage could safely operate without them. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke clarified the point that IDA approval would be required for each automated parking system application received. The meeting was recessed at 6:19 pm to address technical issues and resumed at 6:23 pm. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5607 as amended. Council Member Drucker and Mayor Singer thanked staff and the private sector for their collaboration on the ordinance. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke commented that she would be voting no, not because she did not support the subject, but because she desired a more thorough process for staff analysis and recommendation. Council Member Mayotte thanked staff and other parties involved for their work on the ordinance. Motion carried 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke voting no.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte noted the competition among Florida municipalities called the Florida Race to Zero and explained that the project's goal was to encourage commitment to net zero emissions for climate neutrality. Ms. Mayotte expressed her desire for the City to participate and offered to enlist speakers to come make a presentation. Discussion ensued, and there was consensus for members to hear a presentation from staff at a future meeting. Council Member Drucker commented on her participation at the State Summit of the Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) and noted that City Traffic Engineer Maria Tejera and the City had been nominated for awards. She announced her intention to include discussion on Vision Zero at this year's Strategic Planning and remarked Regular Agenda 3 February 23, 2022 on the number of accidents involving vehicles going around guard gates at railroad crossings. She encouraged all to observe the "no crossing" lights and gate arms. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke inquired of the members if there was interest to address residents' request to enlarge the membership of the Boca Raton Housing Authority (BRHA). Discussion ensued. Members agreed that it was an important topic and there was agreement to review the next set of BRHA minutes in order to get direction on the BRHA position on this topic. Council Member Thomson read a letter from a resident expressing praise and gratitude for the great job done by Recreation Services Athletic Supervisor and COBRA coach Jim Thomas. Mayor Singer echoed the commendation for Mr. Thomas and also acknowledged the hard work of other staff, residents, non-profits, and fellow elected officials on behalf of the City of Boca Raton.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the City Manager and City Clerk to execute a revocable license with 200 East Palmetto Condominium Association for the use of parking spaces; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mr. Ahnell briefly reviewed the resolution. He noted that the proposed agreement was a renewal of the original revocable license for three parking spaces and that the agreement included payment of the daily parking meter rate. The public hearing was opened. Karen Mazurek, property manager for the 200 East Palmetto Condominium, explained that the building does not have sufficient parking for vendors in the existing garage. She noted that the parking spaces were used via their valet service for vendors or repair services only. Upon concluding, she responded to members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke commented on the availability of parking in the Downtown and stressed the importance of making sure ample parking was provided in new development projects. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 24-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering accepting and approving the final plat known as Yamato Villas (a replat of all, or portions of, Lots 1 through 10 of Block 3 of the University Heights Plat) for an approximately 1.7 acre property generally located at 300, 316, 382 and 398 West Yamato Road and 5001, 5033 and 5067 Northwest 3rd Avenue, authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-03/SUB) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Boone, Land Development Coordinator, gave the presentation. She began by reviewing the application. Background of the property's rezoning and master plan approval was discussed. Ms. Boone noted that the proposed final plat was consistent with the previously approved tentative plat, and that limited site work had been permitted to begin in February under an early work authorization. Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Boone made herself available for questions. Jerome Rich, applicant, thanked City staff for their work and made himself available for members' questions. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 19-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte advised that she would not be available to attend the upcoming Environmental Advisory Board meeting and asked if another member could attend in her place. Council Member Drucker and Mayor Singer also noted scheduling conflicts and a brief discussion ensued. Ms. Mayotte then noted that the 1-95 entrance ramp meters had been turned off while the Florida Department of Transportation explored options to improve their operation. She concluded her comments by highlighting the upcoming Food Truck Friday event. Council Member Drucker began by thanking staff for once again providing police reports to Council Members and confirmed with the City Manager that staff would contact the Boca Raton Historical Society regarding Certified Local Government (CLG) status. She ended her report by noting that schools were back in session and highlighted the importance of observing posted speed limits in school zones. Council Member Thomson echoed Ms. Drucker's comments regarding school zones and remarked on the change of traffic pattern at Spanish River High School. Mr. Thomson then read a letter from the principal of Spanish River High School commending Officer Brian Miller on his involvement at the school and dedication to keeping students safe at the crosswalks. Mayor Singer stated that the letter was an example of the many positive comments received regarding City staff and first responders and encouraged all to drive safely.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the property generally located at 6401, 6405, 6409, 6413 and 6421 Congress Avenue: (i) an amendment to an approved Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan (Resolution No. 137-2020) to increase the square footage of the 277-unit multifamily residential project and parking structure, increase the height of the parking structure, reduce the number of parking spaces provided, make related site modifications (and other minor site modifications), and eliminate a requirement to construct a deceleration lane; (ii) site plan approval to authorize development of the 277-unit multifamily residential project; and (iii) the abandonment of portions of a twelve ( 12)-foot water and sewer easement and a twelve (12)-foot sewer easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-18-01R1) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a description of the property and a review of the applicant's request. Components of the application included an amendment to the PMD master plan, a site plan approval, abandonment of a water and sewer easement and abandonment of a sewer easement. Elements of the previously approved Master Plan were noted. Ms. Rahman then reviewed requested modifications that included, but were not limited to, a parking deck on the sixth floor of the parking structure, removal of a previously approved deceleration lane on Congress Avenue, and construction of a 6-foot sidewalk along Congress Avenue. Drawings of the existing site, the proposed master and site plan were reviewed. The Community Appearance Board recommended approval. The previously approved modification of development parameters was reviewed. The traffic trip generation chart and proposed easement abandonments were discussed. Ms. Rahman advised that the project meets the intent of the PMD, and both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval of the project with conditions. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to questions. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, thanked staff for their presentation and made herself available for questions. Ryan Abrams, counsel for Millennium Two, LLC., requested 45 minutes between himself and additional witnesses to present their opposition to the project. Mayor Singer advised that additional time could be offered at the discretion of the Council. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information regarding party status. Arturo Perez, traffic engineer speaking on behalf of Millennium Two, LLC, provided a handout and expressed concerns regarding the traffic study submitted by the applicant. Mr. Abrams asked for, and was granted, ten minutes to make his PowerPoint presentation and Ms. Frieser briefly described two handouts that he had provided to Council. Topics discussed by Mr. Abrams included the applicant's traffic engineering analysis, the removal of the deceleration lane, and parking and traffic impacts. units.text: Bill Millard announced an event on May 21 st at the Mizner Park Amphitheater to raise funds for those in Ukraine directly affected by the war and appealed to Council for financial backing from the City. Resolution No. 33-2022 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for Boca Surgery Center located at 501 Glades Road, an amended and restated site plan (Resolution No. 91-05), to authorize construction of an approximately 11,740 square foot medical office building and other site improvements, including additions and modifications of surface parking area and sidewalks; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-86-01 R4/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. Ordinance No. 5611 would require four votes for adoption. Should item 10.A. not be adopted, item 10.A.1. would not be considered. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures, and the City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a brief description of the applicant's request and provided background information on the property. The proposed site plan was displayed, and renderings of the building elevations were shown. Ms. Rahman then reviewed the results of the site plan traffic analysis. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with several suggestions. Ms. Rahman noted that the required public notices and mailings had been executed. Staff recommended approval with the conditions included in the ordinance and resolution. Upon concluding, she responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. George Gentile, President of 2GHO Inc., landscape architect and planner for the project, made the presentation. He began with drawings of the previously approved site plan compared to the proposed site plan. Components of the architecture were discussed, and renderings of the building elevations were shown. Mr. Gentile noted that less square footage was being requested than was originally approved, and that the applicant would be adding a new 8-foot public sidewalk and landscaping improvements. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Glenn Gromann commented on the lack of prior maintenance of the existing building and landscaping. Harvey Plosker, current Medical Director of the property, spoke in support of the project but expressed concerns about the site plan, landscaping, and parking during construction. Dr. Plosker also inquired about the construction of new and improved monument sign, separate construction debris area, and whether there would be a construction time limit. There was no cross examination or rebuttal. Mr. Gentile made closing comments and addressed concerns raised during the public hearing. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5611. Ms. Rahman responded to Council Member questions. Mr. Gentile provided additional information regarding the designated area for building deliveries. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 33-2022. After providing a brief history of the Temple Beth El synagogue and mausoleum, a drawing of the proposed site plan was shown, and renderings of the proposed addition were displayed. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 31-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering a non-substantive revision to the City's Comprehensive Plan to remove unnecessary (and erroneous) double-asterisks in Policy LU.1.1.6. of the Future Land Use Element regarding density/intensity limits for certain land uses in the land use categories; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-22-01) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He briefly reviewed the background of the Comprehensive Plan and highlighted the future land use categories that would be affected by the proposed clarification. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Joanne Snow spoke in support of the ordinance and shared misgivings regarding a proposed Assisted Living Facility (ALF}. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser noted that the proposed ordinance was not site-specific. Robert Sweetapple, attorney on behalf of Religious Science Unlimited, gave a PowerPoint presentation in opposition of the ordinance. Mr. Sweetapple outlined concerns with the legal advertising of the ordinance's public hearing and the processing of his client's application for an ALF. The City Attorney addressed the comments regarding the public notice and advised that litigation had already been filed by Mr. Sweetapple on behalf of his client. Bill Snow, Patrick Sipple, Janna Evans, Peter Boylan, Shane Kittelson, Lara Kittelson, Jennifer Gilson, Christine Lyons, Gene Hodges, and Lani Gospovic commented in support of the proposed ordinance and against the proposed ALF. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5610. Council Member Thomson commented on the concerns that had been raised regarding the public notice. Discussion ensued with the City Attorney providing additional information. Council Member Thomson spoke in support of re-noticing with revised language to highlight the transmittal of the ordinance. Council Members weighed in. There was consensus to re-notice the ordinance for a future meeting. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke withdrew her motion.

units.text: The City Attorney read the following statement into the record: "In connection with this recent lawsuit filed against the City (which is styled Religious Sciences Unlimited Inc. vs. the City of Boca Raton, case number is 502022CA003848XXXXMB), the Plaintiff in that complaint cites to a proposed amendment to the City's land development regulations generally relating to introducing ALFs into the single-family zoning districts, including the R1 D zoning district. That proposed amendment was "sponsored" by Council Member Mayotte and was assigned Case File number AM-21-07. That proposed amendment was closed by City staff on March 1st of 2022 and is no longer a pending application nor being processed by the City.
