units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering revisions to Policy LU.1.1.6. of the Future Land Use Element of the City's Comprehensive Plan to: (i) remove double asterisks regarding density limits for convalescent homes, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, hospitals, and similar uses (which double asterisks were added in July 2020 during the City's statutorily­ required evaluation and appraisal process); (ii) remove single asterisks regarding density limits for hotels; and for both matters, retaining the purpose of the asterisks in a note; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-22-05) Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing and the first of two public hearings. Three votes would be required to transmit. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He stated that the proposed ordinance was a new version of Ordinance No. 5610 which had been introduced at a prior meeting. Mr. Schaad explained that it was a clarification of the Future Land Use Element of the City's Comprehensive Plan and briefly reviewed the background. He noted that prior amendments to the Comprehensive Plan and the Future Land Use Element had been adopted in 2020, and that the current revisions were being proposed to provide clarification and avoid confusion for future land use designations. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval on a 5 to 2 vote and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Joan Snow, Bill Snow, Gene Hodges, Nicole Droz, Kathy Gilio, Stacy Sipple, Christine Lyons, and Christine Allen spoke in favor of Ordinance 5614 and voiced concerns regarding an assisted living facility (ALF) proposed for SW 12 Avenue. Gene Hodges, Barbara Caccavale-Hodges, Ruth Ronin, Brian Clinton, Ken Deeken, Holli Sutton, Shane Kittleson, and Lara Kittelson expressed their support of Ordinance No. 5614. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to transmit Ordinance No. 5614. Council Member Thomson expressed his support for the ordinance. Council Member Mayotte stated that she felt the vote should be postponed until the outcome of related pending litigation was decided. Motion carried four votes to one; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes; Council Member Monica Mayotte voting no. Mayor Singer repeated that the vote was for transmittal of the ordinance to the State for review.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton pertaining to home-based businesses; amending Chapter 28, Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 9, "Certain Home Businesses and Home Occupations," Code of Ordinances, to rename said section as "Home­ Based Businesses" and modify regulations to ensure consistency with recently enacted state law regarding home-based businesses; amending various sections of Chapter 28, "Zoning," to replace the term "Home Occupation" with the term "Home-Based Business"; and reorganizing and/or restating portions of Chapter 28, "Zoning," Chapter 9, Article IV, Section 9-60, "Supplemental Code Enforcement Procedures," and various sections of Chapter 8, "Local Business Tax and Business Regulations," for clarity and improved organization; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM- 21-09) Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing and the first of two public hearings, and no vote would be taken. Brandon Schaad, Director of Development Services, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Schaad explained that the proposed ordinance would amend the City's existing requirements for home-based businesses by clarifying and improving the existing code language. He advised that the changes would ensure consistency with language in recently adopted Florida Statutes. Two substantive changes in the ordinance had to do with the number of employees allowed at the business and the number of business deliveries or pick-ups allowed. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Mayor Singer announced that the date of the second public hearing would be July 26, 2022.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the reimbursement of the legal defense costs incurred by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke in connection with an election complaint that was determined to be legally insufficient by the Florida Elections Commission; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Andrea O'Rourke recused herself from the discussion and voting on the proposed resolution. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser began by clarifying that the resolution had been previously postponed at Council's request in order to seek opinions from the Palm Beach County and Florida Commissions on Ethics. It was noted that the opinions received from both entities determined that neither Council Member Mayotte nor Council Member Drucker would have a voting conflict on this matter. Ms. Frieser then provided a brief overview of the proposed resolution. She explained that the complaint filed against Deputy Mayor O'Rourke was found to be legally insufficient and that Ms. O'Rourke was entitled to seek reimbursement of the costs for her defense. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Ounjian spoke about political contributions and his concerns regarding the proposed resolution. Glenn Gromann spoke in favor of the resolution. Ms. Frieser responded to statements made during public comments. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 52-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a "relative" includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A "business associate" means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joint venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). ELECTED OFFICERS: In addition to abstaining from voting in the situations described above, you must disclose the conflict: PRIOR TO THE VOTE BEING TAKEN by publicly stating to the assembly the nature of your interest in the measure on which you are abstaining from voting; and WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER THE VOTE OCCURS by completing and filing this form with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who should incorporate the form in the minutes. APPOINTED OFFICERS: Although you must abstain from voting in the situations described above, you are not prohibited by Section 112.3143 from otherwise participating in these matters. However, you must disclose the nature of the conflict before making any attempt to influence the decision, whether orally or in writing and whether made by you or at your direction. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 5-acre vacant property generally located at 8250 North Congress Avenue, an amendment to Exhibit "A" (setting forth the site plan) of a universal conditional (UC) approval amending the Future Land Use Map of the City's Comprehensive Plan (Ordinance No. 5394) to: (i) increase the height of the approved building (from 49 feet, 10 inches to 50 feet), (ii) increase the floor area of the approved building (from approximately 147,000 square-feet to approximately 209,516 square-feet), (iii) change authorized uses (from a 151-bed assisted living facility to a 150-bed convalescent facility and 50-bed assisted living facility, totaling 200 beds), (iv) eliminate an approximately 3,320 square-foot medical clinic, and (v) add an approximately 4,300 square-foot dialysis center; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-04R1/SC) 1. Resolution No. 60-2022 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved Universal Conditional (UC) Site Plan (Resolution No. 83-2017) for an approximately S­ acre vacant property generally located at 8250 North Congress Avenue to: (i) increase the height of the approved building (from 49 feet, 10 inches to 50 feet), (ii) increase the floor area of the approved building (from approximately 147,000 square-feet to approximately 209,516 square-feet), (iii) change authorized uses (from a 151-bed assisted living facility to a 150-bed convalescent facility and 50-bed assisted living facility, totaling 200 beds), (iv) eliminate an approximately 3,320 square-foot medical clinic, and (v) add an approximately 4,300square-foot dialysis center, together with a technical deviation from Section 23-190(d), Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance at the North Congress Avenue driveway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-04R 1/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and 10.A.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Planner Jacob German gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an overview of the applicants' request and provided a comparison to the previous approval. An aerial photograph of the location was shown, and the site plan was displayed. Mr. German reviewed the requested technical deviation for a 30-foot driveway reservoir and the proposed amendment to the FLUM Amendment ordinance to reference the correcUrevised site plan. The proposed medical related uses are permitted in the current zoning district. Mr. German advised that the intensity did not exceed the maximum limit allowed, and although the number of beds proposed was higher than previously approved, the impact on emergency medical services was expected to be lower. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall spoke on behalf of the applicant. He shared renderings of the proposed facility and provided additional information regarding the expected number of emergency medical service calls. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. Jonathan Ounjian voiced his concerns over the project and local zoning. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Marshall responded to a number of comments made by Mr. Ounjian regarding zoning and expected traffic impacts. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5619. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information and Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 60-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

Michael Marshall spoke on behalf of the applicant. He shared renderings of the proposed facility and provided additional information regarding the expected number of emergency medical service calls. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. Jonathan Ounjian voiced his concerns over the project and local zoning. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Marshall responded to a number of comments made by Mr. Ounjian regarding zoning and expected traffic impacts. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5619. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information and Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. units.text: An emergency ordinance of the City of Boca Raton repealing Chapter 9, Article VI, "Prohibition of Conversion Therapy on Minors," Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser read the text of Ordinance No. 5626 and provided some brief background. She explained that in 2017, the City adopted Ordinance No. 5407, prohibiting certain therapeutic practices. Ms. Frieser stated that Palm Beach County had adopted a similar ordinance and both the City and County had then been named as co-defendants in a federal lawsuit challenging the ordinances. Ms. Frieser reviewed case history, concluding with the mandate issued by the 11 th Circuit Court of Appeals on August 1, 2022, which found that the City's and County's ordinances were unconstitutional. Ms. Frieser explained that because the court found the ordinance violated the First Amendment, the City wanted to act quickly to repeal the ordinance and that an emergency ordinance is authorized under Section 3.14 of the City Charter. Ms. Frieser recommended adoption of the emergency ordinance which, if approved, would be in effect for only 60 days, and introduction of a non­ emergency ordinance to similarly repeal the ordinance (permanently). Ms. Frieser noted a communication received by Rand Hoch of the Palm Beach Human Rights Council, an advocate of Ordinance No. 5407, encouraging the City Council to adopt the proposed ordinances in lieu of appealing the case to the U.S. Supreme Court. The public hearing was opened and several members of the public expressed their views. Seeing no one else indicate their desire to speak, the public hearing was closed. The City Attorney briefly highlighted portions of the proposed emergency ordinance that stated that, although the City disagrees with the decision of the Court, it respects the Court's authority, and she concluded by reading a section affirming the City had no intention of reenacting Ordinance No. 5407 or as similar ordinance. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5625. Council Member Mayotte commented that she disagreed with the ruling of the Court but recognized the need for the ordinance, and she proposed a resolution stating the Council's opposition to certain therapeutic practices. Council Members weighed in and echoed Ms. Mayotte's desire for the resolution. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the sale of a parcel of city-owned land, pursuant to Chapter 13, Article Ill, "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances, consisting of approximately 0.015 acres and generally located at 7901 Northeast Spanish Trail Court; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-22-02) 2. Resolution No. 44-2022 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering accepting and approving the plat known as "Banana Patch" (a portion of which is a replat of Tract "A," Tropic Isle 4th Section, together with an unplatted portion consisting of the south one-half of the northwest one­ quarter of Section 33, Township 46 South, Range 43 East), for an approximately 1.1 acre property generally located at 7901 Northeast Spanish Trail Court and 7902 Northeast Palm Way, authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the Plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-21-01) The public hearings on Items B. and B.1. will be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions are related and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures as required by Item 8.1 (Item B is a legislative matter). A separate vote will be taken on Items B. and 8.1. Should Item B. not be approved, Item 8.1. will not be considered. The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and 10.A.2. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Planner Jacob German gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an overview of the applicants' request and provided a comparison to the previous approval. An aerial photograph of the location was shown, and the site plan was displayed. Mr. German reviewed the requested technical deviation for a 30- foot driveway. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Michael Weiner, attorney for the applicant, reviewed the existing conditions of the property. He further explained the request for technical deviation and made himself available for Members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Ordinance No. 5617 Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 44-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 2.03-acre property, located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard and 910 East Palmetto Park Road, an amendment to Exhibit '1' (setting forth the site plan) of a Universal Conditional (UC) Future Land Use Map Amendment (Ordinance No. 5413) to increase the square footage of the 70-unit multifamily residential project, increase the number of parking spaces provided, revise the approved landscape plan and architectural elevations, make related site modifications, and eliminate a previously approved technical deviation from Section 23-190(J), Code of Ordinances, for the reduction in inbound reservoir distance to a gated entrance; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06R1/SC) 1. Resolution No. 61-2022 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.5 acre property located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard, 155 South Ocean Boulevard, and 910 East Palmetto Park Road, an amendment to an approved Universal Conditional (UC) Site Plan (Resolution No. 119-2017) to increase the square footage of the 70-unit multifamily residential project, increase the number of parking spaces provided, revise the approved landscape plan and architectural elevations, make related site modifications, and eliminate a previously approved technical deviation from Section 23-190(J), Code of Ordinances, for the reduction in inbound reservoir distance to a gated entrance; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06R1/SPA) Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items 10.B. and 10.8.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Bonnie Miskal, attorney for the applicant, advised there would be some changes to the interior of the building and therefore requested to postpone the hearing for 60 days. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad advised that, depending on the changes submitted, the item could be reconsidered by Council in 60 days. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser noted that the motion to postpone did not need to specify a date certain. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to postpone Ordinance No. 5621 and Resolution 61-2022. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton equalizing the assessments; levying the same as assessments against benefited properties within the Downtown Special Assessment District, City of Boca Raton, Florida; directing the City Clerk to record assessments in the Improvement Lien Book; establishing priority of lien and payment of principal and interest; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Stephen Timberlake, Special Projects Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He provided a brief history of the Downtown Special Assessment, the requirement to fund the debt service and administrative costs for the special assessment revenue bonds. Mr. Timberlake noted that the purpose of the meeting was to hear and consider any objections to the special assessment. The method of calculating the assessment rate was explained and various charts and graphs were presented. No objection letters were received. Upon concluding, Mr. Timberlake made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Tiery Boykin, business owner, commented on expanding the parameters of who might pay for the assessments since everyone enjoys the benefits of the Downtown. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 91-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: Budget Director Sharon McGuire gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by giving an overview of the proposed millage rate of 3.6784 mils. She further explained the General Fund Operating costs and new additions to the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 budget, including new positions and programs. She also described the Property Tax Bill by Taxing Authority breakdown and provided an example scenario for an average home. Also discussed were the tax rates and Fire Assessment fees of surrounding cities and how we are the lowest of the cities compared. Ms. McGuire concluded the Millage portion of her presentation and responded to a question about the Beautification Fund. She continued by discussing the Capital Improvements Program. Upon concluding she made herself available for questions.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton imposing Fire Services Assessments against Assessed Property (residential , commercial, and industrial) located within the City for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2022; approving the fiscal year 2022-2023 rate of assessment; approving the fiscal year 2022-2023 Assessment Roll (based on the rate of assessment); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Minutes of the Tentative Budget Hearing 2 September 12, 2022 0MB Director Sharon McGuire gave a brief review on the fire assessment fee, noting an increase and described the categories that contributed to the calculation. Upon concluding , Ms. McGuire made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Phyllis Robinson advised that during Covid, she gave all her tenants a discount on their rent and never asked for repayment. She stated her objection to the increase proposed by the City. Daniella Franciscus advised she is aware of the reasons for the increase but asked why the residents need to shoulder this cost. David Eddinger, President of Local 1560 IAFF, explained the need for the increase to the Fire Assessment Fee and the need for additional Fire Rescue Department staffing and equipment. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. The Mayor provided additional comments and information. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 95-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering three (3) separate appeals of the decisions of the Planning and Zoning Board in connection w ith the redevelopment of an approximately 3.5 acre property generally located at 2700 North Federal Highway: (1) an appeal of the site plan approval (Resolution No. 2022-010) authorizing the construction of three new one-story buildings totaling 18,366 square feet in three phases; (2) a second appeal (by the applicant) requesting that the site plan approval be modified to remove certain conditions of approval; and (3) an appeal of the decision of the Planning and Zoning Board to grant variances (Resolution No. 2022-011) from Section 28-752, Code of Ordinances, to allow: (i) a six-foot wide landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way (North Federal Highway}, where the Code requires a ten-foot wide landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way , and (ii) a sidewalk that is parallel to the western property line (adjoining North Federal Highway) where the Code allows sidewalks only generally perpendicular to the plot line within the required landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way, in the Motel-Business (R-B-1 ) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-21-04/21-97500004) (VA-21-08/21-97500004) Ele Zachariades, attorney for Hotel Properties, L.P. applicant/appellant, requested to postpone the hearing to September 28, 2022, in order to allow additional negotiations with the neighborhood association . Larry Schner, attorney for the Harbour East neighborhood association appellant, also requested postponement of the public hearing to September 28, 2022 . Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to postpone the public hearing for Resolution No. 96-2022 to September 28, 2022. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering accepting and approving the plat known as "Reve Del Mizner Plat" (a replat of a portion of Lot 8, Block 8, Rickard's Survey of Boca Raton, Florida) for an approximately 0.39 acre property generally located at 200 East Boca Raton Road, authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer, providing an effective date (SUB-21-05) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She noted that the site plan for the project had been approved by the Community Redevelopment Agency the prior day and advised that the proposed resolution was for the approval of the project plat. Ms. Rahman showed a drawing of the proposed plat and pointed out the right of way dedication, landscape buffer and sidewalk easement. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, referred to her presentation the prior day and made herself available for Members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 80-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, "Administration", Article IV, "Departments", Division 3, "City Manager's Department", Section 2-328(f), to increase the City Manager's authority to enter into contracts for the purchase of budgeted materials and services to $200,000 and of construction services to $500,000 without prior approval of the City Council; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Linda Davidson , Financial Services Director, gave the presentation. She explained that, due to inflation, escalating costs, and supply chain issues, staff recommended that the threshold levels be raised. She noted that recommendation awards are posted to the website. In response to a question posed by Mayor Singer, Ms. Davidson advised that she believed passage of the proposed ordinance would help to expedite certain processes within the City. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5629. Mayor Singer commented on the transparency of the purchasing process and stated that the City Manager advised that additional information could be added to the City's website. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: City Manager Leif Ahnell reviewed the requests for additional funding and amendments to the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget. Topics discussed included the City Manager succession plan, rewriting of the Land Development Code, Art in Public Places, hiring a consultant to streamline Development Services Processes, and Expansion of the City's Recycling Program. The last item discussed was the Government Campus Master Plan. Ms. Drucker urged staff to begin the process of approving the funds to hire a consultant. Discussion ensued and Mr. Ahnell provided additional information. Mayor Singer agreed that the Government Master Plan should be a priority. Mayor Singer proposed a new position to review policies and provide research directly to the Council Members and suggested a proposed budget for this position. Discussion ensued. Mayor Singer then opened the discussion for the Non-Profit funding requests. Mr. Ahnell reviewed the list of the Non-Profit Organizations and provided background on the process. Discussion ensued and Members weighed in. Mr. Ahnell then opened the discussion of the Non-Profit Funding requests. Members considered changes to the funding list that each member had proposed. Working from the Mayor's list, individual requests and modifications were reviewed, and amendments were made.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 1.6-acre property generally located at 7940 North Federal Highway, an amended and restated conditional use approval (amending and restating Resolution No. 174-2003) to authorize the expansion of the existing substance abuse treatment facility (Wellness Resource Center) from 5,100 square feet to 10,933 square feet; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-03-17R1) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hanson, Senior Planner, gave a PowerPoint presentation. She began by describing the subject area and current property uses. Ms. Hanson outlined the applicant's request to expand the size of the facility, noting that the expansion would involve only internal alterations. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval with an additional condition, and staff advised against including the condition suggested by the Board . A map of the site, including parking details and landscaping, was shown. The public notice was reviewed. Staff recommended approval subject to the conditions set forth . Upon concluding, Ms. Hanson responded to Council Members' questions and provided clarification. The public hearing was opened. Jim Frogner, representative on behalf of the owner, thanked staff for their presentation and requested approval of the project. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 114-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering three (3) separate appeals of the decisions of the Planning and Zoning Board in connection with the redevelopment of an approximately 3.5 acre property generally located at 2700 North Federal Highway: (1) an appeal of the site plan approval (Resolution No. 2022-010) authorizing the construction of three new one-story buildings totaling 18,366 square feet in three phases; (2) a second appeal (by the applicant) requesting that the site plan approval be modified to remove certain conditions of approval; and (3) an appeal of the decision of the Planning and Zoning Board to grant variances (Resolution No. 2022-011) from Section 28-752, Code of Ordinances, to allow: (i) a six-foot wide landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way (North Federal Highway), where the Code requires a ten-foot wide landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way, and (ii) a sidewalk that is parallel to the western property line (adjoining North Federal Highway) where the Code allows sidewalks only generally perpendicular to the plot line within the required landscaped yard abutting a street right-of-way, in the Motel-Business (R-B-1) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-21-04/21-97500004) (VA-21-08/21-97500004) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a review of the appeals, noting that the two appeals from the HOA had been withdrawn, and proceeded to review the appeal from Hotel Properties, L.P. She displayed a drawing of the subject property and described the proposed site plan and construction phasing. Ms. Rahman noted the vehicular access points and that a condition of approval by the Florida Department of Transportation (FOOT) would require the applicant to complete a warrant analysis for the construction of a traffic signal at the middle driveway. Another condition of approval would require the applicant to maintain the queueing for the drive­ through on site. The Planning and Zoning Board (PZB) approved the site plan and two variances. Ms. Rahman reviewed the suggested modifications from the applicant and revised conditions of approval regarding project phasing and undergrounding of utility lines. Staff recommended a new condition of approval regarding FOOT authorization for a "No U-Turn" sign. Staff recommended affirming the decision of the PZB with revised and new conditions of approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to Council Members' questions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser reviewed the procedure of the public hearing, noting that a settlement had been reached between the applicant and the Homeowner's Association (HOA), resulting in the withdrawal of the HOA's appeal. A blacklined resolution had been provided to Members that reflected the withdrawal of one appeal and proposed staff revision. Ms. Frieser also noted that, pursuant to the Settlement Agreement (Agreement) between the HOA and property owner, consideration would be paid to the HOA and the applicant would disclose this information. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, representing the property owner appellant, thanked everyone for their work on the project and confirmed that a settlement had been reached that involved payment. She provided additional information regarding the undergrounding of utility lines. At the request of Mayor Singer, Ms. Frieser noted that paragraph 3 of the private Agreement between the Hotel Properties and Harbour East Association, provided for a payment to the HOA upon approval of the project. Ms. Zachariades confirmed the terms noted by Ms. Frieser. Larry Schner, attorney representing the Harbour East Association, confirmed that an Agreement had been reached. He pointed out that not only had monetary conditions been agreed to, but that additional concerns of the HOA had been addressed regarding traffic, noise, pollution, and other issues. Ms. Frieser reiterated that the Agreement was private, and additional requirements or conditions would not be enforced by the City. Mr. Schner stated that the agreed upon conditions in the Agreement were important to the HOA and asked that that be taken into consideration . Chris Dinallo, Tammy Dinallo, Andrew Bessio and Clark Stevens, spoke in opposition to the project, specifically the drive-through restaurant proposed for the property, citing traffic, noise, safety, and privacy concerns. Council Member Andy Thomson then asked the City Attorney to clarify the settlement of the HOA appeal. Ms. Frieser provided information and advised that the appeal of the property owner to modify certain conditions was still being heard. Council Member Mayotte stated that some of the issues raised by speakers appear to have been addressed in the settlement agreement and inquired if it had been shared with the residents of Harbour East. Ms. Frieser reiterated that the City was not a party of the settlement and added that the agreement between the property owner and the Association did not bind every individual homeowner in the neighborhood. Scott Zaslav, counsel for the applicant, explained that the only items they believed were being considered were the two conditions in the appeal. Marilda Hoover, Bill Riley, Kimberly Trombly-Burmeister, Ray Lopez, James Burmeister, Charles Morganstern, and Gloria Branch expressed their opposition to the proposed development, citing concerns with traffic issues, security and safety of the nearby neighborhood, landscaping, and the current building code. Stacy Packer questioned the authority of the HOA to approve a settlement on behalf of all the residents of Harbour East and read a written statement agreed to by neighbors. Mayor Singer then advised that those who had spoken had the opportunity to cross-examine any other speaker. Seeing no one come forward, the appellant was provided the opportunity for rebuttal. Ms. Zachariades provided additional information about the properties' permitted use under the current code and responded to residents' comments regarding signage, traffic, and landscaping. She concluded by responding to Members' questions regarding a barrier wall, landscaping , and the mid-property left turn only lane. The public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 96-2022. Council discussion ensued on issues and concerns brought up by residents. Brandon Schaad , Development Services Director, provided clarification regarding a sidewalk in the abutting neighborhood, additional light poles, lack of space for a barrier wall, an additional med ian cut, and the timing of the traffic study. Naresh Machavarapu, Assistant Traffic engineer, responded to questions regarding the traffic study. Ms. Drucker requested a police report of incidents occurring by the neighborhood. The City Attorney noted that, although the applicant asked that the appeal consider only the two conditions of the P&Z Board decision being challenged, Council had the authority to consider the entire decision of the Board. Further discussion ensued . Ms. Frieser then provided clarification on the black line version of the resolution provided by staff. The meeting was recessed at approximately 9:01 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:19 pm. Discussion resumed, and Ms. Frieser summarized the options available to the Members. Members shared their positions and expressed their desire to have additional information prior to making their decision. Mr. Schaad clarified the supplemental material requested by Council and provided a timeframe to receive information from outside agencies. The public hearing was reopened to consider continuing to a date certain of December 13th. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to continue Resolution No. 96-2022 to December 13, 2022. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a review of the appeals, noting that the two appeals from the HOA had been withdrawn, and proceeded to review the appeal from Hotel Properties, L.P. She displayed a drawing of the subject property and described the proposed site plan and construction phasing. Ms. Rahman noted the vehicular access points and that a condition of approval by the Florida Department of Transportation (FOOT) would require the applicant to complete a warrant analysis for the construction of a traffic signal at the middle driveway. Another condition of approval would require the applicant to maintain the queueing for the drive­ through on site. The Planning and Zoning Board (PZB) approved the site plan and two variances. Ms. Rahman reviewed the suggested modifications from the applicant and revised conditions of approval regarding project phasing and undergrounding of utility lines. Staff recommended a new condition of approval regarding FOOT authorization for a "No U-Turn" sign. Staff recommended affirming the decision of the PZB with revised and new conditions of approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman responded to Council Members' questions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser reviewed the procedure of the public hearing, noting that a settlement had been reached between the applicant and the Homeowner's Association (HOA), resulting in the withdrawal of the HOA's appeal. A blacklined resolution had been provided to Members that reflected the withdrawal of one appeal and proposed staff revision. Ms. Frieser also noted that, pursuant to the Settlement Agreement (Agreement) between the HOA and property owner, consideration would be paid to the HOA and the applicant would disclose this information. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, representing the property owner appellant, thanked everyone for their work on the project and confirmed that a settlement had been reached that involved payment. She provided additional information regarding the undergrounding of utility lines. At the request of Mayor Singer, Ms. Frieser noted that paragraph 3 of the private Agreement between the Hotel Properties and Harbour East Association, provided for a payment to the HOA upon approval of the project. Ms. Zachariades confirmed the terms noted by Ms. Frieser. Larry Schner, attorney representing the Harbour East Association, confirmed that an Agreement had been reached. He pointed out that not only had monetary conditions been agreed to, but that additional concerns of the HOA had been addressed regarding traffic, noise, pollution, and other issues. Ms. Frieser reiterated that the Agreement was private, and additional requirements or conditions would not be enforced by the City. Mr. Schner stated that the agreed upon conditions in the Agreement were important to the HOA and asked that that be taken into consideration . Chris Dinallo, Tammy Dinallo, Andrew Bessio and Clark Stevens, spoke in opposition to the project, specifically the drive-through restaurant proposed for the property, citing traffic, noise, safety, and privacy concerns. Council Member Andy Thomson then asked the City Attorney to clarify the settlement of the HOA appeal. Ms. Frieser provided information and advised that the appeal of the property owner to modify certain conditions was still being heard. Council Member Mayotte stated that some of the issues raised by speakers appear to have been addressed in the settlement agreement and inquired if it had been shared with the residents of Harbour East. Ms. Frieser reiterated that the City was not a party of the settlement and added that the agreement between the property owner and the Association did not bind every individual homeowner in the neighborhood. Scott Zaslav, counsel for the applicant, explained that the only items they believed were being considered were the two conditions in the appeal. Marilda Hoover, Bill Riley, Kimberly Trombly-Burmeister, Ray Lopez, James Burmeister, Charles Morganstern, and Gloria Branch expressed their opposition to the proposed development, citing concerns with traffic issues, security and safety of the nearby neighborhood, landscaping, and the current building code. Stacy Packer questioned the authority of the HOA to approve a settlement on behalf of all the residents of Harbour East and read a written statement agreed to by neighbors. Mayor Singer then advised that those who had spoken had the opportunity to cross-examine any other speaker. Seeing no one come forward, the appellant was provided the opportunity for rebuttal. Ms. Zachariades provided additional information about the properties' permitted use under the current code and responded to residents' comments regarding signage, traffic, and landscaping. She concluded by responding to Members' questions regarding a barrier wall, landscaping , and the mid-property left turn only lane. The public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 96-2022. Council discussion ensued on issues and concerns brought up by residents. Brandon Schaad , Development Services Director, provided clarification regarding a sidewalk in the abutting neighborhood, additional light poles, lack of space for a barrier wall, an additional med ian cut, and the timing of the traffic study. Naresh Machavarapu, Assistant Traffic engineer, responded to questions regarding the traffic study. Ms. Drucker requested a police report of incidents occurring by the neighborhood. The City Attorney noted that, although the applicant asked that the appeal consider only the two conditions of the P&Z Board decision being challenged, Council had the authority to consider the entire decision of the Board. Further discussion ensued . Ms. Frieser then provided clarification on the black line version of the resolution provided by staff. The meeting was recessed at approximately 9:01 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:19 pm. Discussion resumed, and Ms. Frieser summarized the options available to the Members. Members shared their positions and expressed their desire to have additional information prior to making their decision. Mr. Schaad clarified the supplemental material requested by Council and provided a timeframe to receive information from outside agencies. The public hearing was reopened to consider continuing to a date certain of December 13th. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to continue Resolution No. 96-2022 to December 13, 2022. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing a transaction between the City, the Boca Raton Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA), and the Center for Arts & Innovation Inc. (formerly the Boca Raton Arts District Exploratory Corporation (BRADEC)), in connection with the development of a performing arts center at Mizner Park and the redevelopment of the Mizner Park Amphitheater, pursuant to Section 163.380, Florida Statutes, and Chapter 13, Article Ill, "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (The proposed transaction affects parcels of real property owned by the City of Boca Raton and by the Boca Raton Community Redevelopment Agency. The proposed sale of City-owned property is being considered pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 13, Article Ill, City Code of Ordinances. Pursuant to the requirements of Section 163.380, Florida Statutes, notice of the potential disposition of the property owned by the Community Redevelopment Agency was published March 30, 2021 . Because the disposition of the Agency's property would be for less than fair market value, the authorization of the City Council is required to complete the transaction.) George Brown, Deputy City Manager, gave the presentation. He stated that the presentation previously made to the CRA, and the public hearing conducted by the CRA on August 22, 2022, were part of the record. Staff recommended adoption of the ordinance with the changes to the transaction documents as previously discussed and enumerated in the memoranda of September 20th and October 5 th _ Mr. Brown advised the amendment would include language proposed by Council Member Mayotte to the CRA resolution on the same subject, as well as parallel language from an amendment to the CRA resolution proposed by Mayor Singer and Council Member Thomson. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . Michael Manko spoke in opposition of the ordinance, preferring the amphitheater to be kept as an open-air venue and asked that an alternate location be chosen for the performing arts center. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed . Mayor Singer suggested the motion to adopt would include all changes made to the previously approved CRA resolution. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5616 as amended. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote; Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes, Mayor Singer voting no.

Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to remove item 15.A., Resolution No. 119-2022, from the agenda. Council Members provided their thoughts on the ALF issue and whether or not to keep the resolution on the agenda. Ms. Mayotte expressed her concerns with how the resolution was written and Mayor Singer noted that there was litigation pending on a proposed ALF project. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarified and noted that the resolution was about the specific ordinances originally sponsored by Ms. Mayotte, but the language was precise as to whether or not Council wanted to move forward with this specific text amendment. After further discussion, there was consensus to keep the public hearing for Resolution No. 119-2022 on the agenda. Council Member Thomson withdrew his second and the motion died for lack of a second.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton providing legislative direction regarding whether (or not) the City Council desires to consider an amendment to the zoning code to introduce Assisted Living Facilities (ALFs) as an allowable use in the City's single-family zoning districts, and, if the Council desires to consider such an amendment, directing the processing of such an amendment; providing an effective date City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided a handout and gave a PowerPoint presentation. She began with an overview of the resolution which included, but was not limited to, background information on the original text amendment sought to the City's zoning code, the purpose of the proposed amendment, revised language in the final amendment request in February 2022, action taken by City staff and resulting legal action taken by the property owner. Ms. Frieser summarized the lawsuit brought by the property owner and reviewed the focus and purpose of any action to be taken by City Council. She advised the resolution was specifically created in response to the lawsuit and the direction sought from Council was whether or not to process the proposed ALF text amendment. Ms. Frieser stressed that the resolution was not quasi-judicial and did not place limitations on any future council consideration of an ALF amendment. Concern regarding the binary nature of the resolution was addressed. A clean revised version of Section 1 of the resolution was reviewed for clarification, and it was noted that the exhibit should be titled 'B' not 'A'. Notifications of the public hearing had been sent to the property owner of the proposed ALF and some residents of the surrounding neighborhood. The representatives of the property owner confirmed they were aware and agreed with the City to extend the response on the litigation knowing this matter was being discussed. Upon concluding, the City Attorney advised that she, City staff and outside counsel were available to respond to questions. Regular Agenda 4 October 25, 2022 At the request of Council Member Mayotte, Development Services Director Brandon Schaad displayed a map of properties within the City that would be eligible for ALF development under the criteria of the text amendment. Council Member Mayotte clarified the purpose of her request for the map and Mr. Schaad described the potential locations in further detail. The Mayor opened the public hearing. Barbara Caccaval Hodges spoke in opposition of the resolution. Ms. Frieser reiterated that the vote on the resolution would only be to provide direction to staff whether or not to process an application for a particular ALF. Ms. Hodges clarified that she was opposed to staff processing the ALF application. Jay Whelchel, applicant of the proposed ALF, spoke in support of the resolution and commented on the need for assisted living facilities and senior housing in the City. Holli Sutton, William Miller, Brian Stenberg, Jack McWalter, Sheila Mahon, Bill Snow, Laura Sweeney, Christine Lyons, Cynthia Briggs, Kathlean Gilio, Shannon Otto, John Gilio, Janna Evans, Pat Sipple, Glenn Gromann, Sandra Neklewicz, Lara Kittleson, and Ona Zerra expressed their opposition to the processing of the ALF application. Christine Hartofilis and Joanne Jackson spoke in support of processing. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Ms. Frieser commented that an appropriate motion was to either process or not process an amendment to the ALF text. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to direct staff to not process the text amendment. Ms. Frieser read provisions to the resolution into the record and Council Members offered their final thoughts. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Mayotte spoke favorably on the opening of the Wildflower Park and commented on observing an incident where City sanitation workers had been especially courteous and considerate of residents. Council Member Drucker reminded everyone to vote on November 8th. Vice Chair O'Rourke noted this was one of Council Member Andy Thomson's last Council meetings and asked whether there would be discussion to temporarily reappoint someone to the seat or wait until the election in March for his replacement. There was consensus to wait for discussion until the November meeting. Ms. O'Rourke then thanked everyone involved for their hard work to bring the Wildflower Park to its successful completion. Mayor Singer also commented on the success of the Wildflower Park and thanked everyone for their work throughout the process. He then commented on the Boca Raton Beach and Park District's (BPD) plans for the Ocean Breeze property and his concern to make sure that the City is prepared for its discussion at an upcoming Workshop Meeting. Mr. Ahnell provided additional information and turned the discussion over to Deputy Regular Agenda 5 October 25, 2022 Manager George Brown. Mr. Brown showed a slide of the preliminary plan and proceeded to review the proposed amenities noting it was not a fully pledged plan. Topics included, but were not limited to, funding, private/public partnerships and amenities shown on the plan. Ms. Drucker felt the discussion was premature and suggested to hold off on this discussion until the BPD had an opportunity to present. Mayor Singer responded that his concern was that staff had adequate time to review the plan and response time for questions prior to the Workshop. Discussion ensued. There was consensus to get clarification from the BPD as to their presentation and intent. Ms. Frieser provided additional information on the scheduling of a quasi-judicial hearing. Mayor Singer concluded by asking everyone to vote on November 8.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 0.77 acre property generally located at 170 Northwest 20th Street, a conditional use pursuant to Section 28-1098, to authorize a new health and fitness club (gym) (superseding the conditional use for a retail fabric store granted by Resolution No. 220-87) in an existing building in the General Industrial (M-2) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-22-01) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members disclosed their ex-parte discussions. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the presentation. He began by displaying an aerial photo of the subject location and provided a description of the site's existing condition. The applicant's proposed site plan and use as an open floor gym was shown. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval, and staff recommended approval of the conditional use application. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to questions regarding conditional use approvals in the district surrounding 20th Street. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, remarked on the permitted uses of the particular retail location and questioned why her client had been required to apply for a conditional use approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 123-2022. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke requested clarification from staff regarding Ms. Zachariades comments. Mayor Singer asked if Mr. Schaad would suggest any further streamlining to the existing Code regarding uses in industrial districts. Mr. Schaad responded to the questions posed and provided additional information. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 1.13 acre property generally located at 6653 Jog Road, accepting and approving the plat known as "Genesis" (a replat of Parcel No. One of "Plaza Real Plat No. 1"), which replat will result in the elimination of a plat restriction limiting the use of the property (Parcel 1) to a bank only; authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-22-01) The City Attorney confirmed that the quasi-judicial procedures remained in effect. Members disclosed their ex-parte discussions. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by displaying an aerial photo of the subject property and reviewed the components of the applicant's request. He noted that the request involved a replat request of one of two parcels, as well as a site plan amendment. The notice for the public hearing was reviewed, including a mailer and newspaper publication. The Planning and Zoning Board (P&Z) recommended approval. Mr. Bell commented on a discussion by the P&Z regarding potential future uses of one of the parcels and confirmed that future uses would have to meet zoning requirements and be reviewed by the Board. Staff finds that the proposed changes are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and recommend approval. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of the applicant, commented on the history of the parcel and provided additional information. She then she made herself available for Members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 124-2022. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte voting yes.

units.text: A Resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing Brightline Trains Florida LLC to install and maintain a mural on the north wall connecting the main entrances of the Parking Garage and the Train Station on City-owned property generally located at 400 NW 2nd Avenue, 101 NW 4 th Street, and 151 NW 4th Street; Authorizing the City Manager to execute an acknowledgement and waiver by Brightline and the Mural Artist; providing for repealer; providing an effective date. Brightline Vice President Brian Kronberg described the location of the art wall and artist Ben Heller provided his perspective and cited his influences of the design of the proposed mural. Ms. Mayotte thanked Mr. Kronberg and Mr. Heller and expressed her approval of the design 's historical significance. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 5-acre St. David Armenian Church property (generally located at 2300 West Yamato Road), an amended and restated conditional use approval consolidating conditional use Resolution Nos. 4-87, 3-95, and 148-2016 for an existing church and child care center and authorizing construction of a 9,305- square foot expansion to an existing 5,084-square foot child care center, and an increase in the capacity of the child care center from 60 to 247 children; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-94-11 R2) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Eoin Devlin, GIS Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by displaying an aerial photograph of the subject property. Mr. Devlin outlined the applicant's request to expand the child care center and provided a history of the development of the property. The proposed site plan was displayed. Components of the expansion were outlined, and elevations of the build ing were shown. Mr. Devlin reviewed the public notices and advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and City staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions and provided additional information regarding traffic patterns and landscaping. The public hearing was opened. Doug Mummaw, architect for the project, described the renovations and expansion in further detail. The proposed changes to the property were shown on a site plan , and elevations of the proposed addition were displayed and compared to photographs of the existing building. Mr. Mummaw continued by reviewing the traffic pattern and describing the landscape plan. Upon concluding, he made himself available for q uestions. Armen Melkonian, Parish Council Chairman of St. David Armenian Church, asked Council for their support of the project. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, to approve Resolution No. 127-2022. Members made final comments and expressed their support. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser clarified that the motion was to grant the conditional use approval. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, relating to required yards (setbacks) , encroachments, and accessory buildings and structures; amending Article IX, "Single-Family Residential Districts," and Article XV, Division 3, "Encroachments," to set forth the applicable regulations with regard to requi red yards (setbacks), encroachments, and accessory buildings and structures in residential districts; amending, reorganizing and/or restating provisions of Chapter 28, "Zoning ," with regard to required yards (setbacks), encroachments, and accessory buildings and structures, for clarity and improved organization; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for cod ification; providing an effective date (AM-21-10) Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by noting that this was a privately initiated request to permit decorative water features , and that most of the proposed amendments were included in the continuing Zoning Code rewrite. A drawing of a typ ical residential property was displayed, showing property lines and setbacks. Mr. Schaad outlined the components of allowable water features and accessory buildings . Additional changes to the code included adding and amending definitions for clarity and consistency. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. Staff and P&Z recommended approval. He made himself available for questions. He provided additional information regard ing previous requ irements, height of accessory buildings, tiki huts and fence/wall height. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, on behalf of her client, showed a rendering of a proposed water featu re on her client's property and asked if the height limit might be raised from 18 to 24 inches. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Mr. Schaad provided additional information regard ing the height limit of water features that encroach on setbacks. Members weighed in and expressed their desire to keep the height limit at 18 inches. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5636. Members thanked Mr. Schaad and staff for their streamlining efforts. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton proposing an amendment to the City Charter changing the terms of office of the Mayor and City Council Members from three (3) years to four (4) years; extending the terms of those council members who terms are due to expire March 2024 by one additional year; providing for submission of the proposed City Charter amendment to the electors of the City at the regular election on March 14, 2023; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Mayor Scott Singer gave the presentation. The Mayor outlined his reasons for bringing forth the proposed ordinance, citing the amount of time it takes to get acclimated to the duties of the position, the need for consistency and continuity in local government, and the time it takes to see some goals to fruition. He noted most Florida cities similar in population size have 4-year terms, and he named a number of cities that had recently extended their council terms. Mayor Singer advocated extending the terms as a way to not only save on costs and staff time, but to allow candidates to focus more on policy than politics, pointing out that the proposed new election cycle would no longer fall on the same year as presidential races. Upon concluding he made himself available for questions. Council Member Drucker agreed that it takes time to learn the role of Council Member and with the proposed change in election cycles in order to remain non-partisan. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke observed that a component of proposed Ordinance No. 5638 would relieve some of the election duties from staff and stated that all of the correspondence she received from residents had been negative. The public hearing was opened. Brian Stenberg expressed his opposition to the proposed ordinance, inquired which residents and businesses would benefit from it and asked that Members vote no. Amy Price spoke against the proposed term extension and urged the Council to vote no on the ordinance as well as enact term limits for City boards and committees. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5637. Mayor Singer explained that the only way to enact the legislation and not have it affect current Council Members would be to have it take effect in 2029, and that he did not see the merit in postponing it. Council Member Nachlas shared that she would not be supporting the measure as it could directly impact her own term on the Council. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke stated that candidates should prepare as much as possible for the position prior to being elected and that she did not see the benefit in extending terms. Council Member Drucker clarified that there was an inevitable amount of on-the-job learning that comes with the position. Council Member Mayotte agreed that much effort and dedication goes into learning and performing the job, no matter the amount of preparation. Motion passed 3 votes to 2; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte voting yes, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke and Council Member Fran Nachlas voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton strongly encouraging the Florida Legislature to honorarily designate that segment of Glades Road located between Dixie Highway and Federal Hig hway in the Pearl City Neighborhood of Boca Raton, as "Lois D. Martin Way;" providing an effective date Deputy Mayor O'Rourke explained that she had initiated the proposed ordinance after receiving a request from the D.I.S.C. organization. Ms. O'Rourke praised the tremendous advocacy of Lois Martin on behalf of the Pearl City/ Dixie Manor/ Lincoln Manor neighborhoods and expressed her support for the resolution. The public hearing was opened. Joseph Martin shared highlights of his mother's involvement in and service to the community and thanked the Mayor and Council for their support of the proposed resolution. Charles Graves spoke about the life and positivity of Lois Martin and asked that in addition to the road name change, that a plaque or picture of Ms. Martin be erected at the Lois Martin Center. Jeffrey Katz reviewed the history and significance of the Pearl City neighborhood and asked that Council work with State legislators to enact the name change. Marjorie O'Sullivan, Minister Charles Conklin, and Marie Hester spoke of Ms. Martin's accomplishments and her significance to the community and asked that Council support the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 133-2022. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke thanked the Pearl City residents for their advocacy for their community and shared her support for Mr. Graves' suggestion that additional recognition of Ms. Martin be added to the community center that bears her name. Council Member Mayotte commented on the legacy of Lois Martin and thanked the Pearl City neighbors for their continued engagement with the city. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes. The meeting was recessed at approximately 8:49 pm and reconvened at approximately 9:00 pm.
