units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an appeal of the decision of the Planning and Zoning Board in connection with the redevelopment of an approximately 3.5 acre property generally located at 2700 North Federal Highway, specifically an appeal of the site plan approval (Resolution No. 2022-010) (by the applicant) requesting that the site plan approval be modified to remove certain conditions of approval; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-21-04) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tamashbeen Rahman , Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation and noted that this was a continuation of the October 12, 2022, hearing. An aerial map of the subject location was shown, and the current status of the property was described. Ms. Rahman explained that the appellant was requesting removal of conditions relating to undergrounding of utility lines and project phasing, and that she would be presenting the entire project per the City Council's request. The Planning and Zoning Board (P&Z) approvals were reviewed, which included a site plan for three new commercial buildings and two variances. A drawing of the proposed site plan and construction phasing was displayed. Vehicular access, landscape buffers and traffic and parking study results were reviewed. Staff analysis concluded that the proposed uses and site plan met code requirements, and that the requested variances were supported by staff. Ms. Rahman than discussed the applicant's request to change the order of construction phases and to remove the condition of undergrounding utility lines on NE 61h Drive. She then reported on Council questions posed to staff at the October hearing relating to traffic patterns and signal timing. The Florida Department of Transportation (FOOT) had indicated that it was up to the applicant to initiate a request for their inp·ut on the proposed options to modify the access points. Ms. Rahman confirmed that the appellant had not yet taken action or responded to staff. FDOT and City staff had determined that changing the location of the median cut would likely present significant traffic operation challenges. Staff also updated the traffic signal condition to provide greater flexibi lity for the warrant to be completed. Additional information included, but was not limited to, the applicant's traffic study, maintenance responsibility of existing light poles along NE 26th Street, police data regarding the number of accidents near this property, and queuing distance requirements for the proposed restaurant drive-through. Responses from the applicant to requests for the settlement agreement with neighboring residents and an explanation of the site layout had not yet been received. Staff recommended affirmation of the decision of the P&Z Board with revised and new conditions of approval. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman made herself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Todd Armbruster, on behalf of the appellant, advised that his client believed Council's consideration of the appeal should be limited to the issues of the phasing condition and utilities undergrounding condition. He noted that the appellant had worked with staff on the items of the appeal and objected to Council considering additional issues regarding the proposed project. Mayor Singer asked for confirmation that the appellant had chosen not to respond to Council Members' questions from the October meeting. Mr. Armbruster stated that his client had not addressed issues that they felt were beyond the proper scope of Council. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke requested clarification from the City Attorney as to what issues could be discussed during the public hearing. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser advised that she did not agree with the legal conclusions reached by Mr. Armbruster, noting that his theory was based on judicial decisions of courts and that the Council was not a court and the hearing was quasi-judicial. She also informed Members that, pursuant to City code, the Council's delegation to the P&Z Board is subject to an appeal to Council and that they have the authority to review the site plan criteria. Ms. Frieser also informed Members that there was significant case law regarding evidence and commentary by the public, and that consideration of testimony of the public should be limited to that which is fact based and not opinion based. She further clarified that their decision should rely on competent and substantial evidence in the record before them, sworn testimony, and evidence in the complete record of the matter. Kimberly Trombly-Burmeister, on behalf of the Blue Inlet Harbor East Neighborhood Association, voiced concerns over the conditions and safety of the proposed project and possibility of a Chick-Fil-A restaurant. Andrew Bessio, Bill Riley, Chris Dinallo, Steve Wickert, Eric Prego, Rachel Lopez, James Burmeister, Ed Kary, Charles Morgenstein, and Stacey Packer shared a PowerPoint presentation outlining their opposition and spoke on a wide range of topics, including safety of the abutting residential neighborhood, concerns about the proposed development not fitting the area, problem of high-volume drive-through restaurants in neighboring cities, and the potential effect on Police and Fire response times. Tom Hoover, John Kranik, Shannon Otto, and Susan Daly commented on potential impacts of a Chick-Fil-A to nearby residential neighborhoods and asked Council to reconsider the project. Ray Lopez also expressed his opposition to the project and stated that after his initial discussion with restaurant representatives, he had received no further response. There was no cross examination. Mr. Armbruster made his closing remarks and addressed comments made by Ms. Frieser. He reiterated his belief that the sole matters before Council were the phasing and utility undergrounding issues. The public hearing was closed. Council Member Nachlas read questions submitted by Stacey Packer regarding Police and Fire Department reviews and whether the City could conduct an independent traffic study. Members asked additional questions regarding traffic patterns, accident statistics, queuing distances, responsibility for maintenance for certain light poles, and conflicting code requirements. Mr. Schaad, Ms. Rahman, Mr. Ahnell, Municipal Services Director Zach Bihr, and Ms. Frieser provided clarification and additional information. Mayor Singer noted the time and asked for a motion to extend the meeting. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to extend the meeting beyond 11:00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Discussion ensued. City Traffic Engineer Naresh Machavarapu explained the process of reviewing the traffic study and provided information on the queuing/ circulation area within the project. Ms. Frieser responded to a comment made by Mr. Armbruster and clarified that the Council was not sitting as an appellate tribunal body. She also advised that property owners have the right to submit an application, but the applicant still must satisfy the criteria of City code. She the outlined the options for Members to consider: to affirm the decision of the P&Z Board, affirm the decision with additional or modified conditions, reverse the decision of the board, or remand the decision back to the P&Z Board for further deliberation. Ms. Frieser then read Code Section 28-56 in response to remarks by Mr. Armbruster. The meeting was recessed at approximately 11:17 pm and reconvened at approximately 11:39 pm. The elements of site plan criteria from City code were displayed for review. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy MayorAndrea Levine O'Rourke, to reverse the decision of the Planning and Zoning Board and to deny the site plan. Members made final comments and shared their positions. The City Attorney clarified the motion. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton relating to legislative efforts by the Boca Raton Airport Authority to update its Special Act: authorizing the Mayor to communicate City concerns regarding proposed language and revisions to the Palm Beach County legislative delegation; directing City administration to transmit a certified copy of this resolution to the Palm Beach County Legislative Delegation and other interested parties; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mayor Singer provided a brief explanation of the proposed resolution. He referred to the draft legislation provided by the Boca Raton Airport Authority (Authority), and questioned language relating to their ability to act outside of the airport property and concerns about governance of the board relating to the Executive Director. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke asked about the timing of the resolution, and Mr. Singer advised that the final language was to be presented to the legislative delegation by December 20th . The City Attorney provided more information and reported that she had collaborated briefly with the attorney for the Authority. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Jim Nau, Chair of the Boca Raton Airport Authority, clarified the deadline. He explained that the purpose of the Authority's resolution was to modernize and clarify their enabling legislation. Chris DeSilva shared his thoughts. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 145-2022. Members discussed what would comprise a majority vote, and whether it was of the total membership or of the quorum, and whether or not to delete Section 2. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend the motion on the floor and strike Section 2. Further discussion ensued, and Ms. Frieser proposed removing Section 3, as well. She then clarified what was required from the City by the deadline. Mayor Singer withdrew his previous motion to amend. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Drucker, to strike the clause in the title of the Resolution beginning with the word "authorizing" and ending with the word "parties", and striking Sections 2 and 3. Motion carried unanimously. units.full: Resolution No. 145-2022 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton relating to legislative efforts by the Boca Raton Airport Authority to update its Special Act: authorizing the Mayor to communicate City concerns regarding proposed language and revisions to the Palm Beach County legislative delegation; directing City administration to transmit a certified copy of this resolution to the Palm Beach County Legislative Delegation and other interested parties; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mayor Singer provided a brief explanation of the proposed resolution. He referred to the draft legislation provided by the Boca Raton Airport Authority (Authority), and questioned language relating to their ability to act outside of the airport property and concerns about governance of the board relating to the Executive Director. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke asked about the timing of the resolution, and Mr. Singer advised that the final language was to be presented to the legislative delegation by December 20th . The City Attorney provided more information and reported that she had collaborated briefly with the attorney for the Authority. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Jim Nau, Chair of the Boca Raton Airport Authority, clarified the deadline. He explained that the purpose of the Authority's resolution was to modernize and clarify their enabling legislation. Chris DeSilva shared his thoughts. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 145-2022. Members discussed what would comprise a majority vote, and whether it was of the total membership or of the quorum, and whether or not to delete Section 2. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to amend the motion on the floor and strike Section 2. Further discussion ensued, and Ms. Frieser proposed removing Section 3, as well. She then clarified what was required from the City by the deadline. Mayor Singer withdrew his previous motion to amend. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Drucker, to strike the clause in the title of the Resolution beginning with the word "authorizing" and ending with the word "parties", and striking Sections 2 and 3. Motion carried unanimously. Motion to approve Resolution No. 145-2022 as amended carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: Mr. Ahnell advised that staff was available to provide information on a Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) issue regard ing SW 18th Street. Zach Bihr, Municipal Services Director, gave a brief PowerPoint Presentation on the TAC (Technical Advisory Committee) meeting held by the TPA. He advised that during the meeting, it was stated that $21 million could be taken from local projects to fund a State Road 7 initiative. He noted that, due to this change, the City's SW 18th Street shared use path project would not be funded. Council Member Drucker, TPA Committee Member, advised that she had not yet had the opportunity to discuss the matter with a TPA representative, and that the issue would be going to a vote of the TPA body soon. Naresh Machavarapu, City Traffic Engineer, outlined the process for municipalities to submit projects and asked that the SW 18th Street project be supported. Mr. Ahnell explained that there was one set of funds designated for local projects, alternative sources of funds for non-local projects, and that local funds were being redirected to cover costs for non-local initiatives. Staff strong ly recommended that TPA members vote against this. Council Member Mayotte, also a TPA Member, advised that she would be meeting with a TPA representative the following day. There was consensus among Members that TPA members vote against this proposal.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 8.5 acre property generally located at 1751 North Military Trail and 21046 Commercial Trail, an amendment to the approved Planning and Zoning Board Site Plan (Board Resolution No. 2021-014) to authorize the construction of an approximately 121,030 square foot five-(5) story building consisting of approximately 89,500 square feet of medical office, 23,817 square feet of general office, and 7,813 square feet of restaurant and a six-(6) story parking structure; removing the approximately 1.7 acre portion of the adjacent Lake Worth Drainage District L-46 Canal from the approved site plan; authorizing an alternative landscape plan and four (4) technical deviations: (i) To allow required parking to be provided off-site on the aforementioned 1.7 acre L-46 Canal Property, (ii) Reduce the required width of the existing southern driveway on Commercial Trail (from 24 feet to 23 feet); (iii) Reduce the required reservoir distance of the existing northern driveway along Commercial Trail (from 50 feet to 30 feet); and (iv) Reduce the required turning radii of the existing northern driveway along Commercial Trail (from 30 feet to 25 feet); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-20-13R1) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex-parte disclosures. Assistant City Clerk Phillip W. Daly administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Long Range Project Manager Jim Bell gave the presentation. Mr. Bell started with a brief overview of the project and a history of the property. Slides shown were site plans, proposed amendments, mobility improvements and architectural renderings . The traffic and parking study was discussed, including the technical deviations for offsite parking, and altering the driveways entering the property. The Plan ning & Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. Bell made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued. Mr. Bell responded to Members' questions regarding the covered walkway and the number of parking spaces. The public hearing was opened. Attorney for the applicant, Bonnie Miskal, advised Mr. Bell had thoroughly covered her presentation and made herself available for questions. Mayor Singer asked for addit ional site renderings which were displayed. Ms. Miska! reviewed the renderings and spoke regarding some of the features of the building, including a rooftop terrace, the overall architecture, and landscape designs. Upon concluding , Ms. Miska! responded to Members' questions. Glenn Gromann spoke in favor of the project and commented on the need for Class A office space. Jonathan Ounjian advised that the Zoning should be consistent throughout the City. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. In summation, project architect Juan Caycedo responded to a question concerning the landscape design. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information on comments made by Mr. Caycedo. Council Member O'Rourke asked Mr. Schaad to clarify a question Mr. Ounjian brought forward. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 01-2023. Council Members commented on the beauty of the building design . Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes. Regular Agenda 4 January 1o, 2023

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the procedures for approval of site plans, conditional uses, and conditional future land use map amendments and cond itional rezonings; amending Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," Article VI, "Conditional Land Use Amendments and Rezoning," Code of Ordinances, to (i) authorize amendments to approvals pursuant to the conditional future land use map amendment and rezoning approval procedures without reference to said procedures where the original approval has been fully implemented (except in cases which increase residential density), and (ii) clarify language and procedures, and delete obsolete provisions; amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article II , Division 2, "Site Plans," Code of Ordinances, to (i) authorize the City Manager to take administrative action on certain minor site plan amendments, as defined, and (ii) clarify language and procedures, and delete obsolete provisions; amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article II, Division 4, "Conditional Use Approval," Code of Ordinances, to (i) allow an amendment to a site plan associated with a conditional use to be amended without requiring an amendment to the conditional use where the site plan amendment will not result in a change of use (except to a permitted use in the zoning district, or a conditional use already approved by the City Council), an increase in density or intensity, a reduction in open space or previously required landscaping or a violation of any condition of the cond itional use approval, (ii) increase the time available for obtaining a building permit prior to expiration of a conditional use approval (from 18 to 24 months), and (iii) clarify language and procedures, and delete obsolete provisions; creating Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article I, Section 28-9, "Standard Application Processing Procedures," and Section 28-10, "Appeals," to provide a uniform method for the processing of applications for development approval and appeals of decisions in connection with such applications; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an codification; providing an effective date (AM-21-02) Director of Development Services Brandon Schaad gave the presentation. Mr. Schaad began with a background of the proposed changes, including the streamlining process. He reviewed the code rewrite, deletions, and updates to the code language. Mr. Schaad advised this is the most significant streamlining, major modernization, and the most significant progress in the ongoing land development code rewrite to date. This would also free up staff time to allow for more impactful and longer-term project development. Staff and the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval, Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for questions. Council Member Mayotte thanked staff for their effort and inquired if the proposed size of 50,000 square feet could be adjusted in the future if necessary. Ms. O'Rourke also thanked staff and asked about the 50,000 s.f. limitations. Discussion ensued with Mr. Schaad answering Members' questions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional insight. Council Member Drucker advised she was not comfortable with the 50,000 s.f. threshold and would not support approval of the Ordinance. Council Member Nachlas was also concerned over the 50,000 s.f. threshold and concurred with Ms. Drucker that 25,000 s.f. would be more manageable. Ms. Frieser clarified comments made by Council Members and reviewed the revisions and deletions of the proposal. Discussion ensued. Mr. Ahnell, Ms. Frieser, and Mr. Schaad answered questions related to the Council Members questions. Ms. Frieser provided clarification and reviewed the technical changes to the code rewrite. The public hearing was opened. Glenn Gromann complemented staff for the proposal and advised there are not many projects that would require Council approval in this size range, and he recommended staff approve the project. Jonathan Ounjian voiced his concern over the size of the proposal and the ability to add 50,000 s.f. to a property without Council's approval. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer, Ms. Frieser, and Mr. Schaad provided additional information in response to remarks made during public comment. The meeting was recessed at approximately 8: 15 pm and reconvened at approximately 8:42 pm. Regular Agenda 6 January 10, 2023 Upon returning from recess, Ms. Frieser and Mr. Schaad recapped the proposed changes and revisions. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas and seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte to approve the Ordinance with the revisions as presented. Additional discussion ensued. Mr. Schaad advised the 50,000 s.f. threshold was only for projects that meet every requirement with no technical deviations or no zoning changes. Motion passed on a vote of 4-1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Monice Mayotte, and Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, voting yes, Council Member Yvette Drucker voting no.

units.text: Council Member Fran Nachlas mentioned she and her family had taken a ride on Brightline and reminded the public to be cautious around the rail crossings and congratulated Council Member-elect Mark Wigder. Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke inquired about the beautification of the rear of a private building which is visible from the Brightline Station . Ms. O'Rourke stated she would like to be notified when development projects are in the planning stages. She stated the City Boards should meet with Council fo r the potential of provid ing tasks, direction, and meeting frequency. Discussion ensued and members weighed in. There was consensus for Citizen's Pedestrian & Bikeway Advisory Board, Community Advisory Panel, Library Board, Marine Advisory Board, Parks and Recreation Board, and Sustainability Board to provide a list of proposed tasks. She wished everyone a happy and healthy New Year. Council Member Yvette Drucker advised the first step to Vision Zero was passing the resolution. Next steps w ill include attaining grants and developing plans. Ms. Drucker provided additional information regarding the Florida League of Cities and Council Members involvement with the League. Council Member Monica Mayotte echoed Ms. Drucker's comments on the Florida League of Cities and commented on the meeting schedule of the advisory boards. Mayor Scott Singer congratulated Council Member elect Wigder. He highlighted City events and noted an upcoming education session by the Florida Department of Transportation for the new Glades Road Diverging Diamond Interchange at 1-95. units.text: Council Member Nachlas commented favorably on the Martin Luther King, Jr. Day celebration events and congratulated her daughter and son-in-law on the birth of their daughter, Harper. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke offered her congratulations to Ms. Nachlas and her family. Council Member Drucker reminded everyone of the Divergent Diamond Interchange (DOI) construction and road closings at Glades Rd. and 1-95. She also commented on a celebration of the Lunar New Year with an event partnered by Brightline Trains and Kapow Noodle Bar and stated that she hoped to see more of these partnerships in the Downtown. Council Member Mayotte noted the Brightline and Tri-Rail safety presentations at the last Workshop Meeting and noted how important it is for the public to be educated on train safety. She encouraged everyone to please pay attention when they are around the train tracks. Mayor Singer announced the Brandt Drive bridge scheduled reopening, the DOI opening at Glades Rd. and 1-95, and a lane changeover at the Palmetto Park Road/ El Rio bridge. He then highlighted the upcoming Boca Raton First Responder Expo at the Town Center Mall and the Boca Raton Free Shred Event at 6500 North Congress Avenue.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton establishing a Parking Meter Zone consisting of approximately two hundred forty (240) parking spaces within the parking lots generally located east of Boca Raton Boulevard, around the Downtown Library and north of 3rd Street; authorizing the City Manager to implement the Parking Meter Zone; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Manager Leif Ahnell gave a brief overview of the proposed parking meter zone at the Downtown Library. Council Member Yvette Drucker stated that the parking will be a free service for the library. Ms. O'Rourke asked how the metered zone will affect the library patrons. Discussion ensued. George Brown Deputy City Manager clarified comments made and responded to Members' questions. The public comment period was opened. Cyndi Bloom spoke on behalf of the Friends of the Boca Raton Library (Friends). Ms. Bloom remarked on the amount of funds that the Friends had raised for the library, stated that she is against the proposed parking meter zone and offered suggestions for an alternative solution. Patricia Moran, Board Member of the Friends, expressed her concerns about the implementation of a parking meter zone. Seeing no one else come forward , the public comment period was closed. Discussion ensued and Members providing additional ideas and Mr. Ahnell offered more information. Ms. Drucker clarified that the metered zone for the library would be a free service for the patrons. Ms. Mayotte stated that there are many free events at the library and was concerned about the availability of parking spaces. Ms. Nachlas suggested to log/ sign in with a library card to use the free parking . There was consensus to add signage and postpone the proposed meters to a later date. Motion was made by Council Member Andrea Levine O'Rourke, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to delete item 9. C., Resolution 20-2023. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 15.24 acre property generally located at 3320 Airport Road known as Premier Park: (i) an amended and restated site plan approval consolidating Master Plan Resolution No. 137-2013 (as amended by Resolution No. 99-2015), and Site Plan Resolution No. 139-2013 (as amended by Resolution No. 101-2015), and (ii) a site plan amendment to authorize, for Phase 2, the construction of a two (2)-story, 50,942 square foot retail (furniture store) and business/professional office building; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-13-06R2) The Mayor noted that the hearing on items on 10.A. and 10.B. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related , and a separate vote would be taken on each item. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Members disclosed their ex-parte discussions. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Development Services Planner Heather Hanson gave the presentation. She began by giving an overview of the Premier Park Master Plan. She described the proposed amendments and site plan changes. The Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services recommended approval as proposed. Upon concluding , Ms. Hansen made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. David Milledge spoke on behalf of the applicant and gave a brief presentation. Mr. Milledge shared aerial photos of the subject location, provided details about the existing property, and shared an overview of the proposed changes. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Jonathan Ounjian made comments concerning fair zoning for all areas of the City. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 17-2023. Deputy Mayor O'Rourke spoke in favor of the project. Mayor Singer provided final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Monica Mayotte, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 18-2023. units.text: Richard Carlson, representative of the Deerhurst Homeowners Association (HOA) provided a brief history of the subdivision and the common area landscaping. He explained to Council Members the difficulty of the homeowners to continue to maintain the irrigation, due to the failing of the existing well. He further stated that the HOA does not have the right to charge the owners for the maintenance of the well, and that it should not be their responsibility to maintain the common area landscaping. Phyliss Robinson stated that she was appalled over the loud vehicles racing up and down Palmetto Park Road and that it was affecting quality of life at outdoor dining establishments. Adam Galicki, President of the Deerhurst Homeowners Association, stated that he was concerned over the legal right of the owners to irrigate and maintain the common areas. Regular Agenda 3 February 28, 2023 Bruce Klarberg, from the Library Commons Homeowners Association, voiced his concern about a safety hazard on the Brightline Station train platform near the Library Commons property line. He stated that there was a dangerous opening at the end of the platform, and suggested a fence be installed. Jonathan Ounjian spoke about the disparity of the zoning for his office building compared to other areas throughout the City. In response to the request of the Deerhurst Homeowners Association, Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik provided a brief history and overview of the area and noted he had spoken with the members of the Deerhurst community. Mr. Lukasik explained the City's history of not maintaining common areas and rights-of-way irrigation. He further stated the City had offered alternative solutions and was willing to help the community by locating a new well or provide a water meter. Discussion ensued. City Attorney Diana Grubb Frieser provided additional insight. Regarding the concern about loud and speeding vehicles, Deputy City Manager George Brown advised that the City had been proactive when dealing with speeding vehicles and described several actions the City was taking. Deputy Mayor Andrea Levine O'Rourke mentioned that the City had taken steps to alleviate the noise issue, urged the citizens to continue to be diligent and thanked the public for making the effort to report their concerns. Mr. Brown then addressed the issue about the train station platform, and advised that Brightline will erect a fence at the property line and would continue to add landscaping. Council Member Monica Mayotte mentioned a drainage issue and wanted to know if it was tied to the same issue.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Code of Ordinances, to expand the uses required to provide electric vehicle parking spaces (from multifamily residential, commercial and industrial uses, to multifamily residential and all non-residential uses) and increase the number of electric vehicle parking spaces required for such uses (from 2% to 5% of the total required off-street parking spaces), decrease the development threshold at which the requirements for electric vehicle parking spaces are imposed (from 50 total parking spaces to 20 total parking spaces) , provide definitions for "EV-capable," "EV-ready" and "EV-installed" parking spaces, and add requirements for such spaces; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-07) Sustainability Manager Lindsey Nieratka gave the presentation. Ms. Nieratka began with a summary of the current regulations and proposed changes to expand the requirements of electric vehicle parking. She showed slides describing the background and purpose of the ordinance and noted that Boca Raton has a higher-than-average ownership rate of electric vehicles. Upon concluding, Ms. Nieratka responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Ounjian asked if this proposed change would affect alterations of properties and not just new development. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Members discussed the question raised by Mr. Ounjian and Mayor Singer proposed amended language. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser and City Manager Leif Ahnell offered insight and additional information. Ms. Frieser suggested tabling the topic until a later date in order to provide time for staff to conduct additional research. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to continue Ordinance No. 5644 to the meeting ofApril 25, 2023. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.header: Comments by Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Fran Nachlas, and Council Member
units.text: Marc Wigder Mayor Singer welcomed Mr. Wigder to the dais and commented on the attributes and assets of the City. He noted he was looking forward to the journey ahead and thanked his colleagues, city staff, community leaders, family, and friends. Council Member Fran Nachlas shared that she was grateful to be able to serve the City and was excited to begin her first term. She thanked everyone for their support including her family, campaign team, colleagues, and residents. Council Member Wigder thanked Ms. O'Rourke for her contributions and service to the City and, in recognition of her service in Seat B, he personally presented her with a Queen B award. He then commented that he was looking forward to serving the City and thanked his family, friends, campaign and business teams, and his new colleagues. Mr. Wigder also discussed several of his priorities, which included maintaining fiscal discipline, City management succession and civic center planning, continuing to improve downtown connectivity and vibrancy and creating opportunities for local housing affordability and sustainable growth. He gave a final shout out to the F AU Owls. Mayor Singer thanked his campaign team, his late parents, extended family, and residents who supported him.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton denouncing and condemning racism and bigotry in all of its forms, including an alarming rise in antisemitism; adopting the non-legally binding International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance working definition of antisemitism; denouncing and condemning hate speech; affirming the City's commitment to protect the rights and safety of all residents in the City; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Regular Agenda 4 A pril 11 , 2023 Mayor Singer explained that jurisdictions around the country were adopting similar measures and that the proposed resolution, while decrying bigotry of all forms, focused on antisemitism due to the increase in number of antisemitic incidents that had occurred both locally and nationally. Council Member Wigder noted the recent passing of Ben Ferencz, the last Nuremberg prosecutor, and all Members thanked the Mayor for bringing forward the resolution and expressed their support. The public hearing was opened. Lisa Beers, President of the American Jewish Committee Palm Beach County Board of Directors, thanked the City for their consideration of the resolution and spoke in support of its adoption. Albert Cacace expressed his approval. Jonathan Ounjian also shared his support of the resolution. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 34-2023. Mayor Singer responded to public comments and advised that while there were no penalties associated with the resolution, he believed it still held great importance. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Wigder gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. He began by noting the growth of the City and the diversity of local businesses. Mr. Wigder cited a travel guide's list of top activities and hotels within the City. He remarked on the hybridization of the workforce that had evolved over the past few years and emphasized a number of benefits that Boca Raton offered to workers, including the quality of life, local office options that facilitated collaborations and many local options for socializing. Tables were shown that displayed migration and relocation trends, highlighting the much larger number of those moving to Boca Raton as opposed to those leaving. Mr. Wigder reiterated the tremendous opportunities the City provides for both corporate and individual entities and the need for us to communicate our City's strengths. He encouraged residents to get involved and tell their Boca Story and concluded by reminding all that the celebration for the FAU Men's Basketball Team had been moved to April 19th. Council Member Drucker remarked on her recent visit to Tallahassee in support of Home Rule and advised that she would give a comprehensive update when the current legislative session concluded. Deputy Mayor Mayotte advised that filmmaker Rory Fielding, producer of the film Troubled Waters, had another movie on the subject of how plastics affect human health. Ms. Mayotte also highlighted the Great American Clean Up taking place at South Beach Park. Council Member Nachlas welcomed Council Member Wigder and thanked him for his presentation. Ms. Nachlas inquired about an update on reports by the advisory boards and noted that there was a bust of Ben Ferencz by artist Yaacov Heller available for viewing in the Royal Palm Shopping Plaza. Regular Agenda 5 April 11, 2023 Ms. Drucker shared additional event details about the Great American Clean Up. Mayor Singer commented on the boards and suggested Members think about the direction, goals, and specific tasks that they would like to assign to each board. He concluded by noting the upcoming celebration for the FAU Owls Men's Basketball team at the Mizner Park Amphitheater.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement with the Gumbo Limbo Coastal Stewards, Inc. regarding the operation and management of sea turtle rescue, rehabilitation, research, and release activities at the Gumbo limbo Nature Center; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Council Member Wigder left the dais. Assistant City Manager Chrissy Gibson gave the presentation . She provided a brief background of the Gumbo Limbo Nature Center, the purpose, and terms of the agreement. Upon concluding Ms. Gibson made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Manju Pendakur voiced his appreciation for the agreement between the City and the Coastal Stewards and supports its approval. Robyn Marigerate expressed her support of the agreement and gave a brief overview of her time spent as a volunteer. Sheila Reinken Regular Agenda 3 April 25, 2023 spoke in favor of the agreement. Executive Director of the Coastal Stewards John Holloway thanked his team and commented favorably on the agreement between the Coastal Stewards and the City. Roy Fielding shared his support of the agreement and highlighted a film he produced that would help fund the Coastal Stewards. Janixx Parisi spoke against the firing of the employees, shared her concern for the turtles, and her opposition to the agreement. Willi Harreys, a volunteer at Gumbo Limbo, relayed his concern for the turtles and the issuance of the permit. Beverly Knight stated that she did not support the agreement. Mary Craumer also spoke against the agreement. Seeing no one else come forward the public hearing was closed. Assistant City Manager Chrissy Gibson provided additional insight from questions raised during the public comment period and responded to Members' questions. John Holloway offered additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 42-2023. Motion passed 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

Manju Pendakur voiced his appreciation for the agreement between the City and the Coastal Stewards and supports its approval. Robyn Marigerate expressed her support of the agreement and gave a brief overview of her time spent as a volunteer. Sheila Reinken Regular Agenda 3 April 25, 2023 spoke in favor of the agreement. Executive Director of the Coastal Stewards John Holloway thanked his team and commented favorably on the agreement between the Coastal Stewards and the City. Roy Fielding shared his support of the agreement and highlighted a film he produced that would help fund the Coastal Stewards. Janixx Parisi spoke against the firing of the employees, shared her concern for the turtles, and her opposition to the agreement. Willi Harreys, a volunteer at Gumbo Limbo, relayed his concern for the turtles and the issuance of the permit. Beverly Knight stated that she did not support the agreement. Mary Craumer also spoke against the agreement. Seeing no one else come forward the public hearing was closed. Assistant City Manager Chrissy Gibson provided additional insight from questions raised during the public comment period and responded to Members' questions. John Holloway offered additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 42-2023. Motion passed 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning, " Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Code of Ordinances, to expand the uses required to provide electric vehicle parking spaces (from multifamily residential, commercial and industrial uses, to multifamily residential and all non-residential uses) and increase the number of electric vehicle parking spaces required for such uses (from 2% to 5% of the total required off-street parking spaces), decrease the development threshold at which the requirements for electric vehicle parking spaces are imposed (from 50 total parking spaces to 20 total parking spaces), provide definitions for "EV-capable," "EV-ready" and "EV-installed" parking spaces, and add requirements for such spaces; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-07) Sustainability Manager Lindsay Nieratka gave a presentation. She provided a summary of the amendments to the Code of Ordinances. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional insight to the requirements for modifying a property or change of use and bringing the EV requirements up to code. He continued by providing examples of recently constructed properties which are compliant with the proposed ordinance. Discussion ensued. Council Member Marc Wigder raised concerns over the change of use for a property and the types of electrical services that may be required for various types of vehicles and the related costs. City Manager Leif Ahnell and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information. Council Member Fran Nachlas discussed the costs involved with the retro fitting of properties and asked for language to be added to clarify that a request for change of use, without additional parking requirements, would not trigger Ordinance No. 5644 on existing buildings. Council Member Yvette Drucker agreed with the new EV construction but had concerns over the retrofitting for EV spaces. Further discussion ensued . The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Ounjian presented slides and spoke against the EV parking requirements. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte spoke in favor of EV parking requirements. Discussion ensued. Brandon Schaad and Lindsay Nieratka responded to Members' comments and provided additional information. Regular Agenda 4 April 25, 2023 Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5644. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, and Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Kathrin Walsh, for a settlement and reduction of one (1) code enforcement lien imposed against property located at 1356 Cypress Way; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Code Enforcement Manager Doug Sheedy gave a brief overview of the code case and lien reduction request. Council Member Marc Wigder stated that he was in favor of a reduction. Attorney for the owner presented reasons why the lien should be reduced or removed. Homeowner Kathrin Walsh briefly described her situation that led to the fines. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder to reduce the fine to $5,000. Motion failed for a lack of a second. Members weighed in and a consensus was reached to reduce the fine by $5,000. Motion was amended by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to reduce the fine by $5,000 to $24, 115 and to make payment in full within 60 days. Members made additional comments and Ms. Frieser clarified the motion. Motion passed 4 votes to 1; Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, and Mayor Scott Singer voting no. units.text: Mayor Singer highlighted the need for proactive communication and internal collaboration. He noted staffing level issues and the volume of public inquiries and concluded by stating that he was appreciative of the work that was being done. Council Member Marc Wigder stated that he appreciated Mr. Ahnell answering his questions and the time the City Manager had spent advising him on various issues and providing historical context. Council Member Yvette Drucker thanked Mr. Ahnell for responding to her requests. She advised that she desired to have better communication with administrative staff and noted the need for additional staffing on the third floor. Ms. Drucker also noted the time required to settle expense reports. Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte agreed with prior comments made and stated that she appreciated Mr. Ahnell's dedication and financial acumen . She highlighted that communications could be enhanced . Ms. Mayotte suggested additional ideas for improvement such as collaboration with community partners and better implementation of complicated projects. She further stated that the politics of issues should be left to the Council Members and not the staff. Council Member Fran Nachlas complimented her interactions with Mr. Ahnell and agreed with other comments made. She highlighted the need for proactive communication and staffing levels on the third floor. Mayor Singer made final comments. Regular Agenda 4 May 9, 2023

units.text: Mayor Singer reiterated the importance of communications and stated that he would like to be aware of high profile matters. Deputy Mayor Mayotte agreed that communication could be improved and looked forward to working together in a more proactive way. She mentioned that the legal review needed to be involved earlier in the development process. She concluded by stating we need to be good stewards of taxpayer funds. Council Member Nachlas thanked the City Attorney for taking the time to work with her and agreed that legal should be involved in City processes earlier. Council Member Wigder thanked Ms. Frieser for all she had done and stated that there was always room for improvement, noting areas of promptness, collaboration, and earlier engagement. Council Member Drucker thanked Ms. Frieser for the help she provided and how she accommodated Ms. Drucker's schedule. Mayor Singer made final comments. Council Member Wigder began his report by noting that the City had completed an RFP for an outside consulting firm to find a new City Manager. Mr. Wigder complimented Deputy City Manager George Brown, noting his more than 40 years of service, and stated that he should be appointed as the next City Manager. Mr. Wigder then made a motion to promote Deputy City Manager George Brown as the next City Manager, seconded by Ms. Mayotte. Discussion ensued. Members spoke favorably of Mr. Brown and discussed the timing and transition process. The City Attorney requested clarification and advised that an agreement could be drafted. Discussion ensued regarding the transition of other executive level positions. Additional comments were made for the succession of Mr. Brown to City Manager. Mr. Brown stated that he agrees with accepting the position only when Mr. Ahnell was ready to retire. Ms. Frieser advised that the motion should be withdrawn , and she would provide additional information at the next meeting. It was not withdrawn; Mayor Singer made a motion to lay the current motion on the table, seconded by Council Member Drucker. The motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Mr. Wigder continued with his report and advised that he is happy that there will be continuity and urged that he was looking forward to Strategic Planning . Council Member Drucker shared that she was also looking forward to the Strategic Planning Session . Deputy Mayor Mayotte reiterated comments made, noted this would be her last Strategic Planning session and asked the City Manager for a copy of the PMD matrix. Council Member Nachlas expressed her eagerness for the upcoming Strategic Planning. Ms. Nachlas mentioned while she was bike riding, she witnessed a cyclist who had been struck by a car and highlighted the need for Vision Zero and the safety for our pedestrians and cyclists. She continued by congratulating the FAU Sandy Owls women's beach volleyball team on reaching the NCAA Championships and concluded by highlighting National Nurses' Week. Mayor Singer also congratulated FAU women's volleyball team. He then noted that Deputy City Manager George Brown, Council Member Yvette Drucker, and he had been awarded the Home Rule Hero award for their efforts during the 2023 Legislative Session. The Mayor turned the discussion to the upcoming Strategic Planning Sessions, noting the goals and priorities focused on in the past. He expressed his desire to keep the discussions focused on high level strategies rather. Council Member Drucker commented on Vision Zero, the importance of creating an action plan, and the need for staff specifically dedicated to mobility and complete streets. Members reviewed topics for the upcoming Planning Sessions. Regular Agenda 5 May 9, 2023

units.text: The City Attorney gave a brief overview of the steps to be followed for the succession of George Brown to the position of City Manager. Council Member Marc Wigder stated that he did not agree with the steps set forth in the City Attorney' s memorandum and advised that he would make a motion to pull the tabled motion from the previous meeting. Mr. Wigder explained that he believed the Mayor should be authorized to handle negotiations, as discussed in the previous meeting, expressed concern regarding delegation to the City Attorney and Human Resources Director, and noted that the Charter allows for special counsel to be hired to assist with the matter. Mayor Singer expressed concerns about a delegation of authority allowing him to handle negotiations as there may be Sunshine Law ramifications. The City Attorney confirmed that the Sunshine Law might be implicated and noted that her memorandum did not include delegation to the City Attorney or the Human Resources Director. Ms. Frieser provided information regarding the potential Sunshine Law impact( when there is a delegation to one member of an elected body, negotiations resulting from that delegation must occur within a noticed forum). She also RegularAgenda 6 May 23, 2023 explained that the Human Resources Department would conduct a salary compensation survey. Mr. Wigder advised that, as the HR Director works for the current City Manager, he believed that presented a conflict and he reiterated that the City Council, by Charter, hires the City Manager. Discussion ensued. The Mayor indicated that all Members were free to talk to Mr. Brown regarding terms of the contract. Deputy City Manager George Brown advised that salary data is easily obtained and that he felt HR was capable of compiling the information, that he was comfortable working with the City Attorney on the terms of the agreement and did not believe outside counsel should be retained, and that the City Council would make the final decision. Mayor Singer reviewed the points on which consensus appeared to be reached after the discussion. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to proceed with negotiations to hire George Brown as the next City Manager, HR will compile the data and circulate it, Council Members would have discussions as necessary, and the City Attorney and Mr. Brown would negotiate the terms of the contract form to be brought to Members for review, advice, consent, and approval when ready. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 2.03-acre property, located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard and 91 O East Palmetto Park Road, an amendment to Exhibit "1" (setting forth the site plan) of a Universal Conditional (UC) Future Land Use Map Amendment (Ordinance No. 5413) to increase the square footage of the 70-unit multifamily residential project, increase the number of parking spaces provided, revise the approved landscape plan and architectural elevations, make related site modifications, and remove a previously approved technical deviation from Section 23-190(J), Code of Ordinances, for the reduction in inbound reservoir distance to a gated entrance, together with the addition of a technical deviation from Section 23-190, Code of Ordinances, to eliminate a required turnaround in advance of a gated entry to a residential development; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06R 1/SC) 1. Resolution No. 54-2023 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.5 acre property located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard, 155 South Ocean Boulevard, and 910 East Palmetto Park Road, an amendment to an approved Universal Conditional (UC) Site Plan (Resolution No. 119-2017) to increase the square footage of the 70-unit multifamily residential project, increase the number of parking spaces provided, revise the approved landscape plan and architectural elevations, make related site modifications, and remove a previously approved technical deviation from Section 23-190(J), Code of Ordinances, for the reduction in inbound reservoir distance to a gated entrance together with the addition of a technical deviation from Section 23-190, Code of Ordinances, to eliminate a required turnaround in advance of a gated entry to a residential development; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06R1/SPA) 2. Resolution No. 55-2023 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 3.5 acre property located at 1 South Ocean Boulevard, 155 South Ocean Boulevard, and 910 East Palmetto Park Road, a variance from Section 28-676(2), Code of Ordinances, to allow a driveway within the first 25 feet of a required yard abutting a street right-of-way Regular Agenda 3 June 13, 2023 (Southeast Wavecrest Way), a portion ofwhich is parallel to the front plot line (adjoining Southeast Wavecrest Way), where the code requires driveways within the first 25 feet of a required yard abutting a street right-of-way to be generally perpendicular to the front plot line, in the Multifamily Residential (R-5-A) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-16-06R1NA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A., 10.A.1., and 10.A.2. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures as required for items 10.A. 1. and 1O.A.2. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.A. not be adopted, items 10.A.1. and 10.A.2. would not be considered. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Chief Planner Tamashbeen Rahman gave the PowerPoint presentation. She provided a brief history of the project and outlined components of the requested amendment. The requested modifications, technical deviations, and driveway variance were reviewed. Renderings of the proposed building and traffic impacts were also discussed. The Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval of the application and staff recommended approval with a proposed recommendation of approval regarding the hours of operation of pool amenity areas. Upon concluding, Ms. Rahman made herself available for Members' questions. Discussion ensued and Traffic Engineer Naresh Machavarapu provided additional information regarding traffic and mobility concerns. The public hearing was opened. Attorney Bonnie Miskel, on behalf of the applicant, gave a presentation. Ms. Miskel reviewed the project history and the requested modifications and variance. She reviewed modifications to the original site plan and explained the proposed circulation plan through the property. Upon concluding, Ms. Miskel responded to Members' questions. Discussion ensued . On behalf of the applicant, Juan Pablo Alfonso and architect Roger Grave de Peralta provided additional information. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad added clarification regarding drainage requirements. Keith Nelson, of the Riviera Civic Association (RCA), spoke against the pool bar and asked for a stipulation that the bar not be staffed. Kevin Meaney stated that he was in favor of the proposed changes. Cynthia Wohl inquired how the berm would retain or defuse a flooding situation and asked if the residents could be advised to be considerate of the single-family homes along Wavecrest Way. Glenn Gromann spoke in favor of the project and encouraged Members' approval. Katy McDougal advised that members of the RCA were not against the proposed pool but were opposed to the commercial operation of the bar area. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. There was no cross examination. Ms. Miskel offered final comments on behalf of the applicant and responded to additional questions from Council Members. Further discussion ensued regarding the use of the proposed pool area. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5650. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser and Mr. Schaad provided additional clarification. At the Mayor's request, Ms. Frieser read into the record a proposed condition which prohibited amplified sound in the outside areas between 8pm and 8am. Ms. Frieser and Mr. Schaad then confirmed that the restricted hours for the pool amenities area would replace condition number 10 and the condition regarding amplified noise would become condition number 11. Ms. Frieser noted that the conditions would apply to both Ordinance No. 5650 and Resolution No. 54-2023. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to amend the motion on the floor to include conditions 10 and 11. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion to approve Ordinance No. 5650 as amended carried unanimously: Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Regular Agenda 4 June 13, 2023 Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 54-2023 as amended, including conditions 10 and 11. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 55-2023. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton naming the Community Garden at Meadows Park in honor of Susan Whelchel, former Council Member and Mayor of the City of Boca Raton, to commemorate her years of dedicated service to the City; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Council Member Yvette Drucker gave the presentation and highlighted former Mayor Susan Whelchel's dedication to the City of Boca Raton. Members expressed their gratitude for the impact of Ms. Whelchel's years of service to the community and shared their support for the renaming of the Garden in her honor. The public hearing was opened. Jamie Sauer, on behalf of the Junior League, thanked Council Member Drucker and Mayor Singer for bringing forward the resolution and extended her appreciation to the entire Council for the recognition of the former Mayor. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 59-2023. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

Mr. Wigder shared some of the topics that were covered and expressed his gratitude for the opportunity to attend. Council Member Drucker thanked members of the Junior League for attending the meeting and wished everyone a safe summer. Mayor Singer highlighted upcoming City events and wished everyone a safe summer.

Council Member Nachlas requested that the consideration of Ordinance No. 5652 be postponed until after the August 21 st Joint Meeting with the Beach and Park District. City Manager Leif Ahnell provided additional information. Council Members weighed in and discussion ensued. Members agreed to postpone the public hearing of the ordinance until after the Joint Meeting. Council Member Wigder gave a brief presentation on the Institute for Elected Officials he attended that was hosted by the Florida League of Cities. Mr. Wigder shared some of the topics that were covered and expressed his gratitude for the opportunity to attend. Council Member Drucker thanked members of the Junior League for attending the meeting and wished everyone a safe summer. Mayor Singer highlighted upcoming City events and wished everyone a safe summer.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 80.8 acre Saint Andrew's School property generally located at 3900 Jog Road, an amendment to Resolution No. 123-2011 (as amended by Resolution Nos. 65-2013, 31-2016, and 155-2018), to grant conditional use approval for the following school uses in the R-1-A Single Family Residential zoning district: (i) replacement of Rooks Hall, an existing two (2)-story, 19,380 square foot high school building with a two (2)-story, 26,274 square foot, high school building; and (ii) re­ approval of eight (8) previously approved buildings, totaling approximately 19,159 square feet, and 62 parking spaces that were never constructed (which improvements will be located at the same site and remain the same size as previously approved); and grant conditional use approval for five (5) of the aforementioned non-residential buildings (the new Rooks Hall, the Indoor Squash, the Surprenant Hall addition , the Learning Lab, and the Clock/Stair Tower) to exceed 25 feet in height; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-07-01 R5/CA) 1. Resolution No. 47-2023 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 80.8 acre Saint Andrew's School property generally located at 3900 Jog Road: (i) an amended and restated site plan consolidating portions of City Council Resolution Nos. 173-98, 41-2002, and 156-2018, and Planning and Zoning Board Resolution Nos. 07-16, 11-11 , 13-10, and 2016-004 ; and (ii) a site plan amendment to authorize replacement of Rooks Hall, an existing 19,380 square foot, high school building with a 26 ,274 square foot, high school building ; and re-approval of eight (8) previously approved buildings, totaling approximately 19,159 square feet, and 62 parking spaces that were never constructed (which improvements will be located at the same site and remain the same size as previously approved); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-07-01 R5/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and 10.A. 1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related , and pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures as required for item 10.A.1 . He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.A. not be adopted, item 10.A.1 . would not be considered. The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearing. Council Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner for Development Services, gave the presentation. She provided a brief history of the property and discussed the applicant's request. The proposed master site plan was displayed, and public notice dates and staff analysis were provided. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. The public hearing was opened. Brian Schmier, Board of Trustees member for St. Andrew's School, gave a brief overview and made himself available for Members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 46-2023. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Regular Agenda 5 J uly 25, 2023 Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 47-2023. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing procedures and regulations to implement Section 166.04151 (7), Florida Statutes, as created by Chapter 2023-17, Laws of Florida (Live Local Act of 2023) for development of statutorily authorized mixed-use residential development (including affordable housing); noting the business and commercial, industrial, and miscellaneous zoning districts in which the mixed-use directive is applicable; providing land development regulations (including those generally applicable in multifamily zoning districts and providing an administrative approval process); noting the statutorily mandated maximums for density and height; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-23-07) Acting City Manager George Brown gave the presentation. He began with a brief review of the Live Local Act and the proposed Ordinance No. 5653, noting that the intent of the ordinance was to comply with the Live Local Act by updating the Zoning and Development processes. He further advised that 65 percent of the total square footage must be residential. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval as revised. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown made himself available for Members' questions. Discussion ensued and Mr. Brown responded to Members' comments and questions. Council Member Marc Wigder proposed an amendment that the Floor Area Ratio (FAR.) be proportional to the new required density. Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte agreed with Mr. Wigder's proposed amendment and asked if the City had any FAR. limits. Council Member Yvette Drucker shared her concern that the City was preempting the State's Live Local Act. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information and answered Members' questions. The public hearing was opened . Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of affordable housing and advised that the density in the downtown should also apply to the new Live Local Act, and this proposed ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Further discussion ensued. Ms. Frieser clarified comments made and provided additional information regarding the FAR. , density, and confirmed that the proposed ordinance was in accordance with the Live Local Act. Members proposed that staff investigate what actions other cities were taking and conduct additional research regarding the nonresidential uses and the location of those uses, the distribution percentages, the FAR. requirement as a limitation, and options to incentivize for bonus affordable units beyond the requirement. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to postpone Ordinance No. 5653. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The meeting was recessed at 8:27PM and resumed at approximately 8:37PM.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Land Use Element Policies LU.1.1.5, LU .1.1.6 and LU.1.1 .10 to create the Enhanced Mobility (EM) Future Land Use category and establish a description and maximum density and intensity for such category; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-01) Regular Agenda 6 July 25, 2023 1. Ordinance No. 5655 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article XVII, "Planned Development," Code of Ordinances, to create a new Division 9, "Enhanced Mobility Development," and , among other things, provide development parameters for such development, and establish procedures and standards for applications, reviews and approvals; amending Chapter 28, Article XII, "Industrial Districts," Division 2, "LIRP Light Industrial Research Park," to create a new Section 28-987, "Enhanced Mobility Development (EMO)," to authorize enhanced mobility development projects within a specified geographic area of the LIRP zoning district located in the vicinity of the Yamato Tri-Rail Station, and, among other things, introduce new EMO uses, provide for increased intensity, and provide for a maximum density; amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article VIII, Section 28-307(1), Code of Ordinances, to establish the building intensity for EMO uses in the LIRP zoning district; deleting obsolete references to LIRP- 2.5 and LIRP-5; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-01) Mayor Singer noted that the hearings on Ordinance Nos. 5654 and 5655 would be held contemporaneously and that this was a transmittal hearing. He noted that this would be the first of two public hearings, and that three votes would be required to transmit Ordinance No. 5654. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the presentation. He began with the background of the subject property and the proposed ordinances. Mr. Schaad discussed the revisions that had been made since the agenda publication, which included geographic eligibility, building massing model, and clarified design standards. He continued by discussing a potential closure of the Yamato Tri-Rail Station, status of existing buildings, and code enforcement where violations impact compliance of the Enhanced Mobility District (EMO). He further advised that there were two areas of disagreement between the City and the applicant: platting requirements and the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for a building without completing all construction in an approved development sequence. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued. Mayor Singer asked if the disagreements could be worked out after the ordinance is approved. The public hearing was opened. Attorney Bonnie Miske! spoke on behalf of the applicant. Ms. Miskel presented her client's concerns regarding the platting, certificate of occupancy (CO), and permitting requirement issues. Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of equal zoning for all districts in the City. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Further discussion ensued. Mr. Schaad clarified comments made and offered additional information relating to the platting and the CO process. Ms. Frieser provided additional information. Mr. Wigder agreed with the platting requirements as proposed by staff and Ms. Miskel agreed that the CO requirements were a non-issue but that additional platting requirements are not necessary. Ms. Nachlas advised that her concern was ensuring the applicant delivers as promised. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to transmit Ordinance No. 5654 as revised. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.
