units.text: MINUTES OF THE JOINT MEETING CITY OF BOCA RATON CITY COUNCIL and GREATER BOCA RATON BEACH & PARK DISTRICT COMMISSIONERS 6500 Building Auditorium Monday, August 21 , 2023 , 6:30 PM Participants: City Council: Greater Boca Raton Beach & Park District: Mayor Scott Singer Commissioner Erin Wright, Chair Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte Commissioner Steve Engel Council Member Yvette Drucker Commissioner Craig Ehrnst Council Member Andrea Fran Nachlas Commissioner Robert K. Rollins, Jr Council Member Marc Wigder Commissioner Susan Vogelgesang Acting City Manager George Brown Executive Director Briann Harms City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser District Counsel Jacob Horowitz I. Welcome - Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Erin Wright The meeting was called to order at 6:35 pm. Mayor Scott Singer and Chair Erin Wright made opening comments and members introduced themselves. II. Discussion Topics Chair Wright asked to move item I1.E., Patch Reef Park Playground Renovations, to be considered first. There was consensus from all Members to do so. E. Patch Reef Park Playground Renovations Chair Erin Wright asked that the permitting process for this renovation be expedited and that all fees be consolidated for payment at the end of the project. Acting City Manager George Brown advised that City staff would accelerate the playground renovation and confirmed that the fees could be payable at the end . Commissioner Rollins provided additional information regarding the urgency of the request, citing health issues of a local child with special needs. A. Parks and Recreation Master Planning Executive Director Briann Harms noted that she had discussed this topic with Mr. Brown and expressed the desire of the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District (District) to collaborate with the City on where to put recreation facilities so as to make the best use of their resources. Mr. Brown confirmed that he had spoken with Ms. Harms on this subject and agreed that staff of both entities could work together to present a plan to the bodies that would meet current and future recreation needs. Members weighed in and Mr. Brown stated that staff would work on creating a timeframe for the plan. B. North Park Project (Boca Teeca) Update Ms. Wright showed renderings of the conceptual design for the Boca Teeca golf course property, now known as the North Park Project, and reviewed components of the proposal for the southeast and northeast quadrants of the property. Mayor Scott Singer noted that the plans to connect the east and west portions of Jeffery Street were still in process. Liudmila Fuentes, representing consultant Miller Legg, advised that she was aware of the plans for Jeffery Street and was consulting with City staff. Ms. Fuentes then responded to questions and provided additional details regarding the drawings shown. Council Member Marc Wigder inquired about the western portion of the property. Ms. Wright and District Counsel Jacob Horowitz outlined the limits of development on land subject to the bonds, and Ms. Harms stated that 2026 was the earliest the bonds could be paid off without a penalty. Mr. Wigder then asked if there had been consideration given to the City taking over development of the western portion of the property, and Ms. Wright advised that District Commissioners had not had conversations on that topic. Discussion ensued between Council and Commissioners regarding elements of the proposed design , including bike trails, the possibility of a Jeffery Street tunnel, and improved mobility and walkability. There was consensus from Council Members to approve the conceptual plan presented. C. CRA Chair Wright read a statement into the record regarding the District's position on the proposed extension of the CRA and their request for an exemption from the annual tax increment financing (TIF) payments. Mr. Brown then summarized the request for District residents to use the downtown Community Center and advised that an analysis of the impact to City residents had not yet been performed , but that staff could collect the data. Discussion ensued regarding the extension of the TIF, City resident rates compared to those in the district, and the 1986 interlocal agreement between the two bodies. D. Children's Museum Relocation Options Mr. Brown opened the discussion by explaining that the City was exploring the feasibility and relocation options for the Children's Museum in order to incorporate its current location as part of the future government campus. He shared that City staff had discussed with District staff the possibility of relocating the building to Sugar Sand Park, and should that occur, the District's desire for the City to handle operations of the Museum. Conversation followed on a number of topics, including the timeline of the proposed project, the impact on the environment, and other City recreational amenities that might be affected . Ill. Public Comment The floor was opened for public comment. Robert Dukate, on behalf of the Boca Raton Bicycle Club, read a resolution prepared by the Bicycle Club into the record regarding bicycle safety. Raul Travieso thanked Council and District Commissioners for their support of the pickleball playing community and complimented the steps taken to incorporate the sport into City parks. Cil Ciliberti asked that City plans for development of the Golf and Racquet Club be shared with the District. Angelo Sands commented on off-course golf services and expressed his opposition to private groups being involved in the development of the North Park project. Garth Duff-Gray , representing the Boca Raton Junior Rugby Club, thanked the City and District for their support. Harold Chaffee voiced his support for a recreation master plan, a needs assessment, the connectivity of City parks, and expressed concern regarding the safety for pedestrians on the Clint Moore bridge. Veronica Quintero lobbied for more open space for the game of ultimate frisbee. Betsy Caceres highlighted Hispan ic heritage month and requested spaces for programming for the Hispanic community. Peter Sachs spoke in support of his client, one of the applicants to develop a sports/racquet facility on the north portion of the North Park project. John Holloway, President and CEO of Coastal Stewards, shared that the organization was moving forward with the Gumbo Limbo gift shop, the sea turtle educational permit, and the turtle rehabilitation permit. Mary Sol Gonzalez expressed her support for saving the Children's Museum. Jamie Godino requested performance space for the theater that he represented. Council Members and District Commissioners made final comments and thanked all those in attendance for their participation. There was consensus to schedule the next Joint Meeting in six months. The meeting was adjourned without objection at approximately 8:21 pm. ATTEST: MarySidons,?y e-:s

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing procedures and regulations to implement Section 166.04151 (7), Florida Statutes, as created by Chapter 2023-17, Laws of Florida (Live Local Act of 2023) for development of statutorily authorized mixed-use residential development (including affordable housing); noting the business and commercial, industrial, and miscellaneous zoning districts in which the mixed-use directive is applicable; providing land development regulations (including those generally applicable in multifamily zoning districts and providing an administrative approval process); noting the statutorily mandated maximums for density and height; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-23-07) Acting City Manager George Brown briefly reviewed the previous meeting and introduced Development Services Director Brandon Schaad who gave the presentation. Council Members discussed the order of presentation for related items on the agenda and discussion ensued. Mr. Schaad described the changes worked into the proportionality requirement that would provide more flexibility to developers and advised that the floor area ratio (FAR) was not included in this ordinance. Deputy Mayor Mayotte read a portion of a memo from the City Attorney which provided an analysis of the 10% and 40% regulations, and asked if we needed to restate what was already in code. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarification of the information from her memo and, at the request of Council Member Fran Nachlas, explained the statutory provision called the Bert Harris Act. Council Member Wigder noted that the Live Local Act would eventually sunset, and asked if the proposed ordinance would accordingly be sunset in tandem. Ms. Frieser agreed that it would be prudent to add it to the City's ordinance. Council Member Drucker explained her hesitancy to add more regulations to the City code if it wasn't necessary. Regular Agenda 4 August 22, 2023 The public hearing was opened. Michael Marshall explained his thoughts for wanting to exclude the floor area ratio (FAR) component from the ordinance. In response to questions from Council Member Nachlas, he provided clarification of his remarks. Ms. Frieser then referred to City code and provided her thoughts on Mr. Marshall's comments. Bonnie Miske! shared a brief PowerPoint presentation and offered her interpretation of the Live Local Act's rules compared to the ordinance being proposed. Lon Tabatchnick spoke against the FAR limit in the ordinance as it restricts the number of units that can be built. Glenn Gromann expressed his opposition to the restrictions in the proposal and shared his opinion that no builder would want to create a development that met the 40% restrictions. Seeing no one else come forward, public comment was closed. Mr. Brown advised Members that staff would need time to research and redraft the ordinance, and if it was the Council's decision not to adopt the 40% ordinance, then he suggested the applicable multi­ family regulations be drafted into an administrative memorandum to provide direction to staff should an application be received. Mr. Singer and Ms. Nachlas indicated their desire to draft some kind of regulation. Mr. Wigder, Ms. Mayotte, and Ms. Drucker suggested that staff study the issue further. Ms. Mayotte asked for staff to research how municipalities are handling applications based on the 40% projects if they do not have an ordinance addressing it. Additional discussion ensued. There was consensus from Members to postpone the item until a later date when staff could provide further clarity. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to continue Ordinance No. 5653 to the September 27, 2023, City Council Meeting. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes; Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget through the Third Budget Amendment; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mr. Brown gave a brief overview of the ordinance and made himself available for Members' questions, noting that it was not expected that the funds would be expended this fiscal year. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5656. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Land Use Element Policy LU.1.1.5 to increase the maximum floor area ratio (FAR), from 0.6 to 0.85, for office uses on certain parcels in the Planned Mobility (PM) Future Land Use category; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-05) 1. Ordinance No. 5660 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances by amending Article XII, "Industrial Districts, " Division 2, "LIRP Light Industrial and Research Park," to: (i) increase maximum floor area ratio (FAR), increase maximum building height, and reduce minimum parking requirements for new or expanded office buildings that satisfy certain specified requirements, (ii) add "Business, Professional and Governmental Office" as a permitted use in the LIRP zoning district (replacing existing , limited office allowances), (iii) add call centers as a conditional use in the LIRP zoning district, (iv) eliminate a requirement that certain commercial uses in the LIRP zoning district have pedestrian access only from the interior of a building, and (v) revise various provisions for clarity and consistency; amending Article VIII , Section 28-307, "Building Intensity," to increase the maximum FAR in the LIRP zoning district in certain circumstances; amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," to create a definition of "call center;" and amending Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, to create a new Section 28-1 317 that sets forth requirements for call centers; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-08) Regular Agenda 6 August 22, 2023 Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on items E. and E.1 would be conducted contemporaneously, as the petitions were related, and that the Council may vote to consider the transmittal of Ordinance No. 5659. The second public hearing for these ordinances would be scheduled at a later date. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by giving the background of the proposed ordinances and the Council direction to create incentives and terminate current restrictions regarding general and medical office use. Incentives were outlined, including an increase in floor area ratio (FAR), an increase in allowable height, and reduced parking requirements. Mr. Schaad reviewed additional requirements and explained that there was additional cleanup of language for clarity and consistency. Both the Planning & Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions on a number of topics and provided additional information about call centers, required setbacks, and parking requirements. The public hearing was opened . Michael Marshall thanked staff for their work on this proposal and conveyed his support for the ordinance. Jennifer Johnson urged Council to ensure that the zoning rules and parking ratios were consistent throughout the districts. Glenn Gromann offered suggestions for additional text amendments but advised that he supported the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mr. Schaad addressed the comments made during the public hearing and provided additional information. Mr. Wigder advised that he would like to see the parking requirements be consistent and changed to one per 300 and the 50,000 square foot requirement for incentives be lowered to 25 ,000. Mr. Schaad acknowledged that the amendments would be applicable to Ordinance No. 5660 and the City Attorney acknowledged that those issues could be addressed at the second public hearing for that item. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to transmit Ordinance No. 5659. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.header: Discussion: Live Local Act: 10% Minimum Affordable Units Discretionary Approvals (Item D on
units.text: the 8/21 /23 Workshop Agenda.) Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation . He began with a background of the Live Local Act and the recommended regulations. Eligibility requirements were reviewed and involved transit shelters, sidewalks and street trees, and participation in transit programs, if applicable. Among the recommended regulations would be the requirement that projects be mixed use, meet the maximum density and property development regulations, and have an affordability commitment. Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to Members' questions regarding inclusion of amenities into square footage calculations, transit and mobility, and the impact on City services. Discussion ensued. The public hearing was opened. Lon Tabatchnick spoke in favor of less restriction and against the use of FAR to address density. Bonn ie Miske! shared a brief PowerPoint presentation and spoke in favor of incentivizing the 10% rule in order to make the new rules profitable, and shared information on what other cities are doing. John Donaldson advised that most of the transit stops within the City do not meet the 20-minute headway requirement, and that he would prefer additional reductions made to the parking conditions. Michael Marshall spoke about the public transit concerns with the Regular Agenda 8 August 22, 2023 zoning districts and stated that height limits should be limited by the Federal Aviation Administration. David Abers shared information on the project proposed 40% project in the City of Largo and highlighted the importance of walkability. Juan Caycedo discussed the FAR and the impact on what could be built with those restrictions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Mayor Singer shared that he felt there was value for staff if Council could agree on guidelines for projects that have the 10% minimum affordable units. Deputy Mayor Mayotte asked if there was appetite to consider certain development project applications as a test case. Discussion ensued. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser suggested that it could be regarded as an informal planning session for the development community to give input, but applications for specific development projects would not be received or analyzed and participants would be required to sign a waiver. Lengthy conversation continued. Mr. Wigder asked the City Attorney if there could be a special meeting before the next CRA, on just this issue. Ele Zachariades advised that she and Bonnie Miske! would be interested in participating in the special meeting. There was consensus to have the Workshop first on September 11 th and for staff to finalize the details.

units.section: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: Budget Director Sharon McGuire gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began by reviewing the Mission, Vision and Guiding Principles, and Strategic Priorities. Ms. McGuire explained that the proposed millage rate of 3.6783 mils, which was slightly lower than the FY 2022-23 rate. She further explained the General Fund Operating Costs, new additions to the Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budget, and described the Property Tax Bill by Taxing Authority breakdown. Also discussed were the tax rates and Fire Assessment fees of surrounding cities and how Boca Raton is the lowest of the cities compared . Ms. McGuire then concluded her presentation regarding millage rates and made herself available for Members' questions. City Manager Leif Ahnell explained the budget process to Council Members and responded to questions regarding additional staff. Discussion ensued regarding staffing, as well as the Beautification Fund, electric vehicles and charging stations for same. Ms. McGuire continued by briefly reviewing the Capital Improvements Program for Fiscal Year 2023/24-2028/29 . Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued and there was consensus among members to make the RFP for last mile transit a priority. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser responded to a question regarding piggybacking on vendor contracts with other municipalities. Discussion ensued on moving the Final Budget meeting date and/or time or beginning the Tuesday meetings earlier. There was consensus to add continued budget discussion to the next Workshop agenda.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton adopting an amended and restated Boca Raton Municipal Facilities and Services User Fee Schedule; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Compliance Auditor Jean-Michel Neault gave the presentation . He began with an explanation of the purpose of user fees and gave a brief review of the proposed changes to the User Fee Schedule. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued with consensus to direct staff to research user fees paid between residents and non-residents. City Manager Leif Ahnell responded to questions regarding the cut back in camps, confirmed that there was no increase to boat permits, and advised that staff would research the costs associated with beach events. The public hearing was opened. Josie Machovec expressed her concerns with the beach and park pass increase adding there was no option to pro rate the cost. David Abers commented on the increase in golf fees. Mr. Ahnell responded to comments made regarding the beach permit increase and golf rates. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 88-2023. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting yes.

City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser affirmed that a recommendation will be brought forward for the Council to consider entering a settlement. Discussion ensued. Council Member Wigder thanked his colleagues and the public for their participation during the CRA and Workshop meetings from the previous day. Council Member Yvette Drucker advised she had conducted additional research to gain more information related to SB 102 (Live Local Act). She then reported that work was being done on the interlocal government agreement with the Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) and reported on other transit related issues. She also highlighted Hispanic Heritage Month and thanked the Mayor for a forthcoming proclamation. Discussion ensued. Mayor Scott Singer highlighted City events including the naming of Lois Martin Way outside of Ebeneezer Baptist Church and wished a Happy New Year to everyone celebrating the Jewish Holidays. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article X, "Multifamily Residential Districts," Code of Ordinances, to: (i) specify that the maximum density set forth in the R-3, R-3-A, R-3-B, R-3-C, R-4, R-5 and R-5-A multifamily zoning districts is applicable to single-family residences and duplexes in such districts (where permitted), and (ii) affirm the minimum plot width, minimum plot depth , and minimum plot area for single-family residences in the R-4 district; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-09) The Mayor noted that this was the second of two public hearings. Tori Boone, Zoning Manager, gave the presentation. She began with a brief overview of the text amendment proposing the same density for single family vs multi-family development. She advised that the Planning & Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Ele Zachariades, attorney on behalf of the client, thanked staff and made herself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5661. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the General Employees' Pension Plan ; providing for a one-time lump sum payment paid for certain retired or disabled general employees; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date Linda Davidson, Financial Services Director, gave the presentation. She gave a brief overview and advised that the City recommended certain changes in a one-time lump sum of their annual retirement benefit. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Steve Griffith spoke about the benefits of working for a municipality but expressed concerns with the Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) process and explained that he was would rather receive the COLA as a raise than a one-time lump sum payment. Tim Tritle also spoke in favor of receiving a percentage COLA for the General Employees' Pension. Mark Griffith advised that he was in favor of a percentage as a raise instead of the lump sum payments. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued. Mr. Ahnell answered questions raised during the public comment period and offered additional insight. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5667. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte highlighted National Clean Energy week aimed at reducing fossil fuels. She continued by thanking those who have embraced and installed solar energy systems. Ms. Mayotte concluded by mentioning the upcoming Timbertech Tournament to be held at the newly renovated Old Course at Broken Sound Club and was looking forward to attending. Council Member Yvette Drucker noted that it was Hispanic Heritage month. She gave a report on the TPA meeting she attended and advised that the public could go online to comment about the Vision 20/50 Long Reach Transit Plan. Ms. Drucker concluded by recognizing the Florida League of Cities' promotion for Mobility Week. Council Member Fran Nachlas thanked staff for working hard on the City's budget, especially for extending programs without raising taxes. She then highlighted upcoming City events. Council Member Marc Wigder mentioned the fantastic fiscal position that City Manager Ahnell has led the City through during his tenure. He continued by discussing the solar initiative and recommended that the City should expand into this field. Mayor Scott Singer praised staffs work regarding staying fisca lly responsible. He continued by discussing a request regarding large scale commercial indoor recreation. The Mayor noted that the required square footage for these projects is 50,000 square feet, but that a proposed new project was smaller and did not meet the size requirement. He asked if staff could work to amend the zoning to allow for smaller facilities. Discussion ensued , and there was consensus to direct staff to amend the zoning requirement.

Council Member Fran Nachlas thanked staff for working hard on the City's budget, especially for extending programs without raising taxes. She then highlighted upcoming City events. Council Member Marc Wigder mentioned the fantastic fiscal position that City Manager Ahnell has led the City through during his tenure. He continued by discussing the solar initiative and recommended that the City should expand into this field. Mayor Scott Singer praised staffs work regarding staying fisca lly responsible. He continued by discussing a request regarding large scale commercial indoor recreation. The Mayor noted that the required square footage for these projects is 50,000 square feet, but that a proposed new project was smaller and did not meet the size requirement. He asked if staff could work to amend the zoning to allow for smaller facilities. Discussion ensued , and there was consensus to direct staff to amend the zoning requirement.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton adopting a final budget and appropriating funds for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2023 and ending September 30, 2024; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The City Clerk read Ordinance No. 5664 in full and the title of Ordinance No. 5665. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Final Budget Hearing M inutes September 27, 2023 Mayor Singer explained that Exhibit 1 had been discussed at the prior day's CRA meeting, and Deputy Mayor Mayotte noted that her line item for 100 Mermaids would require additional vetting and could be removed from consideration for now. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to amend Ordinance No. 5665 to include items on Exhibits 1, 2, and 3. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Nachlas requested funds to enhance the bike lane at the Don Estridge School entrance on Spanish River Boulevard. Members weighed in and discussion ensued. Zach Bihr, Municipal Services Director, answered Members' questions and provided insight for options relating to improved safety features for bike lanes. Council Member Wigder then introduced his proposal to add funds for City Hall refurbishment. Mayor Singer referred to Exhibit 4 and highlighted the items for TOD consultant, air quality improvements for City Hall, and the proposed COLA increase. Discussion ensued on additional line items in Exhibit 4 and there was consensus from Members to not include the suggested COLA increase. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to amend Ordinance No. 5665 to include the line items discussed in Exhibit 4. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Mayor Singer reviewed the Non-Profit Funding request process. Members discussed their proposed changes to the list and, working from the Mayor's list, agreed to changes resulting in an increase of $52,000.00 to the total amount of non-profit fund ing. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to amend Ordinance No. 5665 to include additional funding of non­ profit organizations as stated by the Mayor. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Council Member Wigder then disclosed that he would recuse himself from the discussion and voting for the funding requests from the Gumbo Limbo Coastal Stewards and the FAU Research Park due to a conflict of interest for those items. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to amend Ordinance No. 5665 by removing funding consideration of $150,000.00 for the FAU Research Park. Motion carried 4 votes to 0.

FORM 8B MEMORANDUM OF VOTING CONFLICT FOR COUNTY, MUNICIPAL, AND OTHER LOCAL PUBLIC OFFICERS LAST NAME-FIRST NAME-MIDDLE NAME fC\ l\ru..- ll A-rnsN ~ ELECTIVE □ APPOINTIVE WHO MUST FILE FORM 88 This form is for use by any person serving at the county, city, or other local level of government on an appointed or elected board , council, commission, authority, or committee. It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented w ith a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form . INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain -or ·IDss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of commun ity redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163._35'6 or 163.357, F.S. , and officers·of independent special tax-districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law,·a "relative" includes only the 0fficer's father; mother, son, daughter, ·husband, w ife, brbther, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A "business associate" means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joir,t venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). • • *· ELECTED OFFICERS: In addition to abstaining from voting in the situations described above, you must disclose the conflict: PRIOR TO THE VOTE BEING TAKEN by publicly stating to the assembly the nature of your interest in the measure on which you are abstaining from voting; and WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER THE VOTE OCCURS by completing and filing this form with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who should incorporate the form in the minutes. APPOINTED OFFICERS: Although you must abstain from voting in the situations described above, you are not prohibited by Section 112.3143 from otherwise participating in these matters. However, you must disclose the nature of the conflict before making any attempt to influence the decision, whether orally or in writing and whether made by you or at your direction. IF YOU INTEND TO MAKE ANY ATTEMPT TO IN FLUENCE TH E DECISION PRIOR TO THE MEETING AT WHICH THE VOTE WILL BE TAKEN: You must complete and file this form (before making any attempt to influence the decision) with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting, who will incorporate the form in the minutes. IF YOU MAKE NO ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE THE DECISION EXCEPT BY DISCUSSION AT THE MEETING: • You must disclose orally the nature of your conflict in the measure before participating. • You must complete the form and file it within 15 days after the vote occurs with the person responsible for recording the minutes of the form in the minutes. A copy of the form must be provided immediately to the other members of the meeting, who must incorporate the _ agency, and the form must be read publicly at the next meeting after the form is filed. units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a plat entitled "SRR Plat" (a replat of portions of Lots 4 and 5, Block 5, Spanish River Land Company Subdivision , Unit One) for the approximately 0.49 acre property generally located at 1075 Spanish River Road; authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-22-05) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Tori Boone, Zoning Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Boone provided a history of the property and reviewed the proposed subdivision of the parcel. She advised that the Planning & Zoning Board and staff recommended approval with conditions. Upon concluding, she made herself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades, attorney on behalf of the client, made herself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Resolution No. 102-2023. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing procedures and regulations to implement Section 166.04151(7), Florida Statutes, as created by Chapter 2023-17, Laws of Florida (Live Local Act of 2023) for development of statutorily authorized mixed-use residential development (including affordable housing); noting the business and commercial, industrial, and miscellaneous zoning districts in which the mixed-use directive is applicable; providing land development regulations (including those generally applicable in multifamily zoning districts and providing an administrative approval process); noting the statutorily mandated maximums for density and height; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-23-07) The public hearings on Items B. and B.1 will be conducted contemporaneously, as the petitions are related. This is the second of two required public hearings on the ordinances in accordance with Chapter 163 and Chapter 166, Florida Statutes, respectively. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation . Mr. Schaad gave a brief overview of the Live Local Act (SB 102), the draft ordinance, the proposed changes to the Floor Area Ration (FAR), setbacks, and potential parking reduction. He continued by advising that both Planning & Zoning and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. Discussion ensued and Mr. Schaad responded to questions and provided additional information. The public comment period was opened . Jonathan Ounjian spoke about the density requirements and questioned if the City is following SB 102 as it was intended. Seeing no one else come forward. the public comment period was closed. Discussion ensued . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5653. Council Member Wigder advised that SB 102 was written and imposed by the State and this was a meaningful first step at implementing a new building code. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided insight. There was consensus to move forward. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Land Use Element Policies LU.1.1.5, LU .1.1.6 and LU.1.1.10 to create the Enhanced Mobility (EM) Future Land Use category and establish a description and maximum density and intensity for such category; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-01) 1. Ordinance No. 5655 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article XVII , "Planned Development," Code of Ordinances, to create a new Division 9, "Enhanced Mobility Development," and, among other things, provide development parameters for such development, and establish procedures and standards for applications, reviews and approvals; amending Chapter 28, Article XII, "Industrial Districts," Division 2, "LIRP Light Industrial Research Park," to create a new Section 28-987, "Enhanced Mobility Development (EMO)," to authorize enhanced mobility development projects within a specified geographic area of the LIRP zoning district located in the vicinity of the Yamato Tri-Rail Station, and, among other things, introduce new EMO uses , provide for increased intensity, and provide for a maximum density; amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Article VIII, Section 28-307(1), Code of Ordinances, to establish the building intensity for EMO uses in the LIRP zoning district; deleting obsolete references to LIRP- 2.5 and LIRP-5; providing for severability; providing fo r repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-22-01) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11.B. and 11 .8 .1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11 .B. not be approved, no vote on item 11 .B.1. would be taken. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He gave an overview of the proposed amendments and changes to the Light Industrial Research Park (LIRP) zoning district. Mr. Schaad continued by describing the density, Floor Area Ratio (FAR), site design, vehicle, and bicycle parking. Additional details were provided regarding the plats and the platting process versus development plans. He stated that both the Planning & Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. Discussion ensued with Mr. Schaad providing additional information regarding permitting and phasing of projects. Members reviewed the proposed changes to the language in the ordinance, and Mr. Schaad and City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser answered questions and provided clarification . Consensus was made for staff to further revise the language in the ordinance. The public comment period was opened. Bonnie Miskel, attorney on behalf of the client, shared a PowerPoint presentation and reviewed changes that she proposed to the language regarding platting. Discussion ensued and Ms. Miskel responded to Members' questions. The meeting was recessed at 7:19 P.M. and resumed at 7:42 P.M. The City Attorney read proposed revisions into the record for Section 28-1875(4)(a) and Section 28-1875(4)(b). Ms. Miskel confirmed that she agreed with the changes and there was consensus from Members to accept the revisions. Jonathan Ounjian urged Council Members to ensure that what is promised by developers is what gets delivered. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. There was additional discussion among Members and staff provided clarification. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5654. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5655 as amended. Discussion ensued. Ms. Frieser and Mr. Schaad responded to questions and provided additional information. Members made final comments and thanked staff for their hard work on this project. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Land Use Element Policy LU .1 .1.5 to increase the maximum floor area ratio (FAR), from 0.6 to 0.85, for office uses on certain parcels in the Planned Mobility (PM) Future Land Use category; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-05) 1. Ordinance No. 5660 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances by amending Article XII, "Industrial Districts," Division 2, "LIRP Light Industrial and Research Park," to: (i) increase maximum floor area ratio (FAR), increase maximum building height, and reduce minimum parking requirements for new or expanded office buildings that satisfy certain specified requirements, (ii) add "Business, Professional and Governmental Office" as a permitted use in the LIRP zoning district (replacing existing, limited office allowances), (iii) add call centers as a conditional use in the LIRP zoning district, (iv) eliminate a requirement that certain commercial uses in the LIRP zoning district have pedestrian access only from the interior of a building, and (v) revise various provisions for clarity and consistency; amending Article VIII, Section 28-307, "Building Intensity," to increase the maximum FAR in the LIRP zoning district in certain circumstances; amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," to create a definition of "call center;" and amending Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, to create a new Section 28-1317 that sets forth requirements for call centers; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-22-08) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 11.C. and 11.C.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.C. not be approved, no vote on item 11.C.1. would be taken. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Schaad began by providing an overview of the proposed changes and incentives for building new office and mixed-use projects in the LIRP zoning district, and removal of some restrictions for certain uses. Mr. Schaad then reviewed other use changes and advised there were additional language changes to provide clarity and consistency in the code. He advised that staff and the Planning & Zoning Board had recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Jennifer Johnson spoke in favor of equal zoning and parking regulations for all districts within the City. Michael Marshall spoke on behalf of the Arvida Park of Commerce (APOC) property owners' associations and urged Council to approve the proposed ordinances. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the proposed ordinance but expressed concerns with the parking requirements. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5659. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5660 as amended. Further discussion ensued and Mr. Wigder recommended an amendment to the parking requirements. Mr. Schaad provided additional information. Mayor Singer made final comments, thanked staff for their work on this project and suggested a name change for the LIRP zoning district. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder to amend the medical parking to 1 per 300. Motion died for a lack of a second. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Council Member Wigder highlighted the "Walk Against Hate" at the Spanish River Library and shared that he was very pleased with the attendance. He continued by asking if the City could put out an RFP to add a cafe at the library. Mr. Wigder noted the extra police presence at the local schools related to tensions regarding the war in Israel. Council Member Yvette Drucker highlighted local events regarding mobility and transportation. She advised that she had attended the FAU Homecoming event, and thanked staff for providing promotional material for residents that emphasized Mobility Week. She then shared that she attended a Latin Shabot mass and thanked Police Services for their continued patrols at local synagogues. Deputy Mayor Mayotte shared slides that showed examples of tactical urbanism and public safety in Aspen, Colorado. She commented on the recent recycling conference she attended and highlighted best recycling practices. Council Member Nachlas mentioned that the upcoming TimberTech Golf Tournament would be recycling all the waste generated from the event. She highlighted events for Mobility Week and concluded by stating that she continues to stand with Israel. Mayor Scott Singer reiterated his support of Israel, highlighted upcoming City events, and thanked the City's first responders.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, "Administration," Article 11, "City Council," Section 2-27, "Rules of Procedure," Code of Ordinances, to reduce the minimum speaking time allotted to a person wishing to address the Council from five (5) minutes to three (3) minutes; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification: providing an effective date Acting City Manager George Brown offered the results of a survey performed by staff, noting that all municipalities in Palm Beach County and those contacted in Broward County offer three minutes or less of public comment time. Mayor Singer provided comments in favor of the proposed reduction in time and advised that time could always be extended at the discretion of the Council. The public comment period was opened. Amy Price spoke against the proposed change in public comment time. Jonathan Ounjian shared his opposition to the proposed ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Mayor Singer responded to comments made during public comment and offered additional insight. Deputy Mayor Mayotte spoke against the reduction of time and advised that she would not be supporting this ordinance. Council Member Nachlas explained that she would support the ordinance if time could be adjusted or extended as needed. Council Member Yvette Drucker spoke in favor of the reduction and advised that she supports the ordinance. Council Member Marc Wigder shared that he would support the ordinance, as well as adjustments of the time allotted as demand necessitated. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5678. Motion passed 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes; Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting no.

Resolution No. 118-2023 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton amending the "Schedule of Minimum Civil Penalties for Violations Enforced Pursuant to Section 9-60, Code of Ordinances" (Resolution No. 163-2018, as amended by Resolution No. 68-2022) to provide for a civil penalty for violations of Section 5-4 (nuisance-causing and wildlife feeding prohibited), Section 9-110 (prohibition of the sale or distribution of polystyrene foam products on City property), Section 9-111 (prohibition of balloons and confetti in outdoor areas on City property), Section 10-64(1) (time of day of construction activity), and Section 14-11 (bulk and vegetative waste collection time/placement); and update a cross reference to the Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Mayor Singer noted that the public hearings on item 11.C. and 11.C.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related, and a separate vote would be taken on each item. Should item 11.C. not be adopted, no vote would be taken on item 11 .C.1. Jim Bell, Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Bell gave a brief background of the proposed ordinance and the associated violation fees and made himself available for Members' questions. Mr. Wigder asked about the additional fines being proposed aside from the nuisance­ causing wildlife feeding. Ms. Drucker also inquired about the enforcement of the fines and the number of violations that were occurring. Deputy Mayor Mayotte questioned which animals were included in the ordinance. Ms. Nachlas agreed that the wildlife fine should not be included with the other items in the resolution. Mr. Bell and Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, responded to Members' questions and provided additional information. The public comment period was opened. Mark Stahlbaum spoke in favor of the ordinance and urged Council to approve it. Jonathan Ounjian raised concerns over exactly what would be considered a nuisance animal and how the ordinance would be enforced. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Extended discussion ensued. City Attorney Diana Grubb Frieser and Mr. Brown provided clarification, highlighted sections of the code, and answered Members' questions. There was consensus to withdraw Ordinance No. 5679 from consideration, and to table Resolution No. 118-2023 to November 28, 2023, to be brought back as revised. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to withdraw Ordinance No. 5679. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to table Resolution No. 118-2023 to November 28, 2023. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: Robert DuKate highlighted pedestrian and bicyclist safety regarding the proposed railroad crossing at Jeffery Street. Mr. DuKate stated that he believed the information submitted on the application to the FOOT was outdated and encouraged Council Members to take public safety into account. Harold Chaffee also expressed his concerns regarding the proposed extension of Jeffrey Street and cautioned Members to consider public safety impacts. Tony Bazant, retired City of Boca Raton employee, commented on the General Employee pension and the desire for retirees to have a cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) . Cil Ciliberti commented on opening Jeffrey Street and encouraged transparency between the City and the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District in the development of the North Park Project. Jonathan Ounjian expressed his opposition to the new time limit for public comment and provided a copy of the State Statute regarding affordable housing. Mr. Ounjian then requested that the City Attorney provide information regarding her legal interpretation of Senate Bill 102. Lily Perez addressed comments made by her neighbor at a previous Council meeting about her feeding of pigeons. At the request of Mayor Singer, Acting City Manager Brown provided additional information in response to comments made.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Land Use Element Policies LU.1 .1.5 and LU .1.1.6. and adding new housing element policy HO.1. 3.23 to establish a framework for the affordable housing provisions of Subsections 166.04151 (6) and (7), Florida Statutes; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-14) The public hearings on Items B. and B.1. will be conducted contemporaneously as the items are related. A separate vote will be taken on Items B. and B.1. Should Item B. not be approved, no vote will be taken on item B.1 . Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing and the first of two public hearings. The second hearing would be after the return of the State's review of the Ordinance. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by explaining that the ordinance was drafted at the request of Council to address an optional provision in subsection six of the Live Local Act of 2023 regarding affordable housing and workforce housing. The number of dwelling units and units per acre of the proposed regulations were reviewed, as well as mandatory provisions of the Act. Mr. Schaad advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval and reviewed the future public hearing schedule for the ordinance. Upon concluding, he made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Ounjian spoke against the proposed limits of affordable housing units, noting that he did not believe this ordinance to be necessary. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to transmit Ordinance No. 5680 as revised. Discussion ensued. Members provided comments and asked for clarification. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser and Mr. Schaad provided additional information. Members shared their positions on the ordinance and their desire to see affordable and workforce housing within the City. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Amy Price expressed concerns about large-scale implementation of affordable and workforce housing due to the potential impacts on existing infrastructure and suggested that it be initially addressed as a pilot program. Steve Reiss spoke on the recent surge of auto crimes and noted the increase in police presence. Michael Majhess shared his distress regarding auto crimes in the City and the increasing boldness of criminals, especially in the Golden Harbour and Golden Triangle areas. He asked for better communication with City staff and additional police assistance. Steve Griffith commented on the biennial review of benefits for the General Employee's Pension Plan and asked that, in light of the general employee's service to the City, the cost-of-living-adjustment (COLA) for general employees be reconsidered. Matthew Chapnick highlighted the work of staff of the City's parks and beaches and asked that the City take care of the general union employees. Joseph Brenner, representative of City employees on behalf of the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), spoke about the one-time lump sum given to non-union represented City employees and asked for consideration that the same be given to employees represented by the SEIU. Roy Ageloff commented about the escalation of auto crimes and expressed concern that the crimes could become more serious. Gregory Ryan noted the work done by representatives of the general employee's union and shared his disappointment that the lump sum given to non-bargaining employees was not given to union members. Joe Majhess remarked on the increase in frequency and severity of auto crimes in the City and asked for a public education campaign to raise awareness of the issue, as well as a review of current police policies and procedures. Stacy McLaughlin relayed her concerns about safety in light of the recent auto crimes in the Golden Harbour area. David Bungarz advised that he was part of the most recent SEIU negotiations and asked that the lump sum payment be revisited for general union employees. Tom Desernia asked for additional collaboration between the City and residents in those areas most affected by the recent increase in crime. Mayor Singer responded to concerns regarding public safety and the rise in auto crimes, union negotiations, the public request timeclock, and the Live Local Act. At the request of Mayor Singer, Mr. Brown provided clarification regarding Florida statutes and the City's pursuit policy. He noted that staff could work on a public education campaign and that the issue regarding a lack of communication would be addressed . Mr. Brown also advised that patrols had been increased to the areas most affected and that there were other actions being taken that were not publicized. Council Members each relayed their commitment to public safety and to enhanced communication with residents. Mr. Brown reiterated that staff would work on public education and outreach to residents regarding the recent rise in auto thefts. He also expressed his gratitude to the general employees and the work that they do to keep the City running and advised that he would look into the issues they raised. The Council Members thanked the union members present for relaying their concerns and shared their appreciation for the dedication to the City .

units.text: Deputy Mayor Mayotte noted an email that she received from Outfront Media referencing a letter previously sent and advised that she had not been given the original letter. Ms. Frieser provided clarification and shared that, although the letter had been addressed as if it were sent to the Council Members, that had not been the case. Mayor Singer also stated that he had not received the letter and asked that correspondence be forwarded in the future. Council Member Nachlas remarked that she also had not received the original letter. She thanked staff for their work throughout the year and shared that she was looking forward to another great year. Ms. Nachlas concluded by reading a letter she had written thanking Mr. Ahnell for his service and wishing him the best in his retirement. Council Member Wigder noted that he also had not received the letter from Outfront Media. Mr. Wigder then remarked on Mr. Ahnell's financial leadership of the City, thanked him for his years of service, and wished him well in the future. Council Member Drucker advised that she did not like the Jersey barriers proposed for Sanborn Square and would like to revisit this topic when Council meets next. She continued by commenting on safety issues surrounding the Brightline trains and thanked Mr. Ahnell for his years of service. Mayor Singer clarified an earlier comment to note that an individual who had a pending development proposal did not consider himself to be a developer and to repeat his view that both residents and non-resident taxpayers like business owners were all important and valued. He reiterated his steadfast support of Israel, thanked Mr. Ahnell for his work on behalf of the City, and shared that he would be signing the employment contract with Mr. Brown following the meeting . The Mayor concluded by highlighting upcoming events and wished all a happy holiday.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide for fleet vehicle parking as a main (as opposed to accessory) use; amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," to add a definition of "Fleet Vehicle Parking"; amending Article XVI , "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1646, "Definitions," to delete the definition "Fleet Vehicles"; amending Article XII , "Industrial Districts," Division 8, "M-3 Manufacturing Industrial District," Section 28-1123, "Permitted Uses," to add "Fleet Vehicle Parking" as a permitted use; amending Article XV, Division 1, "Supplementary District Regulations," by creating Section 28-1317, "Fleet Vehicle Parking," to establish regulations for such use; amending Article XVI , "Off-Street Parking and Loading ," Section 28-1655 , "Required Off-Street Parking ," to clarify the number of required fleet vehicle parking spaces; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM- 22-05) Jim Bell, Long Range Project Manager, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He gave an overview of the revised ordinance with the Planning and Zoning Board proposed amendments to fleet vehicle parking , including the proposed restriction of pick up and drop off times, which staff does not support. He advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval with modifications. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued . Mr. Bell and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad answered Members' questions and provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades requested that the limitations be removed for EV parking. John Donaldson spoke on behalf of his client and shared their opposition to restrictions on AM and PM traffic flow. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas to approve Ordinance No. 5682 as revised. Council Member Wigder proposed a revision to remove the electric vehicle (EV) requirement and ease the AM/PM restrictions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided clarification and City Manager George Brown advised that applicants could apply for a technical deviation regarding the EV requirement. Deputy Mayor Mayotte agreed with Mr. Wigder's suggestions and Council Member Nachlas expressed her support for the technical deviation of the EV requirements. Both Mayor Singer and Council Member Drucker noted that they were opposed to removing the proposed AM/PM restrictions. Further discussion ensued. Members requested additional data regarding effects of fleet vehicles during peak traffic times Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to open and continue the public hearing of Ordinance No. 5682 to the Regular Council Meeting of February 27, 2024. Ms. Frieser clarified the motion and responded to Members' questions. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing procedures and regulations pursuant to Section 166.04151 (6), Florida Statutes, for development of affordable housing (referred to as "Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development" or "CIMO"), including workforce housing; establishing eligibility requirements, development standards, and approval procedures applicable to such development, (including reduced parking requirements, where applicable); adding CIMO as a permitted use in the following zoning districts (where the Future Land Use Designation is Planned Mobility): R-B-1 (Motel Business), B-2 (Community Business), MC (Medical Center), POI (Professional, Office, and Institutional), City CG (Commercial General City), CHO (Commercial High Office), LIRP (Light Industrial Research Park), M-3 (Manufacturing Industrial) and W-1 (Warehouse District); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-23-10) Mr. Brown advised that two copies of the ordinance had been provided; one that reflected changes made by staff and the other by Council Member Nachlas. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation . He began by giving a board overview of the proposed revisions and highlights from previous meetings. Mr. Schaad advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. At Mayor Singer's request, Mr. Schaad provided additional information on the changes to the ordinance by staff, noting that it consisted of removal of repetitive wording and language cleanup that were not substantive. In response to a question by Mr. Wigder, he advised that the latest changes proposed by Ms. Nachlas had not been reviewed by the Planning and Zoning Board. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the ordinance and asked that the City ensure that plans approved for retail and commercial actually get completed by the developers. Lon Tabatchnick shared his support for the ordinance and asked that developers be given credit for incorporating additional amenities in their properties. Ele Zachariades thanked staff for their work on this ordinance and advised that she approves the changes as revised. Michael Marshall also thanked staff for their work on this ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing, was closed. Deputy Mayor Mayotte shared her reasons for not wanting to restrict office uses in mixed-use areas. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas to approve Ordinance No. 5684 as revised by staff and with proposed revisions by Ms. Nachlas. Motion died for lack of a second. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5684 as revised by staff but without the changes proposed by Ms. Nachlas. Discussion ensued . Ms. Nachlas explained the intent behind her proposed changes to the ordinance, advising that additional restaurant or retail uses, rather than office use, would provide a better experience to residents of the planned developments, result in fewer car trips on local roads, and add to pedestrian friendliness. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas to approve Ordinance No. 5684 as revised by staff and with proposed revisions by Ms. Nachlas. Extended discussion ensued. Ms. Zachariades commented and advised that she had suggested the amendments proposed by Ms. Nachlas. Ms. Drucker shared that she would need more data on the potential impact of the revisions in order to consider them and Mr. Wigder and Ms. Mayotte indicated their support for certain sections of the proposed changes. The meeting was recessed at 8:15 PM and resumed at 8:25 PM. Members weighed in and consensus was reached to table the public hearing to a future date. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to open and continue the public hearing of Ordinance No. 5684 to the Regular Council Meeting ofFebruary 13, 2024. Motion passed unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton establishing procedures and regulations pursuant to Section 166. 04151( 6), Florida Statutes, for development of affordable housing ( referred to as Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development' or " CIMD"), including workforce housing; establishing eligibility requirements, development standards, and approval procedures applicable to such development, ( including reduced parking requirements, where applicable); adding CIMD as a permitted use in the following zoning districts ( where the Future Land Use Designation is Planned Mobility): R- B- 1 ( Motel Business), B- 2 ( Community Business), MC Medical Center), POI ( Professional, Office, and Institutional), City CG ( Commercial General City), CHO ( Commercial High Office), LIRP ( Light Industrial Research Park), M- 3 Manufacturing Industrial) and W-1 ( Warehouse District); providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date ( AM-23-10) Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation. He provided an overview of the proposed ordinance and noted that it had been revised to remove redundant or duplicative language. Mr. Schaad then outlined the changes proposed by Council Member Nachlas and those recommended by Council Member Wigder. He advised that staff recommended approval with the revisions as proposed by staff and Council Member Nachlas on January 23, 2024, and that the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the ordinance prior to the January 23rd revisions. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. Mayor Singer shared his position on the proposed changes and stated that he was not inclined to support the revisions proposed by Council Member Nachlas. Discussion ensued. At the request of Ms. Nachlas, City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided information regarding the Bert Harris Private Property Rights Protection Act. The public hearing was opened. Ele Zachariades spoke in favor of the ordinance and the proposed changes and responded to Members' questions. Malcolm Butters shared that he was not in favor of this ordinance as presented and would like the proposed retail requirement removed. Juan Caycedo spoke in favor of passing the ordinance but without the retail condition. Lon Tabatchnik spoke against the ordinance as proposed, supporting the original version of the ordinance, and suggested that restaurant/ retail condition should not be included. David Abers spoke in favor of the ordinance and urged Council to support it. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the ordinance as proposed but expressed concerns regarding the parking. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5684 with the proposed revisions dated February 8, 2024. The meeting was recessed at 7: 26 PM and resumed at 7:41 PM. Council Member Nachlas proposed that her amendment of a retail/ restaurant condition for accessory use be reduced to 2, 000 square feet from 5, 000, and that a waiver of the parking requirements still be included. Ms. Frieser clarified the amendment and read proposed language into the record on page 9, subsection ( 2)( b). Mr. Schaad confirmed that the retail or restaurant use did not need to be located within the residential building, as long as it was on -site on the ground floor. At the request of Ms. Nachlas, Lon Tabatchnik shared that he was in favor of the revised amendment. Council Member Wigder expressed his support of the revision, including his amendment on lines 15-17 from page 9. Ms. Frieser clarified the amendment. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to amend the motion and approve the revisions to Ordinance No. 5684 as read by City Attorney Diana Grub Friesen Motion passed on a vote of 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting no. Deputy Mayor Mayotte clarified her objections to the proposed amendments. She stated that she believed the revisions would result in more expense to the builders and would negatively affect the affordability of the residential units, and that changes could be made at a later time. Ms. Mayotte shared her support for the original ordinance and for affordable housing. Further discussion ensued and Council Members weighed in. Ms. Frieser suggested that the motion be further amended to clarify that the language being amended was based on the document dated January 23, 2024, including all revisions reflected in grey and green highlighting and with the additional modification on page 9, item 2)( b), as read into the record. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to further amend Ordinance No. 5684 as specified by City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser. Ms. Frieser and Mr. Schaad provided additional information regarding the on -site non- residential requirement. Motion to amend carried on a 4-1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, - Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting no. Members made final comments. The main motion to approve Ordinance No. 5684 as amended carried on a 4-1 vote; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes; Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to provide for fleet vehicle parking as a main (as opposed to accessory) use; amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions, " to add a definition of "Fleet Vehicle Parking"; amending Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1646, "Definitions," to delete the definition "Fleet Vehicles"; amending Article XII , "Industrial Districts," Division 8, "M-3 Manufacturing Industrial District," Section 28-1123, "Permitted Uses," to add "Fleet Vehicle Parking" as a permitted use; amending Article XV, Division 1, "Supplementary District Regulations," by creating Section 28-1317, "Fleet Vehicle Parking," to establish regulations for such use; amending Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1655, "Required Off-Street Parking," to clarify the number of required fleet vehicle parking spaces; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM- 22-05) Long Range Project Manager Jim Bell gave the PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Bell provided a summary of the history and purpose of the proposed amendment and advised that representatives of affected businesses opposed the suggested changes. He presented the results of a survey of peak-time traffic from an applicant's property conducted since the last public hearing and noted that the impact of the ordinance would apply to the entire M-3 zoned area . Staff recommended approval of the ordinance as revised after the Planning and Zoning approval. Upon concluding, Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Mr. Bell answered Members' questions and provided additional information. The public hearing period was opened. Attorney Ele Zachariades spoke on behalf of her client and expressed their opposition to the proposed restrictions. Traffic Engineer John Donaldson, representing the same applicant, shared concerns regarding staffs recommended peak-time limitations. Ms. Zachariades and Mr. Donaldson responded to Members' questions. Seeing no one else come forward to speak, the public hearing was closed. Discussion ensued . Mr. Schaad responded to Members' concerns and noted that the proposed regulations were not intended for one particular property, but for an entire zoning district. The meeting was recessed at 6:52 PM and resumed at 6:55 PM. At the request of Mayor Singer, City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser read into the record proposed language on page 5, Section 3, lines 7-9,which focused on limiting the number of vehicles trips during peak hours , rather than prohibiting pick-ups or drop-offs entirely . Ele Zachariades noted her approval of the amended language. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5682 as revised. Ms. Frieser read an additional clarification of the proposed amendment into the record. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5682 as revised and amended. Motion carried unanimously: Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: SEIU representative Joseph Brenner, speaking on behalf of Union-represented employees, shared concerns from the membership regarding their negotiated contract and their request for the non-pensionable bonus that the non-bargaining employees had received . City Manager George Brown provided an overview of a previous meeting with union leadership and stated that the contract had been agreed upon, was ratified by Union members, and is valid until September 2025. City employees and SEIU members Craig Fritz, Mike Clarke, Sandra Santillan, Carlos Gaobin, Brad Hughes, David Bungarz, and Melissa Wade shared their disappointment at not receiving the lump sum payment that the non-bargaining employees received and urged Council and City staff to revisit the possibility of offering the lump sum payment to SEIU members. Mr. Brown provided additional information , advised that the City had negotiated in good faith, and that both sides had agreed to the contract. Council Members shared their thoughts, and all expressed how deeply they appreciated union members and the work they perform.
