units.text: Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte gave a PowerPoint presentation for items remaining on her to-do list that she considered inspirational and urged staff to think outside the box concerning City operations. She listed a number of ideas to help connect with residents and made a number of suggestions, including the modernizing of Ordinance No. 4035, online renewal of beach stickers, and providing more options for metered parking. Council Member Yvette Drucker referred to parking options that are available in neighboring cities and suggested that City staff investigate creative alternatives to the current parking payment structure. Mr. Brown advised that staff was exploring a number of options regarding the current metered parking. Ms. Nachlas expressed her support for a number of the innovative parking ideas shared by Ms. Mayotte. Council Member Fran Nachlas reported on a recent Orlando site visit that she and Ms. Drucker had made with the Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) to review new mobility options. She also commented on the Cultural Consortium Member event and noted the amount of cultural activity that there was in the City. Council Member Yvette Drucker provided details of her trip to Orlando and the revitalization of an area near a transportation hub. Ms. Drucker inquired if Ms. Mayotte would attend the on line IPARC Issues Forum meeting in her place as she would be attending the Safe Streets Summit in Miami. She then highlighted City events and advised that the City had been nominated for a number of Safe Streets Awards. Council Member Marc Wigder shared pictures of a collapsed seawall and inquired about the possibility of acquiring grants from State or Federal funding for infrastructure repairs. Mayor Singer highlighted City events and the upcoming Municipal Election.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton providing for the vacation and abandonment of a utility easement, approving and accepting a replacement utility easement deed, for the property generally located at 215 SE Spanish Trail, as more specifically described herein; providing conditions for vacation and abandonment; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (EA-23-05) Development Services Deputy Director Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation and provided a brief overview of the relocation of the utility easement. She advised that staff recommended approval and, upon concluding, responded to Members' questions. The public comment period was opened. David Milledge spoke on behalf of the applicant. He stated that the relocation of the sewer easement was completed, already benefitting drainage in the area and they are waiting for approval of this ordinance to get the final inspection. Seeing no one else come forward, public comment period was closed. Mayor Singer added that he had spoken with City Manager George Brown regarding staff approval for these types of easements, and Mr. Brown advised that staff was looking into streamlining processes so items such as this could be approved administratively. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, to approve Ordinance No. 5689. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Mayor Singer suggested to save the bulk of comments for outgoing Deputy Mayor Monica Mayotte for next Monday's Organizational Meeting. Deputy Mayor Mayotte gave a PowerPoint presentation providing her final thoughts and suggestions as Deputy Mayor and encouraged her fellow Council Members and staff to be more productive by working smarter and making changes for the better. Council Member Drucker expressed her disappointment with the delay of the circulator RFP and hoped the vendor contract would come before them at the first April meeting. She then commented positively on Ms. Mayotte's tenure and wished her well. Council Member Nachlas congratulated Ms. Drucker on her reelection, as well as Mr. Thomson's election. She also echoed Ms. Drucker's comments and thanked Ms. Mayotte for her service to the City. Council Member Wigder also remarked favorably on Ms. Mayotte's tenure and shared his appreciation for her service to the City. Mayor Singer highlighted the Organizational Meeting on April 1st and the State of the City on April 1oth at the Mizner Park Amphitheater. The Mayor highlighted Ms. Mayotte's advocacy of environmentalism and sustainability and thanked her for her friendship.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a plat entitled "Lot 8 of Lago Mar Shores" (a replat of a parcel of land lying in Section 16, Township 47 South, Range 43 East) for the approximately 0.17 acre property generally located at 980 Lago Mar Lane; authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SUB-23-02) The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Ketcia Fleurilus, Land Development Coordinator, gave the PowerPoint presentation. She gave a brief history of the property and provided the proposed replat details and revisions. Ms. Fleurilus advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. She then read revised language regarding the pedestrian access easement. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Attorney for the applicant Sarah Thompson, thanked staff, made herself available for questions, and noted that the applicant agreed with the additional revisions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution 24-2024 as revised. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

She gave a brief history of the property and provided the proposed replat details and revisions. Ms. Fleurilus advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. She then read revised language regarding the pedestrian access easement. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. The public hearing was opened. Attorney for the applicant Sarah Thompson, thanked staff, made herself available for questions, and noted that the applicant agreed with the additional revisions. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution 24-2024 as revised. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for OM Redevelopment LTD. (a partnership between the Boca Raton Housing Authority and Atlantic Pacific Communities, LLC), for the approximately 10.04 acre property generally located at 1350 North Dixie Highway, a universal conditional (UC) amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan , pursuant to Chapter 23, Article VI, Code of Ordinances, from Residential Medium (RM) to Residential High (RH), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map, for the Residences at Martin Manor Project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-04/SC) 1. Ordinance No. 5694 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for OM Redevelopment LTD. (a partnership between the Boca Raton Housing Authority and Atlantic Pacific Communities, LLC), for the approximately 10.04 acre property generally located at 1350 North Dixie Highway, a universal conditional (UC) rezoning, pursuant to Chapter 23, Article VI , Code of Ordinances, from Multifamily Residential (R-3) to Multifamily Residential (R-5-A), subject to conditions ; providing for the appropriate revision of the Zoning District Map, for the Residences at Martin Manor Project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-04/ZC) Regular Agenda 4 May 14, 2024 2. Resolution No. 36-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for DM Redevelopment LTD. (a partnership between the Boca Raton Housing Authority and Atlantic Pacific Communities, LLC), for the approximately 10.04 acre property generally located at 1350 North Dixie Highway, a conditional use approval, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize an existing nursery and afterschool program in the Multifamily Residential (R-5-A) zoning district, for the Residences at Martin Manor Project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-04/CA) 3. Resolution No. 37-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for DM Redevelopment LTD. (a partnership between the Boca Raton Housing Authority and Atlantic Pacific Communities, LLC), for the approximately 10.04 acre property generally located at 1350 North Dixie Highway, a site plan, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize the construction of three (3), three (3)-story buildings with a total of 95 low­ income housing units totaling 99,926 square feet, construction of a 4,265 square foot clubhouse building and outdoor amenity area, and retention of an existing 4,929 square foot community center and 1,000 square foot maintenance building, together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655(1)(b), Code of Ordinances, to reduce the number of required vehicular parking spaces from 197 to 124 (a reduction of 73 parking spaces), and a technical deviation from Section 28-1655(2)(a), Code of Ordinances, to (i) reduce the number of electric vehicle (EV)-installed parking spaces from 10 to zero ( a reduction of 10 EV-installed parking spaces), and (ii) reduce the number of EV-capable spaces from 40 to zero (a reduction of 40 EV-capable parking spaces), for the Residences at Martin Manor Project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-04/SPA) 4. Resolution No. 38-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for DM Redevelopment LTD. (a partnership between the Boca Raton Housing Authority and Atlantic Pacific Communities, LLC), for the approximately 10.04 acre property generally located at 1350 North Dixie Highway, pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request: (i) variances from Section 28-673, Code of Ordinances, to allow a front (west) yard (setback) of 24 feet, nine (9) inches in lieu of the minimum 32 feet required, to allow a side (north) yard (setback) of 32 feet, six (6) inches in lieu of the minimum 46 feet required, and to allow a side (east) yard (setback) of 27 feet, seven (7) inches in lieu of the minimum 42 feet required, and (ii) a variance from Section 28-676(2), Code of Ordinances, to allow a sidewalk that is parallel to the western property line (adjacent to North Dixie Highway) where the code allows sidewalks only generally perpendicular to the required 25 foot landscaping buffer, in the Multifamily Residential (R-5-A) zoning district, for the Residences at Martin Manor Project; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-04/VA) The Deputy Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. through A.4 would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. She noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.A. not be approved, no vote would be taken on the remaining items. Ordinance No. 5693 requires four votes for adoption. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jacob German, Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began by noting that since the introduction at the last Regular City Council Meeting, updated drawings had been submitted by the applicant and his presentation had been updated to reflect the revisions. He then proceeded to review the application, including the conditional use and site plan approvals, variances, and technical deviations. Aerial photos and site plans of the property and landscape plans were shown. Mr. German discussed the request for two variances and two technical deviations, which were supported by staff. Both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, Mr. German Regular Agenda 5 May 14, 2024 and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to Members' questions. City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser provided additional information on proposed SB 1084 preemption of EV parking requirements. The public hearing was opened. Attorney Ele Zachariades of Miske! Backman gave a brief overview of the request including future development, rezoning, site plan, and examples of proposed interactive historic exhibits. The request for conditional use, variance setbacks and parking analysis were also reviewed. She then discussed changes made since the Planning and Zoning Board meeting and response to residents' concerns. Upon concluding, Ms. Zachariades responded to questions and Mr. Schaad provided additional information. Discussion ensued on the possibility of preserving one of the buildings for historical reference. Jeffrey Katz expressed concerns with parking, lack of trash chutes and elevators, expressed support for the preservation of one building for historical purposes but asked that Council Members vote no on the project. Cherie Bender spoke in opposition to the project. Marie Hester commented on being a good steward of history, spoke favorably of the Boca Raton Historical Museum, and advocated preserving one of the buildings. Charles Graves commented on meetings with the developer and residents' requests for elevators, trash chutes in the buildings and additional parking. John Martin spoke about preservation of one of the buildings, proposed traffic calming, and recognition of the community in the City's Centennial celebration. Erica White, Cassie Moorman, Vichaun Mansfield, Chiquita Lofton, Kristen Silvestre, Geline Saint Martin, Shaniece Williams, Fabiola Bernier, Angela McDonald , and Calvin Davis also spoke in support of the project and preservation of a building. Joseph Martin spoke about the history of the Tuskegee Airmen, support of preserving the historic barracks and asked Council to reject the project. Boca Raton Housing Authority Executive Director Ashley Whidby spoke on the importance of the preservation of history and steps they are taking in that direction. She then responded to questions. Chuck Ridley, chair of Unify Palm Beach County, spoke in support of preserving the history of Dixie Manor. Danielle Iverson, chair of the Boca Raton Housing Authority, thanked Council and residents for this discussion and spoke in support of providing affordable housing and encouraged approval of the application. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5693. Mayor Singer shared his comments in support of the application and suggested a recess to discuss an amendment to ensure the preservation of a building for historical purposes. There was consensus for recess and Ms. Frieser noted that the applicant waived their rebuttal time. The meeting was recessed at 8:42 PM and resumed at approximately 9:07 PM. City Attorney Frieser advised that, during the recess, additional language was drafted and agreed upon by both parties. She then read language proposed to be added on page 8, Condition 6 of the Site Plan Amendment, Resolution No. 37-2024, which provided for the preservation of one building prior to demolition if funding from a third party was secured. Ms. Frieser noted that this would also result in an amended exhibit to the Comprehensive Plan (Ordinance No. 5693). The applicant indicated that they agreed to the additional language as read. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to amend the original motion to include the language as read by the City Attorney with the modification to add 'at least one building'. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Mayor Singer noted that he was joining the meeting remotely due to his attendance at a conference of government officials on behalf of the City and, if there was a positive consensus among the Council Members to move forward with the amendment to the FLUM , he would leave the remaining items to be determined by his colleagues. Ms. Frieser reiterated that revised site plan sheets were previously distributed to Council Members and those revised sheets would be attached to the approval, not the original ones in the approval packet. Mr. German confirmed that the revised site plan was the plan included in his presentation. Both Mayor Singer and Council Member Wigder confirmed that the motion they made included the revised site plans. Mr. Wigder then gave a brief PowerPoint presentation Regular Agenda 6 May 14, 2024 sharing his thoughts on current evaluations and local considerations of the project. He shared photos of similar affordable housing projects that did not include elevators, commented on the raising of the proposed playground area elevation and additional dumpsters. Members gave their comments in support of the project. Motion to approve Ordinance No. 5693 as amended, with additional language as read by the City Attorney and the revised site plans carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Ms. Frieser noted that the changes just discussed and adopted on the Comprehensive Plan and the site plan would apply to the remaining ordinance and resolutions. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5694 as amended previously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 36-2024 as amended previously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 37-2024 as amended previously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 38-2024 as amended previously. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. At this point, Mayor Singer left the meeting.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 23, "Planning and Development," Article IV, "Development Regulations," Division 2, "Housing," Section 23-110, "The Affordable Housing Advisory Committee," Code of Ordinances, to provide for staggered terms of appointment for the members of the Committee; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date City Manager Brown briefly reviewed the ordinance and made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Jeffery Katz and Fabiola Bernier each spoke in support of the appointment of Charles Graves to the Affordable Housing Advisory Committee. Seeing no one else come forward, th e public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5692. Motion carried on a 4-0 vote; Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Deputy Mayor Drucker noted that Mayor Singer was no longer online and did not vote. Regular Agenda 7 May 14, 2024 1. Board Appointments - Affordable Housing Advisory Committee Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to appoint Charles Graves to the Affordable Housing Advisory Committee. Motion carried 4-0 on a voice vote. City Manager Brown stated that Mr. Graves confirmed that he would accept one of the positions with a 4-year term. Council Member Wigder noted that there were still specific positions that needed to be filled and encouraged those with qualifications to apply.

units.text: Council Member Nachlas thanked Ms. Frieser for her hard work and years of service. Council Member Thomson thanked Ms. Frieser for her continued efforts and advised that he would expound more at the next Council meeting. Deputy Mayor Drucker thanked Ms. Frieser for her service and stated that she looked forward to communication improvements. Mayor Singer advised that communication had improved, however, he believed the mitigation of harm to the City could be enhanced, and that Mr. Frieser's impending retirement and subsequent transition to a new City Attorney should be considered. He concluded by thanking Ms. Frieser for her service. Council Member Wigder advised there was a need for extended discussion regarding the transition to a new City Attorney, whether it be an internal or external hire. Ms. Frieser advised that she appreciated both the compliments and constructive comments and was very proud of her 25 years of service to the City. She advised that she would work with the Mayor and Council on a smooth transition when the time comes. Regular Agenda 4 June 11, 2024

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of Edilane Piedra, for a settlement and reduction of one (1) code enforcement lien imposed against the properties located at 4720 Northwest 2nd Avenue, Units 0104 and 0105; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Deputy Development Services Director Erin Sita gave a brief overview of the code violations and the proposed lien reduction from $152,115 to $76,115. Ms. Sita advised that staff recommended approval and made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued. The public comment period was opened. Sergio Piedra, the applicant, provided details on why he was requesting the lien be further reduced from $76,115 to $50,115. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the lien reduction and gave an example of another property that was not in compliance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Further discussion ensued and Ms. Sita responded to Members' questions and provided additional details. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 57-2024 as amended, lowering the fine from $152, 115 to $50, 115, to be payable within 30 days. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Council Member Andy Thomson suggested the City's Special Magistrates be authorized to adjust fines at their hearings and City Manager Brown advised that City staff was currently considering this suggestion. The meeting was recessed at 7:33pm and resumed at 7:42pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering a Separation of Employment Agreement with Diana Grub Frieser; authorizing the execution of such Agreement; providing an effective date City Manager George Brown gave a brief overview of the agreement. Discussion ensued. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 70-2024 as amended to include the termination date of January 31, 2025. The public comment period was opened. Jonathan Ounjian voiced his concerns over the separation agreement and stated that he looked forward to a new City Attorney . Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Council Member Thomson suggested that an outside attorney evaluate the separation agreement and Members debated whether or not to seek an external review. Extended discussion ensued among the Members and Mr. Brown provided additional information. The meeting recessed at 8:20pm and resumed at 8:36pm. Upon further discussion, there was a consensus to revise the separation date to October 31, 2024. Regular Agenda 8 July 23, 2024 Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to amend the motion on the floor to change the separation date from January 31, 2025, to October 31, 2024. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 70-2024 as amended with the separation date of October 31, 2024. Motion carried 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes and Council Member Andy Thomson voting no.

Mr. Brown advised that, if approved, the change would take effect October 1, 2024, and asked for Council's approval to proceed. There was consensus from Members to enact the change. Mayor Singer provided an opportunity for the public to speak and, seeing no one come forward, the public comment period was closed.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, by: (i) amending Article XVI , "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1655, "Required Off­ Street Parking," to reduce the minimum parking requirement for medical and dental offices and clinics from one space per 175 square feet to one space per 200 square feet for the first 4,000 square feet and one space per 300 square feet thereafter (matching the existing parking rate for General Office), and establish a minimum parking requirement for "Outpatient Surgery Centers" of one space per 175 square feet; and (ii) amending Article I, Section 28-2, "Definitions," to define the term "Outpatient Surgery Center"; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-24-05) Zoning Manager Tori Boone gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began with a brief overview of the Medical Parking rates and the proposed amendments and advised that staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions and discussion ensued. Council Member Wigder shared a brief PowerPoint and suggested additional language that would further define facilities affected by the proposed Code amendment. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Ms. Boone provided additional details and information. The public comment period was opened. Jonathan Ounjian voiced his concern over the amount of allowable parking based on certain definitions of uses. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Members made final comments regarding the amended language to Sections 28-2 and 28-1655 of the Code. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Ordinance No. 5698 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton equalizing the assessments; levying the same as assessments against benefited properties within the Downtown Special Assessment District, City of Boca Raton, Florida; directing the City Clerk to record assessments in the Improvement Lien Book; establishing priority of lien and payment of principal and interest; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Stephen Timberlake, Special Projects Manager, gave the presentation. He provided a brief history of the Downtown Special Assessment, the requirement to fund the debt service, and administrative costs for the special assessment revenue bonds. Mr. Timberlake noted that the purpose of the meeting was to hear and consider any objections to the special assessment. The method of calculating the assessment rate was explained and various charts and graphs were presented. No objection letters were received. Upon concluding, Mr. Timberlake made himself available for questions. In response to Council Member Wigder's question, Mr. Timberlake advised that the special assessment bonds would be paid off in 2030. The public hearing was opened. Eddie Weinstein had no objection to the assessment but noted that the biggest problem was parking ; he commented on developers building multimillion dollar condominiums with only 1.75 parking spaces per unit, parking meters, clarification on the benefit of the assessment and planting additional shade trees. Jonathan Ounjian commented on the assessment report and stated he felt some numbers were inaccurate. City Manager George Brown provided additional information on the initial downtown assessment, shade trees, parking meters, and crosswalks. The reasons for the downtown assessment were also elaborated. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 85-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton adopting an amended and restated Boca Raton Municipal Facilities and Services User Fee Schedule; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Compliance Auditor Jean-Michel Neault gave the presentation. He began with an explanation of the purpose of user fees and gave a brief review of the proposed changes to the User Fee Schedule. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. Council Member Wigder voiced his concerns with the increase in golf fees, especially since the Golf and Racquet Club was under construction. He then asked if consideration would be given to not increasing the fees. Discussion ensued and Mr. Brown provided additional information. The public hearing was opened and, seeing no one come forward, was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 90-2024. Under discussion, Council Member Wigder asked that they consider not increasing golf fees or the frequent player card annual fee at both the Golf and Racquet Club and Red Reef Golf Courses. Motion was made by Council Member Wigder to amend Resolution No. 90-2024 to eliminate the increase to the daily fees, resident and non-resident fees at both golf courses and the frequent player card cost at the Golf and Racquet Club. Discussion ensued . Mr. Brown recommended Council adopt the User Fee Schedule as presented , and advised staff would then gather the information on the proposed increase for Council, and the schedule could be amended at any time thereafter. Council Member Wigder withdrew his motion to amend. On the original motion to approve Resolution No. 90-2024 as presented, motion carried 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes, Council Member Marc Wigder voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 2-acre property generally located at 6403 West Rogers Circle, a conditional use pursuant to Section 28-1124(b), to authorize the storage, service, repair and cleaning of motor vehicles in an existing building in the Manufacturing Industrial (M-3) Zoning District; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-23-02) 1. Resolution No. 81-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 2 acre property generally located at 6403 West Rogers Circle, an amendment to the approved site plan (Resolution No. 87-32) to authorize modifications to the existing building fa9ade and interior floor plan , and additional site modifications including parking lot and landscaping improvements, to accommodate a motor vehicle showroom and the storage, service, repair and cleaning of motor vehicles, together with three (3) technical deviations from (i) Section 23-190(d), Code of Ordinances, to eliminate an additional required 12 foot wide egress lane, (ii) Section 23-190(d}, Code of Ordinances, to eliminate a required four (4) foot driveway median, and (iii) Section 28-1655(1), Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required number of vehicle parking spaces from 77 spaces to 56 spaces; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-88-07R1 ) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 1O.A. and A.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 1O.A. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The Deputy City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave a PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Devlin noted the concerns from the previous application and highlighted the recent revisions. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and the Development Services Department recommended approval. Upon concluding he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued with Mr. Devlin answering Members' questions. David Milledge, attorney for the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation. He noted the changes from the previous meeting which included site plan changes and technical deviations, and upon concluding he answered Members' questions. The public comment period was opened. Thomas Laird , Charles Rhein , Louis Rosner, Zach Taminosian, Jim Falzone, Dale Gregory, Eric Poklyak, and Jim Smirglio all spoke against the project and urged Council to deny the application. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the project and urged Council to approve the application. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. David Milledge provided responses to commenters concerns. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 80-2024. Extended discussion ensued. Traffic Engineer Naresh Machavarapu and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad answered Members' questions and provided further details. Members made final comments. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 81-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: Mayor Singer suggested that, due to the elimination of three vacant employee positions, the savings of that amount be subtracted from the millage rate. Financial Services Director James Zervis explained the reduction to the General Fund and that adjusting the millage rate accordingly would result in the overall millage rate being reduced from 3.6782 to 3.6734 and the percentage over the roll back rate would be reduced from 6.92% to 6. 78%. In effect, the savings from the vacant positions would reduce the property tax roll by that same amount resulting in a savings for residents. Mayor Singer reviewed the Non-Profit Funding request process. Members discussed the proposed list and agreed to changes. Council Member Nachlas advocated for adding two non-profit organizations that had not submitted their applications. After further discussion, Members felt that those organizations should not be included this year. Mr. Zervis then summarized the amounts line by line and advised a net increase of $21,000 over the prior year. Council Members thanked the 0MB and Financial Services staff for their hard work.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, pertaining to carwashes, to: (i) create Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, Section 28-1319, "Carwashes," to reorganize existing carwash regulations and add new regulations for carwash operations; (ii) amend Article XI , "Business and Commercial Districts," Division 3, "R-B-1 Motel-Business District," Section 28-743, "Conditional Uses" to allow "carwash" as a conditional use in the R-B-1 Motel-Business District, subject to certain requirements and limitations; (iii) amend the B-4, LIRP and M-1 Zoning Districts to update terminology, replacing "Car Laundries" and "Auto Laundries" with "Carwashes"; and (iv) amend Article XVI, "Off-Street Parking and Loading," Section 28-1655, "Required Off-Street Parking" to add parking requirements for carwashes; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-23-11) Senior Planner Heather Hansen gave the PowerPoint presentation. She provided an overview of the proposed text amendments, a history of the property, and details of the new regulations. She advised that staff recommended approval and upon concluding, made herself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Jonathan Ounjian advised that he supported the proposed text amendment and urged Council to approve the ordinance. Attorney Ele Zachariades, on behalf of her client, advised that she would have a presentation available for the second hearing of this ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. The Mayor advised that the next hearing for this ordinance would be on October 22, 2024. Regular Agenda 5 September 24, 2024

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Thoroughfare Right­ of-Way Protection Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating a certain segment of the Northwest ("NW") 5th Avenue right-of-way requiring protection, consisting of approximately 1,301 feet in length, generally located west of 2500 and 2600 NW 5th Avenue, from 100 feet to 90 feet in width; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-24-03) The Mayor noted that this was a transmittal hearing and the first of two public hearings. The second hearing would be after the return of the State's review of the Ordinance. Senior Planner Peter Begovich gave the PowerPoint presentation. He advised that this was a City­ initiated application to amend the City's Right-of-way (ROW) protection and gave a brief history of the ROWs. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened and, seeing no one come forward, was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve the transmittal of Ordinance No. 5702. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, "Administration," Article 111, "Boards, Committees, Commissions and Special Magistrates," Division 3, "Special Magistrates," Code of Ordinances, to delegate authority to the Special Magistrate to consider and act upon applications for code compliance lien reductions and to establish procedures for lien reduction requests; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-24-09) Deputy Director of Development Services Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation. She gave an overview of the Code Compliance process, the proposed amendments, and advised that staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued . Development Services Director Brandon Schaad answered Members' question and provided additional information. The public comment period was opened. Jonathan Ounjian spoke against the handling of the Dan burg project. Chris DeSilva addressed random topics. Seeing no one else come forward, the public comment period was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5705. Extended discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson advised that the proposed changes to procedure were in line with those of neighboring municipalities. Mayor Singer and Deputy Mayor Drucker agreed that appeals should be handled at the Special Magistrate level but that the current process could be revised . Council Member Wigder shared his opposition to applications returning to the original magistrate for appeal hearing, and Council Member Nachlas expressed concerns with the process and advised that she would support postponing the decision to a future date. Mr. Schaad and Ms. Sita provided additional information and clarification. There was consensus to postpone the public hearing to November 19, 2024. Regular Agenda 6 September 24, 2024 Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to postpone the hearing until November 19, 2024. Motion carried 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson voting yes, Council Member Marc Wigder voting no.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 11 .87-acre property generally located at 1800 North Military Trail, an amendment to an approved site plan (Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 05-29 as amended by Resolution No. 07-21) for a Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development (CIMO) to authorize the construction of a new six (6)-story, 295-unit multi-family residential building , including 10% affordable and 5% workforce housing units, and related site improvements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-04-25/R4) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Peter Begovich , Senior Planner, gave the presentation . He began with a review of the request, project location, and overall site plan of the property. Multimodal features were reviewed, and Mr. Begovich highlighted the public benefits of the proposed project. Elevations and renderings were displayed , as well as photos of the existing office building . The affordable units and workforce rental information was outlined, and staff analysis showed that the project is compatible with adjacent land uses and complies with all applicable code requirements. Mr. Begovich noted that the applicant requested modifications and both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , Mr. Begovich made himself available for questions. Brandon Schaad, Development Services Director, provided information regarding staff challenges of the first project under the CIMO. Discussion ensued on topics including processing applications for affordable housing and verification of income. The public hearing was opened . Ele Zachariades, attorney for the applicant, gave the presentation . Ms. Zachariades began by highlighting the site plan and CIMO regulations. She then reviewed the setback and landscape buffers and advised that the project met workforce housing and equivalency requirements and exceeded parking requirements. David Abers, on behalf of the applicant, continued the presentation with an expanded summary of the location, project renderings , and the restricted covenant. Lon Tabachnick expressed his approval of the project but stated that he did not support the restricted covenant. Jonathan Ounjian shared his approval. Bonnie Miske! commented on the cooperation between City staff and the developers but noted her concern with some details of the covenant. Mr. Koehler noted that, should Council wish to move forward , the covenant could be amended at a future date. Discussion ensued and Mr. Schaad and Mr. Koehler provided additional information. Mr. Schaad proposed alternative language in page 18, as did Ms. Miskel, and Mr. Brown suggested additional language on page 7. Discussion continued and there was consensus to move forward with additional language in the covenant as discussed. There was no cross examination . During the rebuttal, Mr. Abers commented further on the covenant being a work in progress but stated that the document was acceptable in its current form. Mr. Brown suggest further additions to the language on page 9. Ms. Zachariades suggested the Council move forward with a vote and that the revised covenant could be revisited at a future date. Members weighed in, both Mr. Koehler and Mr. Brown read the amended language, and the applicant provided their approval of the revisions . The public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve the amended language to Resolution No. 104-2024. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Regular Agenda 3 October 8, 2024 Members made final comments and Mr. Brown and Mr. Schaad advised that staff would come back before Council in January regarding the declaration of covenant. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 104-2024 as amended. Motion passed unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. The meeting was recessed at 7:37 pm and resumed at 7:44 pm.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering, for a Residential (R-3- F) zoned approximately 0.42 acre property generally located at 2600 North Ocean Boulevard, a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a four-story, approximately 38- foot tall, 6,931 square-foot single-family residence seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-16-08) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Chief Planner Ta mash been Rahman gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with a description of the application and advised that the request for variance was being heard as part of a re-hearing process. The subject property was described , and a site plan was shown . Placement of the proposed building on the property was outlined and Ms. Rahman advised that the project met both zoning and dimensional requirements. Renderings of the proposed building were displayed and a chart comparing the previous proposal with the current application was presented . She reviewed the applicant's updated Environmental Assessment Report and listed conditions of approval including , but not limited to, phased construction work, a sea turtle lighting plan , a tree pruning plan , and pre-construction requirements. Ms. Rahman advised that the Environmental Advisory Board (EAB) recommended denial. Development Services staff recommended approval of the revised application, including the conditions of approval, subject to the applicant obtaining approvals from all necessary State agencies. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown, Ms. Rahman, and Mr. Schaad responded to questions. The public hearing was opened . William Stoddard , representative on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation . Mr. Stoddard began with a review of his professional background and highlighted the number of coastal construction permits approved throughout the state of Florida. A history of the project and list of professional consultants were shown . Mr. Stoddard noted the collaboration between project consultants and City staff to make plan revisions following the court ordered rehearing from the 4th District of Appeals. The minimization of impacts, strict adherence to building codes, landscaping plans, and comparison of prior and current proposals were discussed. Renderings of the proposed building 's elevations were shown , and Mr. Stoddard noted that the footprint of the building was landward and not in the location of recorded marine turtle nests. Robert Sweetapple, attorney for the applicant, continued the presentation . He noted that the applicant agreed to every condition requested by the City, that the property had originally been platted for residential development, and that public comments made at the EAB meeting objecting to the project were not quasi-jud icially accepted evidence. Mr. Sweetapple stated that the standards to grant the CCCL variance had been met and asked Council to recognize his client's rights. Tucker Gibbs, representing homeowners of the Yacht and Raquet Club, expressed the concerns of the Club's residents that the project had not met the criteria for a variance and requested denial. Stephen Margolis spoke against granting a variance for the project citing potential harm to the environment and public safety concerns. Jorge Salinger, president of the Yacht and Raquet Club , expressed concerns regarding the sea turtles, vegetation , and the dunes. Michael Laszlo stated that he believed the applicant failed to meet the Regular Agenda 4 October 8, 2024 criteria of a special and unique condition . Debby Teich read a statement regarding the negative impact of lighting on the sea turtles. Matthew Pintchik, Richard Hutner, Lewis Kurtz, Jaime Akkusu , Linda Shapiro, Henry Barnet, Jacob Abraham, Daniel Mancini, Kevin Meaney, Grant Kelly, Paul Gaba spoke against granting the variance for the project. There was no cross examination . During the rebuttal, Mr. Sweetapple responded to the comments made, advising that speakers had a misunderstanding of the conditions and noting that his client did not cause the special and unique condition. He then responded to question regarding natural plantings and the removal of invasive or exotic species. The public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued , and Mr. Schaad , Mr. Brown , Ms. Rahman , and David Anderson, Sea Turtle Conservation Coordinator for Gumbo Limbo, responded to Members' questions. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 105-2024 with conditions as outlined by staff. units.full: Resolution No. 105-2024 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering, for a Residential (R-3- F) zoned approximately 0.42 acre property generally located at 2600 North Ocean Boulevard, a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance, from Section 28-1556(3), Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a four-story, approximately 38- foot tall, 6,931 square-foot single-family residence seaward of the CCCL (where no structure is permitted seaward of the CCCL without a variance); providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-16-08) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Chief Planner Ta mash been Rahman gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with a description of the application and advised that the request for variance was being heard as part of a re-hearing process. The subject property was described , and a site plan was shown . Placement of the proposed building on the property was outlined and Ms. Rahman advised that the project met both zoning and dimensional requirements. Renderings of the proposed building were displayed and a chart comparing the previous proposal with the current application was presented . She reviewed the applicant's updated Environmental Assessment Report and listed conditions of approval including , but not limited to, phased construction work, a sea turtle lighting plan , a tree pruning plan , and pre-construction requirements. Ms. Rahman advised that the Environmental Advisory Board (EAB) recommended denial. Development Services staff recommended approval of the revised application, including the conditions of approval, subject to the applicant obtaining approvals from all necessary State agencies. Upon concluding, Mr. Brown, Ms. Rahman, and Mr. Schaad responded to questions. The public hearing was opened . William Stoddard , representative on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation . Mr. Stoddard began with a review of his professional background and highlighted the number of coastal construction permits approved throughout the state of Florida. A history of the project and list of professional consultants were shown . Mr. Stoddard noted the collaboration between project consultants and City staff to make plan revisions following the court ordered rehearing from the 4th District of Appeals. The minimization of impacts, strict adherence to building codes, landscaping plans, and comparison of prior and current proposals were discussed. Renderings of the proposed building 's elevations were shown , and Mr. Stoddard noted that the footprint of the building was landward and not in the location of recorded marine turtle nests. Robert Sweetapple, attorney for the applicant, continued the presentation . He noted that the applicant agreed to every condition requested by the City, that the property had originally been platted for residential development, and that public comments made at the EAB meeting objecting to the project were not quasi-jud icially accepted evidence. Mr. Sweetapple stated that the standards to grant the CCCL variance had been met and asked Council to recognize his client's rights. Tucker Gibbs, representing homeowners of the Yacht and Raquet Club, expressed the concerns of the Club's residents that the project had not met the criteria for a variance and requested denial. Stephen Margolis spoke against granting a variance for the project citing potential harm to the environment and public safety concerns. Jorge Salinger, president of the Yacht and Raquet Club , expressed concerns regarding the sea turtles, vegetation , and the dunes. Michael Laszlo stated that he believed the applicant failed to meet the Regular Agenda 4 October 8, 2024 criteria of a special and unique condition . Debby Teich read a statement regarding the negative impact of lighting on the sea turtles. Matthew Pintchik, Richard Hutner, Lewis Kurtz, Jaime Akkusu , Linda Shapiro, Henry Barnet, Jacob Abraham, Daniel Mancini, Kevin Meaney, Grant Kelly, Paul Gaba spoke against granting the variance for the project. There was no cross examination . During the rebuttal, Mr. Sweetapple responded to the comments made, advising that speakers had a misunderstanding of the conditions and noting that his client did not cause the special and unique condition. He then responded to question regarding natural plantings and the removal of invasive or exotic species. The public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued , and Mr. Schaad , Mr. Brown , Ms. Rahman , and David Anderson, Sea Turtle Conservation Coordinator for Gumbo Limbo, responded to Members' questions. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 105-2024 with conditions as outlined by staff. Mayor Singer, Deputy Mayor Drucker, Council Member Nachlas and Council Member Wigder made final comments, noting their reluctance to approve construction eastward of the CCCL but recogn izing the property owner's rights and their agreement with the proposed conditions. Motion passed 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no.

units.text: Deputy Mayor Drucker encouraged everyone to be safe and sign up for City alerts. Council Member Wigder gave a PowerPoint presentation on new laws taking effect and highlighted those regarding flood disclosure and grant programs for flood resilient projects. He spoke about alternative mobility fees that allowed for local governments to have their own government fee schedule, and the resiliency of Boca Raton . Deputy Mayor Drucker noted that !PARC was creating a multi-jurisdictional issues coordination forum to help formulate a county-wide transportation plan and she would be getting input from Council Members and sharing information from the committee. Mr. Brown advised that Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik represented the City for the Palm Beach County City Managers Association and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad served on the technical committee, and that both would be contributing information for the creation of the transportation plan . Council Member Fran Nachlas reported on her membership in the Development, Code Compliance, and Redevelopment Committee and focus areas of that committee, including the Live Local Act, national housing trends, and vacation rental updates. She advised that they would meet on November 8th • and she would come back with more information after that meeting . Mayor Singer requested a follow-up regarding the consultant for The Center for Arts & Innovation (TCAI) issues and Mr. Brown provided information . Mr. Singer thanked everyone for their hard work preparing for Hurricane Milton, reminded everyone to be prepared and stay alert.

Resolution No. 107-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for a 5.24-acre portion of the approximately 74. 72-acre North Park, site plan approval to authorize construction of a two (2)-story, approximately 77,218 square foot paddle and pickleball facility that will include 14 indoor pickleball courts, two (2) indoor paddle courts, nine (9) outdoor pickleball courts, locker rooms , food & beverage service and other site improvements including surface parking lot; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA- 23-15R1) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and A 1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related . He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.A. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The Deputy City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation . He gave a brief overview of the property location, amenities, and proposed construction. He advised that Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued. Mr. Devlin responded to Members' questions and provided additional information. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant David Milledge reviewed the location, site plans, and the text of the conditional use proposal. Robert Dukate spoke in opposition to the project. Delaney Beighley, Chris D'Angelo, Sil Ciliberti, and Jay Sway spoke in favor of the project. Juan Caycedo expressed concern about the connectivity of the North and South portions of the park and the eventual opening of the Jeffrey Street crossing . In rebuttal, David Milledge responded to comments made and provided clarification . Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 106-2024. Regular Agenda 2 October 22, 2024 Council Member Wigder asked for clarification from the City Attorney regarding the authority of Council to hear this project. Deputy City Attorney Josh Koehler clarified Council's role in approving the resolutions. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Future Land Use Map (FLUM) of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 0.034 acres generally located at 7900 North Federal Highway, from Commercial (C) to Residential Low (RL), subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the FLUM; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-24-01) 1. Ordinance No. 5709 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering the rezoning of certain property consisting of approximately 0.034 acres generally located at 7900 North Federal Highway, from Motel-Business (R-B-1) to Single Family Residential (R-1-B) ; providing for the appropriate revision of the zoning district map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (ZC-24-01) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.B. and C., C.1., C.2., C.3., D., and D.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related . He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.B. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining items. The Deputy City Attorney confirmed that the quasi-judicial procedures which were read for the prior items would also govern this public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Heather Hansen gave the PowerPoint presentation for Ordinance No. 5701 . She reviewed the history of the property, and the proposed zoning and text amendment changes. She advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Council Member Wigder asked for clarification regarding the R-B-1/ R-1-B zoning and Ms. Hansen provided additional information. Ms. Hansen then continued her presentation on the subsequent agenda items concerning 7900 North Federal Highway. She reviewed the consolidation of the properties, the creation a new sidewalk along Bailey Street, parking requirements, traffic impacts, and landscape buffering . She advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Ms. Hansen responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant Ele Zachariades gave a PowerPoint presentation . She briefly reviewed the proposals and text amendment changes and made herself available for questions. Finola Fordham and Jerry Fordham, owners of the adjacent residential property located on Bailey Street, shared their opposition the project. David Daskel, Michael Mancusi, and Roger Greene expressed their support for the project and urged Council to vote yes. Ms. Zachariades provided additional details and information related to comments made during public comment. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5701 . Discussion ensued . Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5710. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the Boca Beach Club Hotel, on the approximately 12.42 acre property generally located at 900 South Ocean Boulevard, a Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) variance from Section 28-1556(3) , Code of Ordinances, which variance is required for the construction of a new event lawn and hardscape and landscape improvements to the existing poolside lanai and bar area, together with the repeal of a previous CCCL variance (Resolution No. 51-2023) that approved the installation of two pergolas seaward of the CCCL, but which was never constructed; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-23-13) The Deputy City Attorney confirmed that the same quasi-judicial procedures read earlier in the meeting would also govern this public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation. He provided a background of the Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) , history of the property, and details of the requested variance. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval without the conditions as recommended by the Environmental Advisory Board (EAB) . Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued and Mr. Devlin answered Members' questions and provided additional details. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant David Milledge gave a PowerPoint presentation and provided a brief history of the property as well as the proposed changes to the project. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 112-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. The meeting was recessed at 7:58 pm and resumed at 8:08 pm. Regular Agenda 5 October 22, 2024

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Master Site Plan for the approximately 141-acre Town Center at Boca Raton Mall generally located at 6000 West Glades Road (including the approximately 123.62-acre original mall property generally located at 5700, 5800 , 5840 , 5860, 5900 and 6000 West Glades Road) (Palm Beach County Resolution No. R-77-1196, as amended) to authorize, for the original mall property portion of the overall site: the expansion of existing outdoor patio area from 940 Square feet to 2,140 square feet (an increase of approximately 1,200 square feet) and other minor site modifications (landscaping and hardscaping), together with a technical deviation from Section 28-936, Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required number of off-street parking spaces from 8,015 parking spaces to 8,009 parking spaces; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-09-05R3). Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 114-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton relating to the regulation and enhancement of community aesthetics and standards, the authority of Community Appearance Board, and the streamlining of the review process; amending Chapter 2, "Administration," Article Ill Division 4, "Community Appearance Board ," and various provisions of Chapter 19, "Building Regulations, " Chapter 23, "Planning and Development, " Chapter 27, "Vegetation" and Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, to amend and restate the powers and duties of the Community Appearance Board , and to delegate certain approval authority previously held by the Community Appearance Board to the City Manager or Designee (subject to appeal); reformatting and restating various provisions for clarity; amending the "Supplemental Criteria And Procedural Rules Of The Community Appearance Board ," to revise the lists of recommended and prohibited tree species for meeting landscaping requirements, relocate certain procedural provisions to the Code of Ordinances, and amend and restate said provisions; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-24-07) Development Services Deputy Director Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation . She reviewed the summary of proposed changes, powers and duties of the CAB, the reduction of the membership from 8 to 7, and the revision of the qualifications for membership. She advised that the Planning and Zoning Board voted to table the proposed text amendment at their last meeting on October 17, 2024 . Development Services staff recommended approval. Upon concluding she made herself available for questions and discussion ensued . Regular Agenda 6 October 22, 2024 The public hearing was opened . Community Appearance Board Member Jessica Dornblazer voiced her concerns over the proposed changes that would affect how the CAB operates. Jay Sway shared his thoughts about the number of members resigning from the board . David Milledge advised that the CAB process would be clearer going forward with the proposed changes. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Additional discussion ensued, and Ms. Sita and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided information and responded to Members' questions. Deputy City Attorney Josh Koehler shared additional information. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve the amendments as discussed. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5706 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of BAF Assets, LLC, for a settlement and reduction of one (1) code enforcement lien imposed against property located at 628 SW 18th Avenue; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Regular Agenda 9 October 22, 2024 Development Services Deputy Director Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation . She gave a case summary, advised that the applicant requested a lien reduction from $13,615 to $3,000 for a total reduction of $10,615, and advised that staff does not support the request for reduction. Discussion ensued with Ms. Sita answering Members' questions. Code Enforcement Officer Dennis Spellman advised that he agreed with Ms. Sita's presentation . The public hearing was opened . Property Manager Ronald Ferrin spoke on behalf of the owners, indicated that the property is now in compliance, and requested a reduction of the total amount to $5,000. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, to reduce the fine by 50% to $6,750, plus the administrative costs. Motion died for lack of a second. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 115-2024, with the full amount of the fine of $13,615, due in 30 days. Extended discussion ensued . Motion passed on a vote of 3 to 2; Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Mayor Scott Singer voting yes, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker and Council Member Marc Wigder voting no.

units.text: Mayor Singer advised that the purpose for today's meeting was to conduct interviews for the City Attorney position and thanked outgoing City Attorney Diana Grub Frieser for her years of service. City Manager George Brown gave a brief explanation of the process and introduced Jim Dineen, Recruiter who facilitated acquiring the candidates. Mr. Dineen explained the search, qualifications required, and the interview process. Applicants were brought in one at a time in alphabetical order and were all asked the same ten questions. Clayton F. Knowles was interviewed first. He offered a brief background of his education and experience. Joshua P. Koehler the current Deputy City Attorney of Boca Raton provided his education and experience and then began the interview process. The meeting was recessed at 3:47 pm and resumed at 4:09 pm. Ronald Tomasko was interviewed and gave a brief background of his education and career and was the last to be interviewed . Upon concluding there was discussion amongst the members. Council Member Andy Thomson suggested reopening the posting in light of one applicant withdrawing from consideration . After extended discussion , consensus was had to select Joshua P. Koehler as the new City Attorney . Mayor Singer was nominated to negotiate the contract. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to enter negotiations of drafting an employment agreement with Joshua

units.text: Representative Marie Woodson expressed her desire that City employees who are members of SEIU receive bonuses equal to those of non-union employees. John Clubb spoke on the topic of sexual abuse of children , shared that he was an advocate for ending the statute of limitations for prosecuting offenders, and requested the Council's support in his endeavors. Alphonso Mayfield, Political Coordinator for the SEIU , Charles Ridley , Matthew Chapnick, Linda Joseph, Angela McDonald, Sheila Gaines, Michael Clarke, Afifa Khaliq , and Charmaine Postal all spoke in favor of bonuses and re-negotiating a contract for the union employees. George Brown gave a brief history of the most recent contract and urged the union employees and representatives to look ahead to upcoming negotiations. Discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson advised that he was in favor of staff looking into a one-time bonus for the union employees. Deputy Mayor Drucker noted that the current City Manager and Acting City Attorney were not part of contract negotiations for the current SEIU contract, and asked Mr. Brown if he could research the possibility of providing the requested bonus to Union employees . Council Member Wigder noted the recent appointments of the new City Manager and City Attorney , assured union members that their upcoming contract would be negotiated in good faith and asked them to give the City Manager and Acting City Attorney time to look into their request. Council Member Nachlas echoed comments made by Mr. Wigder, shared her appreciation for the Union employees and urged them to work closely with their representatives when negotiating. Mayor Singer also thanked the Union employees for their service, highlighted the City Manager's addition of the day after Thanksgiving as a City holiday , and noted Mr. Brown's respect for the dedication of hard-working City employees.
