Ordinance No. 5718 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 8.01 acre property generally located at 2600 Northwest 5th Avenue, a universal conditional (UC) rezoning from multi-family residential (R-3-D) to multi-family residential (R-3-B), pursuant to Article VI , Chapter 23, Code of Ordinances, subject to conditions; providing for the appropriate revision of the Zoning District Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-01/ZC) 2. Resolution No. 124-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 8.01 acre property generally located at 2600 Northwest 5th Avenue, a site plan approval pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request, to authorize construction of a multi-family residential project with 22 , three (3) story, "Townhome-style" apartment buildings with a total of 120 units, a two (2) story clubhouse building with leasing office, and other site improvements, together with a technical deviation from Section 23-190U), Code of Ord inances, to reduce a required minimum inbound driveway reservoir distance for a gated residential development from 100 feet to 70 feet; considering the abandonment of portions of a water sewer easement and a lake maintenance easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-23-01/SPA) The Mayor noted that hearings on items A. , B., B.1., and B.2. would be conducted contemporaneously as the petitions were related , with Items B.1. and B.2. pursuant to quasi-judicial procedures. A separate vote would be taken on each item , and should items A. and B. not be approved, items B.1. and B.2. would not be considered . The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to all those who wished to speak. Peter Begovich , Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation . He began with a brief history of the proposed amendment in Ordinance No. 5702. The existing Right-of-Way (ROW) and properties adjacent to it were displayed , as well as the projected widening of NW 5th Avenue. Mr. Begovich advised that both the Planning and Zoning Board and Development Services staff recommend approval , that Council voted 5-0 to transmit the amendment to the State for review and it had been returned with no comments. Continuing with the remaining agenda items for this topic, he then reviewed the applicant's related request and the consistency , compatibility , and concurrency of the proposed project. Mr. Begovich discussed the proposed rezoning of the site, and shared the site plan , traffic study results , and landscaping plans. The applicant's request for a technical deviation had been evaluated and staff had no comments. Mr. Begovich noted the applicant's concerns with two cond itions of the site plan resolution , Condition #3 and #7a i. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval of the project. Upon concluding , he responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened . Bonnie Miskal, attorney for the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation . She provided a history of the site and reviewed the previous applications compared to the current proposal. Ms. Miskel discussed the components of the application , which included the FLUM and rezoning , site plan approval, technical deviation of vehicle reservoir length , abandonment of sewer/water and lake maintenance easements. She advised that the applicant and staff had met with neighbors who were concerned with additional traffic that would result from the proposed project. Ms. Miskel shared that her client offered to increase the height of trees that would provide a buffer to the adjacent neighborhood , from 16 to 20 feet. She advised that her client's only remaining concern was the condition requiring them to underground the current overhead utility lines. Discussion ensued and Ms. Miskal responded to Members' questions. Manuel Martinez, on behalf of the applicant, advised that there were ADA accommodations in the amenity areas, but not within the individual residential units. Maryanne Sarner spoke in opposition to the proposed project, citing concerns with additional traffic. Neal Tempel shared his objections to the project, noting the increased traffic from the 1-95 interchange and future expansion of NW 5th Avenue. Kathleen MacDonald agreed that the 1-95 exit on Spanish River had added a lot of traffic on NW 5th Avenue and cautioned against adding more density without the necessary infrastructure. There was no cross examination or rebuttal, and Ms. Miskel concluded her presentation with an appeal to Members for modification of the condition requiring undergrounding of power lines. Members made additional ex parte disclosures, and the public hearing was closed . Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided clarification of the condition in question. He advised that if the undergrounding was not feasible , the applicant would need to submit proof that they had attempted to fulfill the condition. Naresh Machavarapu , Traffic Engineer, provided the results of a traffic study , planned improved signalization and the timeline of widening NW 5th Avenue. Discussion ensued and Members weighed in. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5702. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: Chuck Ridley, political coordinator for the SEIU , requested a meeting with the City Manager to discuss a bonus for its Union members. Irwin Cineus, SEIU Representative, spoke on behalf of the Union members receiving bonuses equal to non­ union employees. Linda Joseph shared her support for the request of Un ion members to receive bonuses. Jack Nixon thanked Council for the student beach parking permit program and highlighted the rise in housing costs for students . He noted the availability of student government coordinators to work with Council Members on initiatives and concluded by highlighting the importance of public education about the danger of rip currents atour~cal beaches . James Garner expressed his support for SEIU members receiving bonuses. Discussion ensued regarding the requests of SEIU members , and there was consensus for the City Manager to meet with Union representatives. Mr. Brown advised that the Union was currently under contract and that the collective bargaining would begin in Spring of 2025. Mr. Brown stated that he would be happy to meet with Union representatives and City staff to learn more about what happened in previous negotiations.

units.text: Mr. Brown requested confirmation regarding the administrative direction given at the previous day's Workshop meeting relating to the public bidding process for the Government Campus Plan , and asked that the following motion be adopted, "That staff be directed, in accordance with the City's administrative policy for managing unsolicited public private partnership proposals and Florida Statutes 255.065, to proceed with the public bidding process for the qualifying projects described in the two unsolicited proposals received by the City , and provided the notice will state that the City has deemed the proposals to be qualifying projects and that the City will accept other proposals for the same project, and to direct staff to set the timeframe for accepting proposals to conclude on Thursday , January 9, 2025." Mr. Brown concluded his report by wishing all a Happy Thanksgiving and thanked Members for their support of adding the day after Thanksgiving to employees' holidays.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 4.32-acre property generally located at 1081 Holland Drive, Conditional Use Approval, pursuant to Section 28-1198, Code of Ordinances to authorize, within the existing approximately 76,000 square foot industrial building, conversion of 28,365 square feet, and the addition of a 1,370 square foot mezzanine, for a large-scale indoor commercial recreation use (a padel facility) in the Manufacturing Industrial (M-3) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-24-01) 1. Resolution No. 141-2024 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 4.32-acre property generally located at 1081 Holland Drive, a site plan approval to authorize, within the existing approximately 76,000 square foot industrial building, conversion of 28,365 square feet, and the addition of a 1,370 square foot mezzanine, for a large­ scale indoor commercial recreation use (a padel facility) and other site improvements, including installation of a sidewalk, together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655, Code of Ordinances, to reduce the number of off-street parking spaces from 173 spaces to 153 spaces; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-24-06) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on items 10.A. and A.1. would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were related. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 10.A. not be approved, no vote would be taken on 10.A.1. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Heather Hansen, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. Ms. Hansen provided a brief background of the proposed Conditional Use and Site Plan Approvals. She advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and Staff recommend approval. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Javier E. Fernandez, attorney for the applicant, responded to Members' questions. Ms. Hansen noted that the square footage of the space should be 28,356 Square feet, and not 28,365 and advised that it would be corrected in the final resolution. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 140-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 141-2024. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan to redesignate the approximately 124.21-acre Boca Raton Innovation Campus (BRIC) property, generally located at 5000 T-Rex Avenue, from Planned Mobility (PM) to Enhanced Mobility (EM); providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-24-05) Mayor Singer noted that this was a transmittal hearing and the first of two public hearings, and three votes would be required to transmit. Peter Begovich, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He discussed the background of the property, zoning, and proposed amendments and land use changes to the Future Land Use Map (FLUM). He advised that Planning and Zoning and Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding, he made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened. Jonathan Ounjian commented about the TR Danburg project, the number of residential units that would be approved with this project and stated that the Zoning should be fair for all zones. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5719 for transmittal. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 19, "Building Regulations," Articles I, Ill, VI and VII, Code of Ordinances, and Chapter 21, "Flood Damage Prevention and Floodplain Management," Article I, Code of Ordinances, to: update the date of the Flood Insurance Study and Flood Insurance Rate Maps, provide a definition of the term "Crown of Road," establish distinctions in required finish floor elevations between new construction and additions to existing buildings and structures in non-special flood hazard areas, adopt provisions and definitions regarding newly established floodways (including sections of the El Rio Canal}, reduce the substantial improvement threshold (from 50% to 49%) and reduce the period for tracking cumulative cost of improvements (from three (3) years to one (1) year); remove obsolete provisions relating to flood-resistant design requirements contained in Section 19-239 and Section 19-240, Code of Ordinances; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date (AM-24-11) Eoin Devlin, Senior Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation. He noted that the City participates in several National Flood Insurance programs and as a result, residents can apply for discounted rates. He reviewed the current statistics and proposed amendments for continued City participation. Mr. Devlin advised that staff recommended approval and made himself available for questions. The public comment period was opened and, seeing no one come forward, closed. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5720. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: The purposes of the meeting are to: provide an opportunity for the City Council, potential responders to the Downtown campus opportunity, and members of the public to have a public discussion before the January 9, 2025 response deadline (" Deadline") and give an opportunity for interested parties to ask questions and have a dialogue; and allow City Council members to confirm their expectations and provide direction for how the City will proceed. Mayor Singer welcomed everyone and provided an overview of the meeting . A chart was shown with a timeline which described the process for receiving proposals, evaluation , ranking, and public discussion opportunities. Members discussed how rapidly the process should proceed . Council Member Wigder gave a presentation on the needs of the Police Headquarters, City Hall , Community Center, and other public facilities in addition to the proposed retail component. Extended discussion ensued . The public comment period was opened . Lorraine Blank cautioned about growing the area beyond its capacity , shared concerns about having a hotel within a few blocks of her home, and the effect on safety and quality of life. Alfred Bonner relayed concerns about the aggressive timeline and encouraged getting more feedback from residents . Jorge Garcia urged staff to take the time to lay out the needs and wants and utilize a schedule. Lauren Bishop inquired about the conservation of the athletic fields . David Kaye shared his opposition to any allowance of City funds to build City offices, suggested the developers rebuild the new Police Station first, asked that the Downtown library be preserved , and that consideration of pedestrians and cyclists be prioritized . Mark Sneckenburg noted the existing traffic congestion in the Downtown and expressed concerns that it would worsen with the proposed development. Cyndi Bloom suggested a schematic or scale model be created for the public to view the proposed development. Seeing no one else come forward , the public comment period was closed . Discussion ensued . The Mayor and City Manager George Brown responded to questions and concerns raised during the public comment period . Further discussion ensued , and CBRE Executive Vice-President Michael McShea answered Members' questions and provided additional information . Council Members stressed their commitment to transparency and to receiving input from the residents . City Attorney Joshua Koehler confirmed that public discussions were permitted , and that after January 9th , private discussions were prohibited . There was consensus to have staff implement the timeline, finalize the space needs for City Hall , continue land-use planning updates, begin work on an interim agreement and start planning the long-term needs for a partnership agreement. There was consensus to approve the timeline for review and public comments . Mr. McShea confirmed that financial plans would be expected from the proposers and that CBRE would create a dashboard to make all of the pertinent information available.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the City's Comprehensive Plan by amending Future Housing Element Policy HO .1.5.3 to create the potential to authorize additional density and intensity for a commercial industrial multifamily development (CIMO) that is integrated with the Boca Raton Tri-Rail Station as a bonus and incentive to encourage such development; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-24-07) 1. Ordinance No. 5716 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zon ing ," Article XV , Division 15, "Affordable and Workforce Housing in Commercial and Industrial Zoning Districts," Code of Ordinances, to create the potential to authorize additional density and intensity for a commercial industrial multifamily development (CIMO) that is integrated with the Boca Raton Tri-Rail Station as a bonus and incentive to encourage such development; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-24-08) 2. Resolution No. 3-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 8.23-acre Boca Raton Tri-Rail Station property generally located at 680 W. Yamato Road , an amendment to an approved site plan (City Council Resolution No. 65-2003) for a commercial industrial multifamily development (CIMO) to authorize the construction of a new eight (8)-story mixed-use building consisting of a 340-unit multi-family complex, including 10% affordable housing units and 5% workforce housing units , and approximately 30,100 square feet of commercial uses , and related site improvements together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655(kk) , Code of Ordinances , to reduce the number of required parking spaces on the property from 793 spaces to 684 spaces (a reduction of 109 spaces) , and four (4) technical deviations from Section 23-190(d), Code of Ordinances, for an internal driveway to: (i) reduce the required width of one ingress lane from 14 feet to 12 feet; (ii) eliminate one (1) of the two (2) required egress lanes, (iii) eliminate a required driveway median , and (iv) reduce a required minimum inbound driveway reseNoir distance from 100 feet to 60 feet; considering the abandonment of a portion of a twelve (12)-foot utility easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-03-22R1) The Mayor announced that the public hearings on items 10.A, 10.A.1 , and 10.A.2 were interrelated , would be heard together and voted upon separately. If item 10.A was not approved , item 10.A. 1 would not be voted on , and if item 10.A. 1 was not approved , there would be no vote for item 10.A.2. He then noted that this would be the second public hearing for Ordinance No. 5715 . The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Council Members disclosed their ex-parte communications . The Clerk gave the oath to those who would be speaking . Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with background information of Ordinance No. 5175 and the subsequent request to amend the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Code Text Amendment. Components of the request were highlighted. Analysis of the project was reviewed and both staff and the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Ms. Rahman proceeded to review the request for a new 8-story mixed-use CIMO. The proposed site plan was shown , and requests for technical deviations were discussed. Renderings of the proposed buildings were shown and Ms. Rahman noted that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , Ms. Rahman made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . David Milledge, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed components of the request and displayed aerial photos of the current subject area and an overlay of the proposed changes to the property. Maps of the pedestrian and traffic circulation and renderings of the building elevations were shown . The requested water easement abandonment and technical deviations were discussed . Upon concluding , Mr. Milledge responded to Council Members' questions about continuity of seNice to the Tri-Rail station . Mr. Schaad , Development SeNices Director, provided additional information regarding the sidewalk addition along Yamato Road. Deputy Mayor Drucker and Council Member Nachlas expressed their support for the Transit Oriented Development. Jonathan Ounjian expressed concerns about the parking requirements , traffic impacts, and that the proposed density would not be extended to nearby properties. Lillia Perez explained her opposition to the project and shared that she felt the City was being overdeveloped . Mark Sneckenburg spoke about current traffic and parking issues in the subject area and his concern that the development would worsen those matters. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . There was no cross examination or summation . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5715. Ordinance No. 5716 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zon ing ," Article XV , Division 15, "Affordable and Workforce Housing in Commercial and Industrial Zoning Districts," Code of Ordinances, to create the potential to authorize additional density and intensity for a commercial industrial multifamily development (CIMO) that is integrated with the Boca Raton Tri-Rail Station as a bonus and incentive to encourage such development; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-24-08) 2. Resolution No. 3-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 8.23-acre Boca Raton Tri-Rail Station property generally located at 680 W. Yamato Road , an amendment to an approved site plan (City Council Resolution No. 65-2003) for a commercial industrial multifamily development (CIMO) to authorize the construction of a new eight (8)-story mixed-use building consisting of a 340-unit multi-family complex, including 10% affordable housing units and 5% workforce housing units , and approximately 30,100 square feet of commercial uses , and related site improvements together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655(kk) , Code of Ordinances , to reduce the number of required parking spaces on the property from 793 spaces to 684 spaces (a reduction of 109 spaces) , and four (4) technical deviations from Section 23-190(d), Code of Ordinances, for an internal driveway to: (i) reduce the required width of one ingress lane from 14 feet to 12 feet; (ii) eliminate one (1) of the two (2) required egress lanes, (iii) eliminate a required driveway median , and (iv) reduce a required minimum inbound driveway reseNoir distance from 100 feet to 60 feet; considering the abandonment of a portion of a twelve (12)-foot utility easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-03-22R1) The Mayor announced that the public hearings on items 10.A, 10.A.1 , and 10.A.2 were interrelated , would be heard together and voted upon separately. If item 10.A was not approved , item 10.A. 1 would not be voted on , and if item 10.A. 1 was not approved , there would be no vote for item 10.A.2. He then noted that this would be the second public hearing for Ordinance No. 5715 . The City Attorney reviewed the quasi-judicial procedures that would govern the public hearings. Council Members disclosed their ex-parte communications . The Clerk gave the oath to those who would be speaking . Tamash Rahman, Chief Planner, gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with background information of Ordinance No. 5175 and the subsequent request to amend the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Code Text Amendment. Components of the request were highlighted. Analysis of the project was reviewed and both staff and the Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval. Ms. Rahman proceeded to review the request for a new 8-story mixed-use CIMO. The proposed site plan was shown , and requests for technical deviations were discussed. Renderings of the proposed buildings were shown and Ms. Rahman noted that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , Ms. Rahman made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . David Milledge, on behalf of the applicant, gave a PowerPoint presentation. He reviewed components of the request and displayed aerial photos of the current subject area and an overlay of the proposed changes to the property. Maps of the pedestrian and traffic circulation and renderings of the building elevations were shown . The requested water easement abandonment and technical deviations were discussed . Upon concluding , Mr. Milledge responded to Council Members' questions about continuity of seNice to the Tri-Rail station . Mr. Schaad , Development SeNices Director, provided additional information regarding the sidewalk addition along Yamato Road. Deputy Mayor Drucker and Council Member Nachlas expressed their support for the Transit Oriented Development. Jonathan Ounjian expressed concerns about the parking requirements , traffic impacts, and that the proposed density would not be extended to nearby properties. Lillia Perez explained her opposition to the project and shared that she felt the City was being overdeveloped . Mark Sneckenburg spoke about current traffic and parking issues in the subject area and his concern that the development would worsen those matters. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . There was no cross examination or summation . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5715. John Blount, Chris Inman, Colby Wohlub, Preston Hoover, Jonathan Ounjian, Martin Arrive, Jon Schwartz, Vic Rose, Jorge Garcia, Rudy Havelka, Mark Jacobson, Juan Caycedo, Aracibo Quintana, Nicholas Ferraro, T.W. Anderson, Derek Vander Ploeg, Bruce Retzsch, Amber Tollefson, shared their support of the project, identified Terra Frisbie or Related Ross as their preferred partner and highlighted the topics of greenspace, retail and commercial space, sense of place, company reputation, and the opportunity for high level jobs. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 24-2025 as amended with the ranking of Terra Frisbie ranked as first and Related Ross as second. Mr. Koehler advised that with the adoption of Resolution No. 24-2025, the cone of silence was no longer in effect.

units.text: 1. Resolution No. 18-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for the approximately 28.89-acre property generally located at 6600 North Military Trail, an amendment to an approved site plan (Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 08-20) for a Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development (CIMO), construction of which will be in four phases, to include: in Phase I, the demolition of 245,983 square feet of office; in Phase II, the construction of 42,840 square feet of commercial retail and restaurant use; in Phase 111, the construction of a 36,396 square foot fitness and wellness facility; and Phase IV, the construction of an eight (8)-story, 500-unit multi-family residential building, inclusive of 10% affordable housing units (with all non-residential uses expressly conditioned upon the timely completion of Phase IV), and related site improvements including the installation of walkways and landscaping; together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655, Code of Ordinances, to temporarily reduce the number of required parking spaces from 1,166 spaces to 1,160 spaces (a reduction of 6 spaces during Phases I, II and Ill); considering the abandonment of multiple portions [two (2) 20-foot and one (1) 32-foot] of a utility easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date. (SPA-06-08/CIMD) The City Attorney confirmed the quasi-judicial procedures were still in effect which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Planner Heather Waldstein gave the PowerPoint presentation. She gave a brief history of the project, technical deviations, phased site plan, multimodal plans, and site plan elevations. She advised the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. She reviewed the revisions and applicant requested modifications. Upon concluding, she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued. Ms. Waldstein provided clarity and answered Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Attorneys for the applicant, Bonnie Miske! and David Milledge, provided clarification by reading into the record revisions to proposed conditions. Discussion ensued. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the project and his support for additional development in the area. Juan Caycedo, designer for the project, spoke favorably and urged Council's approval. David Milledge made final comments and thanked the Council for their consideration. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 18-2025 as amended. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. The meeting was recessed 9:45 PM and resumed at 9:59 PM.

Ordinance No. 5719 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan to redesignate the approximately 124.21-acre Boca Raton Innovation Campus (BRIC) property, generally located at 5000 T-Rex Avenue, from Planned Mobility (PM) to Enhanced Mobility (EM); providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-24-05) The Mayor advised that this was the second of two public hearings and that four votes would be required for approval. Paul Polcyn spoke against the project and advised that his community HOA had been neglected by the potential adjacent development. Richard DeWitt, attorney for property owners at Telecom 1 & 2, cited concerns with spot zoning and requested this item be tabled for revision or denied. Leslie Del Monte expressed apprehension regarding spot zoning for the proposed property and urged inclusion of the surrounding properties. Bonnie Miske! clarified information shared during public comments. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the amendment and future development. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5719. Richard DeWitt, attorney for property owners at Telecom 1 & 2, cited concerns with spot zoning and requested this item be tabled for revision or denied. Leslie Del Monte expressed apprehension regarding spot zoning for the proposed property and urged inclusion of the surrounding properties. Bonnie Miske! clarified information shared during public comments. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of the amendment and future development. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5719. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: 1. Reports from Staff and CBRE Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik provided the update. He noted changes to the timeline and highlighted the major milestones. 2. Public Comment Daniel Kleeman , Monique Rambo, and Andrew Wade expressed concerns about traffic, pedestrian safety , noise, overcrowding , recreation , and limiting development of retail and commercial buildings. City Manager George Brown responded to questions raised and advised that additional traffic enforcement was being implemented Downtown . Mr. Brown also noted that the City intends to replace all existing tennis courts with the addition of four more , and that every recreational amenity currently in the Downtown will be replaced , but not necessarily in their current locations. Margit Parkinson , Cheryl Fisher, Jason Esposito , Judy Morrow, Lucas Ross, Patricia Dervisai , Angela Mazzei, Rickie Black, Patricia Spinella , Alexandra Avalas , Heidi Claire, Nancy Beaver, and Shannon Otto spoke in opposition to the project. 3. Approval of Interim Agreement with Boca Raton City Center, LLC (i) Resolution 42-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton , Florida , authorizing the City Manager to execute an interim agreement with Boca Raton City Center, LLC (Terra/Frisbie) for the Downtown Campus Project; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution 42-2025. Members thanked residents for coming to the meeting and speaking. They assured citizens of the City's commitments to parks and recreation , advised that public input would be welcomed throughout the process of the Downtown redevelopment, and asked that those in attendance share the facts provided by staff at the meeting and on the City 's website. Council Member Andy Thomson suggested amending the resolution to add a provision prohibiting the P3 partner from contributing to the political campaigns of City elected officials. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson to amend Resolution No. 42-2025 to include language to prevent the Downtown Redevelopment partner from contributing to Council Members political campaigns. Motion died for lack of a second. City Attorney Joshua Koehler explained a previous clause from 2002 preventing Members from accepting political campaign contributions. Members weighed in and expressed concerns with the language proposed by Mr. Thomson. Extended discussion ensued and Members suggested alternative amendments. Council Member Nachlas suggested language to require adherence to the State and County ethics laws. Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to amend the Resolution to include adherence to State and County ethics laws. Mr. Kohler read the language into the record. Motion to amend was approved on a vote of 4 to 1, with Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. Members confirmed with the City Attorney that additional changes to the timeline could be made in the future . Motion to approve Resolution No. 42-2025 as amended passed on a vote of 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. The meeting recessed at 8:18 PM and resumed at 8:36 PM.

units.text: 1. Resolution No. 39-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 5. 98-acre property generally located at 5801 Congress Avenue, Conditional Use Approval , pursuant to Section 28-978 , Code of Ordinances, to authorize an 11 ,980 square foot athletic training facility in an existing 47,116 square foot warehouse and office building , in the Light Industrial Research Park (LIRP) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-24-02) 2. Resolution No. 40-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 5.98-acre property generally located at 5801 Congress Avenue, an amendment to an approved site plan (amending Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 06-14) to authorize minor site improvements including updating tabular data for a new athletic training facility use on the property , restriping portions of the surface parking area , providing a new six (6) foot sidewalk for a section of the property frontage along Northwest Broken Sound Parkway, increasing the existing sidewalk width to six (6) feet for a section of the property frontage along Northwest Broken Sound Parkway , and increasing the existing sidewalk width to six (6) feet for the property frontage along Congress Avenue providing interior crosswalks and additional landscaping , together with a technical deviation from Section 28-1655 , Code of Ordinances , to reduce the number of off­ street parking spaces from 139 spaces to 127 spaces; providing for repealer and specifically repealing Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 82-51 ; providing an effective date (SPA-06-09R1) The Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation. He provided a background of the property and reviewed the conditional use, site plan amendment, and a requested technical deviation. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions . Discussion ensued and Mr. Devlin answered Members' questions regarding the parking reduction requirement. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant David Milledge answered Members' questions. John Donaldson provided additional details on the parking requirement reduction . Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . There was no cross examination or summation . Motion was made by Council Member Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 39-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 40-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering an appeal of the Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 2025-001 , which approved a site plan amendment for an approximately 3.0-acre property generally located at 1001 East Telecom Drive, to authorize construction of a 10,860 square foot free-standing emergency room and related site improvements, including three (3) techn ical deviations: (i) from Section 23-190(d )2, Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance for the westernmost driveway on East Telecom Drive from 25 feet to 13.74 feet, (ii) from Section 28-1655 , Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required number of vehicle parking spaces from 120 spaces to 82 spaces, and (iii) from Section 28-1651 (1)(d), Code of Ordinances, to increase the maximum number of reserved parking spaces from five (5) spaces to nine (9) spaces; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-03-13R1) The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation. He gave a description of the location, parking requirements , and compatibility with the proposed area. He continued with the description of the site plan , the permitted uses, and the appellants arguments against the proposed development and use. Mr. Devlin advised that Planning and Zoning Board approved the project by a 4-1 vote, staff affirms their decision and recommends approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued and Mr. Devlin answered Members' questions and provided additional clarification . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson , to extend the meeting beyond 11 :00 pm. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote. The publ ic hearing was opened. Attorney for the appellant Bonnie Miskel gave the presentation . She gave a summary of the appeal justification and provided the following reasons : not a permitted use, parking requirements were not met, and surgical procedures requiring an overnight stay could be performed. She continued by stating precedent from similar cases. Brian Kelly , Traffic Engineer for the appellant, provided the technical deviations for the parking and throat distance requirement. Discussion ensued . Attorney for the applicant Michael Marshall provided a timeline of the original application submittal and advised that it was passed without objection. Kenneth Jones, CEO of HCA Northwest Hospital , gave a background of the company 's Free Standing Emergency Room (FSER) facilities , benefits to the community , and the staffing and parking requirements. Lindsay Li bes with WGI Engineering gave her professional opinion agreeing with this use of the Medical Office. Mr. Marshall continued with case law examples . Discussion ensued . John Donaldson , Traffic Engineer, provided additional information and details. The public comment period was opened . Ross Donahue, Gershen Zwirez , Glen Golish , Juan Caycedo, Steven Alter, Issac Newman , Michael Zimmerman , and Chaim Glazer spoke in favor of the project. Dr. Ari Wirtschafter and Dr. Evan Goldstein expressed their opposition to the facility . Dr. Robert Bader relayed his experiences with emergency services. Scott Zaslov, attorney for the appellant, provided the definition for a FSER and an urgent care facility . Bonnie Miskel cited case law and provided final comments. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Michael Marshall, attorney for the original applicant, provided his summation . Kenneth Jones provided additional details and answered Members' questions. The meeting was recessed at 1:06 AM and resumed at 1:20 AM . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder to continue until the next meeting. Discussion ensued and additional information was provided by Development Services Director Brandon Schaad and Kenneth Jones. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer to continue Resolution No. 34-2025 to the April 8, 2025, Regular City Council Meeting. Motion carried on a 4 to 1 vote. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Yvette Drucker, Council Member Fran Nachlas, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no.

units.text: 1. Resolution No. 45-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 10.0-acre property generally located at 791 Park of Commerce Boulevard , a conditional use approval , pursuant to Section 28-978 , Code of Ordinances , to authorize an approximately 72,400 square foot amateur recreation use in an existing approximately 130,510 square foot office building , in the Light Industrial and Research Park (LIRP) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-24-05) 2. Resolution No. 46-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 10.0-acre property generally located at 791 Park of Commerce Boulevard , an amendment to an approved site plan (Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 99-03) to authorize a Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development (CIMO) including: (a) conversion of the existing approximately 130,510 square foot office building to a mix of uses, including a fast-casual restaurant with 11 ,447 square feet of indoor area and 2,570 square foot of outdoor dining , a 72 ,428 square foot amateur recreation facility , and 46,635 square feet of office space; and (b) construction of 243 multifamily residential units, including 10% affordable and 5% workforce units, with 226 units in an eight (8)-story apartment building with an eight (8)-level integrated parking structure and 17 units in five (5) , three (3)-story townhome-style buildings; together with a technical deviation from Section 23-190(b) , Code of Ordinances, to increase the maximum length of two (2) parking rows from 250 feet to 296 feet; and considering the abandonment of a portion of a 12- foot waterline easement; providing for repealer and specifically repealing Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 93-12; providing an effective date (SPA-98-34R1) The Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1 . not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Heather Hansen gave the PowerPoint presentation . She reviewed the site plans which included an integrated parking structure, residential tower, townhomes, restaurant, and an indoor sports facility . She advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional answers to Members' questions and advised that staff was researching the CIMO requirements for public transportation . The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant Ele Zachariades gave a brief PowerPoint presentation which reviewed the proposed buildings and site plans . Ms. Zachariades advised that her client was not asking for any variances and only one technical deviation for the parking . She concluded by showing renderings of the proposed project and then made herself available for questions. Engineer for the applicant John Donaldson provided additional information. Jonathan Ounjian shared his support for the project but had concerns with the units per acre and the transit program. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . • Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 45-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 46-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: 1. Resolution No. 34-2025 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering an appeal of the Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 2025-001 , which approved a site plan amendment for an approximately 3.0-acre property generally located at 1001 East Telecom Drive, to authorize construction of a 10,860 square foot free-standing emergency room and related site improvements, including three (3) technical deviations: (i) from Section 23-190(d)2 , Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance for the westernmost driveway on East Telecom Drive from 25 feet to 13.74 feet, (ii) from Section 28-1655 , Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required number of vehicle parking spaces from 120 spaces to 82 spaces, and (iii) from Section 28-1651(1)(d) , Code of Ordinances, to increase the maximum number of reserved parking spaces from five (5) spaces to nine (9) spaces; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-03-13R1) The Mayor noted that an extensive quasi-judicial public hearing had been held on March 18, 2025 , during which both parties presented evidence , testimony , and argument. He advised that the hearing had been formally closed but that, due to the passage of time, both parties had been invited to submit a recap of their March 18th presentations , and they would be afforded 10 minutes each to address the City Council. The City Attorney confirmed that the quasi-judicial procedures would still govern the limited public hearing. Council Members made ex parte disclosures that occurred since the March 18, 2025, public hearing and it was confirmed that the individuals speaking at this continued public hearing had been duly sworn at the beginning of the March 18th hearing. The public hearing was reopened . Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave a brief recap and addressed comments made from the previous meeting. He re iterated that a free-standing emergency room was a permitted use in the area and that the requested technical deviation for the driveway reservoir wou ld not interfere with multi-modal improvements. Mr. Schaad also advised that the applicant's accompanying design requirements were the deciding factor in the approval of the reduced parking requirements. Bonnie Miskel, attorney for the appellant, provided a recap and advised that her client's main objections were to the parking reduction , the driveway reservoir reduction , and the free­ standing emergency medical room use. Ms. Miskel stated that the operational plan for the driveway was not available for the Planning and Zoning Board 's review and that the parking provided would be insufficient to meet future demand. The Mayor noted that Ms. Miskel had been afforded 59 additional seconds and that this would be provided to the applicant, as well. Ms. Miskel then responded to Members' questions. Michael Marshall, attorney for the applicant, provided a review of his applicant's case. He reminded Council Members that the application had been approved by the Planning and Zoning Board and by City staff, and that the burden was on the appellant to support their case. Mr. Marshall stated that the medical office use was permitted in the subject location, that information provided by the appellant was hypothetical , and that he did not believe the appellant had provided evidence to support their objection to the parking reduction. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Mayor Singer noted that Mr. Marshall had received an additional 13 seconds and asked Ms. Miskel if she would like the same amount of time, which she declined. The public hearing was closed. The Mayor then reviewed the voting options available to Council. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 34-2025 and grant the appeal. Members made final comments. There was consensus regarding the need for additional medical resources , but Members shared concerns about the technical requirements and proposed parking . Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

Michael Marshall, attorney for the applicant, provided a review of his applicant's case. He reminded Council Members that the application had been approved by the Planning and Zoning Board and by City staff, and that the burden was on the appellant to support their case. Mr. Marshall stated that the medical office use was permitted in the subject location, that information provided by the appellant was hypothetical , and that he did not believe the appellant had provided evidence to support their objection to the parking reduction. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. Mayor Singer noted that Mr. Marshall had received an additional 13 seconds and asked Ms. Miskel if she would like the same amount of time, which she declined. The public hearing was closed. The Mayor then reviewed the voting options available to Council. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 34-2025 and grant the appeal. Members made final comments. There was consensus regarding the need for additional medical resources , but Members shared concerns about the technical requirements and proposed parking . Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the Boca Raton Christian School , an approximately 19. 84-acre property generally located at 470 Northwest 4th Avenue, five (5) technical deviations from Section 23-190(d) , Code of Ordinances, as follows: (i) for an existing driveway on Northwest 4th Avenue, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance from 100 feet to 25 feet, (ii) for an existing driveway on Crawford Boulevard , to reduce in the required driveway reservoir distance from 100 feet to 15 feet, eliminate a required four (4) foot wide median separator, and to reduce the required number of egress lanes from two (2) to one (1 ), and (iii) for an existing driveway on Northwest 7th Street, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance from 100 feet to 40 feet; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-25-04) The Mayor advised that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated . He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi­ judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex-pa rte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Jacob German , Planner II , gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a review of the applicant's request, including the project location , history of the school's 2008 master plan , and approved site plan . Mr. German advised that staff supported the requested technical deviations, and he shared a drawing of the property's queuing diagram. Staff analysis found the proposed project was consistent and compatible with the City's Comprehensive Plan . The Planning and Zoning Board and Staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , Mr. German responded to Council Members' questions and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. The public hearing was opened . Bonnie Miske!, representing the applicant, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation which reviewed the proposed conditional use and technical deviations. Pastor Cameron Free , speaking on behalf of the school , provided additional information on the history of the school and asked for Council's support. Project architect Juliet Schiff and traffic engineer John Donaldson provided additional information. Ms. Miske! concluded by reviewing the criteria for the technical deviation of driveways and made herself and her colleagues available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . There was no cross examination or summation . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 55-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering the application of 1489 Mortgagee, LLC , for a settlement and reduction of one (1) code enforcement lien imposed against property located at 1489 West Palmetto Park Road ; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Development Services Deputy Director Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation and provided a case summary of the code violations that led to the lien. She advised that staff recommended a 75% reduction of the total lien and , upon concluding , responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened . Elle Zachariades , attorney for the owner, gave a brief PowerPoint presentation, provided additional information about the property , and noted that the lien had been applied under the building 's previous owners. Anuj Grover, on behalf of Grover Corlew, described the timeline for the purchase of the property. Ms. Zachariades concluded by requesting a 100% reduction of the fine . Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 53-2025 and impose the reduced fine of $30,000. Discussion ensued and Council Members weighed in . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder to further reduce the fine to $7,500. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson to reduce the fine to $0. The discussion continued and Ms. Zachariades, Mr. Grover, Mr. Schaad and City Attorney Joshua Koehler provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to amend the motion on the floor and approve Resolution No. 53-2025 with a reduction of 100% of the lien. Motion to amend passed unanimously on a voice vote. Mr. Brown clarified that Section 1 of the resolution would now reflect that the total amount of the lien due was zero. Motion to approve Resolution No. 53-2025 as amended carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 53-2025 and impose the reduced fine of $30,000. Discussion ensued and Council Members weighed in . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder to further reduce the fine to $7,500. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson to reduce the fine to $0. The discussion continued and Ms. Zachariades, Mr. Grover, Mr. Schaad and City Attorney Joshua Koehler provided additional information. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to amend the motion on the floor and approve Resolution No. 53-2025 with a reduction of 100% of the lien. Motion to amend passed unanimously on a voice vote. Mr. Brown clarified that Section 1 of the resolution would now reflect that the total amount of the lien due was zero. Motion to approve Resolution No. 53-2025 as amended carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton , Florida, rejecting a recommendation issued pursuant to Section 70.51 , Florida Statutes, known as the "Florida Land Use and Environmental Dispute Resolution Act" (FLUEDRA), regarding approximately 4 acres of predominantly submerged real property adjacent to the lntracoastal Waterway , located at 3000 NE 8th Avenue and owned by NE 32nd Street, LLC; providing for a written decision regarding allowable uses; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date City Manager George Brown provided an overview of the proposed resolution and history of the submerged property at NE 8th Avenue. He advised that staff supported the adoption of the resolution . City Attorney Josh Koehler reviewed the legal issues pertaining to the property. Hope Calhoun, attorney for the property owner, advised that they did not support the denial of this Resolution and asked that the property owner be allowed to fill the submerged land and develop the property. William Swaim, owner of the property, also urged Council Members to reject the recommendation by staff. Mr. Koehler provided legal details and responded to Members' questions. Further discussion ensued . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 81-2025. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, and Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. The motion passed 4 to 1.

units.text: 1. Reports from Staff and CBRE Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik provided an update to the interim master plan and advised that a voice vote could be taken to approve the amended changes to the uses, densities, and intensity. Discussion ensued. Council Member Drucker advised that this master plan should include a transit hub. Deputy Mayor Nachlas also supported the addition of a transit hub and enhanced recreation . Council Member Wigder thanked staff and the consultants for their work and advised that this was a checkpoint along a long path . Mayor Singer advised that there would be more public outreach in the future and plans would continue to evolve. 2. Public Comment Judy Morrow spoke in support of keeping tennis in the Downtown area and urged Council to build eight courts in both the Downtown and Meadows Park. Jon Pearlman expressed his opposition to the Government Campus Redevelopment. Evan Bennett spoke against over development, questioned the bifurcation of the Police Station, and the size of City Hall. Patty Dervishi shared concerns about over development of the Downtown . Alexandra Avala spoke against the redevelopment of the Government Campus. Mayor Singer and City Manager George Brown offered additional information and reiterated that plans have been downsized and would continue to develop. Council Member Thomson noted that the City was offering a sensible and responsible development for both the green space , recreation, and government facilities but stated that he was concerned with the amount of commercial development. He advised that he would not support tonight's Interim Plan as presented. Extended discussion ensued . Council Member Drucker proposed a transit hub and reiterated that the scale and scope of the project has been downsized. Council Member Wigder explained that the P3 partnership was necessary for the affordability of the Government Campus. Council Member Thomson advised that the residents' questions needed to be addressed before he would vote in favor of the plan. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve staff to move forward on the Interim Master Plan. Additional discussion ensued . Motion passed on a vote of 4 to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. The meeting was recessed at 8: 11 PM and resumed at 8:24 PM .

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to an approved site plan (Resolution No. 57-2014, as amended by Resolution No. 91-2016) for a Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development (CIMO) to authorize construction, in Phase II of a Planned Mobility Development (PMD) Master Plan, a new seven (?)­ story, 289-unit multi-family residential building, including 10% affordable and 5% workforce housing units, a parking structure and related site improvements, together with one (1) technical deviation from Section 23-190(d)2 , Code of Ordinances, to reduce the required driveway reservoir distance for the easternmost driveway on Northwest Broken Sound Parkway from 100 feet to 70 feet; for the property generally located at 850 and 900 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PMD-13-01 R4/SPA/CIMD) The Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1 . not be approved, no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an overview of the property location, history, proposed zoning amendments, and technical deviations. He advised that the Community Advisory Board recommended approval with modifications, and they were subsequently incorporated into the plans. He further advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval and , upon concluding, made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . Beth Thomson, the attorney for the applicant, answered Members' questions and Director of Development Services Brandon Schaad provided additional details. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Thomson thanked the applicant for including affordable and workforce housing in the plans. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 78-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1 . not be approved, no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with an overview of the property location, history, proposed zoning amendments, and technical deviations. He advised that the Community Advisory Board recommended approval with modifications, and they were subsequently incorporated into the plans. He further advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval and , upon concluding, made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . Beth Thomson, the attorney for the applicant, answered Members' questions and Director of Development Services Brandon Schaad provided additional details. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Council Member Thomson thanked the applicant for including affordable and workforce housing in the plans. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 78-2025. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: 1. Reports from Staff and CBRE Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik gave an update on the phasing , economic impacts, benefits to the community, and advised that all information has been posted to the City 's website. 2. Public Comment Brett Lassen , Arianna Curia, Joe Majhess , Yvonne Zurn Tobel, Lorraine Blank , Rita Head , Elaine DiCostanzo, Jon Pearlman , Joseph Gambarelli, Lucas Ross, Lyudmilla Pearlman , Joe Graubart, Patti Dervishi , Jon Ounjian , Judy Morrow, Kevin Meaney, Holly Schutler, Natasha Rattray, Pedro Voyer, James Hendrey, Greg Ryan , Felipe Ramirez, David Kaiyalethe, Patricia Spinella, Christina Restepo, Lori Colbert, Alexandra Avela , Monique Rambo. Robert DuKate, Kimberly Patton , and Tom Reid all spoke in opposition to the Government Campus Project. Vic Rose spoke in favor of the project. The meeting recessed at 8:23 PM and resumed at 8:35 PM . Mayor Singer and City Manager George Brown addressed questions raised during public comments . Mr. Brown advised that the current Police Station is well past its usable life and needs to be in a new, larger location . He continued by highlighting the purchase of 6551 Park of Commerce and noted that the Building and Code Departments were scheduled for relocation to utilize previously allocated funds. Discussion ensued and Members weighed in . Council Member Marc Wigder advised that all the buildings on the current campus are past their useable life, need to be replaced , and all of the cost analysis needed to be completed before finalizing the plans. Deputy Mayor Nachlas advised that she had spoken to many people, would continue to reach out to anyone who contacted her, and represented all residents of the City no matter where in the City they lived . units.text: 1. Ordinance No. 5737 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering an amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan by redesignating certain property consisting of approximately 0.70 acres generally located at 5458 Town Center Road and 1 Town Center Road, from Planned Mobility (PM) to Conservation (N) ; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC- 25-03) The Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1. not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining item . The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Heather Waldstein gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by giving the history of the property, detailed the location , the proposed amendments , designated preserve area, and site plans. She reviewed the proposed recommendations from the Planning and Zoning Board and Environmental Advisory Board. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval 5 to 2 and the Environmental Advisory Board voted 4 to 1 to deny the project. Staff recommended approval. The public comment period was opened. Attorney for the applicant Bonnie Miska! made herself available for questions. Karen Golembeski spoke in favor of saving the preserve and urged Council to deny the project. Isaac Shalom asked Council for more time to review the proposed project. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of protecting the preserve. Bonnie Miska! advised that she would work with the affected neighbor. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information . 2. Resolution No. 80-2025 A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 18. 59-acre property generally located at 5458 Town Center Road and 1 Town Center Road , an amended and restated site plan approval consolidating Palm Beach County Resolution Nos. 76-1168, 88-1210 , 89-0711 , and 90-1295, and authorizing: (i) the reduction of an existing environmental preserve area from 2.1 acres to 0.70 acres (reduction of 1.4 acres) ; (ii) the creation of a new approximately 0.70- acre preserve area, and (iii) installation of new landscape and hardscape improvements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-25-03) Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5737. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 80-2025. Discussion ensued. Ms. Waldstein provided additional information relating to the preserve and maintenance of it. ' Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 4.1-acre property generally located at 1141 South Rogers Circle, an amended and restated conditional use approval (amending and restating Resolution No. 23-2014, as amended by Resolution No. 1-2016) for the Barrel of Monks Brewery , to amend the conditions of approval to (a) expand the accessory brewery tasting area from approximately 867 square feet of interior space to approximately 1,728 square feet of interior space and approximately 1,000 square feet of outdoor patio space; (b) change the hours of operation of the accessory tasting areas; (c) authorize the incidental sale of beverages not manufactured at the brewery; and (d) allow the serving and consumption of alcohol in the outdoor patio tasting area; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-13-04R2) The City Attorney confirmed that the Quasi-Judicial procedures are still in effect. She provided a location of the site, reviewed the applicant request which included increasing the tasting area , and changes to hours of operation and other operational characteristics. She advised that this amendment would bring the business into compliance with its current operating conditions. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval, and upon concluding , Ms. Hansen made herself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant Ele Zachariades gave a PowerPoint presentation . She gave a brief history of the proposed amendments that would bring the property and uses to be brought up to code. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to approve Resolution No. 100-2025. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 4.06-acre property generally located at 202 West Yamato Road , an amendment to an approved Universal Conditional (UC) rezoning ordinance (Ordinance No. 4500) , to delete a restriction that prohibits free-standing restaurant buildings with drive-throughs; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-99-02R3) Senior Planner Heather Hansen gave the PowerPoint presentation . Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5736. Motion carried 4 to 0; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: City Manager George Brown gave a brief summary of the purpose for the meeting and introduced recruiter David Deutsch . Mayor Scott Singer summarized the objective for the day. An opportunity was provided for the public to speak. Seeing no one come forward , the public comment period was closed . Discussion ensued regarding the questions that would be asked during the interviews. Members identified seven questions to ask each candidate and the interviews began . Jorge Camejo offered a brief introduction and was interviewed by Council Members. The meeting recessed at 10:10 am and resumed at 10:20 am. Mark Sohaney offered a brief introduction and was interviewed by Council Members. The meeting recessed at 11 :15 am and resumed at 11 :23 am. Patrick Jordan offered a brief introduction and was interviewed by Council Members. The meeting recessed for lunch at 12:09 pm and resumed at 1:00 pm. Jim Zervis offered a brief introduction and was interviewed by Council Members. The meeting recessed at 2:00 pm and resumed at 2:14 pm. Stan Morris offered a brief introduction and was interviewed by Council Members. The meeting recessed at 3:03 pm and resumed at 3:16 pm . Mayor Singer expressed his appreciation to Mr. Brown for his decades of service and thanked David Deutsch for his assistance with the recruiting process. Mayor Singer then thanked all of the applicants, praised their accomplishments, recognized the service of those applicants who are City employees, and noted the strength of the applicant pool. = Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to appoint Mark Sohaney to the position of City Manager. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson to appoint Jim Zervis to the position of City Manager. The Mayor and all Council Members expressed gratitude to the applicants and appreciation for the service of the internal applicants. Mayor Singer offered his services as a contract talks facilitator to work with the City Attorney on terms of the new City Manager contract, subject to final approval by the Council. There was consensus from Members to have the Mayor work with the attorney as facilitator, and that, within a year, the new City Manager move to within , or 5 miles from , the City limits. Motion to appoint Mark Sohaney to the position of City Manager, with the condition that the City Manager live within 5 miles of the City limits of Boca Raton, passed unanimously on a voice vote. Discussion ensued regarding terms of the contract and Mr. Koehler advised that Mr. Brown's employment contract was still in effect. Mr. Brown noted that he intended to work until January 4, 2026 , but that he was willing to work on the transition period desired by Council. He advised that a contract for the new City Manager could be ready for consideration at the September 9th City Council meeting.
