units.text: 1. Reports from Staff and CBRE Deputy City Manager Andrew Lukasik and Principal of Frisbie Group , Rob Frisbie, provided an update on the Government Campus Redevelopment project. Items highlighted included the construction of a new state~of-the-art Community Center, City Hall with Council Chambers , and recreational amenities . The project also focuses on enhancing transportation and infrastructure, with efforts to slow traffic speeds through increased landscaping and traffic calming devices. The project was proposed to be developed in phases, with the first phase including the civic buildings , mixed-use residential , and retail spaces, as well as children's playgrounds. The second phase would incorporate office spaces, a hotel , residential units, and restaurants . Off-site developments and improvements included a new tennis center and courts at Meadows Park, preserving the Singing Pines historical building with additional parking , and creating a community garden at the North Park location . Other parks would also see improvements, including new softball fields , restrooms , a nature trail , batting cages , and a concession stand . A skate park was proposed to be built at North Park in conjunction with the Beach and Park District. Mr. Frisbie noted that the project was expected to generate over $3 billion in economic impact. City Manager George Brown provided a brief history of Memorial Park and the surrounding property. 2. Public Comment Bob Tucker spoke in favor of the Government Campus Project. Joe Majhess, Max Viciedo, Martha Parker, Lisa Mulhall , Stacey Sipple, Mary Powers, Mac Johnson , Jan Sjostrom, Sandi Medlicott, Kevin Meanay, Barbara Powers , Barry Goldin , Jonathan Ounjian , Alex Pollock, Pam Paschke, Lyudmila Pearlman , Betsy Nieporte, Jon Pearlman , Holly Schuttler, Buffy Tucker, Mark Grosberg , Eddie Morris, Lucas Ross , Richard Warner, Keith Nelson , Bob Sloane, all spoke in opposition to the Government Campus Project. The meeting recessed at 8:27 PM and resumed at 8:40 PM . Kolin Kraft, Kathleen Kraft, Silke Dodel, Christopher Ferrer, Robert Otto, Shannon Otto, June Wagner, Elizabeth Decker, Laurie Colbert, Judy Morrow, Ivana Pace, Mary Louise Cammorata , Aphrodite Petinakis, Meredith Madsen , John Linn , Barry Smith , Frank Paton , Alexandra Avelar, Michael Schneider, all spoke in opposition to the Government Campus Project. Mayor Singer, City Manager George Brown , and Deputy City Manager/ CFO James Zervis provided additional information , clarification , and details in response to questions raised during public comments. Discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson thanked everyone for their participation and advised that he was against the scope and scale of this project and would continue to ask that the City to fund the project on its own. Mr. Thomson also mentioned past litigation involving the Terra and Frisbe Group. Michael Thomas, counsel for the Terra Frisbie Group (TFG) advised that they had no culpability in the Surfside Towers collapse and that it will have no effect on their ability to develop this project. Deputy Mayor Nachlas thanked everyone for coming out and stated that, although she lives west of 1-95, she represents all of the City and has not made a final decision on the project. Council Member Wigder thanked the public for coming out and providing their input. He advised that the City should continue doing their due diligence and referenced The Center for Cultural Arts project as an example of a project that did not meet requirements and did not go forward , adding that the City has a duty to not raise taxes and a P3 partnership would be beneficial by allowing alternate funding . Council Member Drucker clarified comments made earlier in the meeting , advised that it is the duty of the Council to be fiscally responsible when making these decisions, and asked the public to continue to provide constructive feedback. Mayor Singer reminded everyone that no vote would take place tonight and stated that this process should continue to get feedback and outreach from the public. The meeting recessed at 10:38 PM and resumed at 10:49 PM . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Andy Thomson, to extend the meeting beyond 11.·00 PM. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote .

Resolution No. 104-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 2.17 acre property generally located at 6800 North Federal Highway, a Planned Development (PD) master plan and a site plan , pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request , to authorize construction of a total of 20 residential units comprised of 16 units in eight (8) , two (2)-story, approximately 21 foot , eight (8)-inch tall duplex buildings and one (1 ), four (4)-unit, two (2)-story approximately 21 foot eight (8)-inch tall townhouse building , and related on-site and off-site improvements including sidewalks in the Appleby Street and Berkeley Street rights-of-way ; approving modifications of development parameters for plot width , plot depth , plot coverage , required yards, balcony encroachments, pool deck encroachments, pool setbacks, perimeter building setbacks, landscaped perimeter yards , and right-of-way width; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date (UC- 23-02/PD/SPA) 5. Resolution No. 105-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 1.08 acre property generally located at 6750 North Federal Highway , the abandonment of a 6,049 square foot portion of a required 25-foot-wide right-of-way known as Appleby Street; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date (AB-23-04) 6. Resolution No. 106-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 0.88 acre property generally located at 685 Berkeley street, the abandonment of a 5,946 square foot portion of a required 25-foot-wide right-of-way known as Appleby street; providing for repealer; providing for an effective date (AB-23-05) The Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated . He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should item 11.A.1 . not be approved , no vote would be taken on the remaining items. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex-parte disclosures. The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Peter Begovich gave the PowerPoint presentation . He began with the location and history of the property, and the proposed amendments and rezoning code changes for the project. Mr. Begovich advised that the right-of-way abandonment would benefit the public welfare by enhancing and providing new sidewalks. He advised that the Community Appearance Board , the Planning and Zoning Board , and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Attorney for the applicant Bonnie Miskel provided additional detail of the property and mentioned that the former owner of the property was the Town of Highland Beach. Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Brief discussion ensued . units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Ordinance No. 4035 (the Boca Raton Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order) , as amended , to provide that the office allocation in Downtown Subarea D and Downtown Subarea G may be reduced by up to ninety percent (90%) ; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (AM-25-05/PZCO) Arlene Cheese-Nelson, DORI Planning Analyst , gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with the history of Ordinance 4035, background of the DORI subareas , and maximum amount of uses for the areas. She continued with the proposed amendments and subarea use changes. Ms. Cheese­ Nelson advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to Members' questions . The public comment period was opened. Attorney Ele Zachariades provided additional information and details regarding the changes that were proposed. Jonathan Ounjian shared concern about the allowable density in the downtown area. Jon Pearlman spoke against further development in the Downtown . John Donaldson spoke in favor of the proposed changes and explained that, as a result of ongoing development, the conversions and transfers of the subareas are needed to determine allowable density of future projects. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5735. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton considering the appeal of the decision of the Community Appearance Board denying a master sign plan for Congress Corporate Plaza I (Application No. PZSSA-2024-00008) generally located at 901-949 Clint Moore Road ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The City Attorney confirmed the Quasi-Judicial procedures are still in effect Members made their ex­ parte disclosures . The City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Zoning Manager Tori Boone gave the PowerPoint presentation . She began with the location of the subject property , the request for appeal, and history of denials regarding the sign request. She advised that staff recommend the City Council reverse the Community Appearance Board's decision to deny the Master Sign Plan . Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued with Ms. Boone and Mr. Schaad answering Members' questions . The public hearing was opened . Bobra Bush President of the Congress Corporate Condo Association spoke on behalf of the Association. She provided additional details and information related to her appeal and asked Council to overturn the denial. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 114-2025, granting the appeal. Extended discussion ensued. Development Services Director Brandon Schaad further explained the updates that were made to the sign code and advised that they were streamlined to limit these types of appeals from coming to the Council. There was consensus for staff to further streamline the Master Sign Code process. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.header: PRESENTATION ON TENTATIVE BUDGET, PROPOSED MILLAGE RATES, AND CAPITAL
units.text: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: Budget Director Sharon McGuire gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by reviewing the City's Vision , Mission and Values, as well as the Strategic Focus Areas and Priorities. Ms. McGuire announced the proposed millage rate of 3.6649 mils, which was slightly lower than the FY 2024-25 rate. A statement of fund balances for the general fund was displayed and additions for the new fiscal year were outlined . Ms. McGuire then described the Property Tax Bill by Taxing Authority breakdown. Also noted the tax rates and Fire Assessment fees of surrounding cities and how Boca Raton is the lowest of the cities compared. Ms. McGuire concluded her presentation with a review of City-wide operating costs and made herself available for Members' questions. Mayor Singer asked for clarification regarding an increase for certain areas of the budget. Deputy City Manager/CFO Jim Zervis advised that this was not a rise in costs but a transfer between funds to more correctly categorize the expenditures. Mr. Zervis noted that staff had worked diligently to cut approximately 9 million from the overall budget and confirmed that no sacrifice in service occurred due to the reductions. Ms. McGuire continued by briefly reviewing the Capital Improvements Program for Fiscal Year 2025/26 through 2030/31 and how each project aligned with the City's Key Priorities. Upon concluding , she and Mr. Zervis responded to Members' questions.
units.full: IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM: Budget Director Sharon McGuire gave the PowerPoint presentation. She began by reviewing the City's Vision , Mission and Values, as well as the Strategic Focus Areas and Priorities. Ms. McGuire announced the proposed millage rate of 3.6649 mils, which was slightly lower than the FY 2024-25 rate. A statement of fund balances for the general fund was displayed and additions for the new fiscal year were outlined . Ms. McGuire then described the Property Tax Bill by Taxing Authority breakdown. Also noted the tax rates and Fire Assessment fees of surrounding cities and how Boca Raton is the lowest of the cities compared. Ms. McGuire concluded her presentation with a review of City-wide operating costs and made herself available for Members' questions. Mayor Singer asked for clarification regarding an increase for certain areas of the budget. Deputy City Manager/CFO Jim Zervis advised that this was not a rise in costs but a transfer between funds to more correctly categorize the expenditures. Mr. Zervis noted that staff had worked diligently to cut approximately 9 million from the overall budget and confirmed that no sacrifice in service occurred due to the reductions. Ms. McGuire continued by briefly reviewing the Capital Improvements Program for Fiscal Year 2025/26 through 2030/31 and how each project aligned with the City's Key Priorities. Upon concluding , she and Mr. Zervis responded to Members' questions.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing , pursuant to chapter 13, Article Ill , "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances, the sale of an easement for telecommunications purposes over approximately 0.493 acres of City-owned land within Spanish River Park (located at 3001 North Ocean Blvd) ; authorizing the execution of a purchase and sale agreement; authorizing the execution of an easement deed pursuant to such purchase and sale agreement; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Deputy Director of Development Services Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation. She gave a history of the location , intended use of the easement, and reviewed the purchase and sale agreement. She advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , she answered Members' questions . The public comment period was opened. William Swaim wanted assurances that this cable would not cross his property. Jonathan Pearlman advised that the City does not need the money from this easement sale/lease, the site is environmentally sensitive, and the City should not rush into this sale/ lease. Seeing no one else come forward , the public comment period was closed . Discussion ensued with City Attorney Josh Koehler advising that this use is specifically permitted by City Code. Mr. Schaad and Ms. Sita provided additional information and answered Members' questions. Guillermo Canete, on behalf of the applicant, advised that there is no new construction and they are utilizing existing infrastructure and conduits. Council Member Thomson questioned whether a fiber optic cable constitutes infrastructure and still had concerns. Further discussion ensued . City Manager Brown and Mr. Koehler provided additional details regarding this type of telecommunications easement and permitted uses. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No.5749. Motion passed four votes to one (4 to 1); Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton adopting a final budget and appropriating funds for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2025, and ending September 30, 2026; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Pearlman requested information regarding the Tree Legacy Program and costs associated with Government Campus Redevelopment , stated that new costs associated with the Government Campus Redevelopment should not be included in the proposed budget, and asked that the tree survey of Sugar Sand Park be halted . Don Huber expressed concern about the need for local governments to reduce expenses . Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . The Mayor noted that the City has the lowest property tax rate of any other full-service City, and Mr. Zervis advised that cost-cutting measures had resulted in the reduction of operating expenses by two million dollars. Mr. Zervis also clarified that there was no increase in the millage rate , and if the voters approved a final development agreement for the Government Campus Redevelopment, a budget amendment would be brought forth to address fiscal impacts related to the development order. City Manager George Brown advised that the tree location survey taking place in Sugar Sand Park was necessary to map the condition of the Park and update the City's survey of the property. Deputy Mayor Nachlas shared a brief PowerPoint regarding boat charters picking up and dropping off at Silver Palm Park and expressed concerns about the activity from the Marine Advisory Board. Mr. Brown provided additional details about the issue, suggested staff collect more data , and come back to Members with options to address the problem . Members weighed in and there was consensus for staff to research the issue and present solutions for Council to review . Council Member Wigder outlined his suggested revisions to the budget, including both reduction and addition of staff, implementation of Al programs, permit waivers for new businesses , updating of the Parks Master Plan , and park beautification . Mr. Brown , Mr. Zervis, and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided additional information. They shared details on the positions that were highlighted and advised that a number of the requests could be addressed through existing operations or with funds already budgeted. Mayor Singer then addressed the requests from non-profit organizations and there was consensus from Members to revise the non-profit awards as noted. Council Members thanked the 0MB and Financial Services staff for their hard work. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to adopt Ordinance No. 5751. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Fran Nachlas, to adopt Ordinance No. 5752 as amended to include Exhibits 1,2,3 as presented and the revisions to the Non-profits as discussed. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton adopting the FY 2025/26-2030/31 Capital Improvements Program for the City of Boca Raton; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Manager George Brown advised that the full presentation had been made previously by staff. Mr. Zervis confirmed that the previous presentation incorporated modifications that were presented in Exhibit 3. The public hearing was opened. Jon Pearlman commented on CIP funds being allocated to Public Works & Engineering and Utilities Services, and made a public records request for the costs for the next 2- and 5-year plans. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . The Mayor noted that the requested information was available on the City website and confirmed that Mr. Zervis had already reached out to Mr. Pearlman with a link to the CIP document that contained a project-by-project description . Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to adopt Resolution No. 142-2025 as amended to include Exhibit 4. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Mayor Singer and Members thanked staff and Mr. Brown for their work on the budget. In honor of his decades of service to the residents of Boca Raton , the Mayor presented Mr. Brown with a key to the City. Mr. Brown shared that this would be his last meeting in his current role and noted that he had attended roughly 2,100 meetings during his tenure. He shared that he looked forward to his continuing involvement with the City and believed that great things were ahead .

Mr. Zervis confirmed that the previous presentation incorporated modifications that were presented in Exhibit 3. The public hearing was opened. Jon Pearlman commented on CIP funds being allocated to Public Works & Engineering and Utilities Services, and made a public records request for the costs for the next 2- and 5-year plans. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . The Mayor noted that the requested information was available on the City website and confirmed that Mr. Zervis had already reached out to Mr. Pearlman with a link to the CIP document that contained a project-by-project description . Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to adopt Resolution No. 142-2025 as amended to include Exhibit 4. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Mayor Singer and Members thanked staff and Mr. Brown for their work on the budget. In honor of his decades of service to the residents of Boca Raton , the Mayor presented Mr. Brown with a key to the City. Mr. Brown shared that this would be his last meeting in his current role and noted that he had attended roughly 2,100 meetings during his tenure. He shared that he looked forward to his continuing involvement with the City and believed that great things were ahead .

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton providing for submission to the electors of a proposed Charter amendment prohibiting the lease, sale, or other alienation of City-owned land greater than one-half (0.5) acre, or any part thereof, without voter approval by referendum ; providing for s special election to be held on March 10, 2026; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Attorney Joshua Koehler gave a presentation detailing the merits of the two resolutions relating to the proposed Charter and Ordinance amendments. Upon concluding , he responded to Members' questions. The public hearing was opened. Alex Pollack, Joe Majhess, Mike Liebelson , Jon Pearlman , Richard Warner, and Jonathan Ounjian , all spoke against proposed Resolutions 159-2025 and 160-2025 and encouraged Members to take up the ordinances attached to each resolution. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 159-2025 as amended to reflect the Special Election date of January 13, 2026. Discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson stated that he approved of the residents getting the opportunity to vote on the proposed amendments to the Charter and Ordinance. Council Member Wigder advised that he did not agree with the proposed language in the Charter and Ordinance amendments and noted that, as written , they could have unintended negative consequences to both the City and its not-for-profit partners. Deputy Mayor Nachlas and Council Member Drucker emphasized that the City Council must represent all residents of the City , not just those of one area, and agreed that the ordinances needed to be on a ballot for the voters. Mayor Singer agreed that, while that the ordinances should go to the voters , he had concerns with portions of the language and how they could be legally interpreted. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 160-2025 as amended to reflect the Special Election date of January 13, 2026. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: 1. Reports from Staff Deputy City Manager and Chief Financial Officer Jim Zervis gave a presentation on the economic and fiscal impact analysis. Members from PFM Mallory Richards and Kevin Plenzler provided an executive summary of the development overview, projected economic impacts, and fiscal impacts. P3 review findings were highlighted , as well as the Public Development Construction Impact. Methodology used to assess the data was described . The Pro Forma analysis was reviewed and financing considerations were discussed, with Mr. Zervis providing additional information . After sharing the Preliminary Series Bond Summaries, discussion ensued with Mr. Zervis and PFM representatives answering Members' questions and providing additional details. 2. Public Comment Mike Massare Ila, Susan Imrie, and Vic Rose spoke in favor of the Government Campus Project. Lorraine Blank, Richard Warner, Martha Parker, Sue White, Michael Kohner, Joe Mahjess, Richard Grubel , Mike Liebelson, Pam Paschke, Ivonne Zurn Tobel, Steve Zurn Tobel , Jonathan Pearlman, Michelle Grau, Jacob Abraham, Mike Manko, Judy Morrow, Betsy Nieporte, Joseph Graubart, Pedro Voyer, Meredith Madsen, Martin Bell, Mario Bennese, Eric Blanchette, and Joseph Bujalski all spoke against the Government Campus Project. The meeting was recessed at 8:01 PM and resumed at 8:20 PM . Discussion ensued, with Mr. Zervis and PFM providing answers to questions raised during public comment and offering additional details and clarified facts.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, providing for submission to the electors of a referendum question in connection with the proposed downtown campus public-private partnership (P3) project, to be considered at the March 10, 2026, Uniform Municipal Election; providing for severability; providing for repealer; and providing an effective date Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 18-2025 and send the ballot language to the Supervisor of Elections to be included on the March 10, 2026 ballot following the bond referendum question. Council Member Thomson then proposed a new version of the ballot language that he believed to be more neutral. He shared a PowerPoint presentation with Members and explained his reasoning for requesting the amended language. Motion was made by Council Member Andy Thomson, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to amend the ballot language included in Resolution No. 180-2025. Council Member Wigder then gave a PowerPoint presentation that addressed the resiliency of the City, reviewed the timeline of the Government Campus Project, and endorsed a balanced path forward. Members weighed in and suggested alternate versions of the language. Lengthy discussion ensued . The meeting recessed at 10:25 PM and resumed at 10:52 PM . Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to amend the proposed revised language. Further Discussion ensued. City Attorney Joshua Koehler provided details relating to the upcoming timeline of the Municipal election and when ballot language needed to be approved . Debate continued over potential language and consensus was reached to approve a final version. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 178-2025 as amended; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes, Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. Motion passed 4 to 1.

Resolution No. 172-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 10.44-acre property generally located at 1700 Clint Moore Road and 6111 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway, accepting and approving the plat known as Atrium at Boca Raton (a replat of parcel O, Arivda Park of Commerce plat No. 4, together with a portion of Section 1, Township 47 South, Range 42, East) pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request; authorizing the Mayor, City Manager, City Civil Engineer, and City Clerk to execute the plat; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (UC-24-02/SUB) 4. Resolution No. 173-2025 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering, for an approximately 8.92-acre property generally located at 1700 Clint Moore Road and 6111 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway, an amendment to an approved Site Plan (Planning and Zoning Board Resolution No. 08-14), pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request to (i) add a 0.90- acre portion of the 2.43-acre parcel at 1700 Clint Moore Road to the parcel at 6111 Northwest Broken Sound Parkway, and (ii) authorize a Commercial Industrial Multifamily Development (CIMD) to construct a new eight (8)-story, 222-unit, approximately 289,677 square foot multifamily residential building with a four (4)-level integrated parking structure, including ten (10) percent affordable housing units and five (5) percent workforce housing units and approximately 2,015 square feet of restaurant/retail space to be located on the ground floor, with related on-site and off-site improvements; providing for repealer and specifically repealing Planning and Zoning Board Resolutions Nos. 84-25R and 98-42; providing an effective date (UC-24-02/SPA) The Deputy Mayor noted that the public hearings would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. She noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item and should items A.1 and B.1 not be approved, no vote would be taken on the remaining items. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex- parte disclosures, and the City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Jim Bell gave the PowerPoint presentation. He began with a history of the property, and reviewed the application requests, zoning change, and future land use changes. He advised that the Community Appearance Board approved the application with recommendations, the Planning and Zoning Board approved, and staff recommend approval with one condition. Upon concluding, he responded to Members' questions. Attorney for the applicant Michael Marshall advised that he had a presentation but it was covered by staff's material and he offered to respond to any questions. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Pearlman questioned the parking and proposed uses. Mike Liebelson expressed concerns about ex-parte procedures. Vivian Lesher relayed her worry that the construction would disturb any wildlife that was on the property. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Discussion ensued and Development Services Director Brandon Schaad responded to Member's questions. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 177-2025. Motion passed 4 votes to 0; Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. units.text: Jonathan Pearlman expressed concern with comments of a prior speaker and spoke against agenda item 15.E, Ordinance No. 5766. Joe Majhess noted the amount of time it took to get a local street repair completed and recommended significant due diligence be performed in regard to picking P3 partners. Richard Warner spoke against agenda item 15.E, Ordinance No. 5766. Michelle Grau presented a PowerPoint addressing the discount rate used in the financial analysis and urged the Council to be fiscally responsible. Mike Liebelson questioned comparables used in the PFM appraisal and the final appraisal amount. Deputy City Manager and CFO Jim Zervis responded to comments made and provided additional information and details related to the appraisal.

units.text: 1. Reports from Staff Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik gave an update to the Government Campus project. He reviewed the timeline and then provided a brief overview of the design of the park, infrastructure and civic buildings. He clarified comments made at the previous days' CRA and Workshop Meetings and updated the financial projections. He concluded by discussing the asthetics, height and building mass. Upon concluding, he introduced CBRE representatives Lee Ann Korst and Mike McShea. The City Attorney reviewed the terms of the agreement and answered Members' questions. Discussion ensued. Council Member Thomson shared a PowerPoint presentation and raised questions concerning the language in the agreement and proposed an alternate version . 2. Public Comment Lorraine Blank, Steve Zurn Tobel, Richard Warner, Michelle Grau, Jon Pearlman, Mac Johnson, Pam Paschke, Martha Parker, Joe Majhess, Holli Schutler, and Ely Gascoyne relayed their opposition to the project. Mike Massarella read an excerpt from a Sun Sentinel article, and Gerald Ligouri and Jason Haber expressed their support of the Government Campus Redevelopment project. The meeting was recessed at 8:04 PM and resumed at 8:22 PM . Judy Morrow, Martin Bell , Briana Hagquist, and Mike Liebelson spoke in opposition to the project. Joshua Rosenfeld spoke in favor of the project. Discussion ensued . Deputy City Manager and CFO Jim Zervis and Mike McShea provided clarification regarding the financial projections and discount rate. Members weighed in.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28 , "Zoning," Article XV, Division 14, "Live Local Act of 2023 Affordable Housing," Sections 28-1637, 28-1638, 28-1639 and 28-1640, Code of Ordinances, to align with Chapters 2024-188 and 2025-172, Laws of Florida with respect to: maximum floor area ratio; reductions to minimum parking requirements; limitations on minimum square footage of non-residential uses, maximum building height adjacent to certain single-family residential areas; post-expiration treatment of developments under the Live Local Act; affordability requirements and enforcement; exemptions for certain parcels near airport runways; requiring affordable units to be rental and not owner-occupied ; eliminating an appeal provision ; relocating standards for the determination of maximum density and adding standards for maximum height and maximum floor area ratio (FAR) ; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-24-06) Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation . units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, amending Article I, Division 1, Section 28-2, "Definitions," to create a definition of "Freestanding Emergency Facility" and amending the defin ition of "Outpatient Surgery Center" to exclude emergency room procedures from said definition, amending Article XI, "Business and Commercial Districts, " to provide that Freestanding Emergency Facilities shall be Conditional Uses in the B-4, MC, City CG and City CHO zoning districts, and amending Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, to create a new Section 28-1320, Code of Ordinances, to set forth eligibility criteria for properties to include a Freestanding Emergency Facility ; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-25-11) The Mayor noted that it was the first of two public hearings for th is item and no vote would be taken until the second public hearing. Tamashbeen Rahman gave the PowerPoint presentation . She provided a summary of the proposed text amendment, history of a previous project denial and its subsequent appeal process. She advised that staff recommend approval and made herself available for questions. Council Member Thomson inquired why the project was being heard prior to the Planning and Zoning Board hearing , and Mr. Schaad advised that he was directed to continue with the processing of the item and noted that there would be no vote on the item tonight. The public hearing was opened . Leslie Del Monte advised that the LIRP zone would be a better district because of the population growth in that area. Joe Majhess stated that he was in favor of the project and increasing the available districts for this kind of use. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Mr. Schaad and Ms. Rahman provided additional information. The Mayor reiterated that this was only the first of two public hearings for this item, and that the second public hearing would be February 10, 2026 .

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton , Florida, creating Chapter 13, "Public Lands," Article Ill, "Sale of City property, " Section 13-75, "Protection of City-Owned Lands With Public Purpose Safeguards, " Code of Ordinances, to establish requirements for the sale, lease, or disposition of City-Owned Lands greater than one-half (0 .5) acre; providing that such actions shall require two (2) public hearings and written findings that the action serves a public purpose and benefits City residents; providing exceptions for easements, routine municipal purposes, and certain leases or licenses; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date Development Services Director Brandon Schaad provided an overview of the ordinance and explained that it was intended to create a higher standard for the conveyance of public land greater than 0.5 an acre. The public hearing was opened . Jacob Abraham, Jon Pearlman, and Joe Mahjess spoke against the proposed ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5766. Council Member Thomson shared that he appreciated the efforts to enhance protection of public lands but did not believe the ordinance went far enough . Members weighed in and brief discussion ensued . Motion passed 3 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker voting yes; Council Member Andy Thomson voting no.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton authorizing a transaction between the City, the Boca Raton Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA), and Boca Raton City Center, LLC, relating to the redevelopment of the Downtown Campus; providing for a mixed-use, transit-oriented district on City-owned property east of Northwest Second Avenue and the improvement of City­ owned property west of Northwest Second Avenue for public parks and civic uses, pursuant to Section 163.380, Florida Statutes, and Chapter 13, Article 111 , "Sale of City Property," Code of Ordinances; provid ing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date City Manager Mark Sohaney gave a brief overview of the proposed project, thanked the veterans who provided their input, and commended staff for their work on this project. Deputy City Manager Andy Lukasik highlighted who would be presenting and outlined why and what the Council would be considering later in the meeting. He continued by providing details about the regulatory commitments, site plan requirements, and financing . City Attorney Josh Koehler reviewed the legal agreements, which included the Master Partnership Agreement (MPA), construction phasing, funding , and enforcement rights and remedies. He concluded by referencing the referendum and advised that this agreement would require approval of the residents at the municipal election. Mr. Lukasik provided a quick review of the timeline before introducing Kevin Plenzler, Director at PFM Financial Advisors. Mr. Plenzler shared a summary of the proposed economic and fiscal impacts and expected net revenues to the City. Mr. Zervis provided additional information, and Mr. Plenzler continued with a review of ground rent revenue, capital revenue estimates, and public investment. The public hearing was opened. George Harper, Howard Gainer, John Schrey, Jose Alvarez, Ken Wittenberg , Andy Reese, Larry Colburn, Ed Venezia, Jason Hayward, Ned Kimmelman, Jerry Castillo, Josh Rosenfeld, Ely Nesirie, and Benjamin Schreier, spoke in favor of the project. Joe Majhess, Briana Hagquist, Mike Liebelson, Aphrodite Petinakis, Michelle Grau, Jon Pearlman, Jacob Abraham, Yvonne Zurn Tobe!, Martin Bell, and Betsy Nieporte, spoke against the project. Deputy City Managers Jim Zervis and Andy Lukasik responded to statements made during the public hearing and provided clarification . The meeting was recessed at 12:31 PM and resumed at 1:17 PM . Judy Morrow, Richard Warner, Elly Gascoyne, Pam Paschke, Lyudmila Pearlman, Alexandra Avello, and Joseph Pujalski expressed their opposition to the project. Elie Bennett, Aliza Bennett, George Garcia, Adam Gold, Jonathan Ounjian , and Vic Rose stated their support of the project. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued . Deputy City Manager Jorge Camejo commented on the train station and advised that it was an important feature regardless of who operates it. Mr. Plenzler shared additional comments and information . Council members weighed in and provided their reasons for supporting or opposing the ordinance. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5769; Motion passed 4 votes to 1; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes; Council Member Andy Thomson voting no. The meeting recessed at 2:59 PM and resumed at 3:20 PM .

units.text: A resolution of the City Council of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, regarding a referendum petition affidavit submitted pursuant to City Charter Section 6.02; finding that the relief sought therein is duplicative of and already provided by a binding Citywide referendum scheduled for March 10, 2026; determining that the affidavit does not trigger the Charter's referendum process; directing the City Clerk not to process or accept signature pages submitted pursuant to said affidavit; providing for severability; providing an effective date City Manager Mark Sohaney briefly reviewed the resolution and asked the City Attorney to provide additional information . City Attorney Joshua Koehler reaffirmed that all related agreements, ordinances, and resolution were contingent on the March 10 municipal election , noting that the referendum was already scheduled for the ballot and that both the City's legal team and outside counsel agreed Ordinance 5769 , passed January 20, 2026, was conditional on the election outcome. The public hearing was opened . Joe Majhess and Jonathan Ounjian expressed their support for the ordinance. Jon Pearlman, Richard Warner, and Lyudmilla Pearlman spoke against the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed. Discussion ensued . The Mayor provided additional information in response to statements made and Members expressed their support of the resolution . Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 006-2026. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton, Florida, amending Chapter 28, Zoning , Article XV, Supplementary District Regulations, Division 1, Generally, Code of Ordinances, by creating Section 28-1320, Public and Recreational Use Limitation for City-Owned Public Parks, to limit such parks to public and recreational uses, including accessory uses related thereto; prohibiting the development of other uses thereon ; providing for the continued use and placement of easements, utilities, and infrastructure that do not substantially interfere with such public and recreational uses; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification; providing an effective date Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave a description of the proposed Ordinance and reviewed the proposed protections, limitations, and allowable uses within City parks. He advised that staff recommended approval and made himself available for questions. Council Member Marc Wigder gave a PowerPoint presentation, refuted misinformation , and advised that he supports approval of this ordinance. The public hearing was opened. Jonathan Pearlman spoke against the proposed Government Campus. Richard Warner relayed his disappointment with the wording of the ordinance. Martin Bell proposed alternative plans to the BACE Building and Police Station sites should the referendum be approved. Pam Paschke praised Mr. Pearlman's initial efforts to preserve City park land . Jonathan Ounjian spoke against the Save Boca group. Mike Liebelson was concerned with amending the City Charter regarding City owned land. Judy Morrow spoke about issues relating to tennis. Lyudmila Pearlman had concerns regarding City parks and land protections. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Further discussion ensued . Mr. Wigder advised that he had been working on this project to preserve City parks for several years. Council Member Thomson shared that this ordinance was meaningful and he would support it. Deputy Mayor Nachlas also expressed her support of the ordinance. Mayor Singer advised that he respected healthy discussion and that he believed misinformation by a certain group had been harmful to this project. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5768. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering the adoption of amendments to the Boca Raton Comprehensive Plan and its goals, objectives, and policies in accordance with a requirement in Chapter 163, Florida Statutes, to conduct an evaluation and appraisal of the Comprehensive Plan ; amending the Community Profile, Future Land Use Element, Transportation Element, Housing Element, Infrastructure Element, Coastal Management Element, Conservation Element, Recreation and Open Space Element, Intergovernmental Coordination Element, Historic Preservation Element, Capital Improvements Element and the map series; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC- 25-01) Development Services Long Range Project Manager Jim Bell gave the PowerPoint presentation . He gave a brief history of the Comprehensive Plan (Comp Plan) and its future implementations as required by the State. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board had approved the ordinance by a vote of 6-0, and staff recommended transmitting the ordinance to the Florida Department of Commerce for approval of the proposed amendments. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened. Donna Bloomberg was concerned about storm drainage in flood zones and advised that the City should look at other cities and countries for creative solutions. Mike Liebelson stated that the City should make the plans clearer and implement the actions in the Plan . Brandon Schaad clarified the Comp Plan's current purpose and future intention . Pam Paschke asked if the height of the buildings in the City are included in the Comp Plan and shared concerns about traffic congestion. Richard Warner spoke out against the Comp Plan . Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to transmit Ordinance No. 5770. Discussion ensued. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, Zoning, and Chapter 23, Planning and Development, Code of Ordinances, to create the Downtown Zoning District, replacing land development regulations and review processes set forth in Ordinance No. 4035, as amended (the Downtown Development of Regional Impact (DORI) Development Order) for areas rezoned to the Downtown Zoning District, and setting forth related regulations for future development in Downtown Boca Raton ; establishing specific requirements for the redevelopment of the Government Center area, including regulations related to uses, parking , landscaping , open space and architectural standards; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SC-25-20) Development Services Deputy Director Erin Sita gave the PowerPoint presentation. She gave a brief summary of the Downtown Zoning district and reviewed the proposed amendments. She advised that the amendment was consistent with the Comp Plan and that both the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , she made herself available for questions. Discussion ensued . The public hearing was opened. Donna Bloomberg was concerned with parking. Jonathan Ounjian spoke about the proposed land use and was in favor of ground floor retail on every building in the Downtown . Meredith Madsen suggested City-wide parking passes for residents. Richard Warner spoke against the ordinance. Mike Liebelson was concerned with height variances. Brandon Schaad clarified misinformation and provided additional details. Jon Pearlman spoke against the proposed amendments to ordinances in the Downtown. Pam Paschke was concerned with the height of the proposed buildings in the Government Campus. Discussion ensued and Mr. Schaad clarified comments made. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Further discussion ensued; the Mayor advised that this was the first of two public hearings and no vote would be taken tonight. The meeting recessed at 8:06 PM and resumed at 8: 19 PM.

units.text: A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 1.33-acre portion of the approximately 140.8-acre "The Boca Raton" (F/K/A the Boca Raton Resort and Club) property generally located at 501 East Camino Real, site plan approval to authorize construction of a three (3)-story, approximately 52 foot tall , approximately 31 ,695 square foot fitness center and related site improvements; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (SPA-25-09) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on 11 .A and B would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item, and should item 11 .A not be approved , then no vote would be taken on the remaining item. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing. Members made their ex-parte disclosures, and the City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation . He provided a history of the proposed areas affected , reviewed the applicants request, and highlighted the site plan . He advised that the application would not lead to an increase in onsite activities or an increase in traffic. Mr. Devlin noted that the application was for a relocation of an existing use already on the property, consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and complied with all applicable codes. He further advised that the Planning and Zoning Board , Community Appearance Board , and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for Members' questions. The public hearing was opened . On behalf of the applicant, attorney Bonnie Miske! responded to Members' questions and reviewed the site plans and project renderings. Stephanie Rosenweig and Joseph Pujalski stated their opposition to the project. Bonnie Miske! clarified comments made during the public hearing. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Resolution No. 012-2026. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Resolution No. 013-2026. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 2, "Administration ," Article II , "City Council ," Section 2-27, "Rules of Procedure," of the City Code of Ordinances; updating and modernizing City Council meeting procedures; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date. City Manager Mark Sohaney gave a brief presentation detailing the proposed changes and updates to the Rules of Procedure. City Attorney Joshua Koehler advised that there had been no significant update to the rules since 1966 and they should reflect how the Council operated today. He further advised that, going forward , the Roberts Rules of Order to be used would be the latest edition . The public hearing was opened. Pam Paschke and Richard Warner asked various questions related to the changes. Joseph Pujalski questioned the City's policy concern ing various topics. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued, and Mayor Singer and Mr. Koehler responded to questions and provided additional information. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5757. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Marc Wigder, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning," Code of Ordinances, amending Article I, Division 1, Section 28-2 , "Definitions," to create a definition of "Freestanding Emergency Facility" and amending the definition of "Outpatient Surgery Center" to exclude emergency room procedures from said definition, amending Article XI, "Business and Commercial Districts," to provide that Freestanding Emergency Facilities shall be Conditional Uses in the B-4, MC, City CG and City CHO zoning districts, and amending Article XV, "Supplementary District Regulations," Division 1, to create a new Section 28-1320, Code of Ordinances, to set forth eligibility criteria for properties to include a Freestanding Emergency Facility ; providing for severability; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-25-11) Public Works and Engineering Director Brandon Schaad gave the PowerPoint presentation, noting that this was the continuation of the 2nd of two public hearings on this item. He began with a background of the project, summary of the text amendment, and showed a map of areas eligible for free-standing emergency facilities. He described additional research done of neighboring cities that permit FSEF's and noted that Palm Beach County is considering a similar ordinance. The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval as presented . Upon concluding, Mr. Schaad responded to Members' questions and discussion ensued . The public hearing was opened. John Donaldson advised that he performed traffic studies on this use in other areas and was concerned with the data calculations. Dr. Evan Goldstein provided highlights of his experience in emergency medicine . Discussion ensued and Dr. Goldstein provided additional information in response to Members' questions. Josh Brodie shared his thoughts about the policy and procedural events that led to the item's postponement. Jeffrey Barker, Attorney for a prior applicant, stated his issues with parking and traffic ingress and egress. Gila Brand spoke in favor of the project and relayed concerns about the delay of the ordinance. Jonathan Ounjian spoke in favor of FSEF's in the LIRP district. Richard Warner shared his disappointment with the process of getting this project approved . Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Extended Discussion ensued . The meeting recessed at 8:23 P.M. and resumed at 8:39 P.M. There was consensus to postpone the item for discussion at the next Council Workshop Meeting on March 23, 2026, and the public hearing for the Regular Meeting on March 24, 2026. Motion was made by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker to postpone Ordinance No. 5767 to the next regular Council Meeting on March 24, 2026. Motion carried unanimously on a voice vote.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 28, "Zoning ," Article XV, Division 15, *Affordable and Workforce Housing in Commercial and Industrial Zoning Districts," Code of Ordinances, clarifying requirements for on-site retail sales or services in Commercial Industrial Multifamily Developments (CIMDs) by amending Section 28-1642 to create a definition of "retail sales or services" that specifically excludes gyms or fitness centers and tutoring establishments, or uses similar to either of those, and by amending Section 28-1644 to set forth minimum requirements for such retail sales or services uses in CIMDs, including that such businesses be independent operations that provide for public accessibility , including by separate, ground floor pedestrian entrance from outdoors with exterior business identification, that such businesses publicly advertise and market, and that any change of use be reviewed by the City to ensure any requirement for on-site retail sales or services use(s) continues to be satisfied; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date (AM-25-13) Development Services Director Brandon Schaad gave a PowerPoint presentation . He began with a history of the previous ordinances and the proposed amendments. He advised that the Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon Concluding he made himself available for questions. Discussion ensued . The public comment period was opened . John Donaldson was concerned about the traffic for retail use. Seeing no one else come forward , the public comment period was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Mayor Scott Singer, to approve Ordinance No. 5773 as presented. Discussion ensued and there was consensus to move forward with a minimum of 45 business operating hours for retail and restaurant use. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5773 as amended Motion carried unanimously; Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Mayor Scott Singer, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton amending Chapter 6, "Elections," Section 6-16, "Proof of Residency and Elector Status, " Code of Ordinances, to increase the number of required documents supporting a candidate's residency affidavit for the offices of Mayor and City Council Member from two (2) to three (3); to add to the list of acceptable documents; and to require submission of a current voter information card confirming elector status at the time of qualifying; and to provide for the use of voting history as evidence of nonresidency; providing for severability ; providing for repealer; providing for codification ; providing an effective date City Manager Mark Sohaney gave a brief history of the proposed amendment. City Attorney Joshua Koehler detailed the proposed changes and advised that the existing residency requirements were being strengthened . Discussion ensued . The public hearing was opened . Pam Paschke questioned proof of residency for renters. Richard Warner stated that he agreed with the proposed changes. Joe Majhess suggested two years of residency and expressed his support of the ordinance. Seeing no one else come forward, the public hearing was closed . Extended discussion ensued. Motion was made by Mayor Scott Singer, seconded by Council Member Yvette Drucker, to approve Ordinance No. 5777. Motion carried unanimously; Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder, Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas voting yes.

units.text: Brianna Hagquist spoke regarding banyan trees being taken down for new development in the City . Michelle Grau shared concerns about literature being distributed by a potential developer. Sherri Croyle relayed issues with the number of residential homes being used as student housing . Marjie Alloy requested a modification to construction plans for The Boca Raton in order to save trees. Phil Croyle echoed comments made by Sherri Croyle about homes being rented to students. Richard Warner spoke against short-term rentals such as Airbnb and VRBO. Discussion ensued. City Manager Mark Sohaney advised that Airbnb and VRBO's are not allowed in the City and that staff would continue to monitor the situation Elizabeth Decker questioned the referendum and spoke about the Downtown Campus. Martha Parker spoke about the Downtown Campus and urged citizens to vote no. Judy Morrow expressed her displeasure with the number of mailers being sent to her home from the developer for the Downtown Campus. Meredith Madsen conveyed her opposition to the Downtown redevelopment and urged residents to vote no. Kathy Streinger requested the Council to vote against the zoning change for the golf course at the Boca Raton . Pam Paschke spoke against the Downtown Redevelopment. Martin Bell gave a PowerPoint with his suggestions about what should be done with the Downtown Campus. John Shein stated that no one paid him to speak for OneBoca and looked forward to a new Downtown Campus. Joe Majhess spoke in favor of the FSEF and open discussions about the Downtown Campus. Eric Blanchette opposed Save Boca and urged everyone to understand the facts before voting in the upcoming election . Stefanie Rosenzweig spoke against Mizner Blvd being used for construction traffic for The Boca Raton proposed project. Discussion ensued . Mayor Singer addressed concerns and comments made during public requests.

units.text: A The Boca Raton Residential and Parking Structure 1. Ordinance No. 5780 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 1.774-acre portion of an approximately 140.8-acre property generally located at 501 E. Camino Real , a universal conditional (UC) amendment to the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan , pursuant to Chapter 23, Article VI , Code of Ordinances , from Recreation and Open Space (PR) to Residential High (RH) , subject to conditions; providing for revisions to the Future Land Use Map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PUD-85-09R9/SC) 2. Ordinance No. 5781 An ordinance of the City of Boca Raton considering , for an approximately 1.774-acre portion of an approximately 140.8-acre property generally located at 501 E. Camino Real , a universal conditional (UC) rezoning from Recreational (REC) to Multi-family Residential (R-5) , pursuant to Chapter 23 , Article VI, Code of Ordinances, subject to conditions ; providing for the appropriate revision of the zoning district map; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PUD-85-09R9/ZC) 3. Resolution No. 16-2026 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 189.26-acre property generally located at 501 East Camino Real: (a) an amended and restated Master Plan approval consolidating City Council Resolution Nos . 38-83, 192-90, 225-91 , 152-92, 145-95, 29-97, 59-97, 190-97 and 15-2000, and (b) a master plan amendment to (i) authorize the construction of an eight (8)-story, 76-unit, approximately 505,840 square foot Multifamily Residential Building with one (1 )-level of underground parking ; (ii) reflect a new three (3)-story, approximately 31 ,696 square feet fitness center; (iii) and reflect previously approved site plans including a relocated golf maintenance facility , pool and amenity areas , core and beverage area , and the Mizner ballroom ; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PUD-85-09R9/PUD) 4. Resolution No. 17-2026 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for a 5.224-acre portion of the approximately 140.8 acres Boca Raton Resort and Club generally located at 501 East Camino Real, site plan approval , pursuant to a universal conditional (UC) request to construct a new eight (8)-story, 76-unit, approximately 505 ,840 square foot Multifamily Residential Building with one (1 )-level of underground parking , with related off-site and on-site improvements including the reconfiguration of an internal street, and considering the abandonment of a portion of a twelve (12)-foot utility easement; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (PUD-85-09R9/SPA) The Mayor noted that the public hearings on 11.A.1 through 11 .A.4 would be conducted contemporaneously as the items were interrelated. He noted that a separate vote would be taken on each item, and should item 11 .A not be approved, then no vote would be taken on the remaining items. The City Attorney read the quasi-judicial procedures which would govern the public hearing . Members made their ex-parte disclosures, and the City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Development SeNices Director Brandon Schaad and Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation . Mr. Devlin highlighted the location , history, proposed FLUM amendment, zoning and variance requests, and site plans were shown . The Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommend approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions . Discussion ensued and Mr. Schaad provided additional details. The public hearing was opened. Attorney for the applicant Bonnie Miskel gave a PowerPoint presentation . She began with a history of the property and the affected areas of proposed construction. Jim Tinson of Hart Howerton Architects gave additional details regarding the site plan and residences . Michael Gehart, Landscape Architect, provided information relating to the proposed landscaping. Marjie Alloy , Judith Kaye, Stephanie Rosenzwieg , Mike Liebelson , Richard Warner, Pam Paschke, Joseph Puljalski, Michael Schneider, expressed concerns regarding landscaping , public access, and construction vehicles and access. Attorney for the applicant Bonnie Miskel answered questions and provided additional details in response to public comments. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Discussion ensued . The meeting was recessed at 8:45 PM and resumed at 9:02 PM . Extended discussion ensued . Ms . Miskel addressed concessions agreed upon during the recess. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Council Member Marc Wigder, to approve Ordinance No. 5780 with the scriveners' error corrected. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Ordinance No. 5781 with the scriveners' error corrected. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Marc Wigder, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 16-2026 as amended with conditions. Motion carried unanimously. Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes. Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 17-2026 as amended with conditions. Motion carried unanimously. Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.text: 1. Resolution No. 19-2026 A resolution of the City of Boca Raton considering , for the approximately 4.36-acre property generally located at 6501 and 6531 Park of Commerce Boulevard , conditional use approval , pursuant to Section 28-978 , Code of Ordinances , to authorize a 3,263 square foot athletic training facility in an existing 19,862 square foot warehouse and office building , in the Light Industrial Research Park (LIRP) zoning district; providing for repealer; providing an effective date (CA-25-05) The City Attorney confirmed that the quasi-judicial procedures which governed the public hearing were still in effect. Members made their ex-parte disclosures, and the City Clerk administered the oath to those who wished to speak. Senior Planner Eoin Devlin gave the PowerPoint presentation . He provided a history of the property, outlined the applicant's request , and advised that both Planning and Zoning Board and staff recommended approval. Upon concluding , he made himself available for questions. The public hearing was opened . Attorney for the applicant Christina Bilenki advised that Mr. Devlin covered all points and she made herself available for questions . Pam Paschke inquired if Ms. Bilenki was a lawyer, planner, or lobbyist. Ms. Bilenki responded that she was a lawyer. Seeing no one else come forward , the public hearing was closed . Motion was made by Council Member Yvette Drucker, seconded by Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, to approve Resolution No. 19-2026. Mayor Singer suggested this type of use be handled solely by staff as this should be administrative. Motion carried unanimously; Mayor Scott Singer, Deputy Mayor Fran Nachlas, Council Member Yvette Drucker, Council Member Andy Thomson, Council Member Marc Wigder voting yes.

units.header: Comments by newly elected Mayor and Council Members
units.text: Mayor Thomson thanked those who supported him and gave credit to his faith , family , and friends . He acknowledged his former Council colleagues , expressed his anticipation of working with the new members, and said that after the Memorial Park dedication , a priority would be restoring unity to the City and its residents. Deputy Mayor Grau expressed her appreciation to her family, friends , Save Boca supporters , and all who participated in the election . She outlined goals to put residents first and protect their quality of life, and emphasized the importance of transparency, integrity, and fiscal responsibility. Council Member Pearlman extended his gratitude to his wife, family , and Save Boca supporters. He thanked voters for the historic turnout and pledged to serve all residents. Council Member Sipple thanked her family , supporters, and Save Boca. She emphasized responsible development, the protection of parks, beaches , and public spaces, and highlighted the importance of grace, respect, and a sense of community .
